“And since Master Shen also favors our match, it could not be better. How could I delay further? Third Miss need only wait for my news — a matchmaker will certainly come within these two days.”

Shen Weici’s cheeks flushed prettily at his words, yet she still looked at him with warm, clear eyes and said quietly: “Then I will wait for Young Master Zhang.”

Zhang Yuanheng was nearly stunned by that flush of color on her cheek. In all the time before, he had always sensed one or two degrees of cool reserve in Shen Weici’s gaze, making him feel he couldn’t quite reach into her heart.

Today, he suddenly felt that he had drawn just the tiniest bit closer.

His heart grew warmer and warmer, so warm he longed to pull Shen Weici into his arms right then. The impulse was hard to suppress — though he did suppress it, just barely.

He looked at her, a controlled smile on his face: “I will not fail Third Miss.”

This tender, sweet tableau was, every inch of it, stabbing Song Zhang in the eyes from where he stood above.

He watched coldly as the two of them stood together below, and the hand he had placed on the railing almost ground it to pieces.

Especially when Shen Weici reached out to support Zhang Yuanheng a moment ago — Song Zhang’s face had gone so dark that even Minghé was frightened, quietly taking a step backward.

And now Shen Weici stood with a shy, soft expression beside Zhang Yuanheng, her small, slender figure no more than two or three steps away from him.

The tendons rose visibly on the back of Song Zhang’s hand gripping the railing. Then came a crack — the railing snapped, and splinters rained down below.

Shen Weici and Zhang Yuanheng both heard the sound and looked up in unison toward the building across the way. They saw nothing on the railing over there, and neither could say how it had broken.

chapters.title: Waiting to Be Married
chapters.content:
Shen Weici and Zhang Yuanheng did not linger long in the arbor. It was also the first time Shen Weici had spent time alone with Zhang Yuanheng outdoors, and she was worried that if they stayed too long, the maidservants might see and carry tales back to Madam Wen. So she walked back with him toward Tingzhu Hall.

About halfway there, Zhang Yuanheng suddenly stopped, took a box from his attendant’s hands, and placed it in Shen Weici’s. She was startled and looked up to ask him what it was.

Zhang Yuanheng smiled: “Winter has come, and women are susceptible to the cold. It’s common to carry hand warmers when going out.”

“Last time at the Zhang estate, I saw that Third Miss hadn’t brought one. Her fingers must have been red with the cold. So I had someone buy a new one to send to her.”

He quickly added an explanation: “Third Miss need not read anything into it — I simply happened to see one that was attractive and thought to buy it for her. Nothing more than that.”

Shen Weici paused, then opened the box in her hands. Inside lay a bronze-gilt hand warmer with an entwined peony motif.

The hand warmer was delicate and compact, clearly a finer piece than the one Madam Wen had sent her.

Shen Weici looked at it briefly, then closed the box and pressed it back into Zhang Yuanheng’s hands: “I receive Young Master Zhang’s kind intention.”

“But I dare not accept any more gifts from Young Master Zhang at this time. If Young Master Zhang truly wishes to give it to me, I will wait for him to bring it on the day our betrothal is settled.”

Her delicate fingers brushed lightly across Zhang Yuanheng’s palm. The faint coolness of her touch brought Zhang Yuanheng up short as well, and he looked at Shen Weici: “It’s only a hand warmer — no one can say anything.”

Shen Weici took a step back, looking at Zhang Yuanheng: “True, no one may say anything — but I would be ill at ease. The betrothal is not yet settled; how can I receive gift after gift from Young Master Zhang?”

Zhang Yuanheng looked down at the box returned to his hands, then looked at Shen Weici.

A face soft and lovely as spring blossoms reflected in water — and yet eyes that were firm, luminous, and clear. They held none of the languor her features suggested, and instead resembled more a wildflower growing from a cliff face, seeking rain and light in the sheer rock.

Perhaps what had drawn him the first moment he saw her was not her fresh, tender beauty or her slender, graceful bearing, but the gaze that slowly lifted toward him — cool, without flattery, alluring yet as clear and bright as a white lotus.

He gripped the box tightly, then gave Shen Weici a solemn bow of apology: “It was my oversight. Please do not take it amiss, Third Miss.”

He bowed deeply and sincerely, courteous and modest, not crossing any line of propriety.

Shen Weici found a scholarly gentleman of old family like Zhang Yuanheng more than satisfactory. He was, at his core, a man of propriety and gentle temperament — even if he were to take concubines in the future, he would abide by the rules observed by cultivated families and men of letters.

He would give her a steady, secure life.

When Zhang Yuanheng left, Shen Weici stood in place and watched his back recede. The promise he had made before departing still echoed in her ears.

Once his figure had completely vanished from sight, Shen Weici lowered her gaze. She could only hope that Zhang Yuanheng would keep his word and come within these two days.

And yet Shen Weici didn’t know if there was time left.

She turned her gaze toward Tingzhu Hall, where the lamps were already lit. She called for Yue Deng to wait outside, gathered her sleeves, and walked inside.

In the room, Shen Rongsheng was at his calligraphy, a few sweeping strokes forming a large-character inscription.

Shen Weici went to stand beside him and said quietly as she watched his brushwork: “Young Master Zhang just told me that he will have a matchmaker come to formally propose within these two days. Will Father be here at that time?”

Shen Rongsheng’s hand paused. He turned his head to look at Shen Weici: “I have duties at the palace during the day and likely cannot come back.”

Shen Weici had known full well he would say something like this. She looked at her father and said: “Young Master Zhang loves and values me — he comes to propose with a sincere heart. If all goes well and the betrothal is settled, when the new year comes, I will marry into the Earl’s estate, and Second Elder Sister will marry into a Marquis’s estate. Father will have two joyful occasions to celebrate, and will surely be the envy of all.”

“As for the matter between Young Master Zhang and me — Stepmother is not yet aware. If the Earl’s household suddenly arrives with a matchmaker, and Stepmother doesn’t know what to make of it and puts things on hold, I’m afraid the Earl’s household will be left with unfavorable impressions.”

Shen Weici lowered her gaze and added quietly: “Your daughter has not been by Father’s side to be filial — marrying early and being able to come back and pay my respects more often might be a way to make up for that.”

“And besides, as long as your daughter remains in the Marquis’s estate, I worry that Father and Stepmother will argue again on my account. Your daughter carries guilt over that as well.”

Shen Rongsheng listened to Shen Weici’s words, each point reasonable, and genuinely gave it some serious thought.

Zhang Yuanheng had a solid family background, and beyond that, was young and promising, earning imperial favor, with a bright future in the court. Having Shen Weici successfully wed to Zhang Yuanheng would truly be ideal.

He didn’t want anything to go wrong. He frowned in thought and said: “Very well. I’ll look for an opportunity tomorrow to find Young Master Zhang and ask him to let me know before sending the matchmaker, so I can ask leave from the palace and come back in time.”

He looked at Shen Weici: “Your marriage is something I should be paying closer attention to. Nothing can go wrong.”

“Don’t worry — once your betrothal is settled, you’ll leave the Marquis’s estate with the same fanfare and celebration as your sister.”

Shen Weici was so moved that she shed tears, dabbing the corner of her eye with her handkerchief, looking at her father: “Everything since I came to the Marquis’s estate has been thanks to Father watching over me. Weici keeps Father’s kindness in her heart, and is grateful that Father found such a good match for her.”

“Your daughter has nothing to repay you with at this moment, except to make Father a pair of winter boots — that, at least, would be some small token of filial devotion.”

Shen Rongsheng always felt that Shen Weici’s words had a way of warming his heart. Even if he privately admitted that he hadn’t been as attentive to this daughter as she seemed to believe, her eyes were always full of gratitude and reverence for him — quiet and obedient, always thinking of him.

And careful, as if she were always afraid of making him angry.

He looked at Weici and said quietly: “No need for the boots. Not that I don’t appreciate your thoughtfulness — believe me, I can feel your filial heart.”

“But winter is cold. Making boots is hard on the eyes. And the seamstresses in the estate make boots I’m accustomed to wearing.”

“Besides, now that your betrothal is settled, you should be focusing on preparing your trousseau and looking after your health. Don’t worry yourself over other things.”

Hearing these words from her father, Shen Weici bit her lip and lowered her head, then nodded obediently: “Then I will do as Father says.”

Shen Rongsheng gave a hm of acknowledgment, then said to Shen Weici: “It’s late now — go back and rest. If anything comes up, send someone to let me know. And don’t worry about Stepmother giving you trouble over the engagement.”

“As long as I’m here, she won’t have a say.”

Hearing these words from her father, Shen Weici’s heart eased somewhat. All the effort she had put in was only to ensure things went as smoothly as possible.

What Madam Wen had done by bringing her to meet Zhang Tingyi the other day had made her intentions perfectly clear. The only way now was to secure the betrothal with Zhang Yuanheng before that, and to do so as quickly as possible.

Shen Weici finally took her leave from her father’s study. The winter chill outside scattered the warmth she had carried from within. She looked at Yue Deng walking toward her, and smiled softly, saying quietly: “Let us go home.”

chapters.title: Beautiful Serving Girls
chapters.content:
As Zhang Yuanheng crossed out the front gate and was about to board his carriage, a low, calm voice suddenly came from behind: “Master Zhang.”

Zhang Yuanheng’s movement halted. He turned sideways and found himself looking at a tall, handsome young man.

Zhang Yuanheng recognized the man at once. He had once served under Song Zhang when Song Zhang was the Supreme Commander of the Northern Passes. When Song Zhang returned to the capital to take command of the Imperial Guard, this man had come back with him and become a member of the Feathered Forest Guard.

The Feathered Forest Guard was composed of sons of officials at fifth rank and above, and many of them had grown up in the capital. Qi Minghe was someone Zhang Yuanheng knew by name.

He quickly gave a courteous bow: “What business does Guard Qi have with me?”

Minghe was equally courteous, smiling pleasantly: “My general is inviting Master Zhang for a gathering at the general’s estate.”

Zhang Yuanheng hesitated slightly. He and Song Zhang were not particularly close — they exchanged nods when they met, but nothing more.

Song Zhang’s duties centered on guarding the imperial palace and ensuring the emperor’s safety, as well as managing matters within the imperial city. He was a military man. Zhang Yuanheng, on the other hand, was responsible for recording the emperor’s daily remarks and actions, and offering remonstrance — their positions were essentially unrelated.

Moreover, Song Zhang almost never involved himself in political affairs, and when the emperor occasionally drew him into discussions, Song Zhang would give a perfunctory answer and move on without further engagement.

Zhang Yuanheng truly could not imagine why Song Zhang would invite him. He turned the question over several times in his mind with some hesitation.

Beside him, Minghe saw Zhang Yuanheng’s hesitant expression and smiled: “Master Zhang need not overthink it. My general simply wishes to build a friendship with Master Zhang — just a drink and a gathering, nothing more.”

Declining Song Zhang’s invitation outright was not something Zhang Yuanheng dared to do. After all, Song Zhang held the emperor’s own sword — if he found displeasure with someone, he could have them arrested first and ask questions later. Any pretext would do.

He glanced at his own clothes, then bowed in reply: “It is an honor to be invited by General Song. Of course I will go. Only — might I return briefly to change into something more presentable, as a mark of respect?”

Minghe smiled: “It’s just a casual gathering. There’s no need.”

Zhang Yuanheng had no choice but to leave it at that, and asked: “Where is General Song holding the banquet?”

Minghe replied: “At the general’s own residence in Wuyi Lane. Will Master Zhang ride in his own carriage, or shall I see him there?”

Zhang Yuanheng glanced at Qi Minghe’s horse, then bowed and said: “I came in a carriage. I’ll use my own.”

Minghe nodded without further comment, mounted his horse, and rode off.

Zhang Yuanheng watched his departing figure with the distinct impression that Minghe had been waiting for him at the Marquis’s estate gate. Did that mean Song Zhang knew he was here?

But Zhang Yuanheng did not dwell on it long. He boarded his carriage and set off for Song Zhang’s residence.

This was his first visit to Song Zhang’s private home in Wuyi Lane, a street where the capital’s most prominent and powerful made their residences.

He looked upon the imposing, grand gate before him, and thought of how Song Zhang had racked up one military achievement after another since first entering the barracks, rising steadily through the ranks, and how upon returning to the capital, he had become the talk of the city. Imperial gifts to him had been extravagant and unsparing. Such fortune and privilege were hardly surprising.

Disciplined guards stood at the gate and, seeing Zhang Yuanheng arrive, opened it without a word and let him through.

Song Zhang’s estate was vast, and nothing like the conventional square-grid layout of ordinary houses — instead it resembled a garden in the southern style, with water reflecting the moon through stone archways, emphasizing scenic mood and artistic conception. Every tree, rock, and plant had been transported from regions across the country, evidence of the scale of the project and the depth of imperial favor.

It was hard to imagine that a military man like Song Zhang would have such refined sensibilities.

A guard escorted Zhang Yuanheng to an inner courtyard. At the gateway, guards stood watch once more. Inside, a garden with a rockery pond opened up before him — one crossed a stone bridge to reach a multi-storied building of lavish construction, its floors paved with white jade tiles, its interior beyond imagining.

Walking inside, guards stood watch at every turn, all the way to the threshold. Only once he had crossed inside did the great doors close behind him, leaving the inner space free of guards — only women servants waiting quietly at the sides.

A maidservant spotted him enter and came at once with a smile to guide Zhang Yuanheng toward the interior.

Passing through several layers of curtains, he finally saw Song Zhang at the far end of the room — in a black everyday robe, seated beside a low zitan table, a crane-embroidered cloak draped over his shoulders, his chest casually open at the collar, revealing the warmly tanned skin beneath.

Though his posture was one of casual ease, his hair was bound in a gold coronet, his gaze cool and detached, his eyes sharp as blades.

Beside him, two exquisite women knelt, their clothing scandalously revealing, generous curves on full display, twisting and swaying as they fed Song Zhang wine.

Zhang Yuanheng took one glance and dared not look at the indecently dressed women again, immediately bowing his head in greeting to Song Zhang: “General Song.”

Song Zhang glanced at Zhang Yuanheng, pushed aside the wine cup being offered to him, and turned those sharp eyes on him. He smiled: “Master Zhang. Please sit — across from me.”

Zhang Yuanheng acknowledged the invitation, and without standing on ceremony, spread his robe aside and sat down across from Song Zhang.

But he had barely settled when Song Zhang clapped his hands, and two more stunning women emerged from behind and settled beside Zhang Yuanheng.

These two were not so immodestly dressed, but their eyes were laden with seduction, and their boneless, fluid hands reached toward Zhang Yuanheng’s hands: “Master Zhang, are you cold? It would be most comfortable to lean against me.”

Zhang Yuanheng stiffened and firmly pushed the women’s hands aside, then looked at Song Zhang: “General Song, you invited me here — for what purpose?”

Song Zhang looked at Zhang Yuanheng’s resolutely averted expression and raised an eyebrow: “These two women were tributes of rare beauty sent from the Eastern Commandery. What would Master Zhang say to my giving them to him as serving maids?”

Zhang Yuanheng immediately rose and clasped his hands in a bow before Song Zhang: “I could not possibly accept such a gift, General. I would not dare.”

Song Zhang looked at Zhang Yuanheng’s upright manner and curved his lips slightly: “What is there to be afraid of, Master Zhang? I’m only giving you two maidservants. Once they’re given to you, how you dispose of them is entirely up to you.”

Zhang Yuanheng remained bowed, his voice low: “I have done nothing to merit a reward, General. That you would suddenly give me two maidservants fills me with unease.”

Song Zhang frowned slightly, growing a little impatient. These scholars, their heads full of schemes — he had probably spent the entire time imagining every possible conspiracy.

He set his cup down on the table with a thud. The heavy sound rang through the room, and Zhang Yuanheng’s heart jumped as he looked at Song Zhang.

He genuinely could not afford not to wonder. He didn’t know Song Zhang well, but he knew this man was far from simple in private, and for him to give away serving maids for no reason — was this the emperor’s idea? Were these women meant to watch his conduct?

He watched as Song Zhang’s expression cooled, and those changeable dark eyes settled on him. “Master Zhang need not imagine things. I am giving Master Zhang two serving maids for two reasons. First: I admire Master Zhang and wish to build a genuine friendship with him — specifically to give him two companions close to his heart.”

“Second: I intend to introduce a match for Master Zhang. Would Master Zhang care to hear me out?”

Zhang Yuanheng blinked in surprise and quickly spoke: “I am grateful for the General’s high regard. But there is already someone I care for in my heart, so I ask that you —”

Before Zhang Yuanheng could finish, Song Zhang cut him off with cool disinterest: “Perhaps Master Zhang would sit down and hear me out first.”

Zhang Yuanheng looked at the slight irritation in Song Zhang’s expression, hesitated, and still held his ground: “General Song, I intend to go and propose within these two days. Please do not put me in a difficult position.”

Song Zhang sat listening to Zhang Yuanheng’s words as his expression gradually darkened entirely.

chapters.title: What Brings Young Lord Song Here at Night?
chapters.content:
The women seated beside Zhang Yuanheng were not without beauty — though in Song Zhang’s eyes, who had seen countless beauties, they were nothing more than ordinary. But they were more than good enough to send to Zhang Yuanheng.

He watched Zhang Yuanheng’s upright face as the man carefully averted his gaze, not daring to even glance at the beauties beside him, and found it tiresome.

In Song Zhang’s view, beautiful women were mere playthings for passing the time. A man who didn’t even dare look at women — no wonder he made such a pathetic display of himself before Shen Weici.

Moreover, these two women had been carefully chosen by Song Zhang to resemble Shen Weici’s own soft and alluring manner — not as beautiful, but far beyond what ordinary men would encounter.

He had simply not anticipated that Zhang Yuanheng would be so infatuated — insisting on none but Shen Weici.

He suddenly had no more interest in speaking with Zhang Yuanheng and rose from his seat. His cold, indifferent gaze fell on him: “Whatever I have sent out has never been taken back. If Master Zhang will not accept the gesture, then it would seem he has no wish to befriend me.”

“The women are here. Whether you take them or not is entirely Master Zhang’s choice.”

Song Zhang swept his robe aside and walked out, leaving Zhang Yuanheng standing alone in the grand, empty room, staring blankly at the wine cup before him.

The two women’s pliant bodies leaned against him from either side, their fragrance enveloping him, soft fingers slipping into his sleeve.

“Master Zhang...”

He jolted back to his senses, stepped back quickly, and looked at the two women pressing close again — dark-lashed eyes, red lips, dark hair and lovely features, beauties rarely seen.

At this moment Minghe suddenly appeared at his side. He glanced at the two beauties, then looked at Zhang Yuanheng: “Why does Master Zhang hesitate? My general made a special effort to invite Master Zhang for a small gathering and even offered to arrange a match for him — only to end in this awkward situation.”

“It’s only a matter of accepting two beautiful women. Taking them home and doing with them as you please is entirely your affair. Why make an enemy of the general over this?”

Minghe’s words reminded Zhang Yuanheng that there was indeed no need for him to antagonize Song Zhang. If he truly offended him, given Song Zhang’s ruthless methods, he himself would likely suffer for it.

Something shifted in his expression. He clasped his hands toward Minghe: “Thank you for the reminder.”

He then looked at the two women who were watching him hopefully, let out a sigh, and told them to follow him.

Minghe smiled and had someone see them out.

Once Zhang Yuanheng was seen off, Minghe returned to Rongye Hall where Song Zhang conducted his daily business and found Song Zhang alone at his desk, reading correspondence. He approached and said quietly: “Master Zhang has taken the women with him.”

Song Zhang gave a snort of contempt. His fingertip paused, and he cast Minghe a sideways glance: “Have someone keep an eye on the Earl’s estate. I want to know whether Zhang Yuanheng has touched those women.”

“His so-called”heart already belonging to another” — let’s see if that’s a joke.”

Minghe smiled: “The general can rest easy — someone has been watching already.”

Song Zhang gave a neutral sound of acknowledgment.

Minghe looked at Song Zhang and continued: “A fair number of invitations have come in lately for the general. Are you truly not going to any of them?”

Song Zhang’s expression was distant: “What would I go for? Let those civil officials squabble among themselves. Don’t forget I am the emperor’s man. No matter which gathering I attend, those officials will spin ten possible interpretations of what it means, and only cause me more trouble.”

Minghe looked at Song Zhang with some difficulty: “These days, your second great-uncle’s household has been keeping rather close company with the Fourth Prince, Prince Qin. Might others assume this reflects your intentions as well?”

Song Zhang lowered his gaze: “Let them assume whatever they like. It’s not my doing — let them guess.”

Minghe was somewhat puzzled by Song Zhang’s meaning, but seeing Song Zhang return to his letters, he said nothing more.

After a while, Song Zhang set down the letter he had been reading. His thoughts went to Zhang Yuanheng’s words about proposing within two days.

He gave a cold laugh, rose from the desk, and headed out: “I’m going to the Duke’s estate.”

The following evening, Shen Weici had washed and changed as usual, and sat at her low table doing embroidery. She planned to make Zhang Yuanheng a pouch — she would give it to him on the day their betrothal was settled.

She had already stitched the outline of a design on the stretched fabric, and was intending to embroider a pair of mandarin ducks.

The hour was still not late, and with a charcoal fire burning beside her, Shen Weici had removed her pins and ornaments and let her hair fall loose after bathing, planning to embroider for a while before going to sleep.

The room was quiet. She had left one maidservant to keep watch outside the screen for the night, and Yue Deng sat beside her as company. Shen Weici’s needle and thread moved with practiced ease — impressive enough that even Yue Deng, sitting nearby, admired it and tried to follow her technique with her own piece of stretched fabric.

At this moment, a maidservant’s voice suddenly rose from outside: “Miss, the Second Young Master is here.”

The voice carried just a trace of alarm. Shen Weici started at the sound, and had just set down the embroidery in her hands and was about to rise and go out when she saw a figure approaching through the screen.

She stilled, then looked at Song Zhang, who stood just beyond the screen, and asked: “Is it not somewhat improper for Young Lord Song to come at night like this?”

Song Zhang strolled out from behind the screen with his hands clasped behind his back, and regarded Shen Weici in the lamplight.

She was dressed in gentle, understated elegance, her long skirts spreading to the floor, her hair — even longer — trailing to the ground. A smoky-blue robe, skin like snow, lips like red petals — she had the face of a water goddess.

His gaze swept over the stretched embroidery in her hands. Song Zhang said flatly: “Shen Third Miss is nominally your elder cousin-by-adoption. What is improper about it?”

The moment Shen Weici saw Song Zhang, she felt a knot of tension. She had no idea what trouble he had come to bring her now.

She cut to the point: “Is there something Young Lord Song needs at this hour?”

Song Zhang glanced at Shen Weici’s guarded expression, then stepped forward and, without ceremony, sat down directly across from her. He turned his cold gaze on Yue Deng, then fixed his black eyes on Shen Weici: “Send your maidservant out.”

Shen Weici’s expression shifted slightly: “Is there something Young Lord Song has to say that cannot be said in front of a maidservant?”

Song Zhang’s face darkened. His impatient eyes fixed on Shen Weici: “Don’t make me say it twice. If you don’t believe me, you can try me.”

It was an outright threat, delivered with such conviction from the look on his face that he clearly meant every word.

Shen Weici knew that Song Zhang’s power and authority were absolute — even the people of the Marquis’s estate answered to him, and when the visitors from Yongan Marquis’s estate came, they too had been deferential to him. Against someone like that, she would be utterly outmatched. There was no point in a direct confrontation.

Her way of surviving in the Marquis’s estate had always been careful caution and keeping her head down.

She set the embroidery down on the table, told Yue Deng to step outside, and once Yue Deng had gone, she looked at Song Zhang: “Will Young Lord Song speak now?”

Song Zhang looked at the embroidery Shen Weici had placed on the low table. He snorted softly and picked it up with his slender fingers, turning it over. When he saw the mandarin duck outline stitched on it, the contempt in his eyes deepened. He raised his gaze to Shen Weici: “For Zhang Yuanheng?”

Thinking of all the cutting things Song Zhang had said before, Shen Weici supposed he was probably concocting some new story in his head about how she was scheming to seduce Zhang Yuanheng with handcraft.

She had no desire to explain. She only said: “Whom I embroider for has nothing to do with Young Lord Song.”

Then she turned it back on him: “Or is it that Young Lord Song is actually that curious about whom I’m making this for?”

Song Zhang’s fingers paused. A coldness shot through his eyes. He tossed the embroidery back onto the table and gave a cold laugh: “You think Zhang Yuanheng is so bewitched by you that he couldn’t easily replace you with another woman? Don’t you believe you could be replaced at any time?”

He went on, contempt in his gaze as he looked at Shen Weici’s loose-flowing hair: “Look at you now, bright-eyed and anticipating — aren’t you simply waiting for Zhang Yuanheng to come and marry you grandly, so you can be the young mistress of the Earl’s estate and leap to a high branch in one bound?”

Shen Weici heard Song Zhang’s mocking words and kept her expression unchanged, then looked at him: “Young Lord Song may think whatever he pleases.”

She had long since stopped wanting to explain herself to this man. He had always held himself above others — how could he ever understand?

Song Zhang looked at the composed stillness of Shen Weici’s expression, and for a moment his gaze was unblinking. Then he spoke slowly: “Last night, Zhang Yuanheng left my estate and took two beautiful serving maids back with him. Third Miss might care to guess — did anything happen between him and those women last night?”

chapters.title: You Displease Me in Every Way
chapters.content:
The candlelight shifted softly between them, threading through the faint sound of wind outside. Song Zhang in black sat across from Shen Weici in the lamplight, watching the slight startlement that crossed her face. He saw a strand of hair fall from her shoulder and settle against her cheek — the slightest trembling of it was quietly alluring.

He studied her every expression with leisurely, unabashed scrutiny. His gaze moved without reservation from her dark brows to her jaw, then settled on her eyes, which the candlelight had turned amber — now steady, now dim, composure forced.

He was a hunter watching his prey expose a weakness, waiting for the moment to lunge and close his teeth around her throat.

Under her sleeve, her fingertips drew tighter. Shen Weici knew Song Zhang was watching her.

Her eyes remained on the tabletop. She shook her head and said in an even voice: “I have no interest in knowing.”

She had, in fact, thought it through: even if Zhang Yuanheng had brought those serving maids back and something had occurred, it didn’t prove much. She had been in this world long enough to know that well-born sons of good families almost always had chamber maids. It was hardly a betrayal.

Besides, Shen Weici had never harbored any expectation that she and Zhang Yuanheng would be without other women for the rest of their lives. Taking concubines was ordinary enough.

Song Zhang looked at that placid expression of hers, and something in him — for reasons he could not quite name — lifted slightly: “Oh? You truly don’t want to know?”

He watched her with that same derision: “I suppose Shen Third Miss can probably work out what happened herself.”

“I only hope those two maids haven’t worn Zhang Yuanheng completely hollow. Third Miss, you might want to remind him to take care of himself.”

Shen Weici finally looked at Song Zhang and said quietly: “If Young Lord Song has come only to say this, I have heard it. Can Young Lord Song leave now?”

Shen Weici’s blunt dismissal was something even this favored son of heaven had never encountered before — least of all from a woman.

Song Zhang’s lips pressed together, and the chill in his eyes could have frozen the air around her: “I decide when I leave. You have no business reminding me.”

“The matter of you using my charcoal is not yet settled.”

“Items bestowed by the emperor — if an outsider moves them, that is an offense warranting prison. Shen Third Miss surely has no wish to spend time in a cell?”

Shen Weici heard Song Zhang bring up that matter, as she had expected he would. She said: “Using your charcoal was an unintentional mistake on my part. Those few pieces of charcoal mean nothing to someone like Young Lord Song. Why must you make things difficult for me?”

Song Zhang said with leisurely indifference: “A few pieces of charcoal mean nothing to me — even if fifty jin were used by someone else, I wouldn’t care.”

“But if it’s you who used them, then it’s different.”

Shen Weici paused and looked at Song Zhang: “Why?”

Song Zhang looked directly into her eyes, voice low: “No reason.”

No reason.

So it was simply because he hated her.

Shen Weici did not understand where Song Zhang’s dislike had come from. She had already been careful enough around him.

He seemed to bear her some wordless, inexplicable ill will.

She stared at the tabletop in a daze for a moment, then asked quietly: “Is it because of what happened with the jade pendant that time — Young Lord Song dislikes me and so targets me like this?”

Song Zhang’s gaze fell on Shen Weici’s vacant eyes, and then moved to her collar — a slender neck of white jade was wrapped snugly there. All he could see was that small strip of jade throat, yet he found it impossibly tempting. He averted his eyes with a frown: “No.”

Shen Weici looked up at Song Zhang: “Then what is it about me that has displeased Young Lord Song?”

Song Zhang looked at those eyes turned toward him — innocent, with a faint shadow of loss — and nearly let himself be fooled by them again.

He thought of the letter she had written to Zhang Yuanheng, thought of the coy, yielding shyness she had shown in Zhang Yuanheng’s presence, and an unnameable fire burned in his chest.

His eyes sharpened again: “You displease me in every way. Is that clear?”

“If you want my forgiveness, for the next half month you will come to my courtyard every evening at the hour of Xu to light the charcoal. Otherwise, if you want to get married, you’ll spend some time in a prison cell first. I’ll be curious to see who would still want to marry you then.”

His cold voice was like a merciless blade, making Shen Weici suddenly understand that this man before her would not spare her a shred of consideration.

She had actually, in some foolish corner of her mind, imagined she could reason with him.

He held himself above all — he had never once seen her as someone worthy of any consideration. Why would he ever sit down and speak with her reasonably?

His arrogant voice came again: “Don’t think of asking anyone to intercede for you. Even if you brought it to Old Madam, she couldn’t save you. What I say is what I intend to carry out.”

“If you don’t believe me, you can try. At that point, no amount of goodwill from anyone will matter.”

Song Zhang rose, looked down at Shen Weici’s pale face: “I’d like to know whether the charcoal fires Shen Third Miss lights with these hands of hers burn any warmer.”

He said this, gave Shen Weici one final glance — those downcast eyes and brows — then turned and left.

But once he stepped out into the courtyard, he stopped in place. He turned back and looked at the silhouette on the window.

That seated figure remained still, unmoving — until the maidservant outside came in, and she shifted faintly.

Song Zhang couldn’t help wondering what expression Shen Weici wore right now. He also thought: if she just softened a little and asked him to let it go, he wasn’t entirely unwilling.

She could smile warmly at any other man. She was willing to take the initiative with others. Why was it that before him she was always another way entirely — never once smiling at him of her own accord?

His own standing and position outstripped Zhang Yuanheng’s by far — and they even lived within the same Marquis’s estate. Shouldn’t she logically be choosing him?

Since she had already shown him that yielding, delicate manner, why hadn’t she continued drawing closer to him?

As this thought surfaced, Song Zhang stopped himself. He was taken aback by his own mind.

His heart gave two beats. He was well aware that his attention to Shen Weici had become excessive. He had developed an interest in her — and beyond that, an impulse to possess her.

More than once at night, when thoughts of her came, a certain restlessness was difficult to suppress.

Song Zhang was not particularly troubled by this recognition. Shen Weici was, for him, far too easy to obtain. As long as he was willing, the Second Branch would probably rush to hand her over themselves.

But that was not what he wanted. It shouldn’t be him reaching out first — that would make it look as though he had fallen for her before she had. She should be the one to take the initiative.

If only she could see where things stood.

His expression shifted through several changes. He no longer looked at the shadow on the window, and turned to leave.

On the other side, the moment Yue Deng saw Song Zhang come out, she rushed back inside. She entered to find her Miss propping her head in her hand and staring at the table, utterly absent. She couldn’t help but call out: “Miss.”

Shen Weici heard Yue Deng’s voice and did not react at first. Song Zhang’s words were still turning over in her mind.

He might truly send her to prison. If that happened, every path forward would be sealed off.

She straightened, pushing herself up from the low table. She looked at Yue Deng and said: “Let’s sleep.”

Yue Deng froze, then hurried to help Shen Weici undress, asking as she did: “What did Second Young Master say just now?”

Shen Weici looked at Yue Deng and said quietly: “He said Zhang Yuanheng took two beautiful maidservants from his estate.”

Yue Deng’s hand stalled. Her eyes went wide as she stared at Shen Weici: “Didn’t Young Master Zhang say he was coming to propose within two days? How could he do such a thing?”

“He spoke so convincingly — was he also a false gentleman all along?”

chapters.title: Going to Song Zhang’s Courtyard
chapters.content:
The garment slipped away. Shen Weici sat on the edge of the bed in a single layer of underrobe, regarding the indignant Yue Deng before her.

She let out a quiet sigh. “Whether it’s true or not, let’s not jump to conclusions. Even if it is true, there’s nothing worth being upset about.”

“I’ve actually thought it over carefully. Someone of Young Master Zhang’s age, having no chamber maids all this time, is already remarkable. Bringing home two beautiful women so suddenly from Song Zhang’s estate does seem rather out of character.”

“And given what I’ve come to understand of Young Master Zhang over these days, it wouldn’t be like him to simply ask Song Zhang for women so abruptly.”

“That said, if it’s false, I haven’t quite worked out what reason Song Zhang would have for deceiving me. I can’t say for certain either way. Don’t be angry about it — give it a day or two more and we’ll see.”

Yue Deng listened to Shen Weici’s measured analysis and calmed down. She settled beside Shen Weici and asked: “Miss waited all today and there was no word of a matchmaker coming from the Earl’s household. Will there be someone tomorrow?”

Shen Weici still shook her head: “Perhaps.”

She looked at the wavering candle flame, thinking only that she did not know how much longer this quiet could hold.

By the next day, Shen Weici had waited until dusk with no matchmaker from the Earl’s estate and no word of one coming. She could not help pacing around the room, sensing somehow that something had gone wrong.

Yue Deng was anxious too. “Didn’t Young Master Zhang say he’d come to propose within two days? Why hasn’t he come?”

Shen Weici stood at the window in silence, letting out a faint breath that turned to mist in the cold air.

A leaf drifted down before her eyes. She watched it for a moment, then asked Yue Deng to close the window.

She sat back down beside the brazier. Shen Weici thought that Zhang Yuanheng surely would not break his word for no reason.

Or perhaps he was simply busy these two days. He might come tomorrow.

But if he came too late...

She made herself settle. Still, she had no heart for embroidery and leaned back in her chair, letting her thoughts drift.

Not long after dinner, Shen Weici asked Yue Deng: “How long until the hour of Xu?”

Yue Deng replied: “Less than half an hour now.”

Shen Weici’s brow fell into a slight knot.

Yue Deng noticed that Shen Weici seemed, for once, just a little restless — something she rarely showed. She couldn’t help asking: “Miss, what are you thinking about?”

Shen Weici shook her head: “Nothing.”

Then she said: “In a while I need to go to Young Lord Song’s courtyard. Come with me — and no matter what you see me do, don’t lose your head. Understand?”

Yue Deng was startled. “Miss, why are you going to Second Young Master’s place?”

Shen Weici looked at Yue Deng: “That matter with the charcoal last time — he’s requiring me to come to his courtyard every evening for half a month to light the charcoal fire. Otherwise he’ll have me sent to prison.”

Shen Weici tilted her head and pressed her fingers to her brow: “Someone like him doesn’t joke. I thought it over all last night, and I’ve decided to go along with him this time. Hopefully he’ll leave me alone afterward. I have a feeling things with Young Master Zhang are hanging by a thread — the last thing I need right now is more trouble on top of that.”

Yue Deng shot to her feet in outrage: “This is pure bullying!”

She looked at Shen Weici: “He just wants someone to light the charcoal — can I go in Miss’s place?”

Shen Weici watched Yue Deng’s impulsive expression and pulled her back down to sit: “Let’s go and see first.”

When the hour arrived, Shen Weici set out with Yue Deng and Hexia.

Hexia led the way, then asked curiously: “Miss, what are you doing going to Second Young Master’s at this hour?”

Shen Weici said only quietly: “Young Lord Song asked me to come for something. But don’t go spreading this around — we don’t want people guessing.”

Hexia nodded: “Don’t worry, Miss — my lips are sealed.”

Shen Weici smiled a little, looking out at the fully dark winter sky. She had heard the maidservants say it would snow before long.

When they arrived at Song Zhang’s courtyard, it was considerably grander and more imposing than Shen Weici’s.

Even at the gate, there were no maidservants — only guards.

Two guards lowered their long spears and blocked her way when they saw Shen Weici approach: “The general is not in.”

Shen Weici paused, then relaxed slightly and nodded, about to turn back, when a maidservant appeared from inside and called out to her: “Are you Third Miss?”

Shen Weici stopped and turned to look at the maidservant, then nodded.

The maidservant smiled, then said to the guard: “Our master has given word — if Third Miss comes, she is to be let straight in.”

Hearing this, the guard stepped aside.

As Shen Weici was about to walk in with Yue Deng and Hexia, the maidservant smiled and held up a hand: “Our master also said only Third Miss may enter.”

Shen Weici didn’t want to delay longer than necessary — she would just light the charcoal and be done with it. She turned to Yue Deng and Hexia: “It’s cold outside. There’s no need for you to wait. Just give me the lantern.”

Yue Deng was reluctant: “What if something happens to Miss on the way back alone?”

Shen Weici met Yue Deng’s worried gaze and leaned in to say quietly: “Winter wind is sharp. If you stand out here waiting for me, who’ll take care of me once you’ve caught cold? I’ll only be going and coming back — less than half an hour. We’re still inside the Marquis’s estate — nothing will happen.”

“Besides, let’s time it tonight first. If it’s quick, you can just walk with me tomorrow.”

Yue Deng was persuaded. She nodded, gave Shen Weici one last worried look, put the lantern in her hand, and walked off with Hexia, carrying the other lantern.

Watching Yue Deng go, Shen Weici followed the maidservant inside. She saw five principal rooms in the main building ahead, the center two being open and spacious, flanked by side rooms, then corner rooms — the layout alone more stately than even Madam Wen’s Second Courtyard.

Inside, the maidservant led Shen Weici through shelves of curios and into what appeared to be a study where Song Zhang ordinarily conducted business.

The main wall was mounted with classic texts; the southwest wall had a multi-tiered display cabinet; the floor was covered in a cashmere carpet, with a large zitan writing desk set on top, surrounded by seven or eight lotus-patterned gauze lanterns that lit the room brilliantly.

Incense smoke curled through the air, the entire hall rich with luxury.

The maidservant gestured at the fine charcoal braziers on the floor and told Shen Weici: “Master says Third Miss is to have these braziers all lit.”

Shen Weici looked down. There were five of them. She wasn’t sure whether Song Zhang truly feared the cold that much, or whether he was simply trying to torment her.

She caught a glimpse of the maidservant’s expression — just a hint of gloating, as if she expected to watch her make a fool of herself. Shen Weici pressed her lips together and crouched down.

She was not one of those sheltered young ladies of fine families who had never done a day of rough work. Lighting a charcoal fire was the simplest thing in the world for her.

In winters past, she had made do with the dregs of charcoal her grandmother had thrown at her like charity, and still survived every cold season.

The maidservant standing beside Shen Weici looked on in surprise at how fluently she worked. She had expected this person — who looked every bit the scholar and spoke in the gentlest voice — to struggle with something like this. But a fire was already going in one brazier, and the whole thing had been done with practiced ease.

chapters.title: Afraid to Answer Me?
chapters.content:
Song Zhang entered with a chill clinging to him.

He walked quickly, his frame long and upright, but he slowed his step when he caught sight of the figure behind the screen. With a gesture of his hand, he dismissed the person following behind.

Colonel Wang, who had been in the middle of reporting something at Song Zhang’s back, swallowed the words back and withdrew obediently outside.

Song Zhang stepped around the screen and walked in to find Shen Weici just rising to her feet. She was slender and willowy, her dark hair gleaming softly under the lamplight.

Shen Weici looked up at the sudden appearance of Song Zhang and was momentarily taken aback.

She collected herself and turned to him: “The charcoal fires have all been lit.”

Song Zhang said nothing. He looked steadily at Shen Weici’s face.

On that smooth cheek there was a small smudge of black — faint in color, but vivid against the extraordinary whiteness of her skin. It had probably gotten there when she was pushing her hair back.

He looked at her again — soft and jade-like where she stood, her gaze still carrying the same composure she had shown when exchanging couplets with Shen Zhaozhao.

His eyes swept down to the charcoal braziers on the floor. They had been lit and were now arranged neatly in the corners of the room. The entire space had grown warm.

Shen Weici noticed Song Zhang was watching her without saying a word. Though she didn’t understand his intention, she had done what she was asked to do, and meant to take her leave.

But as she made to pass by him, her wrist was suddenly caught in his grip. She looked up at Song Zhang in confusion, and found him looking back down at her: “You lit all of them yourself?”

Shen Weici met his eyes calmly: “If Young Lord Song doubts it, feel free to ask the maidservant.”

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici evenly, then raised the hand he was holding up to his eye level. Her small, fair palm had a faint dusting of charcoal grey on it.

The silver-thread charcoal he burned was coated in a white layer — touching it briefly wouldn’t leave much black. Unless one had handled quite a bit of it.

He let her hand go, but couldn’t resist one last barb: “Shen Third Miss handles things like this with such familiarity.”

Shen Weici looked at Song Zhang with an undisturbed expression: “Surely Young Lord Song already knew — I am not a cosseted young mistress who grew up in a Marquis’s household. Doing these things is not difficult.”

Song Zhang paused, and studied Shen Weici for a moment more. The scent of her drifted over again, and those full red lips were right before him — he almost couldn’t hold himself back from leaning toward her.

Song Zhang couldn’t understand why, with Shen Weici alone, he couldn’t suppress that impulse. Perhaps it was because he had never seen anyone who was both so fragile and so seemingly unbreakable. Or perhaps it was because she had, all along, been subtly pulling him toward her without even trying.

He asked suddenly: “You draw Zhang Yuanheng to you — is it because you like him?”

“Or because you want to marry into the Earl’s estate.”

Shen Weici heard Song Zhang ask this strange question again and frowned slightly.

She had never given her heart over entirely, not to anyone — not unless she could be sure that person had given theirs entirely to her as well.

She didn’t know whether she loved Zhang Yuanheng, but she did genuinely want to marry into the Earl’s estate. It was the best choice available to her.

But at this moment, Shen Weici thought it was a strange and unreasonable thing for Song Zhang to ask, and she had no desire to answer him or to explain herself.

She truly had nothing that needed explaining.

Her gaze dropped, and she moved to step past Song Zhang. But her wrist was caught again. His cool voice sounded at her ear: “Afraid to answer me?”

Shen Weici had no choice but to turn her head and look at Song Zhang: “I care for Young Master Zhang and I want to marry into the Earl’s estate. Is that answer satisfactory to Young Lord Song?”

Song Zhang looked down at Shen Weici’s upturned face. His expression darkened. He let out a cold laugh and released her.

“Don’t forget the time tomorrow, Shen Third Miss. I will not show you any leniency.”

Shen Weici’s fingers tightened slightly, and she lowered her gaze: “Young Lord Song need not worry.”

And with that, she walked out from beside Song Zhang.

Song Zhang turned and watched Shen Weici’s retreating figure — graceful steps, growing smaller through the layers of gauze curtains.

Only once she had completely disappeared from sight did his expression darken entirely.

He stood in his black robe by the window, looking out into the courtyard. He watched Shen Weici below, holding a lantern, walking toward the courtyard gate. A breath of wind carried her scent past him. Song Zhang’s fingers, clasped behind his back, gave the faintest movement.

Meanwhile, Shen Weici walked home alone in the night, lantern in hand, the cold biting down hard on the way — worse still in the deep of early winter.

She pulled her cape tightly around herself and hurried along with her head bowed.

Halfway back, she happened to come face to face with Shen Rongsheng, who was walking in her direction.

Shen Weici startled, and quickly called out: “Father.”

Shen Rongsheng was equally surprised to see Shen Weici at this hour, and came closer quickly: “What are you doing here at this hour? Were you looking for your stepmother?”

Shen Weici shook her head: “I left something here this morning and only just remembered to fetch it.”

She turned to ask Shen Rongsheng: “Has Father only just returned from outside?”

Shen Rongsheng shook his head: “I’ve been in the study for a while.”

He looked at Shen Weici and opened his mouth as if to say something, then seemed to think better of it. He only let out a sigh and said: “It’s cold at night. Go on back quickly.”

Shen Weici sensed that her father had something he wanted to tell her but was holding back. Her heart gave a jump. She asked: “Does Father have something to tell me?”

Shen Rongsheng only sighed again: “Nothing. Go and get some rest — other things are not for you to worry about.”

He took his attendants and left.

Shen Weici stood in place watching her father’s departing back, and felt a creeping unease.

She turned and walked on. Her mind stayed busy with her thoughts the whole way back.

But she was so lost in them that when she reached a flight of steps, she misjudged her footing and lost her balance — her body pitched off the path and she tumbled to the ground.

A searing pain shot through her knees and elbows. The lantern in her hand went out as it hit the ground.

Darkness closed in completely.

Shen Weici bit her lip and pressed her hands against the ground, pushing herself up. She groped for the lantern and picked it up.

She tilted her head up to look at the moon. She did not feel sorry for herself or aggrieved — only a quiet, oppressive heaviness in her chest.

A thin wash of moonlight spread across the sky, cold gusts of wind blowing one after another. She looked at the winding, uneven path ahead, then leaned against the rockery for a while, watching the mist of her breath slowly dissolve, and walked the rest of the way back by the pale thread of moonlight.

She had not gone far when a weak glow of lantern light appeared ahead. She squinted at it for a moment and called: “Yue Deng.”

The figure ahead heard her voice and hurried over, lantern swinging. “Miss!”

Yue Deng had not been able to put her mind at ease after going back, and had turned around to meet Shen Weici on the path. She hadn’t expected to run into her out here.

She noticed the mud on Shen Weici’s cape and asked quickly: “Miss — did you fall?”

Shen Weici leaned against Yue Deng, fighting down the pain in her body, and said in a hoarse voice: “Let’s talk when we’re back.”

Yue Deng saw the pale, strained look on Shen Weici’s face and didn’t dare ask more. She steadied her and helped her walk home quickly.

chapters.title: The Marriage to Zhang Tingyi
chapters.content:
Back at Linchun Courtyard, Yue Deng helped Shen Weici out of her cape and discovered that the outer robe was caked with mud. When she rolled up the sleeves, she found a raw red wound across the delicate palm.

The other places still ached, but the heavy winter clothing had cushioned most of it — leaving only faint bruising.

Yue Deng was heartbroken and hurriedly called for the maidservants to bring hot water to clean the wounds.

Shen Weici, for her part, felt nothing much. She watched Yue Deng and Hexia rushing about in front of her, her thoughts already elsewhere.

She looked at the blue-green porcelain vase on the table beyond the curtain, the red plum branches inside releasing a faint and quiet fragrance. She turned her eyes away with a trace of melancholy.

Yue Deng’s voice broke through her thoughts: “The medicine in the bottle is all used up. Should I go find the estate physician now to get another bottle?”

Shen Weici glanced at the small cut on her ankle — made by a branch, nothing serious.

She sent Hexia to sleep, then looked at Yue Deng: “Do you remember when you and I used to climb the mountain to gather herbs for my mother? I’d come home with worse injuries than this.”

She sighed quietly: “This is nothing. And it’s not as though becoming the Third Miss of a Marquis’s household has made me any more delicate.”

“What worries me right now is that the betrothal with Young Master Zhang may not go as smoothly as I hoped.”

Yue Deng was startled. She looked at Shen Weici: “What does Miss mean?”

“Has Young Master Zhang gone back on his word?”

Shen Weici unpinned the silver hairpin at her temple and placed it in Yue Deng’s hand. Her dark hair fell loose. She lay back on the bed with weary eyes, looking up at the canopy: “It’s only a guess of mine.”

“But perhaps things aren’t as bad as I think. Don’t worry yourself either.”

She closed her eyes: “Yue Deng, you should sleep too.”

Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici’s slight, solitary back, heard the exhaustion in her voice, silently tucked the quilt corner in more snugly, and finally let down the bed curtain.

The following morning, after Shen Weici went to pay her respects to Madam Wen and was about to leave, Madam Wen unexpectedly held her back: “The estate is having two sets of winter clothing made for all the young ladies in each courtyard. Stay with me for a while. Later, you and Zhaohao can choose your fabric patterns together.”

Shen Weici made no objection and stayed, sitting beside Madam Wen, remaining in the Second Courtyard to have breakfast with both Shen Zhaozhao and Madam Wen.

Shen Zhaozhao had reined in her hostility toward Shen Weici considerably of late. Though still cool and distant, she no longer actively sought trouble — even when the two of them sat together, she did not take a jab at her.

After a short while, several matrons brought in bolts of fabric for Shen Weici and Shen Zhaozhao to choose from. Shen Weici didn’t make a move, intending to let Shen Zhaozhao choose first, but Madam Wen spoke up: “Zhaohao, you’re the elder sister — let your younger sister go first.”

Shen Zhaozhao glanced at her mother, then said with clear reluctance to Shen Weici: “Hurry up and choose.”

Shen Weici noted Shen Zhaozhao’s expression — she was forcing herself to comply and barely keeping her feelings in check. Shen Weici let her gaze rest there for just a moment and turned back. She looked at the fabrics before her and casually pointed to a bolt of unremarkable pink with purple magpies and another of white with sparrow patterns.

Madam Wen smiled and had a matron take the two bolts away to have winter garments made for Shen Weici.

She then asked warmly after Shen Weici’s illness: “I told you to rest a few more days before coming to pay respects, and you only rested one day. Have you recovered these past two?”

Shen Weici raised her handkerchief to her lips and gave a small, staged cough, then said quietly: “Second Madam need not worry — I’m much better.”

Madam Wen heard her say “Second Madam” and smiled: “Why so formal? Your mother is gone. From now on, just call me Mother, the same as Zhaohao does.”

Shen Weici hesitated shyly, then obediently called out: “Mother.”

Madam Wen was pleased by the address. She added: “There’s no need to be distant with me from now on, either. You’ve called me Mother — I’ll look out for your good as well.”

“As long as you listen to me from now on, I’ll certainly find you a good match. Whatever comfortable life you could want will be within your reach.”

Shen Weici’s heart sank at those words.

But she could not bring up the matter with Zhang Yuanheng yet.

Zhang Yuanheng had not come in two days, and had not even sent a letter. Shen Weici didn’t know whether something had gone wrong on his end. If she said it now and Zhang Yuanheng still failed to come for the proposal, Madam Wen would have cause to say she had been meeting with a man in private without sanction.

She could only raise it when her father was present. Shen Weici decided to wait one more day.

Then she heard Madam Wen’s voice continue: “Tomorrow the estate is expecting a distinguished guest. Wake up early and dress yourself nicely, and come meet the guest with the rest of us.”

Shen Weici looked at Madam Wen, puzzled: “What distinguished guest is coming tomorrow?”

Madam Wen gave her a look: “Someone you’ve already met. The Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review, Master Zhang.”

Shen Weici asked quietly: “If Master Zhang is coming to the Marquis’s estate, surely it must be on important business. Would it be appropriate for me to be there?”

Madam Wen smiled: “What’s inappropriate about it?”

She looked at Shen Weici with meaningful eyes: “You’ve already met him. His younger sister is now the Imperial Consort, dearly favored by the emperor. At a single birthday banquet, how many dignitaries rushed to pay their respects?”

“To be seen by him again would be a blessing for you.”

Shen Weici said nothing more. She rose, curtsied to Madam Wen, and said: “The estate physician told me to take two more doses of medicine this morning and I still have one dose to take. I worry I might bring some sickness into the gathering tomorrow. I’ll excuse myself now.”

Madam Wen heard her out and didn’t press. She simply nodded: “Go and take care of your health. You’ve looked haggard these two days — rest well.”

Shen Weici lowered her head respectfully and withdrew from the room.

The moment she lifted the curtain and stepped outside, Shen Zhaozhao looked at her mother in displeasure: “Why are you being so nice to her, Mother? Her marriage is yours to arrange. Even if she doesn’t want it, she’d have to go along quietly.”

“And she has no backing of any kind. Even if she used Zhang Tingyi to retaliate someday, the interests of gentry families are bound up together so tightly that she’d never have the means to do anything. If she had the skill to get back at people, she wouldn’t have come looking for refuge at the Marquis’s estate in the first place.”

Madam Wen leaned back in her chair, leisurely sipping her tea. She looked at Shen Zhaozhao and smiled: “Zhang Tingyi is coming tomorrow, and he’s clearly taken with Shen Weici. Wouldn’t it be a shame if she came in and started crying?”

“Besides, it doesn’t hurt to let her feel a little gratitude right now. Being kind to her for a while costs nothing.”

Shen Zhaozhao rested her head against her mother’s shoulder and pouted: “I can’t wait for her to hurry up and marry that old man. Whenever I see her face, I feel ill-omened.”

Madam Wen patted her daughter’s hand: “Why the rush? Zhang Tingyi is coming tomorrow precisely to discuss the marriage arrangement. I’ll settle it on the same day. If Zhang Tingyi is in a hurry, after the three letters and six betrothal rites, she could be married off in half a month — perhaps even before the new year.”

Shen Zhaozhao smiled: “That would be best.”

“Who knows, maybe she’d actually be secretly pleased to marry Zhang Tingyi with her background.”

chapters.title: What Are You Thinking About?
chapters.content:
Back at Linchun Courtyard, Yue Deng fetched more wound medicine from the estate physician and applied it to the cut on Shen Weici’s palm.

As she worked, she looked up at Shen Weici: “Miss, what did the Second Madam’s words mean?”

Shen Weici leaned back in her chair and said nothing, only sipping her hot tea slowly.

That afternoon, Shen Weici sent Yue Deng to the front gate to ask whether her father had come home yet.

Yue Deng hurried out and came hurrying back to report that the Second Master had not yet returned.

Shen Weici looked at the sky, which had already grown heavy with dusk. The courtyard lanterns at the outer gates were lit, and before long, full dark would descend.

She looked at the sheet of paper spread open before her, deliberated for a long while, and finally decided to write to Zhang Yuanheng.

She didn’t want to be always pressing him to come for the proposal, but at the very least she wanted to know why he had said he’d come and then not come — and not even sent a letter. If she had some sense of what was happening on his end, she could figure out how to deal with things herself.

She thought carefully for a long time before at last putting brush to paper.

Yue Deng stood beside her the whole time, attentively grinding ink, the inner room quiet, the window shut, candles burning, shadows wavering — a sparse and lonely silhouette.

After some time, Yue Deng saw Shen Weici set down her brush and asked: “Are we sending it today?”

Shen Weici held the letter paper over the flame to dry it. The white of her fingers caught the amber glow, and one cheek was half-swallowed in the candlelight — her expression quiet, clear, yet steeped in silence.

Her eyes were still in the candlelight — steady, composed — but she said nothing for a long time.

Yue Deng saw that Miss wouldn’t speak. She watched her lower her head and slip the thin sheet of paper into its envelope, then hand it to her: “Give Laifu a little extra and ask him to take this over right away.”

“And tell the gatekeeper at the front gate that if Father comes home, to come let me know at once.”

Yue Deng nodded and hurried off.

Once Yue Deng had gone, Shen Weici looked at the practice characters spread across the desk, but felt no desire to write any more.

Her eyes landed on the half-finished pouch beside the inkstone. She reached out and picked it up, then set it back down on the table.

Shen Weici waited for news of her father’s return all the way until it was time to go to Song Zhang’s courtyard — and still no word came from the front gate.

Yue Deng draped the cape over Shen Weici’s shoulders: “This time I’ll wait outside for Miss.”

Shen Weici thought it wouldn’t take long and nodded. She gave her other cape to Yue Deng.

Yue Deng was startled and protested: “How could I wear Miss’s cape?”

Shen Weici looked quietly at Yue Deng: “I didn’t take you in to be my servant. All these years, having you by my side taking care of me — you’ve been more someone I lean on than anything else. I don’t know how I’d have gotten through everything without you.”

She patted Yue Deng’s hand and turned to lift the curtain and step outside first.

Yue Deng stood where she was for a moment, looking at Shen Weici’s retreating figure. Her eyes grew warm. She pressed her sleeve to her eyes, then wrapped herself up quickly and followed her out.

The weather had grown colder and colder. Shen Weici pulled up the hood attached to her cape, covering most of her face.

From not far away, a voice called out: “Hey, who are you?”

Shen Weici stopped and looked down another path, where she saw Shen Zhaozhao heading this way.

Shen Zhaozhao wore a large purple cape trimmed with silver and grey squirrel fur, a winter hat on her head, a hand warmer tucked in her palms, and four or five maidservants trailing behind her — imperious and well-dressed, with all the wealthy ease of an official daughter.

This was the fork in the path, and Shen Zhaozhao had apparently just come from Madam Wen’s quarters. Running into each other here was chance.

Shen Weici loosened her grip on the cape and raised her face: “Second Elder Sister.”

Shen Zhaozhao saw it was Shen Weici and was briefly surprised, then frowned: “This path leads to Young Lord Song’s Guansong Residence. Why are you walking this way?”

Shen Weici’s expression remained unchanged: “This goes to Guansong Residence? It seems I’ve taken the wrong path.”

“I was going to the Second Courtyard to find Father. Has Second Elder Sister just come from Mother’s quarters? Has Father come home?”

Shen Zhaozhao looked at Shen Weici with a skeptical expression: “Why do you want to find Father at this hour?”

Shen Weici smiled: “Just a small matter.”

Shen Zhaozhao glanced at her dismissively: “Father’s attendants came back to say he has a social engagement tonight and won’t be back until late.”

Shen Weici nodded: “I see, then never mind.”

She turned to Yue Deng: “Didn’t the wind blow your handkerchief away? Go and pick it up — I’ll wait here.”

Yue Deng paused for just a moment before nodding and going to fetch the handkerchief.

Shen Zhaozhao gave Shen Weici one more look, then without any intention of walking back with her, took her maidservants and went on her way without another word.

Once Shen Zhaozhao was out of sight, Yue Deng came back to Shen Weici’s side and said: “Second Master has gone to a social engagement — Miss won’t be able to see him tonight.”

Shen Weici kept her head down and walked on, then said quietly when she heard: “Let’s talk about it when we’re back.”

When she arrived, Yue Deng stood waiting under the covered walkway at the courtyard gate, while Shen Weici went in alone. She had expected that Song Zhang would again be absent as he had been before, but to her surprise, she walked in to find him already there — half-reclining against the chair behind his desk, both feet propped up on the tabletop with complete disregard for propriety.

His appearance suggested he had just bathed — a white underrobe inside, with a large red cloak embroidered with cranes draped loosely over his shoulders, the collar slack and wide open. His hair was pinned up with a jade pin, though some of it had fallen loose and still looked slightly damp.

From the moment she entered, those cool, languid phoenix eyes had not once left her — carrying a faint chill, and something of a careless, flippant ease.

Shen Weici noticed the maidservant standing behind Song Zhang who had been massaging his shoulders. In her impression of him, Song Zhang always had beautiful attendants nearby, always wearing that same cold and aloof expression. He had not left a particularly good impression on her.

She didn’t want to say much, or pay attention to Song Zhang’s watching gaze, and just quietly bent down to light the charcoal.

But her heart was heavy with worries, and even though her hands moved quickly, there were moments when she drifted.

When lighting the last brazier, her finger grazed the scalding copper surface. She let out a small cry and pulled back, and found two large blisters rising on her fingertip.

This hand had not been fully healed since that business with Song Zhang — the scrape now had a burn on top of it. She endured the pain and stood up. She looked at Song Zhang to say she was leaving, but found him already standing right in front of her, without knowing when he had moved.

His tall frame loomed oppressively close, especially with that open chest directly before her. Shen Weici froze for a moment and stepped back. But then her wrist was caught in Song Zhang’s grip, and he lifted it before his eyes to examine it.

Shen Weici stared at him in bewilderment. She tried to pull her wrist free but couldn’t, and could only raise her eyes to ask: “Could Young Lord Song release my hand first?”

Song Zhang tilted his head, looking down at Shen Weici — the faint pallor on her face, and just a flicker of agitation in her expression.

From the moment she had come in today, she’d been distracted. He looked into her eyes: “What are you thinking about?”

chapters.title: I Simply Enjoy Tormenting People
chapters.content:
Song Zhang’s voice was low and quiet, and the warmth of his palm was almost scalding.

Shen Weici knew she had been a little hasty just now, eager to finish and get back to see whether any letter had come from Zhang Yuanheng.

But even if she had moved faster than usual, she hadn’t made any mistakes.

She looked at him in confusion, tilting her face up to meet his eyes: “I wasn’t thinking about anything in particular. My only thought was to light the charcoal as quickly as possible.”

Song Zhang’s tone, which had just been low and even, suddenly turned mocking. A snort: “Letting your mind wander while working for me — no one working under me has ever dared to be so halfhearted.”

This was nitpicking, plain and simple — deliberately finding fault.

She kept her patience and answered him in the same even voice: “I am not under Young Lord Song.”

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici coldly: “Yet right now you are lighting charcoal for me.”

Shen Weici closed her eyes, drew a slow breath, and genuinely couldn’t understand how she had ended up in this unreasonable man’s path.

She was by nature mild and unwilling to argue over matters of right and wrong. But just now, a sliver of real irritation stirred in her.

Since coming to the Marquis’s estate, she had been pushed and stepped on from every direction. She had swallowed her anger and held her tongue, and what she had earned in return was only more and more brazen mistreatment.

It was exactly like her mother’s brother’s family back in Yuyang — every quiet concession she and her mother made had only invited the others to go further, and it had never won them a good ending.

A mild person moved to anger — she raised her eyes to Song Zhang: “There are things I have kept pressed down and preferred not to argue about, but Young Lord Song makes things difficult for me at every turn. At its core, isn’t it simply that you see I am easy to push around?”

“The first time we met, Young Lord Song pointed a sword at me. The second time, you set a dog on me. May I ask — even if I am not well-regarded here in the Marquis’s estate, did I go out of my way to provoke you or anyone else even once?”

“That charcoal was left in my corridor. My maidservants didn’t recognize it for what it was and used it by mistake. I knew it was not right that it was used without asking, so I apologized to Young Lord Song — and yet Young Lord Song showed not the slightest regard for that and chose to humiliate me deliberately.”

“I have endured all of it. I only wanted to live out my days in the Marquis’s estate quietly, without making trouble or causing anyone grief. And yet whatever I do appears to be wrong in Young Lord Song’s eyes. Even though I did light all the charcoal properly, Young Lord Song still found the absurd reason that I was”halfhearted” as an excuse to pick at me.”

“Even a clay figure has three parts of temper. Does Young Lord Song not feel any unease in his conscience, bullying me like this?”

Song Zhang rarely heard Shen Weici string together such a long speech. Before this, whenever he had seen her, she was always quiet and composed — even when Shen Zhaozhao deliberately set her up, she remained gracious and restrained in front of everyone, never rising to the bait.

In the couplet exchange, she neither led the field nor finished last, always placing herself in an unnoticeable position. When she spoke to people, she wore that warm, steady smile and used that gentle, unhurried voice.

In the sleepless hours of the night, Song Zhang often thought to himself that he was surely bewitched — because the moment he closed his eyes, it was Shen Weici’s quietly smiling face. He had never seen anyone so gentle before, and kept wondering: what would a person like this look like when angry?

He had honestly begun to think she had somewhat the nature of a clay figure.

Now, watching that face become just slightly more alive with expression, he noted with interest: no powder, no rouge, natural features smooth as white jade, delicately arched brows with a hint of distant mountains, the only striking things those eyes — half-feigning anger, half-genuinely it, heavy with feeling, like the hazy moon emerging from clouds, at once languorous and bewitching.

Song Zhang, who had seen countless beauties, could not help but acknowledge that Shen Weici’s looks were rare. Even the tribute women from Loulan, a land renowned for producing beautiful women, were nothing more than pretty on the surface when you looked closely. What he saw in her was something unadorned, that quality of beauty that needed nothing added — one glance and you were caught.

For the first time in his life, he found himself drawn to a woman in something like the way his soldiers always went when they encountered a beauty — he’d spotted her and simply wanted to tease her, even if it meant making her angry, even if it meant showing cold indifference right to her face.

An unassailable young lord was always more inclined to let the other person come to him. She needed only to crook a finger and give him one heated, alluring look — a young man still new to these feelings would perhaps have his blood running hot.

But Shen Weici was quiet by nature — even a thunderclap wouldn’t stir her — which left Song Zhang, still finding his footing in these unfamiliar feelings, equally unsure whether what he felt was truly liking.

The only thing clear to him was that he wanted to find ways to see her more often.

Even if those ways amounted to doing nothing but tormenting her.

Song Zhang gave a low laugh, his brow arched as he looked at Shen Weici with deliberate provocation: “I feel not the slightest unease in my conscience. I simply enjoy tormenting people. What of it?”

These words, overheard from his hiding place in the shadows, made even Minghe give a long, slow shake of his head. The general was a man who had walked through a garden of ten thousand flowers without a single petal sticking to him — surely he hadn’t sunk this low. Even if he’d never had the knack for winning a woman’s heart, surely he hadn’t become this hopeless.

He couldn’t bear to keep looking. These past days he had seen it clearly enough: the general plainly had feelings for this person, and was being the most stubborn, thickheaded fool about admitting it to himself. Otherwise, why would he have run over just now the moment he saw her burn her hand?

With the way things were going, the general would never find himself a wife.

Shen Weici had not expected that Song Zhang could say such shameless words with such ease.

But then — she had spent a month in the Marquis’s estate, and though she didn’t know Song Zhang well, she knew he was imperial kin on his mother’s side, a duchess’s son, who had sailed through life unchallenged and rose to his current position untouched by failure. Why would she have imagined he’d have a sudden crisis of conscience?

Shen Weici felt that continuing to speak with Song Zhang was pointless. She could barely help herself at the moment — why waste any more breath on him?

She swallowed her feelings again and looked at Song Zhang: “Then what would Young Lord Song need from me, before he would let go of my hand?”

Song Zhang’s thumb idly moved against that smooth skin — those slender fingers, delicate as spring onion, the more he looked the more his eyes burned. She was close enough that her scent was curling around him, and before he’d quite caught himself, he’d pulled her a step closer, tilting his head as he looked at her with studied amusement: “My clothing has come undone. Put me right, and I’ll let you go for today. What do you say?”

Minghe, in the shadows, wanted to gouge out his own eyes. This was indistinguishable from harassment.

Shen Weici heard Song Zhang’s words and froze. Her fingers curled inside her sleeve. The humiliation of it was enough to make her lose her composure entirely. Anger and mortification flared in her eyes, and her voice came out wavering: “I am not your servant.”

Song Zhang saw the fury in Shen Weici’s expression and frowned. In all his experience, women had fallen over themselves for any chance to be near him. He had never given any of them the opportunity — and here she was, actually angry about it.

And then he saw her eyes slowly reddening. In the candlelight, those glittering eyes glared at him with a shimmer of unshed tears. He paused.

The moment Song Zhang released her, Shen Weici turned and walked out without looking back, leaving Song Zhang standing in place, uncharacteristically caught off guard.

He thought of the blistered fingertip he had seen just moments ago, alongside those small scrapes. Against the whiteness of her skin, they had been impossible to miss.

He watched the retreating back of Shen Weici’s angry departure, and Song Zhang felt a restlessness settle over him. He dropped back into his chair, and a maidservant hurried forward to resume massaging his shoulders, only to be frightened half to death by a single, flat “get out,” and fled.

Minghe stepped out from the shadows and looked at Song Zhang’s grim face, weighing carefully what he was about to say: “Earlier, this subordinate noticed that Third Miss’s fingers were burned. Would it be appropriate for me to send her a bottle of wound medicine?”

Song Zhang’s dark eyes settled on Minghe, cold and flat: “You think I need to court her favor by sending medicine?”

That one sentence shut Minghe’s mouth entirely. He didn’t dare say another word.
