She had been about to bring up all the memorials censuring the Second Lord at court, but thought better of it — the Old Madam might think she was taking too much pleasure in others’ misfortune and make trouble for her. So she let it go.

She watched Lady Wen go with a cold smile: “Give it a few more days, and she will not be holding that head so high.”

With that, in rather good spirits, she went back with her maids to enjoy the plum blossoms.

Meanwhile Lady Wen went to the Old Madam’s quarters with a face full of grievance, wanting to discuss what was to be done.

The Old Madam was chatting and laughing with her maids when Lady Wen came in looking crestfallen. She frowned with displeasure: “Why do you come in looking like that? Do you mean to show me on purpose?”

Lady Wen had not expected the Old Madam to read it that way. She hurried to sit down: “Old Madam is misjudging me. Have you heard the rumors that have been going around these past days?”

The Old Madam’s heavy eyelids lifted toward Lady Wen: “What rumors?”

She frowned at her personal maid Yuehong: “What else are you lot hiding from me?”

Yuehong heard this and dropped immediately to her knees: “Those rumors are false, and we were afraid if Old Madam heard them your health would suffer, so we did not tell you.”

The Old Madam had been confined to her warm room these past two days, drowsy and seldom going out. With her maids keeping things from her, of course she had not heard what was being said outside.

Hearing Yuehong’s words, her expression darkened: “Tell me exactly what is being said outside.”

Yuehong knelt on the floor and looked at the Old Madam, head bowed low, speaking in a halting whisper: “They are saying outside that Old Madam is cruel — that she is driving her own granddaughter to death…”

“And also…”

Yuehong did not dare continue. She trembled on the floor and kowtowed: “These are only wild talk from outside. Old Madam, please do not take them to heart.”

The Old Madam almost fainted from fury at just this one line. She hurled the teacup in her hand to the floor and pointed at Yuehong with trembling fingers: “Continue…”

Yuehong looked at the shattered teacup that had landed beside her. Her voice shook even harder, but she had no choice — she raised her head and continued: “Outside they are also saying that it is because Old Madam indulges cruelty that the Second Lord was willing to do such a thing, selling his daughter for advancement…”

“And that the Jian’an Marquis Manor’s growing decline is also because of Old Madam…”

When Yuehong finished the last sentence she was drenched in sweat, her forehead pressed to the floor, not daring to raise her eyes even a fraction.

The warm inner chamber fell so silent that the drop of a pin could have been heard. The maids standing nearby all went rigid with fear, not a sound among them.

Even Lady Wen did not dare open her mouth.

In truth, the words about the Old Madam were among the milder things being said. The accusations against Lady Wen herself — calling her a tigress, a she-demon — were far more numerous. The Manor was now using ‘tigress’ for her behind closed doors. Lady Wen had already punished several servants over it, but could not stop their mouths.

The Old Madam sat for a stunned moment, then came to herself, nearly unable to draw in a breath. She brought her hand down hard on the table: “Who on earth started spreading this talk?!”

Lady Wen looked at the Old Madam: “I also felt something was strange about how quickly this spread. I specifically sent maids outside to trace where it began — and what they found was that it started with several storytellers.”

“Those storytellers are vicious. They have painted me as a demon mother who drove her stepdaughter to death, and said things equally awful about Old Madam. When my maids asked the storytellers who told them to say all this, they only said: if you don’t want it known, don’t do the deed — and no amount of questioning could get anything more out of them.”

The Old Madam’s expression went cold: “Who would spread these things without cause? It must be that courtyard — Linchun.”

“And here I thought she had been so quiet. She has been working from behind the scenes.”

She looked at Yuehong: “Go and bring all the gate boys from the main gate and every side gate. I want to ask which ones have gone in and out recently.”

chapters.title: The Old Madam’s Fury, and Zhang Yuanheng’s Second Visit
chapters.content:
Within minutes, the warm inner chamber of the West Small Compound was crowded with servants kneeling in a solid mass across the floor.

The Old Madam’s gaze pressed heavily down upon one of them: “You are saying that yesterday afternoon Linchun Courtyard’s Yue Deng went out? How long before she came back?”

The gate boy immediately replied: “She went out in the afternoon, carrying the Second Lord’s token. She was back within about an hour and a half.”

The Old Madam looked at the coachman from that day: “Where did she go?”

The coachman knelt before the Old Madam and gave a truthful account: “Yue Deng went first to a pharmacy to collect medicine, then to the Yiyong Earl’s Manor. Yue Deng said the Third Young Miss was no longer connected to the Earl’s Manor and asked her to return the keepsake. This old servant did indeed see Yue Deng hand back the item she carried to the master of the Earl’s Manor in person. Second Young Master Song happened to also be present at the time.”

Lady Wen heard this and frowned, looking sternly at the coachman: “You are certain every word is true?”

The coachman kowtowed repeatedly: “Second Lady, Old Madam, every word is the truth. I have hidden nothing.”

Lady Wen thought about it — the coachman had no reason to hide anything. And besides, she had heard the full story of Shen Weici and the Second Young Master of the Earl’s Manor from her husband — she knew that Zhang Yuanheng had indeed been intending to come and propose, and that he had even given her a keepsake.

Now that Shen Weici had returned the keepsake, perhaps she had simply accepted her fate and was preparing to marry Zhang Tingyi.

There was not a single fault to find in any of it — on the contrary, the girl had been remarkably obedient.

She turned to the Old Madam with a darkened expression: “Could it be that the gossip was started by maids who went home to visit their families?”

The Old Madam’s face was grim as she instructed the housekeeper standing nearby to bring every maid who had left the compound in the past few days.

The housekeeper complied, and quickly compiled a list of everyone who had gone out over the past three days for the Old Madam to review.

The maids on the list included rough-work girls, Third Branch maids, and First Branch maids — seven or eight in total.

The housekeeper said awkwardly: “The maid from the Second Young Master of the First Branch’s rooms may be a little difficult to summon.”

The Old Madam’s brow furrowed. She looked at the names on the register in her hand, and with a sudden surge of fury threw it to the floor.

“Then bring the rest of the maids to the front courtyard and give each of them thirty strokes of the board. Have the other servants watch. Let that be a warning — if anyone dares gossip outside again, they will face the same.”

The housekeeper hurried to carry this out, taking with him everyone kneeling in the room as he went.

Lady Wen looked at the Old Madam: “Even if we beat and kill a few servants now, the gossip outside has already spread.”

“And I have been thinking — those storytellers gave such a vivid, detailed account. Maids simply whispering to each other would not produce that. A few servants gossiping at most would keep it to whispers. Would they dare take it out in public and broadcast it?”

“I keep feeling that with the way this has blown up, someone must be behind it, fanning the flames.”

The Old Madam gave Lady Wen a cold look: “What use is there in saying all this now?”

“The story is already out. You cannot silence everyone outside. Now you should be thinking about how to stop the talking!”

Lady Wen, jolted by the Old Madam’s shout, looked at her and said: “What if Zhang Tingyi steps in to help?”

The Old Madam’s expression went colder still: “You fool. Do you think the situation needs to get any bigger?”

Lady Wen fell silent and then asked timidly: “Then what should we do now? We have already offended Zhang Tingyi — who else can we turn to for help?”

The wrinkled face of the Old Madam went dark and low as she said: “The only thing now is to get Shen Weici’s illness to clear up as quickly as possible, get the marriage done, and have her stand up at the wedding banquet and say she married Zhang Tingyi of her own free will. That way we neither offend Zhang Tingyi nor have to confront this matter directly, and the whole thing blows over.”

Lady Wen asked hesitantly: “But will Shen Weici be obedient enough to say at the wedding banquet that she married willingly?”

The Old Madam looked at Lady Wen mildly: “Did you not hear just now? She has already returned the Earl’s Manor keepsake. That means she has accepted her fate and is willing to marry Zhang Tingyi.”

“She herself has accepted it — what does it cost her to say one sentence at the banquet?”

“At most you can give her a little more in the way of wedding gifts.”

Lady Wen heard the Old Madam’s words and felt this was the only viable option left. She nodded: “I will go and check on her this afternoon and see how the illness is getting along.”

The Old Madam looked at Lady Wen: “Go and settle her emotions carefully. Speak with more warmth. Tell her about all the advantages of marrying into the Zhang household.”

“A girl from a small place like her — how much of fine living has she seen? Tell her all about the Zhang household’s wealth. She may even end up grateful to you.”

“But do not tell her about the rumors outside. She has not left her courtyard these days and should still not know what is being said. Remind the maids in her room as well not to breathe a word of it to me.”

Lady Wen nodded: “Then we will follow the Old Madam’s plan.”

News of the flogging in the front courtyard spread through the entire Manor within moments, leaving everyone walking on eggshells. The whispered conversations dropped even lower — a few maids behind closed doors in the servants’ room at most.

When Yue Deng went out to pick plum blossoms for tea, she heard the news and ran with Hexia to the front courtyard to have a look.

There were more servants gathered at the front courtyard than ever before. Yue Deng saw the person strapped to the bench being beaten half to death without being able to cry out, the cloth at their hips soaked red. She felt a chill run up her back.

Nearby someone murmured: “Old Madam really is cold — flogging people whether they were guilty or not. At that pace, the woman might not be able to have children after this. No wonder there are all those rumors outside…”

Before the words were out, someone beside her clapped a hand over her mouth: “Are you mad? Saying that at a time like this?”

The first woman hurriedly shut her mouth.

Yue Deng looked a moment longer, the scene all red in her eyes, and quickly pulled Hexia away.

Back in Linchun Courtyard, Yue Deng told Shen Weici about the front courtyard: “Old Madam really is vicious. Miss didn’t see what that maid looked like — all blood. They say she will probably never carry a child after this. It must be because the rumors outside got pretty loud, and Old Madam heard and called in all the servants who had gone out in the past few days to take the beating.”

Shen Weici was sitting at the window sewing her embroidery pouch. She heard Yue Deng’s words and her needle paused. She looked out for a moment and sighed: “After all, others have been implicated because of me.”

“But I had no choice…”

Yue Deng heard Shen Weici say this and hurried to say: “How can Miss be blamed for that?”

“This whole thing was wrong of them in the first place. Miss only told that small medicine boy — who would have thought he was such a talker? In just this short a time, and already this many people know?”

Shen Weici frowned: “I do not know exactly what is being said outside. I cannot go beyond Linchun Courtyard these days. The maids in here had best also stay put — otherwise it will arouse the Second Lady’s suspicion.”

“In ordinary circumstances it should not have traveled this fast.”

Yue Deng, seeing Shen Weici frowning, said: “The faster it spreads outside, the better — it will show the Old Madam and the Second Lady whether they still have the face to force Miss into marrying Zhang Tingyi.”

Then she asked: “I also went out yesterday — how come Old Madam didn’t punish me?”

Shen Weici looked up at Yue Deng: “She didn’t punish you for two reasons. First, you were only out a short while and went to the Earl’s Manor to return the keepsake — which satisfies Old Madam that I am being obedient. Second, you are my closest maid. If Old Madam beat you, how would she get me to go along willingly with marrying Zhang Tingyi?”

“If you had gone somewhere else yesterday, or gone to the Earl’s Manor without telling the coachman, you would probably be in that front courtyard right now.”

Yue Deng nodded in understanding: “No wonder Miss specifically told me to tell the coachman truthfully what we were going to the Earl’s Manor for. Otherwise, knowing Old Madam’s tricks, she would have decided right away that I was the one who spread the gossip outside.”

Shen Weici squeezed Yue Deng’s hand and said quietly: “From now on, wherever you are, do not use words like ‘old witch.’ The people around us in this Manor are not necessarily trustworthy — we arrived here as strangers and don’t know who might turn on us. You also have to be careful and not tell everyone everything.”

Yue Deng bowed her head and said softly: “I just dislike Old Madam’s way of looking so compassionate and yet showing not a shred of kindness to the servants.”

Shen Weici lowered her head and embroidered one more stitch in the pattern on her work, then paused and put another embroidery hoop from the table into Yue Deng’s hands: “That is not something for you to think about. Come and embroider with me.”

Yue Deng took the hoop and had no choice but to sit obediently beside Shen Weici and keep her mouth shut.

Hexia came in carrying tea made with plum blossoms, and a faint fragrance drifted in with her. A sliver of winter sunlight through the window fell on Shen Weici. She looked down and took a sip of the warm tea, then narrowed her eyes and looked out the window.

That afternoon, Shen Rongsheng arrived home to find Zhang Yuanheng waiting at the main gate — evidently there for him.

Shen Rongsheng felt he had lost face before Zhang Yuanheng too, having been the one who orchestrated the match between them in the first place. Now for this to have happened was mortifying.

He did not dare meet Zhang Yuanheng’s eyes. Averting his gaze as though he had not seen him, he tried to walk straight through the gate. But Zhang Yuanheng came after him calling: “Lord Shen.”

He called twice. Pretending any longer would have been too obvious. Shen Rongsheng had no choice but to turn around.

He was bracing himself for an awkward exchange when Zhang Yuanheng unexpectedly folded his hands and bowed deeply, then offered his apology: “I should have come to propose marriage earlier. But my household encountered some difficulties, and I was delayed. I come today specifically to offer my apologies.”

Zhang Yuanheng looked at Shen Rongsheng: “If my failure to come to propose is why Lord Shen has arranged for Third Young Miss Shen to marry Lord Zhang, I ask Lord Shen to give me one more chance. I will persuade my family, and will come to propose very shortly.”

In truth Zhang Yuanheng had already come the previous day, only to be turned away by Shen Rongsheng. Today he had come earlier and waited at the main gate.

When he had returned home that time, he had been planning to have his mother and a matchmaker come to propose the very next day — but to his complete surprise, that next day a representative of the third branch of the Song Ducal Manor arrived saying they were interested in joining the two families by marriage. His father and mother immediately changed their minds.

He had been in the palace at the time and knew nothing of it. He still thought his mother had already gone to propose. Only when he returned home did he learn she had done no such thing.

His father had urged him to reconsider. Zhang Yuanheng had said, firmly and without hesitation: he would marry no one but Shen Weici.

The third concubine-born daughter of the Song Ducal Manor’s third branch — he had never met her. And even if the Song Ducal household was the most powerful and prestigious in the capital, with a pedigree of a hundred years of prominence, holders of military power, intimates of the Son of Heaven, and virtually the first among noble families — that was all quite beside the point. He had no interest whatsoever.

But his father had placed every hope for the Earl’s Manor’s rise on him, convinced that marrying a daughter of the Song Ducal household would instantly elevate him, and by extension restore the Earl’s Manor’s standing in the capital.

Zhang Yuanheng had never been the kind of man who needed to climb on another’s power. He wanted to rise on his own ability.

Yet his father and mother held firm. He had missed his moment, was too ashamed to face Shen Weici directly, and had written a letter asking her to wait a little longer — he would definitely come to propose.

But then, within just a few days, came the news that she was to marry Zhang Tingyi.

And the day before, he had seen his father return the keepsake he had sent her. The pain that struck him was immediate. He knew Shen Weici had misunderstood him. He rushed over that very night to seek an audience, only to be turned away by Shen Rongsheng. He had the letter passed to the gate servant, only to have the servant return it to him with the word that his letters could no longer be delivered.

Zhang Yuanheng’s heart had gone completely cold in that instant. He walked home in a daze and did not sleep all night.

Thinking of Shen Weici being pushed to the point of coughing up blood, he hurried back today the moment he left his duties, wanting to see her just once.

Shen Rongsheng stared at Zhang Yuanheng in confusion, bowing and apologizing like that — he had assumed he was coming to reproach him for breaking faith.

He suddenly recalled that Shen Weici had said the Earl’s Manor intended to come and propose the day Zhang Tingyi came. How was it that now he was bowing and saying he had been delayed and could not come?

Was this a roundabout pleasantry?

But given the current situation, he could not agree to Zhang Yuanheng’s request yet.

Zhang Tingyi had run into difficulties for now, but his younger sister Lady Zhang Consort had been in solid imperial favor for years. As long as Lady Zhang whispered in the Emperor’s ear, Zhang Tingyi could weather any storm. And if he now reversed course and refused, would that not earn him the name of kicking a man when he was down? Zhang Tingyi would never forgive him.

Yet all that pointing and whispering had stripped him of his dignity, and he was filled with a deep, bitter regret.

Shen Rongsheng was torn. He glanced at Zhang Yuanheng, who was still bowing, then quickly helped him straighten up and went along with his words: “At Lady Zhang’s birthday banquet, Lord Zhang took a liking to Weici, and you still had not come to propose. So the Zhang household sent a matchmaker.”

He sighed as though helpless: “You know that Zhang Tingyi commands his own power at court, and with the crown prince still unestablished, I could not afford to offend him. That is why I had no choice but to agree. But I also do not want Weici to marry him. Give me a little more time — let me see if there is still room to turn this around.”

Shen Rongsheng was already taking precautions on both fronts: stabilize Zhang Yuanheng for now, and redirect the blame onto Zhang Tingyi — leaving himself in the position of the helpless man caught in the middle.

Zhang Yuanheng heard Shen Rongsheng’s explanation and understood its meaning. Though pained, he raised his head and looked at Shen Rongsheng: “I understand Lord Shen’s difficulty. I will wait.”

He added: “I heard Third Young Miss Shen has been seriously ill. Could I go in and see her?”

Shen Rongsheng would certainly not let Zhang Yuanheng in to see Shen Weici at this point. He frowned and sighed: “Weici is seriously ill and cannot receive visitors just now. Please go home first. If the two of us can still find a way to make this match, nothing would be better.”

Zhang Yuanheng heard Shen Rongsheng’s words and understood that much of what had been said was probably meant to put him off. Zhang Tingyi, however powerful, could never simply take a woman in broad daylight. The Yiyong Earl’s Manor and the Jian’an Marquis Manor were both households of standing — Zhang Tingyi would have to show at least some restraint. He had not yet gone so completely lawless.

There was also the possibility that Shen Rongsheng, seeing the Zhang household’s greater prestige and the growing likelihood of the Fourth Prince becoming crown prince, had simply stopped considering him.

But today he absolutely had to see Shen Weici. No matter what, he had to make everything clear to her.

chapters.title: With Young Lord Song Here, Who Dares Make Trouble?
chapters.content:
Yet no matter how Zhang Yuanheng pleaded, Shen Rongsheng would not let him through in the end.

He knew Zhang Yuanheng’s genuine feeling for Shen Weici and humored him with assurances that she was perfectly well, before finally feigning a headache and dismissing him.

Shen Rongsheng watched Zhang Yuanheng’s retreating figure, saw him board his carriage — and let out a long, heavy sigh.

He went back to the Second Branch courtyard with worry written all over his face.

The moment he arrived, Lady Wen stepped forward to meet him: “My lord — have you been to see Lord Zhang yet?”

The sight of Lady Wen now filled Shen Rongsheng with a dull irritation. He shook off her hand and went straight to the inner chamber to change out of his official robes.

Lady Wen, caught off guard by the shove, stumbled back several paces. It was only Shen Zhaozhao, standing behind her, who caught her before she could fall.

Shen Zhaozhao looked at her father’s behavior in confusion: “What is wrong with Father today?”

Lady Wen stared blankly at the swaying curtain, then patted Shen Zhaozhao and pushed through after him.

Inside the inner chamber, one maid was helping Shen Rongsheng out of his official robes while another brought his house clothes.

Lady Wen had just been shoved and still had not recovered from the shock. Since their marriage she had always been the one deferred to, every whim accommodated — to be treated this way, suddenly and without warning, was not something she could accept. Her temper came up at once and, with the maids still present, she pointed at Shen Rongsheng: “If you have suffered outside, do not come home and take it out on me.”

“Shen Rongsheng. You owe me nothing.”

Shen Rongsheng heard these words and was furious in an instant. Heedless of the fact that he was only half into his new clothes, he kicked the maid aside, took two steps to Lady Wen, and brought his hand across her face with full force: “If not for your meddling and going behind my back to force Weici onto Zhang Tingyi, would any of this have happened?!”

“Now the whole court is talking about me, pointing at me, saying I have failed in my duty and sold my daughter for gain. One by one they avoid me as though I were a disease.”

“Two days running with memorials censuring me reaching the Emperor, and now my post is about to be taken from me — are you satisfied?!”

Lady Wen was stunned by the sudden blow. She heard the words he roared and went dazed, covering her face and staring at him in disbelief: “How can it have gotten this serious? You only wanted Shen Weici to marry Zhang Tingyi. Say outside that she chose it herself — what selling daughter for gain?”

Shen Rongsheng had been holding down a full day’s worth of fury. Hearing Lady Wen’s stupid words, he nearly choked with rage: “Do you know how it is being described outside right now?”

“They say Shen Rongsheng is a spineless man, entirely ruled at home by a vicious wife, unable to manage even his own daughter’s life affairs — standing by while the vicious wife wrecked the daughter’s proper match and forced her onto an old man. Practically trying to push the girl to her death.”

“They also say you abused her daily, and then, unmoved by her coughing blood, went straight to her bedside again to pressure her — only waiting to drive someone to an actual death.”

“And they say the Jian’an Marquis Manor grows more decrepit by the day, reduced to relying on a concubine-born daughter to flatter the Zhang household. They say I have shamed the honor of scholars.”

“Now if I say Weici went willingly, do you honestly think anyone will believe it?!”

Lady Wen backed away several paces, frightened by his voice growing louder with each sentence. Shen Zhaozhao, who had just come in behind her, froze at her father’s shouting and went to hold her mother up: “My mother is Shen Weici’s legal stepmother. Mother may marry her to whomever she wishes. What right do people outside have to say a word against Mother?”

“Even if Mother gave her to a beggar, she would not dare say no. How is it that now that she is being given to Zhang Tingyi, people are blaming Mother?”

“Even if the Earl’s Manor intended to come and propose, they came too late — Mother did nothing wrong!”

Shen Rongsheng pointed at Shen Zhaozhao with trembling fingers and turned to Lady Wen: “This is the daughter your upbringing has produced. With a character like this, if she does not change, she will come to grief.”

Lady Wen, now at something of a loss, looked at Shen Rongsheng: “What is the point of saying all this now? You are being censured — think about what to do.”

“This all started because of Zhang Tingyi. Have you gone to speak with Zhang Tingyi about it?”

Shen Rongsheng looked at Lady Wen coldly: “Do you think I have not been to see Zhang Tingyi?”

“When I went to look for him this afternoon, I was told Zhang Tingyi had been kept at the palace. Apparently there was some matter from last night. I tried to ask through the palace attendants when he would come out, but could not find out — I will have to wait until later and go to the Zhang household again.”

Lady Wen hurried to say: “Then what about your brother? Let your brother help again.”

Shen Rongsheng gave a cold snort: “My brother has been dragged into this mess because of me too. Today in court when I was censured, not a single word did my brother say in my defense. Afterward I went to speak with him, and he swept his sleeve and walked away without a backward look. He wants no part of it.”

Lady Wen’s expression shifted: “How can your brother be like this? We are all one household — if one falls, all fall. Being demoted serves no one, including him.”

Shen Rongsheng slumped in the armchair, propping his forehead: “My brother has always cared most about his reputation. He is a man of upright character. When something like this comes out, he feels it has damaged the Manor’s name and refuses to help at the cost of his own reputation.”

Lady Wen, agitated, came to his side: “Should we not ask the Old Madam to persuade your brother? And also have Princess Consort Huimin put in a good word with the Emperor — that might still save your position.”

Shen Rongsheng paused, brow deeply furrowed: “I suppose it is the only way.”

“Though right now Princess Consort Huimin is still at the temple in prayer. I cannot disturb her. The only other hope is to have Song Zhang say something favorable in front of the Emperor.”

He told a maid to hurry up with his clothes, then went to find the Old Madam.

Shen Zhaozhao watched her father leave and said, dissatisfied: “What is the matter with Father today? I have never seen him this angry before.”

“It is only a matter of marrying Shen Weici off to Zhang Tingyi. What is wrong with that, given her origins? If you ask me, she ought to be bowing down and thanking Mother for it.”

Lady Wen cut Shen Zhaozhao off and frowned: “You are not to say those things anymore. Your father’s heart is currently set on that wretched Shen Weici, and the rumors outside cannot be suppressed. Your father is already in a foul mood. If you say this in front of him again, he will only get angrier.”

Shen Zhaozhao pursed her lips and looked at Lady Wen: “I truly cannot understand who started those rumors, or how they spread so badly. I dare not even go out now — the whole city is talking about our Manor. It has almost become common knowledge. They have painted Mother as utterly monstrous. It is truly infuriating!”

Lady Wen also sat down, mildly irritable: “I also never imagined it would spread this far. But those rumors themselves cannot actually harm me in any real way — it is only words from common people. What I never expected was for your father’s position to come into danger as well. The most pressing thing now is truly to find a way to stop the spread.”

Shen Zhaozhao suddenly had an idea: “Those rumors started with the storytellers, didn’t they? Why not have Second Brother round up those storytellers and put a stop to it? Have them go back and say everything they said was false, that Shen Weici chose this willingly — wouldn’t that fix it?”

“And then have Shen Weici stand alongside the storytellers and make the clarification — who could still doubt it?”

“And have Second Brother come along too — with him there, who would dare make any trouble?”

chapters.title: Which Matters More — Your Face or the Manor’s Face?
chapters.content:
The moment Shen Zhaozhao’s words landed, the tight frown on Lady Wen’s face smoothed entirely. She looked at Shen Zhaozhao: “That is actually a real plan.”

“Have Shen Weici stand alongside the storytellers and retract everything — the rumors will collapse on their own, and the Manor’s reputation will be restored. Your father’s name will be protected too.”

“We will need Song Zhang’s help for this. Have his men round up those storytellers and compel them to cooperate. They will fall into line quickly enough.”

She instructed the matron at her side: “Go to the front gate and let me know the moment the Second Young Master returns.”

The matron nodded and hurried off.

Lady Wen rose and, with a full retinue, headed for Linchun Courtyard.

Inside Linchun Courtyard, Hexia came rushing in to say the Second Lady and Second Young Miss had arrived. Shen Weici heard this without much surprise, gave a quiet acknowledgment, set down her embroidery hoop, and told Yue Deng to bring tea.

When Lady Wen came in, she found Shen Weici sitting before the charcoal fire, a thin blanket draped over her lap, a cup of warm tea in hand, leaning against the chair with a wan, sickly air.

Lady Wen was deeply displeased by Shen Weici’s constitution — always catching colds, always coughing blood. People who didn’t know better would think she had been pampered like a daughter of the highest household, more delicate even than a princess from the palace.

Shen Zhaozhao behind her looked at Shen Weici’s pallid face with equal disdain. She could not fathom what Zhang Yuanheng had ever seen in her.

When Shen Weici saw Lady Wen come in, she moved to put down her tea and stand. Lady Wen glanced at her: “You are ill — stay seated. There is no need for formalities.”

Lady Wen took the stool a maid brought, accepted her tea, and looked at Shen Weici with a manner of visible concern: “Are you feeling any better these past days?”

Shen Weici let a look of touched feeling cross her face: “I have caused Stepmother to worry. I have taken two doses of medicine and am feeling much improved.”

Lady Wen gave a performed sigh of relief and nodded at Shen Weici: “I had not imagined your constitution was this fragile. It was probably a hard life in Yuyang that left your foundations weak. Stay here in the Manor and take good care of yourself — build up your health.”

Yue Deng, standing behind Shen Weici, found every word of this transparently hollow. She did not believe for an instant that Lady Wen had suddenly grown any goodwill.

Shen Weici heard Lady Wen’s words and looked up softly: “I know Stepmother cares for me. Only — the weather has been getting colder, and Stepmother should also dress more warmly.”

Lady Wen blinked, then smiled: “You are even more considerate than Zhaozhao. No wonder your father always says how sensible you are.”

Shen Weici lowered her eyes and coughed once, then said quietly: “Father taught me to be respectful and attentive to my stepmother. I have always remembered that.”

Lady Wen thought to herself that this Shen Weici was one she had been underestimating. The girl spoke with not a drop out of place. Even Lady Wen herself could not read whether it was genuine or not.

She looked at that fragile face and could not find a single crack of falseness. This whole mess had started entirely because of her, and yet here she sat, as though the whole thing had nothing to do with her.

Lady Wen smiled faintly, leaned back against the chair, drank her tea at leisure, but kept her eyes fixed sharply on Shen Weici’s: “Have you heard the talk that has been going around outside?”

Shen Weici looked up in apparent surprise: “What talk? I have not left the courtyard these past days and truly do not know.”

Lady Wen smiled mildly and looked into Shen Weici’s eyes: “Outside they are saying I am a cruel woman who abuses her stepdaughter. That your father nearly drove you to your death in his eagerness to sell his daughter for advancement.”

“Even the Old Madam has been denounced. Everyone in the Manor is troubled by it.”

She smiled again: “You are the one who knows nothing here. I suppose that does spare you a good deal of worry.”

Shen Weici looked at Lady Wen with a slightly pale face: “How did it come to be said like that outside?”

Lady Wen replied: “Some storytellers in the capital — no one knows where they got their information — have been holding forth in teahouses. The whole capital knows about it now. Your father’s reputation has been destroyed by those storytellers.”

“And there are those who are censuring your father over it. If your father loses his post because of this, your life will not be easier for it either.”

“Furthermore, all of this may have given offense to Zhang Tingyi. When you are married into his household, he might well take it out on you.”

Shen Weici listened to Lady Wen and, seeing her come here now, felt something jump in her chest.

She had not understood how it had reached the storytellers. Though the effect she had wanted had been achieved, the outcome had not quite gone as she intended — Lady Wen still had not given up the idea of marrying her to Zhang Tingyi.

In her original plan, Lady Wen and her father, under the pressure of public opinion, might have abandoned this marriage. She had not anticipated that their fear of offending Zhang Tingyi would prevent them from letting go.

She understood: as long as Zhang Tingyi remained in imperial favor, this matter would not be resolved so easily.

Shen Weici looked down slightly and sipped her tea: “That it has spread like this is something I truly did not foresee. But these are only rumors — the Emperor is perceptive enough to distinguish what is true. He would surely not punish Father on the basis of unfounded hearsay.”

Lady Wen’s expression stiffened slightly. She had not expected Shen Weici to fail to follow her lead.

The response should have been panic and a plea for what to do — to which Lady Wen would say: go out and make a public retraction. Instead this oblique little thrust at her had arrived.

Everyone in the Manor knew whether the matter was true or false, and the rumors differed little from reality. If it were genuinely false, Lady Wen would not be this helpless. But because it was true, there was no rebuttal to be made.

Lady Wen’s face flickered. She was about to speak when Shen Zhaozhao stepped forward, impatient: “What use is any of that? What is urgent now is to go out and make a clarification.”

She glared at Shen Weici: “I want you to go out tomorrow and make a clarification alongside the storytellers. Once you have cleared it up publicly at the teahouse, people will stop spreading it.”

Shen Weici now fully understood why they had come.

She said with apparent alarm: “But as a woman who has not yet married, to go and show my face in a teahouse like that — what will people think of me afterward?”

Shen Zhaozhao gave a cold snort, her eyes arctic: “What matters more — your face or the Manor’s face?”

“You are going to marry Zhang Tingyi regardless — why worry about what people think?”

“This situation arose because of you — of course you should be the one to explain it. Or would you prefer everyone in this Manor to be denounced by people outside on your behalf?”

“Even Grandmother has been slandered. Can you truly feel at ease staying in Linchun Courtyard, without even a shred of filial feeling?”

“Besides, Young Lord Song will go with you. What are you afraid of?”

The room fell silent in the wake of Shen Zhaozhao’s words.

Lady Wen sipped her tea calmly, but her eyes were sharp and fixed on Shen Weici’s face. She wanted to see how she would refuse.

chapters.title: Adding More Fuel to the Fire
chapters.content:
The room was silent. The maids all looked at Shen Weici where she sat with her eyes quietly downcast.

Yue Deng was almost trembling with the urge to leap to her feet. They had done this unreasonable thing and now had the audacity to accuse the young mistress of having no conscience.

Yue Deng looked down in worried agitation at Shen Weici, fingers clenched tight.

After Shen Zhaozhao finished her volley of pressing words, Shen Weici let out a quiet breath, passed the teacup to Yue Deng beside her, then pressed her handkerchief to her lips and coughed a few times.

Her voice was very soft. She spoke: “Second Sister need not put it that way. My face is of course less important than the Manor’s.”

“Only — going out in public looking this ill would only confirm that I am gravely sick.”

“And as for the storytellers — words once spoken are difficult to take back. If I go to the teahouse and say I am marrying Zhang Tingyi of my own free will, Second Sister — how many people do you think will believe it?”

Shen Zhaozhao gave a cold snort and stepped forward: “Whether they believe it or not is beside the point. You yourself have gone to say it. Even if they don’t believe it, they will stop spreading it.”

“And anyone who still dares say otherwise, Second Brother will have them hauled off to prison.”

Shen Weici looked at Lady Wen: “Is Stepmother of the same mind?”

Lady Wen looked at Shen Weici and sighed: “Right now this is the only approach. I am afraid we must trouble you somewhat.”

Shen Weici nodded: “Since Stepmother is asking me to go, I naturally would not dare refuse. I will do as Stepmother says.”

Lady Wen saw how obedient Shen Weici was and smiled, looking at her: “We have no choice in this. You are also now a daughter of the Marquis Manor — its reputation is part yours too. If you go out and give an explanation, when you come back I will not treat you badly.”

“The Old Madam will not treat you badly either.”

Shen Weici smiled back: “I know all that.”

She then coughed more severely — a long spell of it — and the pallor of her face flushed with a brief pink. Her jade skin beneath the rose glow of that color was startling enough to make even Lady Wen, watching, feel a small shock.

Shen Zhaozhao looked at Shen Weici being this beautiful even while this ill, and clenched her hand inwardly with dark envy. If Zhang Tingyi had not set his sights on her, she would have loved to ruin that face.

Lady Wen frowned at Shen Weici: “Why are you coughing so severely?”

Shen Weici smiled faintly: “It is nothing serious — only the cough is a little worse at times.”

Lady Wen gave an uncertain nod and said a few more words of comfort before concluding: “Rest well today. Tomorrow I will have someone bring you out. Get yourself ready in the morning.”

The moment Lady Wen and Shen Zhaozhao were gone, Yue Deng came at once to Shen Weici: “Miss, are you really going?”

Shen Weici’s face at this moment had none of the wan discomfort it had worn before. She leaned back in her chair and looked at Yue Deng: “The Second Lady has still not given up on forcing me to marry Zhang Tingyi. Going out tomorrow might be another opportunity for me.”

“The talk outside has spread this far, which means the method was right. So we just add more fuel to the fire.”

Yue Deng started at this, then asked urgently: “How do we add fuel?”

Shen Weici gave a quiet sigh and said in a low voice: “I will tell you tonight. Right now — go to Father’s study and see if he is there. If he is, come back and tell me. I will go find him.”

Yue Deng went and was back quickly, reporting that Father had gone to the Old Madam’s and she had come away empty-handed.

Shen Weici heard that her father had gone to the Old Madam, and the last small hope inside her dimmed.

She had meant to go to her father and gently suggest he give up the marriage to Zhang Tingyi — to take the wind out of the rumors. But from the look of things, he had not once thought of giving up.

She frowned slightly and looked down at the needlework in her hands.

She truly did not want to make things this difficult for everyone.

In the imperial palace, Song Zhang sat across from the Emperor over a meal. The table was laid with a dozen dishes, almost all of them things Song Zhang had liked when he lived at the palace.

The Emperor looked at Song Zhang: “You have not stayed to eat with me in quite some time. Sit with me today and have a few more cups.”

Song Zhang smiled and raised the gilded cup before him, draining it in one: “Then this subject first drinks to Your Majesty.”

The Emperor laughed: “You are still as forthright as ever.”

He looked at Song Zhang: “Among the memorials presented to me lately, a good number have been censuring your Second Uncle of the Jian’an household. I have been sitting on the matter. It is not, in itself, a significant affair — only a matter of marrying a daughter off to Zhang Tingyi.”

“This subject does not find it particularly troubling. What is your view?”

Song Zhang looked at the Emperor: “Does Your Majesty wish to know my opinion?”

The Emperor arched an eyebrow: “Why else would I keep you? After all, your mother is in the Jian’an household. I thought I ought to look after them somewhat, on account of that connection.”

Song Zhang rose and bowed: “In truth, if Your Majesty asks this subject, he also thinks the censures have a point.”

The Emperor looked at Song Zhang in surprise: “How so?”

Song Zhang said: “The matter of the Jian’an Manor is now known throughout the court. The Censorate has submitted memorials, and the remonstrating officials raised it in the great hall. If Your Majesty takes no action, the favoritism becomes too obvious and difficult to justify. How then would Your Majesty command the confidence of your officials? If the fashion for flattery and self-advancement grows unchecked, the court will rot from the inside out.”

The Emperor paused, then smiled ruefully at Song Zhang: “Only talking to you do I feel at ease. Only you will speak the truth to me.”

Song Zhang sat back across from the Emperor: “This subject is only thinking of Your Majesty. Giving Second Uncle a measured lesson this time will make the officials feel Your Majesty is even-handed.”

The Emperor nodded: “Since you say so yourself, you cannot later come to me and intercede for your Second Uncle.”

Song Zhang smiled: “I certainly will not.”

The Emperor looked at him once more, set down his chopsticks, and dismissed the attendants, then said to Song Zhang: “As for the business with Zhang Tingyi — turn a blind eye for now. Aside from his excessive appetites, I am otherwise satisfied with him.”

“And he did have one eye put out and an arm broken over this matter by your people, and is still recovering — that is punishment enough.”

Zhang Tingyi’s talent for flattering the Emperor was without equal. He could always leave the Emperor flushed and pleased. He also supplied the Emperor with alchemical tonics, and everyone in the palace knew the Emperor’s trust in Zhang Tingyi knew no bounds.

The Emperor had grown noticeably more muddled these past two years. He went straight to Lady Zhang’s quarters after court, and some memorials were even processed by palace eunuchs on his behalf. The Second Prince had made a suggestion before the throne recently, only to be scolded for it, while the Fourth Prince — born of Lady Zhang — was frequently summoned to keep the Emperor company.

It was no wonder that people at court were gravitating toward the Fourth Prince. Anyone watching could see that the Emperor seemed inclined to establish the Fourth Prince as crown prince.

Song Zhang observed all of this. He had been at the Emperor’s side for many years and understood the imperial mind — the Emperor indulged those he was fond of, and was especially generous with those close to him. While still not quite a foolish ruler, he had grown noticeably more muddle-headed over these past two years.

Song Zhang had long anticipated that Lady Zhang would beg the Emperor for mercy and the matter would be papered over.

He had never expected a single affair to bring Zhang Tingyi down entirely.

chapters.title: Has He Offended You, or Someone You Care About?
chapters.content:
The great hall was very quiet. Sovereign and subject spoke of affairs of state.

Song Zhang looked at the Emperor: “If the woman who died had been a slave or a person of degraded status, a rush mat to wrap her in would be nothing of note. But the woman Zhang Zhengqing tormented to death this time was a freeborn commoner who performed at an entertainment house without having signed any contract of indenture.”

“When the body was carried out, many people witnessed it. My men suppressed the matter, but not before quite a number had already seen. According to the law, Zhang Zhengqing should be stripped of his office and imprisoned, or exiled for three years.”

“Zhang Zhengqing already holds a position in the Court of Judicial Review. That a man who takes human life so lightly would command such a court — who among the people would dare trust in it again?”

“Moreover, he attempted to flee afterward through a back gate, changed his clothes, and had an underling take his place. Had he not changed clothes and run, my men would not have mistakenly injured him — which he deserved.”

“The Censorate is already aware of this. A memorial was submitted today. If Your Majesty is reluctant to punish him, you will chill the hearts of the people and the officials. Would that not do more harm than good?”

Then Song Zhang watched the Emperor’s expression carefully: “Now that the talk throughout the court concerns Your Majesty’s intention to establish the Fourth Prince as crown prince — if Your Majesty also pardons Zhang Tingyi, would that not signal to the court that whatever crime Zhang Tingyi commits, Your Majesty will never fault him? From that point on, only more people will seek to attach themselves to him, and faction-building will grow.”

The words ‘faction-building’ struck the Emperor in the very place that mattered most. As a ruler, nothing was more to be feared than ministers forming factions.

His fingers tapped the table, his brow knitting deep: “That aspect of it I had not considered.”

Song Zhang smiled: “This subject is a military man and does not associate much with the civil officials. His only duty is to stand close by Your Majesty and manage the palace garrison, keeping Your Majesty safe.”

“These words are said entirely with Your Majesty’s interests in mind. As for the schemes of the civil officials at court, this subject has no desire to pry into them — only to analyze what is at stake.”

“The remarks just now were also prompted by the rumors now circulating outside that Your Majesty intends to establish the Fourth Prince as crown prince. If Your Majesty now pardons Zhang Tingyi as well, those rumors will only seem more confirmed.”

The Emperor sighed. In his heart he did want to establish the Fourth Prince as crown prince — the Fourth Prince was his favorite, and though he could not match the Third Prince in battle or the Second Prince in depth of thought, he was the one who brought the Emperor the most peace of mind.

That was why he had been so indulgent toward the Zhang family.

But he did not want factions to form at court, and allowing the Fourth Prince’s power base to grow too large was genuinely not in the court’s interest.

The Emperor considered for a moment, then looked at Song Zhang: “Then how do you think I ought to punish him?”

Song Zhang bent slightly and filled the Emperor’s cup: “How to punish is still Your Majesty’s decision. This subject would not dare offer a conclusion.”

The Emperor looked at his now-filled cup and then at Song Zhang: “Just now you said so much, and now at the critical moment you are deflecting again.”

Song Zhang looked at the Emperor seriously: “This subject believes that having Zhang Tingyi imprisoned for three months, then demoted two grades in rank — would that not serve to balance things? The civil officials will keep guessing at Your Majesty’s intentions and will not be too quick to form parties around him.”

The Emperor frowned: “But Consort Zhang will be displeased…”

Song Zhang looked at the Emperor’s knitted brow and said nothing more, staying silently at the Emperor’s side.

When Song Zhang came out of the great hall, Lady Zhang Consort was waiting anxiously outside. Seeing Song Zhang emerge, she called to him: “Is His Majesty still inside?”

Song Zhang bowed: “His Majesty has had a little too much to drink and is being helped to rest by the attendants.”

Lady Zhang’s expression was uncertain. Her bewitching eyes fell on Song Zhang: “I know it was General Song’s people who dealt with my brother’s matter. Would the General have a moment? I would like to speak with you privately.”

Song Zhang bowed: “This subject still has matters to handle at the Left Palace Guard, and subordinates waiting to make their reports. I am afraid I have no time.”

Lady Zhang had not expected Song Zhang to dare refuse her. Her expression clouded.

But she also understood that the Emperor trusted Song Zhang more than he trusted her own brother. Song Zhang had, after all, grown up under the Emperor’s eye — the Song Ducal household had been at the Emperor’s side when he was crown prince — and besides, Song Zhang’s grandmother on his mother’s side was the Grand Princess. He was closer to the Emperor in every way than her brother ever could be.

Her eyes shifted through several calculations, and then she smiled: “Then go slowly, General.”

Song Zhang bowed respectfully and walked into the night.

Lady Zhang watched Song Zhang’s retreating figure — like jade-stacked stone, a lone pine standing apart, upright as a crane against the wind. If her daughter could marry Song Zhang, then the Emperor establishing the Fourth Prince as crown prince would become a certainty.

She withdrew her gaze beneath the palace lanterns and glided back into the inner chambers.

After leaving, Song Zhang went to the Palace Guard headquarters, where he found the Second Prince, Prince Ming, already waiting for him.

Song Zhang raised an eyebrow as he entered the main hall and looked at Li Rongshan, offering a proper bow: “Your Second Highness.”

Li Rongshan smiled and raised Song Zhang from his bow: “Seeing you has become something of an undertaking these days.”

Song Zhang’s relationship with Li Rongshan at the palace had been the closest of any of the princes — not for any particular calculated reason, only because Li Rongshan’s mother had been a mere palace maid, leaving him constantly bullied within the inner palace. Song Zhang had not been able to stand by and watch, and had helped him several times. One thing led to another and the two became close friends.

During the years Song Zhang had been posted to the frontier, whenever he returned to the capital to report, Li Rongshan was always the first to come and greet him. The bond between them was naturally unlike any other.

Song Zhang, hearing Li Rongshan’s words, smiled and went with him into the inner hall, asking: “What does Your Highness want of me?”

Li Rongshan was direct: “Was the business with Zhang Tingyi your doing?”

Song Zhang looked at Li Rongshan and raised an eyebrow: “I have no such leisure.”

Li Rongshan smiled: “No need to confirm it. I will add fuel from behind — I will make it so Zhang Tingyi cannot recover.”

Then he smiled: “But I did not expect this from you. You have always kept out of court affairs. What made you move against Zhang Tingyi this time?”

“Did he offend you? Or did he offend someone you care about?”

Song Zhang heard this and looked at Li Rongshan: “And you — you are willing to act now? Are you not afraid the Emperor will suspect your people are in the Censorate?”

Li Rongshan sat across from Song Zhang: “As long as Lady Zhang is there, even with your persuasion, Father may not be able to bring himself to make a decision. But if the entire court memorializes together, that is different.”

Song Zhang’s fingers paused on his teacup. He looked up at Li Rongshan: “There are not a few of Zhang Tingyi’s men in the court. There will naturally be those who defend him.”

Li Rongshan smiled: “But there is still you. You push from behind — let the woman whose daughter died make more noise, and getting Zhang Tingyi dismissed is not impossible.”

He looked at Song Zhang: “That ought to be nothing too difficult for you.”

Song Zhang smiled: “I only wanted Zhang Tingyi behind bars for a few months and put through some suffering there — Your Highness wants him stripped of his office entirely.”

Li Rongshan sighed: “As long as Zhang Tingyi remains at court, he will only draw more people toward the Fourth Prince. How can I be at peace?”

Song Zhang heard this and only said to Li Rongshan: “Your Highness need not be anxious. The Third Prince will be returning soon.”

Li Rongshan looked at Song Zhang. Seeing the trace of seriousness behind those easy eyes, he rose and came to stand before Song Zhang, reaching out to rest a hand on Song Zhang’s shoulder, and said in a low voice: “Song Zhang, you know that I have always been the loneliest of men. In all these years only you have understood me.”

“Whatever the outcome — I will make sure you walk away from it whole.”

chapters.title: Going to Ask Song Zhang
chapters.content:
When Song Zhang returned to the Manor that night, the steward at the gate came to meet him: “Second Young Master, the First Lord asks that you stop by the Old Madam’s quarters when you return.”

“The First Lord is also there.”

Song Zhang raised an eyebrow. He rarely made any show of filial duty at the Old Madam’s — he had visited just a handful of times since returning to the capital, and even those had amounted to little more than a few words of greeting. Being summoned there now almost certainly meant someone wanted something done.

Song Zhang felt a mild irritation at the prospect of going, and was on the point of ignoring it — then paused, changed his mind, and headed toward the Old Madam’s quarters.

What could they want at this hour? It had to be something to do with the Second Branch. He was moderately curious to hear what it was.

Two junior servants walked ahead carrying lanterns to light the way. The hour was already late, the path dark and empty. Song Zhang’s steps were unhurried, and he became aware of the wine making itself felt. He breathed out slowly.

The matrons at the courtyard gate saw Song Zhang coming from a distance and went to announce him. By the time he entered the main hall, he looked around — his father and the Second Branch people were all there. He offered an only barely respectable bow of greeting, then took the seat nearest to him with total self-possession.

Shen Shen, catching the smell of wine on Song Zhang, asked: “You have been drinking again?”

Song Zhang smiled: “A few cups with the Emperor.”

Those words made Shen Rongsheng’s expression shift. He looked up at Song Zhang: “Did the Emperor say anything about this business of censuring me?”

Song Zhang lounged back in his chair, accepted the tea a maid brought, and drank a calm sip: “He did not bring it up.”

Shen Rongsheng looked at his brother in a panic: “Brother, what do I do?”

Shen Shen frowned and shot Shen Rongsheng a look: “This is entirely because you failed to manage your own household and let the matter leak out. Now you have dragged the Manor’s reputation through the mud. Chen He has been censuring you for three days straight. Save yourself if you can.”

Shen Rongsheng, having been spoken to sharply by his brother, looked ashamed. Then he turned to Song Zhang: “Song Zhang, all those rumors started with those storytellers. Can you have your Feathered Guard men round them up? The Feathered Guard patrols the streets — you can arrest them on some charge and they will stop their talking.”

Song Zhang crossed his legs and looked at Shen Rongsheng: “If I have people arrested, will that stop the rumor? When it is then said that the Manor is abusing its power to silence people, the rumors will only grow worse. Has Second Uncle not thought of that?”

Shen Rongsheng heard this and hesitated, looking first at the Old Madam and then at his own elder brother.

Shen Shen sighed and spoke to Song Zhang: “Tomorrow your Second Uncle intends to have Weici go to Sanrun Residence — the largest teahouse in the capital — to make a public clarification. Yanli will go along as well. Send some of your men too, to maintain order if things get out of hand.”

“And have those storytellers gathered together in one place to hear what they should be saying going forward. After this, they will not dare open their mouths again.”

Song Zhang heard this and raised an eyebrow. He frowned at Shen Rongsheng: “Would Third Young Miss Shen be willing?”

He gave a cold, unapologetic snort: “From what I hear, those rumors outside do not sound like mere wild talk. If they are not wild talk, what exactly is she going out there to clarify?”

What everyone knew to be true, said outright by Song Zhang — the faces of the Second Branch and the Old Madam all went uncomfortable.

Lady Wen’s expression stiffened and flickered several times. She forced a smile and looked at Song Zhang: “This does concern the Manor’s reputation. The way your Second Uncle and the Old Madam have been described outside is genuinely excessive. Your Second Uncle’s post is at risk as well. Quieting those rumors is the only way to turn things around.”

“We are also doing this for the Manor’s sake.”

Before Lady Wen’s words had finished landing, Song Zhang’s cold gaze swept across. That gaze carried, unmistakably, a trace of disdain and disgust: “If Third Young Miss Shen goes to make a clarification — does that make her responsible for damaging the Manor’s reputation?”

“The woman has been coughing blood and is still in her sickbed. And your plan is to drag her out and put her through all this?”

Shen Shen heard Song Zhang say all of this and was surprised. This kind of small favor was the sort of thing Song Zhang, in any other circumstance, would have sorted out with a few men and not thought twice about. That he was now saying all of this was something else entirely.

In truth, Song Zhang had still shown some degree of respect to Shen Rongsheng and Lady Wen as elders. The words he might otherwise have said would have been considerably harsher.

After speaking, he had no patience to remain. He stood directly: “I have no interest in getting involved in these matters.”

Song Zhang said his piece, and without caring how the hall of people reacted, turned and walked out. Even when the Old Madam called after him, he had not the patience to look back.

He had come tonight only to accompany the Emperor, and had drunk a few more cups than intended to please him. Now to come here and be made to listen to plans for how to bully a young woman — forcing her to go out and show her face in public, to say she had not been wronged when she had — it was something he genuinely could not watch.

With Song Zhang’s departure, everyone exchanged glances. The expressions were all unpleasant.

Lady Wen looked to the Old Madam for help: “Now that Song Zhang will not help either — what do we do?”

The Old Madam’s expression went dark and tight. She murmured: “Then send Weici to Song Zhang’s quarters first and tell him what tomorrow is about. From what I just observed, Song Zhang seemed to be shielding her. Let her go and ask Song Zhang herself — see if there is any room to work with.”

Lady Wen heard this and knew it was the only remaining option. She rose, took her leave of the Old Madam, and hurried with her maids toward Shen Weici’s courtyard.

Shen Weici had only just come out of her bath. She was sitting in a chair, leaning back while Yue Deng dried her hair, working on her embroidery pouch.

Lady Wen came in and stood over her with an air of authority, launching into a long explanation.

Shen Weici listened with her head slightly bowed, the candlelight falling on her eyes and casting the shifting of her feelings there into shadow.

When Lady Wen finished, she asked softly: “If I go to Young Lord Song — and he does not agree?”

Lady Wen looked at Shen Weici: “If you go and he still refuses, that is that. The Manor will send some guards to go with you. Tomorrow Yanli will also be there. You must remember to speak carefully and not cause any further trouble.”

Shen Weici paused, then only nodded.

Lady Wen saw how compliant she was being and was already somewhat satisfied.

She stood and looked at Shen Weici: “In a moment, the matron from my quarters will accompany you. Tidy yourself a little and go now. Early is better. Do you understand?”

Shen Weici did not lift her head to look at Lady Wen’s face, only gave a docile sound of assent.

Lady Wen narrowed her eyes at Shen Weici — always that same soft and gentle manner, always obedient and compliant in front of others, almost never openly defiant. There was truly no way of knowing what was going through her heart.

Compared to Zhang Yuanheng’s open devotion, was she genuinely willing to marry Zhang Tingyi?

The thought came and went in a flash. Lady Wen glanced at Matron Chang at her side: “You go along with Third Young Miss when she visits Song Zhang. Come back and tell me whether he agreed or not.”

Matron Chang quickly nodded: “Madam, rest assured. I will remember.”

Lady Wen had no desire to stay any longer, and gathered her sleeves and left.

The moment Lady Wen was gone, Matron Chang looked at Shen Weici: “Third Young Miss, shall we tidy up and go?”

Yue Deng frowned: “Miss’s hair is not fully dry yet.”

Matron Chang raised an eyebrow at Yue Deng, a trace of displeasure crossing her face. She was not accustomed to having a junior maid push back at her.

Her expression cooled. She looked at Shen Weici and said respectfully but with an underlying condescension: “Third Young Miss, the Second Lady is waiting.”

Shen Weici looked at Yue Deng: “Since Matron Chang is in a hurry, let us go now. No more argument.”

Yue Deng started: “But it is cold outside and very windy. Miss’s hair —”

Before she could finish, Shen Weici had already risen. She turned and placed her hand gently over Yue Deng’s and looked at her with calm eyes: “It is fine. Stepmother is waiting for Matron Chang to bring word back, and I would not want her to feel I was being slow about it. Bring my cloak — better to go sooner and be done with it.”

Shen Weici’s quiet gaze silenced Yue Deng, who turned and went to fetch the cloak.

Matron Chang stood to one side, watching Shen Weici’s silhouette where she stood against the light — slender and graceful, the cascade of dark hair to her waist, her curves perfectly formed. Skin like snow, glowing faintly under the light sage-green of her robes — no wonder Lord Zhang was insisting on having her.

Yue Deng stood behind Shen Weici and gathered her hair, helped her put up the cloak’s hood, then told Hexia to hurry and light a lantern.

Out in the corridor, a slant of moonlight lay across the steps. Shen Weici’s embroidered shoes touched it, and in the soft blur of it her skirt hem caught the light like rippling water.

Matron Chang walked ahead to lead the way. Yue Deng walked at Shen Weici’s side and murmured: “Miss’s constitution is not strong, and there is always that cold ailment. If your head starts to ache later, what then?”

Shen Weici said only quietly: “It will be fine.”

When they reached Guansong Residence, the guards at the door were still blocking the way. Matron Chang smiled and spoke with the guard, who went to have the matter announced. The message came back: “The Second Young Master says only Third Young Miss may come in.”

Matron Chang was taken aback, then pulled Shen Weici aside and whispered: “The fact that the Second Young Master is willing to see you is a good sign. Go in and speak well. Do not let the Second Lady down.”

Shen Weici looked at Matron Chang for a moment. That kind of expectation was rather amusing.

She gave a lowered-eyes, docile nod.

The guards stood aside. Shen Weici followed the maid who had come to guide her inside. The maid led her to an inner chamber and said softly: “The Second Young Master is still bathing. Third Young Miss, please wait a moment.”

Shen Weici knelt on the cushion and glanced around the room. This was not the study where she had come before — it felt more like a private sitting room.

The space was generous, all the hanging blinds let down, the gauze moving faintly in the air. The charcoal fire was generous and warm. The room held low tables and a daybed. By the window there was also a wide wooden lounging bed, with a game of chess in the center — black and white pieces occupying much of the board, a game left unfinished.

Shen Weici glanced at this once and looked away. She knelt on the cushion at the low table. A maid knelt nearby and filled her cup, then quickly withdrew.

Shen Weici drank. The tea was more bitter than usual.

chapters.title: Is This How You Ask a Favor?
chapters.content:
When Song Zhang came in, the first thing he saw was Shen Weici waiting there in perfect silence.

The layered fabric of her robes pooled on the floor. Both hands rested properly on her knees. Her back was straight. The silver pin in her dark hair was especially striking — the loosely wound hair with a few strands already fallen, soft and hanging against her graceful shoulders, swaying into gentle curves as his entrance stirred the air.

Song Zhang walked into the room, his gaze drifting downward and remaining fixed on Shen Weici. He walked past her back, glancing over the nape of her neck. He watched her long lashes give a faint tremble, her skin like white jade with a cast of gold.

As he came around to her side, his gaze fell to the collar of her robe, where a clean white inner collar neatly enclosed every inch of skin. Only the sharp point of her chin revealed a hint of alluring charm.

Above that, half-veiled by her hair, her white earlobe — unadorned, appearing and disappearing.

Though she was covered from head to toe without a sliver of skin exposed, Song Zhang felt she could draw more impure thoughts from him than any other woman.

In the few steps it took to cross the room, Song Zhang had already looked Shen Weici up and down several times.

“Third Young Miss Shen — what brings you to find me?”

Shen Weici knew Song Zhang had come in. Only when he had stopped in front of her did she look up at him.

But that single glance gave Shen Weici a start — she quickly averted her eyes: “Would Young Lord Song please make himself presentable?”

Song Zhang wore only white trousers below, and above, only a black crane-patterned robe draped loose over his shoulders. She had caught a glimpse of water still dripping down his chest as he stood before her, entirely unconcerned.

She had never seen a man’s body before and naturally looked away, while keeping her composure on the surface.

Song Zhang saw Shen Weici turn her face aside, those lovely eyes blinking rapidly as though somewhat flustered.

He raised an eyebrow slightly, looked down at his exposed chest, gave a low, quiet laugh, and drew the robe together as he sat down across from her.

He had not meant any impropriety — he had always been casual in this way. In his quarters, surrounded by men, wearing nothing on top was unremarkable. He had simply forgotten that Shen Weici would not have seen such things.

He sat across from her with relaxed ease and looked at her composed face: “Can you speak now?”

Shen Weici brought her gaze back. She had now noticed that his robe, though gathered, was only casually so — the collarbone still very much visible, right in front of her.

But this time looking over, Shen Weici noticed that a strikingly beautiful woman was kneeling beside Song Zhang, quietly pouring his tea, then kneeling and using a handkerchief to carefully dab the water still on his neck.

Her voice, soft as a warbler’s, murmured: “Why did you come out so quickly, sir? In this cold weather, you really should take care of yourself.”

Shen Weici looked at the woman without meaning to. Her skin like congealed fat, gleaming white, her slender fingers clearly not those of a maidservant.

Song Zhang seemed slightly annoyed by the woman’s attentions: “Go out.”

The woman looked at him as though hurt, then quietly, silently withdrew.

Song Zhang noticed Shen Weici’s gaze follow the woman. He felt a brief impulse to explain, then caught himself with a private laugh. Whether he had ten or twenty women, no one could say a word. Why on earth should he explain himself to Shen Weici?

After the woman had gone, Shen Weici looked back at Song Zhang and lowered her eyes: “Tomorrow I am to go to the teahouse to make a clarification about the rumors outside. Father and Stepmother are asking me to request that Young Lord Song send some men to come along.”

Song Zhang frowned, looking at Shen Weici: “I said I would handle the business with Zhang Tingyi. Why do you still need to go out?”

Shen Weici lowered her eyes: “If I do not go, they will find other ways to make things difficult for me.”

Song Zhang gave a cold laugh: “Spineless.”

Shen Weici pressed her lips together and was quiet a moment before: “If Young Lord Song is unwilling to send men, then I will take my leave.”

Song Zhang heard this and raised an eyebrow. He looked at her with narrowed eyes: “Is this how you ask a favor?”

Shen Weici looked up. Her gaze met Song Zhang’s — those keen, invasive eyes — and she looked aside again.

She had not actually held out much hope that Song Zhang would agree.

On the way here she had already thought it through: how could Lady Wen possibly be the one to send her? It must be that her father had already failed to persuade Song Zhang, and so she had been sent instead.

She also understood her own position: this visit was a performance for Lady Wen. Whether Song Zhang’s men came or not had no real bearing on Shen Weici’s plans.

On the contrary, she had not wanted Song Zhang to help her father.

She said quietly: “It is for Young Lord Song to decide as he sees fit. I will take my leave.”

She braced her hand on the table and began to stand.

A warm, large hand closed around her wrist. Then Song Zhang’s mildly scattered voice came: “Third Young Miss Shen — what is the rush? Have I said I refuse?”

Shen Weici froze and looked up at Song Zhang. His dark eyes were rolling with some unusual feeling she could not make out.

She was about to speak — and then Song Zhang stood abruptly. His hand still held her wrist, and in the moment of her startled uncertainty, he came and sat beside her.

The loosely held robe shifted with his movement and fell fully open, now spread wide right in front of her.

She blinked, unable to understand what Song Zhang intended. She moved her wrist, trying to signal him to let go — but his grip tightened and pulled her forward, and she had to throw out her other hand to catch herself, otherwise she would have fallen into his arms.

By the time she recovered, she was glaring at Song Zhang with genuine irritation: “What does Young Lord Song think he is doing?”

Song Zhang had it in mind to say: I have always only known how to bully people, and I only want to bully you.

But looking at Shen Weici’s eyes lit with that rare flash of indignation — bright and pretty — he released her wrist, and the corner of his lip curved: “Has the pouch been finished?”

Shen Weici blinked: “Not yet.”

Song Zhang’s gaze settled on the faint residual pink still on her cheek. His voice dropped to a low rasp: “Third Young Miss has come all this way. Of course I will agree. Tomorrow I will personally escort Third Young Miss — how would that suit?”

From Shen Weici’s perspective, Song Zhang’s men not coming was already the best outcome. Him coming personally was even more undesirable.

She had no wish to debate this further: “I would not dare impose on Young Lord Song.”

She rose to leave.

Song Zhang felt the unruly thoughts she stirred in him ignite — a prairie fire in a young man’s blood-hot years, the desire for a woman growing only keener.

The shadow from his youth had suppressed it for a time, and returning to the capital had gradually let it come loose again.

Yet Song Zhang felt he had been cursed. The concubines and beautiful women the Emperor sent him stirred nothing in him whatsoever.

chapters.title: In What Way Is He Less Than Zhang Yuanheng?
chapters.content:
Only the two of them were in the room. The swaying candlelight was like the restless stirring rising in his chest.

He watched the jade-green skirt hem sway, the wide sleeve brush across his fingers, trailing a soft, intoxicating scent. His gaze fell on Shen Weici’s slender waist.

The blush-white sash hanging down drew him before he knew it. He reached out and caught Shen Weici’s wrist.

He held it — still slender — and for a moment Song Zhang thought that with a little more pressure he could snap it in his hand.

He squeezed gently. But it was soft, with a slight yielding give. It only looked fragile.

He looked up at Shen Weici’s startled eyes, and said with affected ease: “Third Young Miss Shen — if you do not wish to go tomorrow, you do not have to go. If they make trouble for you afterward, come and find me.”

Shen Weici heard Song Zhang’s words and nearly thought she had misheard.

The expression on Song Zhang’s face now was nothing like his usual cold aloofness, nor his occasional careless irreverence. There was a note of genuine sincerity in it.

This was the first time Shen Weici had ever seen that expression on Song Zhang’s face. She was momentarily still, and then gave a quiet shake of her head: “Young Lord Song’s kindness is appreciated. But I have nothing with which to repay Young Lord Song, and can only disappoint his goodwill.”

She drew her hand from Song Zhang’s, lowered her eyes, and gave a half-bow: “If Young Lord Song is unwilling to send men tomorrow, then I will take my leave now and go back to give my stepmother an answer.”

It was not that Shen Weici was opposed to accepting Song Zhang’s goodwill. First, she simply did not yet dare trust that Song Zhang would so suddenly be this kind to her. Second, even if Song Zhang were willing to help, she was still a member of the Second Branch — Lady Wen would always have ways to get at her afterward. Song Zhang certainly could not be in the Manor at all times. She could not afford to brazenly offend Lady Wen in the open.

Besides, she had always understood that no one is ever genuinely kind to another person without cause — even the nearest relatives harbor private motives. She would not trust anyone.

The warmth on Song Zhang’s face gradually cooled. That briefly heated heart, beneath Shen Weici’s composed and quiet manner, began to die down.

She could accept Zhang Yuanheng’s goodwill, could be bashfully charming in front of Zhang Yuanheng. In front of him, it had never happened.

Even when he reached out to her, she still would not respond.

Song Zhang truly did not know how to read Shen Weici. If she wanted to climb higher, to marry into the Earl’s Manor — he was incomparably better than Zhang Yuanheng in family background, position, official rank. In what way was he less than Zhang Yuanheng?

Or was it that she had genuinely fallen for Zhang Yuanheng?

Song Zhang’s eyes gradually, dangerously narrowed. He gave a cold laugh. He had with some difficulty set aside his pride and taken the first step — and she had trampled it underfoot. He had never in his life thought about trying to please a woman, and now he felt rather ridiculous before Shen Weici.

Song Zhang stood with a darkening face. His tall shadow fell across Shen Weici entirely. He looked down at those eyes of hers, still perfectly calm. The faint flush of pink from just moments ago was gone — like that faintly beating, warming heart of his.

He restored his arrogance to his face, pressed his lips into a cold hard line: “At least you know your place. You are not worth my goodwill.”

His sleeve swept past her shoulder as he walked away in long strides.

Shen Weici heard Song Zhang’s words and paused. She did not feel she had said anything wrong. Song Zhang had always been cold and cutting toward her — she did not trust him.

The faint cold fragrance he had left behind still lingered at the tip of her nose. She calmly gathered her sleeves, took the cloak hanging on the stand nearby, and turned and walked out.

She stood in the corridor, pulled on the cloak, and was crossing the courtyard when she felt a gaze fall on her from behind. She turned to look — and saw Song Zhang standing at the window.

Behind him was a broad band of bright light. His face was in the alternating dark and shadow.

She could not read his expression from here, but she could feel the vast weight of feeling in his gaze, and it gave her a small, quiet jolt.

Shen Weici looked away and pulled the cloak’s hood up over her head.

Matron Chang, waiting at the courtyard gate, came hurrying forward the moment she saw Shen Weici: “What did the Second Young Master say?”

Shen Weici considered for a moment, then opened her mouth: “Just now when I spoke with Young Lord Song, he did not say yes and did not say no. He only told me to go back first.”

Matron Chang’s face creased with difficulty. One could not press Song Zhang for more — she had no choice but to nod: “Then let us go back.”

Back in Linchun Courtyard, Yue Deng took the cloak from Shen Weici’s shoulders and immediately asked: “Is Miss’s head aching?”

Shen Weici shook her head. She sat sideways in the chair, her pale slender fingers held near the fire basin, warmth spreading from her fingertips. The pallor of her face began to take on a little color again. She stared at a point on the floor, lost in thought.

Very early the next morning, Matron Chang from Lady Wen’s quarters came to remind Shen Weici to dress herself promptly.
