Being held this way — a man not closely acquainted with her holding her shoe — her face had gone pale, and there was a kind of helpless uncertainty in her usually composed eyes. She pulled her leg back, but could not match his grip.

She did not answer him. She only said, a little urgently: “Young Lord Song, please let me go first.”

“It is only a scrape. It is not serious.”

Song Zhang saw that Shen Weici would not answer. His brow was heavy. Without waiting for her to react, he removed her embroidered shoe with no ceremony, revealing the white stocking inside, also bearing a smear of blood.

There was not much blood — only a stain spreading into a small patch — but it looked startling.

Song Zhang glanced at Shen Weici, and in the face of her alarmed eyes, with calm efficiency pulled off her white stocking, revealing her white-porcelain foot beneath.

At the ankle there was a small cut — not wide, but a little deep, as though caught on the sharp corner of a stone.

He stood and went to get the medicine, then turned back to her with a threat: “Do not move.”

“Or I will tie you down.”

Shen Weici froze. Her fingers pressed into the edge of the chair, tightening very slightly.

Her eyes blinked several times. She forced herself to endure the mortifying embarrassment that was making her tremble.

A woman’s foot was never to be seen by another — if this were known, her reputation for propriety would be entirely destroyed.

She suffered it in silence and did not want to make noise that would draw the eyes of the maids outside.

She only tried to pull her foot further back under the hem of her skirt.

Song Zhang took the medicine and crouched back down. He found Shen Weici with her head still turned away and her mouth firmly shut, her face tilted so that from his angle he could only see the sharp point of her chin, the gentle line of her profile, and the long lashes trembling steadily.

In his hand, that small foot was warm and white, the toes round and endearing, curled slightly with a shy reluctance — and through the foot he could feel the trembling in Shen Weici’s whole body.

He looked at it, paused — then saw a hand extend toward him, palm open, trembling, a thin voice with a tremor in it, as though tears were near: “Young Lord Song, let me put the medicine on myself.”

The voice stopped for a moment, going dim: “I am asking you.”

Song Zhang felt something rush hotly through him — that indescribable feeling flooding his entire chest.

He did not place the medicine in that reaching hand. He only lowered his head and applied the ointment to her ankle, and this man who had never in his life known tenderness found himself, this time, carefully controlling his strength, afraid of pressing too hard.

He understood her. For the first time he did not speak a cold or cutting word, and said quietly: “Stay still. I will not look more than I need to.”

He paused: “And I will not speak of it.”

He looked up at Shen Weici from time to time, wanting to see her expression — but she was still looking away, hidden in the shadow, and the uncertainty of it made Song Zhang’s thoughts scatter.

He had said he would not look at her foot — but his eyes could not stop stealing glances. It was the first time he had ever seen a woman’s foot, and he suddenly recalled friends who had gone to the pleasure houses and played with the women there, holding their feet. He had found it repulsive at the time. Now he understood something of the appeal.

Truly, he was reluctant to let go. But he wrapped the wound in white cloth with care, all the same.

chapters.title: Very Heartless
chapters.content:
The room was suddenly very quiet. If any of the maids beyond the curtain had lifted it at that moment, they would have seen the Second Young Master who was always cold and arrogant half-crouched at a young woman’s feet, her foot resting on his knee, and he was — with considerable awkwardness — helping her put on her stocking, and fumbling with the ties.

The flush had long since left Shen Weici’s face, replaced by alarm. This woman who could always make herself calm in any situation — this time her face was pale, her teeth biting down on her lower lip, her head still turned to one side, forcing herself through the trembling in her body.

She had taken a strong disliking to Song Zhang in this moment. Her most private self had been exposed by him without any consideration for what she wanted — they were people who should have had nothing between them, and yet he had put her into a position where she could not move.

But she was also struggling with herself inwardly, talking herself into accepting his goodwill — he was crouching below her in this way to apply medicine, and she could not bring herself to say something wounding.

And besides, he had helped her avoid marrying Zhang Tingyi. She should be grateful.

The contradictions in her were a kind of torment, leaving her uneasy and unable to settle — something lodged in her throat that would not move up or down.

Though the person sitting in the chair was silent, Song Zhang knew she was trembling. That foot — smaller than his palm — kept trying to retreat further under the skirt. If he had not been holding it firmly, it would have disappeared entirely.

It was as though in one moment he understood her shyness. Even though he very much wanted to hold it a little longer — in the inner rooms of a woman’s boudoir, this kind of delicacy and intimacy made a heat rise in him, burning and then pressing itself down — he put her embroidered shoe back on for her.

He had always felt there was nothing he would bow or stoop for when it came to a woman — and now experiencing this for the first time, the feeling was beyond words, a satisfaction that filled his entire chest.

He looked up and found her still with her face turned away, staring at one spot on the floor. The smooth line of her chin caught the light. The pink peony flowers on her cloak clustered and full, and he could only think of a beautiful companion for life.

He paused slightly, then released her foot. The embroidered shoe moved. She finally looked back — but did not bring her eyes to him, and only said softly: “Thank you.”

The voice was cool and distant, as though deliberately dissolving the intimacy that had flowed between them.

Her eyes held no expression, still downcast. She braced her hands on the chair and stood, moved past Song Zhang, and seeing him rise, she looked only at his chest, her voice very small: “Please do not see me out, Young Lord Song. Yue Deng is waiting for me outside.”

She paused: “And it is night, after all. If others were to see us together, it would not look well. I ask Young Lord Song to be understanding of my situation.”

She pressed her lips down, looked down, and walked past Song Zhang, lifted the curtain, and went out.

The curtain swayed faintly. The fragrant breeze it had stirred was gone.

Song Zhang stood where he was — gold crown in his hair, brows and eyes sharp, the gold threads in his crane robe catching the light, cold and elegant.

He watched the swaying curtain. In his phoenix eyes there was a faint loss. Watching her walk out with that cool, courteous composure, as if she wished to have no connection to him at all — beneath that unblemished expression, he did not know what he was thinking.

He had caught the faint trace of feeling in her cool, quiet words.

She was blaming him.

Outside, Shen Weici asked the maid at the door to light the candle in her lantern.

The cold night air swept in from the corridor, bringing a slight chill. She suddenly felt a gaze on her from one side and turned — and in the distance, one of the side rooms had lamplight in it, its door standing open. A woman was standing at the doorway, looking toward her.

In the dim light, the woman’s clothes were not the kind a maid would wear — they were quite fine, with ornaments in her hair that glinted faintly.

Her face was somewhat familiar — the strikingly beautiful woman who had been close at Song Zhang’s side when Shen Weici had come here before.

The maid who had just lit the lantern passed it to Shen Weici, and following Shen Weici’s gaze, said quietly: “Third Young Miss, that is the Second Young Master’s concubine.”

Shen Weici lowered her eyes, nodded, and walked toward the courtyard gate.

Song Zhang’s courtyard was large. Plum trees lined either side, the path was blue-gray stone, a covered bridge curved across the middle, and a two-story pavilion stood nearby, its corridors connecting through it — prosperous and elegant.

Shen Weici walked silently toward the gate. As she reached it, she drew the jade bracelet from her wrist from inside the cloak and placed it in the hand of the maid accompanying her: “This is something Young Lord Song left behind. I came to return something, and forgot to give it back. Please be so kind as to return it for me.”

In the faint candlelight, the maid looked at the bracelet in her hand, and one glance told her it was very valuable. She took it carefully, genuinely puzzled about how the Second Young Master could have misplaced something this precious.

And she had been serving at Guansong Residence for quite some time and had never seen any woman’s belongings here. Could the Second Young Master have brought it back as a gift for that concubine?

She said politely to Shen Weici: “Third Young Miss, rest assured — I will give it to the Second Young Master right away.”

Those who could enter Guansong Residence — besides the Princess Consort — were only the Third Young Miss. The Second Young Master treated the Third Young Miss differently, and every servant in the courtyard understood this. Of course one should be courteous to Shen Weici.

Shen Weici glanced once at the bracelet in the maid’s hands, nodded, and walked away.

Xunmei stood watching Shen Weici’s figure slowly disappear into the night — fleeting, wavering, the skirt hem lifting around her in a kind of graceful ease. Even she could not look away.

She came to herself after a long moment and hurried back inside.

Song Zhang was leaning against the chair back, tilted slightly to one side, head resting on his hand. He thought again of the way Shen Weici had turned and walked away — and the feeling sitting in his chest was heavy.

It was as if by sending her out himself, he would have been doing her a harm.

Was she really so afraid of people seeing them standing together?

He had never been looked down on like this before.

From outside came the maid’s voice again: “Second Young Master, the Third Young Miss said you left something behind. She asked me to return it to you.”

Song Zhang’s brow twitched. He told her to bring it in. When he saw the bracelet in Xunmei’s hand, his expression went very dark.

He pressed his lips together. Beneath the dim, shadowed expression was an unreadable emotion.

She used every trick on Zhang Yuanheng to draw closer. In front of him, she acted as though she feared even the slightest connection with him.

Very heartless.

Xunmei, seeing that Song Zhang was not speaking, carefully looked up — and immediately dropped her head back down at what she saw.

That one glance had shown her a face so dark it made her afraid to stay in the room.

After a long silence, the icy voice above her came: “Take it and throw it away.”

Xunmei was stunned. She could not believe she had heard right.

Such a fine bracelet — and just throw it away?

She was still dazed when Song Zhang’s phoenix eyes slid toward her. She quickly came to herself belatedly and answered, taking the bracelet out with her.

Outside, she looked at the thing in her hand, genuinely not knowing where to throw it.

Something this fine — even if thrown, would surely be picked up quickly.

She looked helplessly toward Minhe at the door. Minhe saw the jade in Xunmei’s hand and clicked his tongue inwardly. He was the only one who knew that to find one suitable bracelet, the General had summoned the proprietors of over a dozen establishments in the capital to bring their finest pieces, and had chosen this one from among them after careful deliberation.

He let out a quiet sound of regret, took the bracelet, and told Xunmei to go back inside.

chapters.title: Becoming the Target of His Words
chapters.content:
In truth, Shen Weici’s foot hardly hurt at all. Cuts like that had happened several times before on the hills, and she had never thought much of them.

She could not help thinking once more of Song Zhang applying the medicine and wrapping the wound for her. She pushed the image from her mind with her expression unchanged and quickened her pace.

When she got back to Linchun Courtyard, Yue Deng was already there. The moment she saw Shen Weici come in, she hurried over and murmured in her ear: “That maid went back to the Second Young Miss’s courtyard.”

“I knew there was something familiar about those movements — I must have seen her somewhere before.”

“She is the Second Young Miss’s woman. What is the Second Young Miss having her follow Miss for? Is she up to some trouble again?”

Shen Weici heard this and went inside to wash up, saying quietly to Yue Deng: “Do not say anything about this to others for now.”

Yue Deng followed and asked, puzzled: “Why is she following Miss?”

Shen Weici’s eyes moved to Yue Deng: “She may believe there is something between me and Young Lord Song. Otherwise she would not have gone toward Song Zhang’s direction just now.”

“But do not draw any conclusions yet. Wait and see what she does next.”

Yue Deng nodded and handed Shen Weici a warm, wet cloth from the washstand to clean her face.

When Yue Deng helped Shen Weici take off her shoes before bed, she discovered blood on the white stocking, and immediately asked: “Miss had a fall?”

Shen Weici made a sound of assent and sat on the edge of the bed, then looked at the few pouches on the table beside her and said: “The foot is not a serious matter — it will be fine in a few days. Do not worry about it.”

She spread the pouches out before Yue Deng: “Tomorrow, go out early and take these to the young masters’ courtyards. These other ones go to the young misses.”

“Each pouch has a name in the corner at the bottom. You and Hexia check carefully — do not mix them up. And remember what I told you to say.”

Yue Deng nodded: “Miss, rest assured. It is not the first time.”

She also looked with concern at Shen Weici’s foot: “Miss’s foot is really fine? It is bleeding — maybe put some medicine on it.”

Shen Weici had absolutely no desire to look at her foot. One look and she would be reminded of what had happened earlier, with all its mortification.

She said silently to herself: no more dealings with him. She slid her leg under the quilt, settled back against the pillow, and said to Yue Deng: “The medicine was applied at Young Lord Song’s.”

“The nights are getting colder. Go to sleep early too.”

Yue Deng, seeing Shen Weici was clearly unwilling to say more, said a quiet “mm,” rose to lower the bed curtain, and went out.

In the dim quiet of the bed curtains, Shen Weici stared at the hangings for a while before turning to her side and going to sleep.

The next morning, after a light tidy-up, Shen Weici went to the Old Madam’s quarters.

Today was a rest day, and each branch was expected to gather at the Old Madam’s for a morning of company. As she arrived, she could already hear cheerful talk, and people coming and going — no one paid her arrival any particular notice.

She was again about to find herself an unobtrusive corner to sit in and get through the morning when Shen Mingqiu rose and came to pull at her: “Come, Third Sister, sit next to me.”

In the distance, Shen Zhaozhao watched with cold eyes and gave a scornful sound before turning back to flatter the Old Madam.

Shen Mingqiu knew that Shen Zhaozhao was the cleverest at fawning on the Old Madam and had always looked down on the concubine-born girls, talking to them with a tone of superiority as though she were simply a cut above them.

She had no desire to go and ingratiate herself with Shen Zhaozhao as she once might have. The Second Branch’s reputation was already in ruins. There was no need for her to go near it — she would only end up tainted herself.

She took Shen Weici’s hand and smiled, saying quietly: “Sister truly has fine craftsmanship — you even embroidered the dewdrops on the lotus flower. Come and teach me sometime? Would you be willing, Third Sister?”

Shen Weici had not known when she and Shen Mingqiu had become this close, but smiled back: “I use a slip-stitch technique — there is a small trick to it. If Fourth Sister truly wants to learn, come and find me any time. You may well be even better at it than I am.”

Shen Mingqiu laughed: “Then it is decided — I will come and find you when I am free. You must not say I am a nuisance.”

Shen Weici smiled: “Of course not.”

As they were talking, another person came in — none other than Song Zhang.

He was dressed rather casually today. He had not put on the long layered jacket or fur coat he usually wore in winter, only a black round-collar brocade robe, wrists unfastened, no sword hanging at his waist — only a rather elegant paired-sparrow jade ornament, its white tassel just brushing his robe hem. His face was as fine as ever, his spirit vivid — and without the usual cold sharpness, there was even, very faintly, a suggestion of ease and elegance about him.

The moment Song Zhang entered, he naturally drew every eye in the main hall. He seldom had any dealings with the Marquis Manor’s people and almost never came to the Old Madam’s for these gatherings — even though a special invitation was extended every time, he had never previously attended.

He had only come once before — and yet here he was again. For someone who was the center of everyone’s fascination, how could he not attract notice?

Song Zhang walked in and the Old Madam smiled: “I thought you were not coming again. I was just asking your father about it.”

Song Zhang’s lips curved in a cool, sparse smile: “It has been some time since I came to see the Old Madam, so I thought I would come and join the gathering.”

The Old Madam’s expression brightened considerably: “You are thoughtful to remember me.”

She called a matron to pour tea for Song Zhang herself.

The Jian’an Manor still needed the First Branch to hold things together, and for Song Zhang — though not her blood grandson, not raised at her side, and only recently resident at the Manor — she still could not help being pleased to have someone so accomplished nearby. It was a matter of pride.

The Third Branch’s eldest son, Shen Siwen, was one of the few who could exchange a few more words with Song Zhang on ordinary days. He had passed through the hereditary examination process at the Ministry of Personnel and held a not-very-important official post, and the two occasionally crossed paths at the palace.

He noticed the pouch hanging at Song Zhang’s waist and said with some curiosity: “It is unusual to see you wearing a pouch. Is there something special about this one?”

Seated across the room, Shen Weici glanced at the pouch and went still. She lowered her gaze.

Song Zhang’s eyes swept over the smoke-pink figure and his lips curved.

He sat in the chair a maid had brought, turning the teacup in his hand in an unhurried way. But his voice, though low, was quite distinct in the main hall: “Third Young Miss Shen made it especially for me. She put considerable care into it, so naturally I could not disappoint Third Young Miss Shen’s effort.”

Then he let his gaze drift to where Shen Weici sat, in her unobtrusive corner, his phoenix eyes carrying a faint trace of amusement: “Is that not so, Third Young Miss Shen?”

Every eye in the room shifted at once to Shen Weici — fine brows and bright eyes, delicate shoulders and soft neck, like willow fronds in the breeze, effortlessly captivating to anyone who looked. No one knew exactly when this young woman — who had once seemed like a forgettable nobody, a girl from the countryside — had come to seem so luminous. Every expression and every smile of hers outshone any flower, more striking than any other young woman in the Manor.

chapters.title: Accused of Seduction
chapters.content:
Shen Weici felt the weight of everyone’s gaze. Her fingers tightened slightly around the handkerchief.

From the moment Song Zhang had come in, she had noticed the pouch hanging at his waist, and a vague unease had risen in her. She simply had not expected Song Zhang to come out and say it so openly.

The words, as he phrased them, would give rise to more than a little misunderstanding about her.

She quickly turned the situation over in her mind, and was about to speak when Shen Zhaozhao’s voice broke in from above with a pointed sneer: “Oh — so this is where her shameless scheming was going all along.”

“What a thoroughly common thing to do for a girl from the countryside — practically throwing herself at Second Brother Song.”

“Do you really think Second Brother Song could ever look at you?”

Shen Zhaozhao walked in front of Shen Weici, mockery gleaming cold in her eyes: “Shen Weici, to seduce Second Brother Song — surely you haven’t gone and done something even more degrading?”

“Like going to Second Brother Song’s courtyard at night and offering yourself…”

At Shen Zhaozhao’s words, the main hall went completely silent.

Song Zhang’s expression also darkened. He leaned against the chair back and looked at Shen Zhaozhao with cold eyes, saying two cold words: “Be quiet.”

Shen Zhaozhao’s heart lurched.

Shen Yanli, noticing the contempt in the others’ expressions and the darkened look on Song Zhang’s face, also felt it was embarrassing and quickly pulled Shen Zhaozhao aside: “Zhaozhao, what are you saying?”

But Shen Zhaozhao flung his hand off. She had steeled herself and said loudly: “What am I saying wrong? Why else would she give Second Brother Song a pouch? Clearly she has those kinds of intentions.”

“A pouch is a personal object — for her to give it to Second Brother Song, of course she has shameless intentions!”

“Truly disgraceful.”

Shen Yanli’s brow was deeply furrowed. He could take no more: “Go and sit down!”

“If you will not, leave right now!”

Shen Zhaozhao looked at her brother in shock and felt hugely wronged. She did not understand what she had said wrong, and she cried toward Shen Yanli: “Am I still wrong?”

“Why are you protecting that wretched woman!”

Shen Rongsheng’s expression went leaden. He shot another cutting look at Lady Wen beside him. This was truly a disgrace — she had been spoiled and indulged into this state. And in the presence of the Third Branch and in front of the Old Madam, making a scene like this — as if afraid no one would know how the Second Branch had treated the concubine-born daughter.

Giving a pouch to a man alone was indeed improper. Shen Rongsheng glanced at Shen Weici, was just about to tell her to step back and avoid further humiliation —

When he heard Shen Zuo’s voice from across the room: “Second Older Sister may have misunderstood.”

“This morning, Third Older Sister sent a pouch to my brother and me as well — she said it was because Laba was coming up and she wanted to share the good fortune.”

Then he looked toward Shen Yanli: “Third Older Brother, did Third Older Sister also send you a pouch this morning?”

Shen Yanli’s expression was complicated as he looked at Shen Zhaozhao. He frowned deeply, truly unable to understand how the once lively and bright sister he had known had become this.

He said quietly: “Third Sister’s maid sent a pouch to my courtyard this morning as well. Every courtyard received one. What is this fit about?”

Shen Mingqiu also rose, taking out the pouch in her hand: “This is what Third Sister gave to me just now. I was just asking Third Sister to teach me her embroidery technique. Did Second Sister not receive one?”

Song Zhang’s expression shifted slightly. He looked at the pouch in his hand and pressed his lips together.

Shen Zhaozhao glared furiously at Shen Weici. Rebuked like this by so many people in the hall, and spoken sharply to by her own brother — she was overcome with grievance, and directed all her fury at Shen Weici: “This was all arranged by you, wasn’t it?!”

“You sent something to every courtyard — but deliberately left out mine. You did this on purpose, to humiliate me here today!”

She pointed at Shen Weici with a sharp nail, as though she might lunge at her in the next moment.

Shen Zhaozhao had none of the poise and brightness she had once had. Her fine clothes and jewels only emphasized how far her bearing had deteriorated — the hairpin in her hair trembling, her voice shrill and pressing. Even the Old Madam’s brow furrowed deeply.

Shen Rongsheng found it humiliating. With all the trouble the Second Branch had already been through, and now Shen Zhaozhao making this scene in front of the Third Branch and the Old Madam — it was as if she were determined to announce to the whole world that the Second Branch mistreated their concubine-born daughter.

He could stand no more. He rose sharply and brought his hand across Shen Zhaozhao’s face: “What has come over you — look at where you are. You have made a spectacle of everything.”

Shen Zhaozhao’s face was knocked sideways by the slap. She pressed a hand to it, and large tears rolled down, then she screamed at Shen Rongsheng: “Why is everyone now taking that wretched woman’s side? The way our Second Branch’s name looks outside — isn’t that all because of her?”

“She is nothing but a bastard Father made outside. What right did she have to be raised up as a daughter of the Marquis Manor? If that bastard had never been brought here, none of this would have happened!”

Shen Zhaozhao had said it almost at a shout. Everyone in the hall stared at her in disbelief. It was unimaginable that an unmarried daughter of a noble household would say something this ugly — no one had ever before realized that the Second Young Miss had such a wild and willful streak.

Song Zhang looked toward Shen Weici, and found her face perfectly still, as though none of it was being said about her. His expression darkened slightly.

Shen Weici then rose, and with a trace of sorrow in her eyes, walked to the center of the hall and faced the Old Madam, her voice gentle and clear: “Old Madam, may Weici say a few words — and please do not blame Second Sister for this entirely.”

“This was a misunderstanding from start to finish. Not long ago I had some free time while recovering and embroidered some pouches. Thinking the Laba Festival was approaching and that I had been in the household nearly two months relying on everyone’s goodwill, I embroidered one pouch for each of my older brothers and sisters.”

“This morning, my maid went to Second Sister’s courtyard to deliver hers. The maid at the door said she would need to go in and let Second Sister know first, but then came back and said Second Sister did not want it. My maid brought it home.”

“I thought perhaps Second Sister simply did not care for it, or that it did not feel like a proper enough gesture — so I intended to come today and give it to Second Sister in person. But when I arrived, Second Sister was talking with the Old Madam, and I did not want to interrupt, so I had not yet given it to her. That is the misunderstanding, and it is no wonder Second Sister was confused about my intentions.”

She then reached into her sleeve and held the pouch out toward Shen Zhaozhao: “Second Sister, please do not be angry. This pouch is embroidered with a design of a perfect match for Second Sister. Since Second Sister is getting married after the new year, it is also meant to carry my good wishes.”

This whole account from Shen Weici was knowledgeable and measured — she made no show of her own grievance, placed no fault on Shen Zhaozhao, and in fact explained everything in Shen Zhaozhao’s favor.

Seen together, it was as if Shen Weici were the gracious and composed daughter of a great family, and Shen Zhaozhao a screaming village shrew, the contrast between them plain for all to see.

Even the Old Madam looked at Shen Zhaozhao’s behavior today with visible distaste.

To think the girl’s upbringing had come to this — the Old Madam was deeply disappointed.

Lady Wen, reading the room, knew things had gone far enough. She rose quickly and said to Shen Zhaozhao: “This is all a misunderstanding. Zhaozhao, take the pouch from your Third Sister quickly.”

But Shen Zhaozhao wrenched the pouch from Shen Weici’s hand and dashed it to the floor, stepping on it — and through her weeping cried: “Who wants her so-called goodwill? I would not take anything she has touched.”

“Now you are all on her side. I hate you all!”

She shoved Lady Wen aside with both hands, shot a final venomous look at Shen Weici, and bolted out.

That one look — cold as bone, sharp as a stripping knife — was enough to make Shen Weici’s heart give a small jolt.

She watched Shen Zhaozhao’s figure vanish through the door, watched the matrons and Lady Wen scramble after her, and for a moment the sounds around her faded. Her mind went quiet.

None of this had ever been what she wanted. And yet no one would ever leave her be.

chapters.title: What Do You Take Me For?
chapters.content:
After Shen Zhaozhao’s scene, the hall fell into an awkward silence. People glanced at Shen Rongsheng and Shen Weici and then lowered their heads to murmur among themselves.

Shen Rongsheng felt he had lost face not only at court but here in his own home as well, with not a moment’s peace in his own branch.

He stood, swept his sleeve, and without looking at Shen Weici, walked out with a dark expression.

Shen Weici stood where she was. She looked at the pouch on the floor with dust now on it from being trampled, bent down and picked it up, then excused herself to the room.

With the Second Branch people all gone, there was no reason for her to remain.

The Old Madam watched Shen Weici’s calm and unhurried retreating figure, watched her stand in the corridor with the same composure and let a maid fasten her cloak, and then disappear among the courtyard trees.

Song Zhang glanced at Shen Weici’s retreating figure, rose easily, and also walked out in long strides.

Left in the hall were the Third Branch and First Branch’s First Lord.

Third Mistress Wang could not help saying: “The Second Young Miss really went too far. Only two days ago the Third Young Miss sent me a sachet and I have been sleeping so well with it at night. Such a rare thoughtfulness — and to be treated this way.”

The First Lord looked at the Old Madam: “If the Second Branch goes on like this, trouble will come sooner or later. Mother ought to say something to Second Sister-in-law — she should not carry things this far.”

He rose: “I will go and have a proper word with Rongshen.”

And with that the First Lord also went.

The Third Lord, seeing both elder brothers had left, found no purpose in staying either. He stood, patted his robe, and left for his own courtyard to enjoy his birds.

A rest day that had been meant for cheerful company had become empty and quiet within moments.

The Old Madam’s expression remained poor for a long time. She finally said: “Zhaozhao must be properly managed. If she carries on like this after her marriage, no one will indulge her.”

Third Mistress Wang smiled: “Indeed. Word is that the Young Marquis Xu’s household already has several bed-warmers. If the Second Young Miss takes after Second Sister-in-law’s habits, won’t the marriage be complete chaos?”

The moment the words were out of Lady Wang’s mouth, she felt the Old Madam’s eyes on her and stopped herself.

On her way out, Shen Weici had passed through a secluded stand of banana trees when a hand suddenly shot out and pulled her sideways. Before she could cry out, she was pulled into the shelter of a large embrace and pressed against the wall of a false mountain hollow.

Yue Deng was on the point of screaming when Minhe appeared from somewhere and gave her a fright that almost made her leap into the air.

She heard Minhe say calmly: “My General wants a few words with your young mistress. If you scream and draw people here, the reputation damaged will not be my General’s.”

Yue Deng swallowed the shout. She glared at Minhe: “Where has the Second Young Master taken my young mistress?”

And surely if he wanted to talk, he could have stood somewhere and talked normally — why the grabbing?

Minhe folded his arms and glanced at Yue Deng: “Do not ask too many questions, little maid.”

Yue Deng was fit to burst with indignation.

Inside the hollow, Song Zhang had Shen Weici pressed firmly against him, and the stone behind her was jagged and uneven — she was being jabbed painfully in the back. Yet in front of her was Song Zhang’s chest, and he had his hands braced on either side, with his cold gaze above. Shen Weici knew struggling was useless and simply looked up at Song Zhang: “What does Young Lord Song mean by this?”

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici’s displeasure — that fine, soft brow slightly creased — and snorted coldly. His hand came up to pinch her chin, his dark eyes rolling with deep dissatisfaction: “So Third Young Miss Shen’s carefully hand-sewn pouch — every single person in the household got one.”

“I would like to hear how you explain that.”

Shen Weici’s chin was pinched painfully upward, forced to meet his gaze: “Then why don’t you tell me, Young Lord Song — what did you mean by saying those words in front of all those people just now?”

Song Zhang gave a contemptuous snort: “Do I need to explain to you what I do?”

He held up the pouch before Shen Weici’s face and stared at her coldly: “And you play this kind of trick on me, while telling me again and again you made it especially for me. What do you take me for?”

“Someone to be fooled whenever you like?”

The large hand had moved from her chin to her slender throat. The warmth of that hand was intense — even only resting against her skin, she could feel its strength, as though it might snap her neck at any moment.

Shen Weici forced down the trembling in her body. In this moment she felt, for the first time, the danger that lived in Song Zhang.

Those eyes — which had seen countless lives and deaths — were indifferently merciless, like an ice blade, flaying her one cut at a time.

She thought now: if he truly pressed that hand down and choked the life out of her here, he was probably capable of it.

She was nothing. In this Manor, her status was the most contemptible of all — an illegitimate daughter whom no one took seriously. Her father had little real love for her; she was nothing but a bargaining chip to be exchanged for something useful.

If she truly died, the matter would only be quietly buried.

The pressure at her throat slowly tightened. She blinked back the wetness in her eyes and said with difficulty: “For a young woman to give a pouch to a man she is not connected to would easily give rise to misunderstanding. I simply wanted to be careful so as not to attract gossip.”

“I am currently still negotiating a marriage arrangement with the Earl’s Manor. I did not want to stir up talk.”

“The pouch Young Lord Song holds was truly sewn by me, stitch by stitch. I did not deceive Young Lord Song.”

The tendons in the back of Song Zhang’s hand stood out. He wanted to strangle Shen Weici where she stood.

Yet however much force his hand exerted, he could not make himself tighten it. That throat was too slender and smooth — too fragile.

And even seeing her look of discomfort, his grip, against his will, had already loosened slightly.

He ground his teeth in rage. His darkened eyes were full of contempt: “And she still wants to marry into the Earl’s Manor? You like Zhang Yuanheng that much?”

“You have done everything to draw him in. How certain are you he is the one you want to marry?”

“Do you not know what you are?”

Shen Weici’s eyes wavered. Her eyes were red: “I only want to marry a decent man. In what way does that concern Young Lord Song?”

“Since I came to this Manor, I have never tried to take anything that belonged to someone else. I only want to marry into the Earl’s Manor. To Young Lord Song’s eyes, is that so shameful?”

Song Zhang felt Shen Weici’s words like sharp needles in his ears. The redness in her eyes was equally sharp.

He bore down with the full weight of someone who stood above others — that self-righteous, baseless suspicion — without once thinking about why she did the things she did.

She turned her face away. She did not want to look at Song Zhang for another second. She lowered her eyes to hide the glimmer in them, and she was tired.

She schemed, yes — but only to survive quietly in this Marquis Manor, to find a stable anchor. If no one harmed her, she would not harm anyone.

Song Zhang watched her turn away, saw her shut her eyes in avoidance, and felt a surge of irritation. He grabbed her chin and forced her to look at him: “Lost for words now?”

Shen Weici was made to tilt her face upward. Her eyes were red all around. She blinked — and a trail of wetness moved down her face. Her dark brows were low, her expression fragile and delicate — like a butterfly in rain, smoke-blue curtains of mist, the sound of distant hills and soft falling water.

Song Zhang stared, then said coldly through clenched teeth: “Pulling out your usual tricks again?”

The banana leaves outside the hollow moved gently, and cool air threaded through the branches and into the hidden space, lifting a strand of her hair against Song Zhang’s face. That quiet fragrance curled and spread from his nostrils.

Song Zhang’s dark eyes were heavy with feeling — pressing down until Shen Weici could barely breathe.

She said only, quietly: “If Young Lord Song had not mentioned the pouch in front of all those people today — would Shen Zhaozhao’s scene have happened?”

“Was Young Lord Song not also scheming against me?”

Song Zhang paused. Then his eyes went cold and narrow.

Shen Weici was right. He had been scheming against her.

She refused his things, and the more she kept him at a distance, the more he wanted her connected to him.

He wanted her to see clearly — between himself and Zhang Yuanheng, which one she should actually choose.

The two of them stood in silence. Song Zhang released his fingers and looked at the wetness at the corner of her eye. Then suddenly he said quietly: “If I told your fine father about the vermillion paint you had pressed into the handkerchief in advance — what do you think the consequences would be for you?”

The fingers hidden in her wide sleeve trembled faintly. Shen Weici knew: the one thing she had not done cleanly.

Even if the handkerchief was gone, no one would disbelieve Song Zhang’s word.

This one variable — he had seized the one piece of leverage over her.

Even if she could persuade everyone that the blood had been real, the extent of the vermillion paint on the handkerchief was enough to redirect all suspicion onto her.

She closed her eyes for a moment. For the second time she felt herself utterly drained.

She looked at Song Zhang, her face pale and her eyes still red: “What will it take for Young Lord Song to leave me alone?”

Song Zhang heard this and his expression darkened further. Something struggled in the depths of his eyes. His voice came out low: “Behave yourself. Then I will leave you alone.”

Shen Weici heard what sounded like room to maneuver in Song Zhang’s words. She did not ask what he meant by behaving herself, and did not want to know — for she had never deliberately provoked anyone.

She lowered her brow and answered very obediently: “Understood.”

Song Zhang had not expected Shen Weici to comply this quickly. A contemptuous thought followed at once: with her one secret in his hand, what waves could she make?

An unremarkable concubine-born daughter. Even with some scheming, it amounted to very little.

His dark eyes fell on her white face — those wet marks on her cheeks, the appeal of it — and the earring at her ear still swaying, falling against that impossibly fair cheek, so that even the earlobe looked beautifully white.

Dark hair like cloud, and at the corner of her eye that indefinable, magnetic pull. Small and full lips holding a faint warmth — he had kissed her once, and still he thought of it in the nights, unable to forget that sensation.

His fingers had already, against his will, loosened slightly. He looked down at her — the long lashes still damp. She looked unbearably pitiable.

He had come today wanting to scheme against her, to see how she would manage. To see what she would do if he exposed what she had covered up.

Her cheek was almost touching his chest. The soft warmth of her breathing fell against him, and he almost felt it.

His body bent down just slightly further. He swallowed, and said again in a hoarse voice: “From now on, stop drawing Zhang Yuanheng in. Stay where you are and keep those calculations of yours in check.”

Shen Weici’s gaze rested on Song Zhang’s chest. His breath fell hot against her face.

She could feel how close he was. She had no wish to be entangled with him any further. She gave another very docile and obedient sound of agreement.

Song Zhang saw how compliant Shen Weici was at this moment, then thought again that she was always so compliant — almost no temper at all. Even when she was angry, she would very quickly become agreeable, as though she were deeply practical, or as though she knew how to hold people’s hearts — always yielding and retreating.

Song Zhang found he could not see past her techniques.

Right now, smelling her scent, he even wanted to lower his head and kiss her.

He wondered: she only knew to draw in Zhang Yuanheng — had he simply never entered her eyes?

Or did she think she could not reach him?

This woman understood situations very well. Perhaps she really did think that way.

An impulse moved in him. In the small hollow, only the two of them, the ambiguous air flowing between them, his body barely an inch from pressing against hers.

He wanted her to take some initiative — even a single look of active invitation — and he would pull her into his arms and protect her from everything afterward.

But she did not give him so much as a glance, and instead asked: “May I go now?”

Song Zhang frowned. Was this woman genuinely not understanding, or was she playing hard to get again?

He had come this close, practically had her in his arms, and she said she was leaving.

Song Zhang’s expression went dark. He had always been the one pursued, and could not bring himself to reach out and hold someone back. But watching her try to edge sideways and out, his annoyance flared — and he grabbed her wrist: “In such a hurry?”

Shen Weici glanced at Song Zhang, then looked away, and said in a voice both light and soft: “Does Young Lord Song have something more to say?”

Song Zhang did not know what to say. The threats had been said, the anger expressed — now he only wanted to stay near her a little longer.

He asked her: “Why won’t you accept anything from me?”

Shen Weici did not look at Song Zhang, only said quietly: “Those are not things I should accept.”

Those cool words extinguished every thought in Song Zhang’s chest.

The words he had been trying to form never came out. He was truly furious with himself — and he looked again at the pouch in his hand, the lion on it seeming to mock him for being rejected by a woman. He wanted to throw it away but could not bring himself to, and swept his sleeve and went out first.

chapters.title: Why Won’t You Accept My Things?
chapters.content:
Song Zhang left, and Shen Weici was alone in the hollow.

She pressed her handkerchief to the wetness at the corners of her eyes and waited a while before stepping out.

Yue Deng saw Shen Weici come out from behind the banana leaves and hurried over: “Miss.”

Shen Weici knew what Yue Deng was going to ask and only said: “It is nothing. Let us go back.”

Yue Deng noticed Shen Weici’s faintly red eyes and said nothing, quietly supporting her young mistress as they walked back.

Shen Zhaozhao had run all the way back to her courtyard, thrown herself onto the bed, and wept with her face buried in the pillow. The maids who came after her tried to console her.

One maid crouched beside her and tried to offer comfort. Shen Zhaozhao reached blindly for the teacup at the bedside and hurled it at her face. The maid’s forehead was immediately cut.

Shen Zhaozhao sat up and looked at the maid coldly: “This morning when that woman sent something here — why didn’t you tell me what it was?”

“Did you do it on purpose to harm me?”

Acui’s forehead was still bleeding. She did not dare wipe it, and immediately knelt: “Second Young Miss, this servant was wrongly accused. This morning when this servant came in and told you, you had not heard a full sentence — when this servant said Linchun Courtyard had sent something, you interrupted and said not to accept anything from Linchun Courtyard. This servant dared not say another word after that.”

Shen Zhaozhao heard this and was suddenly furious again. She stood and kicked Acui: “You shameless little wretch — still making excuses!”

She turned and shouted at the matron beside her: “Drag this wretch out to the courtyard and slap her thirty times. I want to see if that mouth of hers still makes such clever excuses.”

The maids in the room were all frightened into silence. They all knew perfectly well that what Acui had said was the truth.

When the maid had come in that morning to report, the Second Young Miss had been sitting at the dressing table getting ready. Acui had barely said that Linchun Courtyard had sent something when the Second Young Miss had not waited for the rest and grown angry, calling Linchun Courtyard’s things dirty and unworthy of touching. After that, how could Acui dare to say another word?

Everyone in the room had heard it. But no one dared speak up for Acui now. Just as the matron was about to drag Acui out, Lady Wen came in.

Lady Wen saw the maid being roughly hauled out and did not say much about it. She only looked at Shen Zhaozhao’s tear-streaked face with some heartache, dismissed the rest of the maids in the room, pulled Shen Zhaozhao into her arms, and sat at the edge of the bed. Sighing, she said: “I have never seen you this impulsive before. How have you gotten so unable to hold yourself back?”

“Your father hit you, and it was not entirely undeserved — in front of the Third Branch and in front of the Old Madam, your father cares about his face. How could he not be angry?”

Shen Zhaozhao heard her mother’s words and felt even more wronged.

She held tight to Lady Wen’s sleeve, weeping loud enough now that her words came out muffled and broken: “I just can’t bear to see people praising that wretched woman. I can’t bear to see her having an easy life.”

“She has ruined the Second Branch’s reputation outside. My old close friends won’t even talk to me anymore. I hate her — I hate her so much.”

“And what makes me hate her even more is that Father is taking her side, and Second Brother Song is helping her. I can’t swallow this.”

Lady Wen well understood Shen Zhaozhao’s grievance. The Second Branch’s reputation had fallen to the gutter, her husband had been demoted, and hardly anyone wanted to associate with them now — even the Third Branch had risen above them.

She gently patted Shen Zhaozhao’s back, and her own eyes cooled: “As long as she is still in my hands, she will not have a smooth road. I will certainly make her suffer.”

Shen Zhaozhao looked up with red eyes at Lady Wen: “But her engagement with the Yiyong Earl’s Manor is almost settled. I think about her becoming the Earl’s Manor’s future young mistress and I feel nothing but hate.”

“She is just a bastard from the countryside — what right does she have to marry so well?”

“With her origins, she should only be fit to marry some old widower — only fit to be a concubine!”

Lady Wen picked up a handkerchief and wiped Shen Zhaozhao’s tears. She said quietly: “Now even the Old Madam is showing interest in her engagement with the Earl’s Manor. I will certainly not let this go so smoothly.”

“Do not worry. As long as I am here, she will not become the Earl’s Manor’s young mistress. I will not let her have her way.”

She looked down at Shen Zhaozhao with tenderness: “How could I ever let her live better than you? Though the Earl’s Manor is in decline, Zhang Erlang has several uncles who do business — the household is wealthy. The Earl’s Manor’s private estate alone is considerable, better even than some Marquis households. Shen Weici marrying in would mean a life of wealth and comfort. I naturally refuse to allow it.”

Shen Zhaozhao blinked her wet eyes at Lady Wen: “But Father and Grandmother both care about this match. The Earl’s Manor will be here in a few days to discuss it. What can Mother do?”

Lady Wen gave a cold smile: “Openly I cannot do too much. But to prevent her from becoming a legitimate wife — that is not difficult.”

“With her origins, she is only fit to be a concubine.”

Shen Zhaozhao’s expression eased slightly at this. She buried her face in her mother’s arms and wept quietly: “Now the cousins in the household are all on her side too. What am I supposed to do?”

Lady Wen sighed, softly stroking Shen Zhaozhao’s long hair: “You are simply too impatient. You must rein in your temper going forward.”

“This time your grandmother is also displeased with you. After the new year when you marry, you still need your grandmother to give you a more generous trousseau — these days, do not stir up any more trouble. Go and win your grandmother’s favor back. After all, you are the one she watched grow up. You are the legitimate daughter of this household — Shen Weici cannot compare to you in this lifetime.”

Shen Zhaozhao pursed her lips. She knew what her mother said was true — but the hatred was there, and she could not get rid of it. She hated Shen Weici’s looks too, hated that standing beside her she herself seemed diminished.

She hated that Shen Weici had been here barely two months and already had so many people in the Manor on her side.

Today in the main hall, everyone had spoken in Shen Weici’s defense. Those disdainful looks directed at her — as though she were the unreasonable villain — made her furious enough to lose her mind.

Shen Zhaozhao gripped her mother’s sleeve hard, rubbed her tears into the fabric, and choked out: “Mother must make Shen Weici’s life miserable. Otherwise I will never have any peace.”

Lady Wen looked down at the intense hatred in Shen Zhaozhao’s eyes and frowned: “Leave the scheming to me from now on. I can see that Shen Weici is not as obedient as she appears on the surface.”

“But no matter how she twists and turns, she cannot escape the palm of a hand. These days you also stay indoors more — do not go looking for trouble. Otherwise your father will be even more fed up with you.”

Shen Zhaozhao heard this and dissolved into fresh tears: “Father does not like me anymore. He used to love me the most, and so did Elder Brother.”

“Today Elder Brother even took her side…”

Lady Wen patted Shen Zhaozhao’s back: “So you must not make any more scenes. Mother will get your revenge for you.”

Only then did Shen Zhaozhao’s agitated heart begin to settle somewhat. She buried herself in her mother’s arms, nodded, and cried.

chapters.title: She Is Only Fit to Be a Concubine
chapters.content:
The moment Song Zhang left, Shen Weici was the only one remaining inside the grotto of the rockery.

She dabbed at the glimmer of tears at the corners of her eyes with her handkerchief, waited a moment, then stepped out.

The instant Yue Deng saw Shen Weici emerge from behind the banana leaves, she hurried over. “Miss.”

Shen Weici knew what Yue Deng wanted to ask. She only said, “It’s nothing. Let’s go back.”

Yue Deng noticed the faint redness around Shen Weici’s eyes, and quietly, without a word, supported her mistress as they made their way back.

On the other end, Shen Zhaozhao ran all the way back to her courtyard, threw herself onto the bed in the inner chamber, and buried her face in it, sobbing loudly. The maidservants who had come running after her rushed to comfort her.

One of them crouched beside Shen Zhaozhao and tried to soothe her, but Shen Zhaozhao grabbed the teacup from the bedside and hurled it at her face without a second thought. Blood immediately welled up from the maidservant’s forehead.

Shen Zhaozhao pushed herself upright and fixed the girl with an icy glare. “This morning, when that wretch sent things over, why didn’t you tell me what she sent?”

“Were you deliberately trying to harm me as well?”

Acui’s forehead was still bleeding, yet she did not dare wipe it. She dropped to her knees at once and begged for mercy. “Second Miss has wronged this servant. This morning, when this servant came in to inform Miss, Miss did not let me finish. The moment Miss heard it was something sent from Linchun Courtyard, she cut me off and said she wanted nothing from Linchun Courtyard. This servant did not dare say another word after that.”

The moment Shen Zhaozhao heard this, fury erupted from her. She rose to her feet and kicked Acui hard. “You insolent slave, how dare you talk back.”

Then she turned on the matron standing nearby and snapped, “Drag this wretched girl out into the courtyard and give her thirty slaps across the mouth. I want to see whether she still has the nerve to talk back after that.”

The other maidservants in the room were too frightened to make a sound. Every one of them knew that what Acui had said was true.

That morning, when Acui had come in to report, Second Miss had been sitting at her dressing table. Acui had barely gotten out the words that Linchun Courtyard had sent something when Second Miss flew into a temper before hearing the rest, ranting that anything from Linchun Courtyard would only dirty her hands. Acui had not dared bring it up again.

All the maidservants in the room had witnessed it, yet not one of them dared speak up for Acui now. The matron had already begun dragging Acui toward the door when Madam Wen walked in.

Madam Wen glanced at the maidservant being hauled out by the matron’s rough hands and did not interfere. She turned her gaze to Shen Zhaozhao, whose face was streaked with tears, and felt a pang of tenderness. She dismissed the rest of the maidservants from the room, then drew Shen Zhaozhao into her arms and sat with her at the edge of the bed, sighing with feeling. “You were never this impulsive before. How is it that you can’t hold yourself together anymore?”

“Your father’s hand was not entirely unjust. The old madam was present, and so were people from the Third Branch. Your father values his dignity, so how could he not be angered?”

Shen Zhaozhao felt even more aggrieved hearing her mother’s words.

She clutched tightly at Madam Wen’s sleeve, her sobs growing louder, her words half-muffled by her weeping. “I simply cannot stand to watch others praise that wretch. Even less can I stand to see her doing well.”

“She ruined the name of our Second Branch. My old friends won’t even look at me anymore. I hate her, I hate her.”

“What makes me hate her even more is that Father takes her side, and Second Brother Song helps her too. I cannot swallow this.”

Madam Wen understood Shen Zhaozhao’s grievances all too well. The reputation of their Second Branch had plummeted outside these walls, the master had been demoted, and almost no one came to seek their company any longer. Even the Third Branch had surpassed them now.

She patted Shen Zhaozhao’s back gently, her eyes cool and calculating. “As long as she remains under my hand, I will not let her sail along so smoothly. I will naturally make things bitter for her.”

Shen Zhaozhao lifted her tear-reddened eyes to Madam Wen. “But her betrothal to the Yiyong Earl’s Mansion is about to be settled. The moment I think that she will one day become the heir consort of the Earl’s Mansion, I burn with hatred.”

“A wild creature from the countryside, what right does she have to marry into such a fine family?”

“Given her origins, she is only fit to marry some old widower, only fit to be a concubine.”

Madam Wen lifted her handkerchief and wiped at Shen Zhaozhao’s tears, lowering her voice. “Now that the old madam has even begun taking an interest in this match between her and the Earl’s Mansion, I will certainly not let things proceed so easily for her.”

“Rest assured, as long as I am here, she will never become the young mistress of the Earl’s Mansion. I will not let her have her way.”

Then Madam Wen looked down at Shen Zhaozhao, her tone tender. “How could I allow her to live better than you? Though the Earl’s Mansion has declined, Second Young Master Zhang’s uncles are all merchants, the family is wealthy, and the Mansion itself holds considerable private assets, more than even some marquisates. For Shen Weici to marry in would mean a life of comfort and riches. I will never agree to that.”

Shen Zhaozhao blinked her tear-bright eyes at Madam Wen. “But Father and Grandmother both care deeply about this match, and the Earl’s Mansion is coming in a few days to discuss the betrothal. What can Mother possibly do?”

Madam Wen gave a cold, quiet smile. “There are things I cannot do openly, but preventing her from entering as a proper wife is not difficult at all.”

“Given her standing, she is only fit to be a concubine.”

The expression on Shen Zhaozhao’s face eased slightly at that. She buried herself in her mother’s arms again and sobbed. “Now even the cousins in the marquis’s household are taking her side. What am I to do?”

Madam Wen sighed and gently stroked Shen Zhaozhao’s long hair. “It is precisely because your temper is too rash. You must learn to rein it in from now on.”

“Your grandmother is displeased with you now as well. When you marry next year, you will still need her to prepare a generous dowry for you. Do not stir up any more trouble these days. Go before your grandmother and make yourself agreeable. After all, you are the one she watched grow up, and you are the legitimate daughter of the marquis’s household. Shen Weici can never match you in this lifetime.”

Shen Zhaozhao pouted. Though she knew her mother was right, she still hated that girl, hated her most of all for her looks, so striking that standing beside her, she herself was nearly overshadowed.

She hated too that in less than two months since she had arrived, so many people in the marquis’s household had already begun to favor her.

Today in the main hall, every single person had spoken up for her. And the looks of contempt they had turned on Shen Zhaozhao, as though she were some unreasonable villain making trouble without cause, had nearly driven her out of her mind with rage.

Shen Zhaozhao gripped her mother’s sleeve tightly, rubbing the fresh tears from her eyes into the fabric of her mother’s robe, and choked out, “Mother must make things difficult for Shen Weici. Otherwise I will never have a moment’s peace.”

Madam Wen looked down at her daughter and frowned at the ferocious hatred burning in Shen Zhaozhao’s eyes. “Leave the scheming to me from now on. I can see that Shen Weici is not as meek and obedient as she appears.”

“But no matter how much she struggles, she will never escape the palm of my hand. Stay in these days, do not go looking for trouble, and do not give your father further reason to turn against you.”

Shen Zhaozhao dissolved into fresh tears at that. “Father doesn’t even care for me anymore. He used to love me best, and Elder Brother too.”

“Today Elder Brother even spoke up for that wretch...”

Madam Wen patted Shen Zhaozhao’s back. “All the more reason not to cause any more scenes. Leave it to Mother to settle the score.”

Only then did the storm of fury and distress inside Shen Zhaozhao begin, slowly, to subside. She buried herself in her mother’s arms and gave a small, aggrieved nod.

That afternoon, Hexia came running in with a face full of delight and drew close to Shen Weici, speaking in a low, excited voice. “Miss, this servant heard that Second Miss and Second Madam were summoned to the old madam’s this afternoon, and that the old madam gave them both a thorough scolding.”

Shen Weici was reclining in her chair, leaning slightly to one side, both hands resting on the armrests, the white brocade of her robes pooling down from the seat’s edge. She was gazing at the charcoal brazier beside her, her expression listless and distracted.

Since the moment she had come out after being drawn aside by Second Young Master Song that morning, Yue Deng had noticed that Miss’s spirits had been low, as though something weighed heavily on her mind.

She had asked once, but Miss said nothing. Now, seeing Shen Weici staring blankly into the distance again, Yue Deng turned to Hexia and asked, “Where did you hear this from?”

Hexia smiled. “Just now, when Yanr and I went to the accounts room to collect the monthly allowance, I ran into an old friend, a sister I used to be close with. She serves in the old madam’s chambers. The way Second Miss carried on today had none of the bearing of a young lady from a proper family.”

“So she whispered to me that the old madam has also punished Second Miss with copying out the Women’s Precepts, and has confined her to her rooms for three days, not allowed to leave.”

Many in the marquis’s household were bondservants born into service, and Hexia was one of them. Her mother helped in the kitchen, her father was a general hand, but she knew a great many people.

Yue Deng looked toward Shen Weici, who still sat with her eyes cast down, and could not help saying, “Second Miss’s insufferable arrogance will finally be kept in check for a while. It’s just as well that the old madam has confined her. At least she won’t keep coming to make trouble for Miss.”

The emotion on Shen Weici’s face remained faint. Her fingers stirred slightly, and then she turned her clear, gentle eyes toward Yue Deng. “This is not quite as good a thing for me as you might think.”

Yue Deng paused, puzzled. “Second Miss has been punished, and yet it is not a good thing?”

Hexia chimed in as well. “This servant also thinks that Second Miss really is too much. It isn’t as though Miss ever provoked her, so why does she always fix herself on Miss and refuse to let go?”

chapters.title: Shen Zhaozhao is Confined
chapters.content:
Shen Weici’s slender fingers tapped lightly on the armrest as she softly said, “The rumors outside have already made them resent me. If this matter spreads, I fear I can no longer stay out of it.”

She sighed softly. “Today’s incident was an accident. She intended to harm me, but I never meant to harm her.”

“Even with a thousand precautions, malicious intentions in the dark are the hardest to guard against. There will always be moments when we can’t protect ourselves.”

He Xia then said, “Even if the Second Young Lady is arrogant, would she dare to harm you openly?”

“Besides, once your marriage to the Earl’s family is settled, you won’t be in the Marquis’s mansion anymore. The Second Young Lady will have no choice but to watch from the sidelines.”

Shen Weici rubbed her temples. “What I’m worried about now is my marriage.”

Normally, Shen Weici was meticulous and careful in her actions. Though the Madam Wen couldn’t find fault with her in other matters, the marriage had to go through Madam Wen’s hands. As her birth mother, there was no way to bypass her.

She feared that Madam Wen might interfere in the process.

Additionally, Song Zhang’s recent threats had unsettled Shen Weici.

These days, she hadn’t sent any more letters to Zhang Yuanheng, and she suspected that even if she wrote any, they wouldn’t be delivered. The people at the front gate were likely no longer reliable for passing messages. If Song Zhang found out, he would probably come to trouble her again.

Upon hearing Shen Weici’s concern about the marriage, Yue Deng smiled and said, “Don’t worry about the marriage, Miss. With Young Master Zhang’s promise, you should have no doubts.”

Shen Weici gave a bitter smile. “I’m not worried about Young Master Zhang.”

Yue Deng was taken aback.

At that moment, Yan’er entered and said, “Miss, Lai Fu has arrived.”

Shen Weici paused, then told Yan’er to let Lai Fu in and ordered the other maids in the room to leave.

As soon as Lai Fu entered, he saw Shen Weici sitting in the chair, her expression slightly relaxed yet not particularly happy.

The light from outside cast a soft glow on her, making even the white hem of her dress look exceptionally beautiful.

He took a few steps forward, not daring to look too much, and lowered his head. In a quiet voice, he said, “Third Young Lady, just now Young Master Zhang came to see the Master, but the Master wasn’t in. Young Master Zhang asked me to deliver a letter to you.”

Shen Weici looked at the letter in Lai Fu’s hand but didn’t take it. Instead, she looked at Lai Fu’s lowered face and asked, “Aren’t you afraid that *he* will find out?”

Lai Fu knew who the “he” Shen Weici referred to. He quickly replied, “When Young Master Zhang gave me the letter, I made sure to block the view of the others at the front gate. No one should have seen it.”

“I also kept it close to my chest. It shouldn’t be discovered.”

Shen Weici sighed. “From now on, you don’t need to deliver letters for me anymore. Don’t take such risks.”

Lai Fu felt a surge of emotion. When had a master ever cared so much for a servant?

In the entire Marquis’s mansion, the one who treated him with the most kindness and spoke to him the most gently was the Third Young Lady.

She even worried about him taking risks. His eyes welled up with tears.

He lowered his head deeply and said in a quiet voice, “Third Young Lady, rest assured. It is my fortune to be able to do things for you.”

Shen Weici straightened her posture slightly and reached out to take the letter from Lai Fu’s hand. She then looked at Lai Fu and asked, “Has Young Master Zhang left?”

Lai Fu looked up and met Shen Weici’s gentle and beautiful eyes, then lowered his head again in shame. “Young Master Zhang said it wouldn’t be appropriate to come see you alone, so he left first.”

Shen Weici knew that Zhang Yuanheng had always been this proper and respectful. She truly wanted to marry him.

She tightened her grip on the letter and looked at Lai Fu again. “Lai Fu, this is the last time you deliver a letter. Don’t do it again next time.”

Lai Fu was stunned, his throat emitting a soft “mm” sound. He then said hoarsely, “Then, Third Young Lady, please take care of yourself. I’ll take my leave now.”

Shen Weici responded with an “mm” and leaned back in her chair, calmly opening the letter in her hand.

Lai Fu retreated to the curtain and, as if possessed, turned his head back. He saw the person leaning on the chair reading the letter, looking like a celestial being. His heart pounded several times, and he hurriedly lifted the curtain and left.

After Lai Fu left, Yue Deng lifted the curtain and entered. Seeing Shen Weici reading the letter, she couldn’t help but exclaim joyfully, “Young Master Zhang wrote to you?”

Shen Weici smiled slightly and lowered her eyes to read the words on the letter carefully.

After she finished reading, she looked at Yue Deng and softly said, “Young Master Zhang has invited me to tour the capital with him on the night of the Laba Festival.”

Yue Deng’s eyes lit up with excitement. “I’ve been in the capital for so long, but I’ve never had the chance to tour it.”

Shen Weici looked at Yue Deng’s excited expression but poured cold water on her enthusiasm. “Do you think it’s that easy to leave the Marquis’s mansion?”

She looked out the window. “Besides, if I leave the Marquis’s mansion, I might be more easily targeted. It might be safer to stay here.”

Moreover, Shen Weici didn’t want Song Zhang to see her with Zhang Yuanheng.

Yue Deng felt sorry for Zhang Yuanheng. “But Young Master Zhang is waiting for you. You haven’t sent him any letters these days either. Won’t this hurt his feelings?”

Shen Weici’s gaze fell on Yue Deng. “I know Young Master Zhang understands my difficulties.”

“He said he would come to propose marriage after the Laba Festival. I’ll wait for him.”

“I trust him.”

She could go without seeing Zhang Yuanheng for these days, but once the marriage was settled, she didn’t believe Song Zhang could say anything.

Two days later, the kitchen sent Laba congee to each courtyard early in the morning.

Shen Weici sat on a low table and took a bite. Listening to He Xia beside her, she said, “Every year on the Laba Festival, the Marquis’s mansion goes to Nan Zheng Street to distribute congee. It lasts until evening. Sometimes, the young masters and ladies of the mansion also go to take a look and go out for a stroll.”

“It’s very lively on the night of the Laba Festival.”

Shen Weici listened quietly, looking at the Laba congee in her hands. The taste was slightly different from that in Yu Yang.

Yue Deng asked He Xia excitedly, “What activities are there in the evening?”

He Xia smiled and said, “There are rituals to drive away evil spirits and plagues, and people line up at the palace gates to receive the emperor’s Laba congee. Of course, there are also various street performances and temple fairs. At Fa Ning Temple in the suburbs, there is the Blessing and Longevity Congee. It is said that getting a bowl can bring longevity and blessings. Many people go there.”

Yue Deng listened with fascination. “I really want to go see it. I’ve never seen what the capital is really like.”

He Xia covered her mouth and laughed. “It’s not just you. Even I only go out once or twice a year. There’s no time to just stroll around leisurely.”

Yue Deng sighed. “There are so many rules in the Marquis’s mansion. You can’t just leave whenever you want. When we were in Yu Yang, on the night of the Laba Festival, there were also temple fairs and markets. It was extremely lively. The Miss and I wore veils and could go wherever we wanted to look.”

Shen Weici listened to their conversation and silently put down her bowl to rinse her mouth.

She didn’t plan to go out today.

However, after sitting in the room for a while in the morning, Shen Mingqiu came to find her. “Eldest Sister, why are you still dressed so plainly? Today, Eldest Sister, come out with me to have some fun.”

Shen Weici quickly shook her head. “You go, Younger Sister. I won’t.”

Shen Mingqiu, upon hearing this, sat next to Shen Weici, looked her up and down, and said, “I see that Eldest Sister’s complexion is much better. Moreover, you’ve been in the Marquis’s mansion for so long. Haven’t you ever wanted to go out and take a look?”

“Tonight will be very lively. In the past, the ladies of the Marquis’s mansion all went out together. The Old Madam also permitted it.”

“My eldest brother and fourth brother will also accompany us. Younger Sister will go together. Otherwise, I won’t even have a close friend to talk to.”

Shen Weici looked at Shen Mingqiu. “Will Yue Qiu and Second Sister not go?”

Shen Mingqiu saw Shen Weici’s expression and couldn’t help but lean close to her ear and whisper, “How come you don’t know even though you’re in the same courtyard? Second Sister has been confined by the Old Madam. Today, she’s still confined and definitely can’t go out.”

“But I heard that she went to the Old Madam again this morning, regardless of everything, to beg to go out. She said she wanted to take this opportunity to see Young Master Xu.”

“I don’t know if the Old Madam agreed.”

“In any case, her crying was loud enough to be laughable.”

Shen Weici pressed her lips together and looked at Shen Mingqiu. “Your information is quite well-informed.”

Shen Mingqiu looked at Shen Weici with sympathy. “My birth mother is nothing like your birth mother, who treats us so harshly. On the contrary, my birth mother has no daughters and treats Yue Qiu and me like her own daughters. She tells me everything and treats me like her own. She is also very good to my mother.”

“All this information is from my birth mother. My mother doesn’t stir up trouble either. She is even more respectful to my birth mother than to my father. My days are indeed much better than yours.”

As she spoke, Shen Mingqiu leaned close to Shen Weici’s ear again and whispered, “In the Marquis’s mansion, who doesn’t know that the one from your second branch is the most difficult to serve? Not even a mosquito can fly into the back courtyard.”

Shen Weici smiled. “Can’t Yue Qiu accompany you?”

Shen Mingqiu took a handful of melon seeds from the plate beside her and said, “Yue Qiu is too young. She can’t talk as pleasantly as you and I can.”

As she spoke, she looked at Shen Weici. “Eldest Sister, you’re so beautiful and have such a good temperament. Who wouldn’t like you?”

“Moreover, you and I are of the same status. Second Sister considers herself superior and looks down on us, the concubine-born daughters. So, we simply ignore her.”

chapters.title: Does Song Shi Leave?
chapters.content:
Shen Mingqiu’s words were indeed true. Over these days, she had also secretly observed Shen Weici and found her to be a truly gentle and heavenly beauty. She was quiet and didn’t cause trouble, yet she seemed to know a little about everything—be it composing couplets, poetry, or playing the game of Shai. In short, she was better than Shen Mingqiu in everything.

Even her embroidery skills were exceptional. The embroidery mistress in the mansion had praised her repeatedly.

They had all studied the female virtues and the six arts from a young age, taught by the same former palace maids who had returned home. Yet none of them were as skilled as Shen Weici.

Probably even Shen Zhaozhao wasn’t this good.

Moreover, Shen Mingqiu didn’t want to fawn over Shen Zhaozhao’s cold face anymore. Her own reputation wasn’t good either. Who would want to approach her?

In the Marquis’s mansion, one needed to have someone to talk to, and Shen Weici was the most suitable.

In fact, Shen Weici also quite liked Shen Mingqiu’s straightforward and warm personality. She spoke directly and affectionately, as if they were the closest of friends.

She pressed her lips and smiled. “It’s just that I can’t accompany you today. My body hasn’t fully recovered yet. I’m afraid of catching a cold.”

Shen Mingqiu frowned. “Are you afraid of running into Second Sister?”

“Even if the Old Madam shows mercy and lets her go out, we can just ignore her. Let her play by herself. Doesn’t she think highly of herself as a legitimate daughter? We won’t go near her.”

As she spoke, she looped her arm through Shen Weici’s. “Eldest Sister, let’s go together. It’s rare to have such a lively occasion.”

Shen Weici smiled. Just as she was about to refuse, she noticed Yue Deng’s hopeful gaze from the side. The words on her lips were swallowed back.

Actually, there wasn’t any absolute reason not to go.

If Shen Zhaozhao went to see Young Master Xu, and she went out with the young masters and ladies of the Marquis’s mansion, perhaps she could catch a glimpse of Young Master Zhang...

She compromised and looked at Shen Mingqiu with a smile. “What time are we leaving?”

Shen Mingqiu’s face lit up with joy. “In the afternoon. We won’t eat at the mansion. We’ll go to a restaurant.”

“This morning, when I went to pay my respects, Eldest Brother said he would treat us.”

Shen Weici knew that the eldest young master of the Marquis’s mansion, Shen Siwen, usually appeared gentle. It seemed he had even spoken up for her that day.

She nodded. “Then come get me before we leave. I’ll get ready after noon.”

Shen Mingqiu put the unfinished melon seeds back into the plate, nodded, and said, “Eldest Sister, teach me embroidery. I really want to learn your skills.”

Shen Weici pressed her lips and smiled, then told Yue Deng to bring the embroidery frame.

Upon hearing that Shen Weici had agreed to go out, Yue Deng happily went to fetch it.

When the embroidery frame arrived, Shen Weici straightened her posture slightly and taught Shen Mingqiu the techniques without holding back, sharing everything with her.

Shen Mingqiu, after a pointer from Shen Weici, seemed to suddenly understand the trick and asked, “Eldest Sister, your embroidery is so good. Who did you learn from?”

Shen Weici smiled. “My mother was an embroidery mistress. She was better than me. I only learned a little from her.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici paused for a moment, suddenly remembering her mother’s appearance.

In the past, her mother hadn’t let her learn embroidery, instead making her study the six arts properly with a female teacher.

Her mother had said she was the daughter of a noble, and in the future, she would become a noble herself. She couldn’t be like her mother, who only knew embroidery.

Shen Weici now thought about it, and her eyes inexplicably welled up with tears.

She let out a soft sigh.

She had never thought about becoming any kind of noble.

Around noon, as Shen Mingqiu was leaving, Shen Weici stood up to see her off at the courtyard gate. As she turned back, she saw the bare, tall tree on the roof and suddenly her eyes reddened.

Behind the house in Yu Yang, there had also been a tree like this.

The residence in Yu Yang had encompassed her entire childhood, holding all her memories with her mother. Now, it no longer belonged to her.

Yue Deng saw Shen Weici standing at the courtyard gate, lost in thought, and couldn’t help but ask softly, “Miss, what’s wrong?”

Shen Weici lowered her eyes, and a tear fell into the dust at her feet. “I miss my mother.”

“I can’t have my mother’s Laba congee anymore.”

Yue Deng was stunned. When she came back to her senses, Shen Weici had already gone into the house.

She also looked up at the big tree behind the house, remembering the mornings of the Laba Festival in the past. She and the Miss would wait early by the stove for the steaming Laba congee, then chase after the mischievous cats that tried to steal the food. The small kitchen would be filled with lively chatter.

The local government in Yu Yang would also distribute congee on this day. One year, the Miss had even volunteered to help among the women, serving the congee. It had only been a few years, but she found that the Miss had become increasingly silent, as if she had never been happy since.

Indeed, how could she be happy? It was all troublesome matters.

She sighed and turned to go back inside.

In the late afternoon, as the sun was setting, Shen Mingqiu came rushing in with Shen Yueqiu, pulling Shen Weici along. “Eldest Brother and Fourth Brother are waiting at the front gate. Eldest Sister, hurry!”

Shen Weici hadn’t even finished tying her cloak, so she had to hold the strings and quietly ask, “Is Song Shi going?”

Shen Mingqiu smiled. “Second Brother Song definitely won’t go with us. Today, the streets are lively, and he has to arrange people to guard and patrol the various streets. Moreover, on such a day, he would certainly stay in the palace to accompany the Emperor.”

“Today, Princess Hui Min and the Eldest Master have also entered the palace. The Grand Princess has returned to the capital from her travel palace. How could Second Brother Song not be there?”

Shen Weici truly felt that Shen Mingqiu seemed to know a little about everything, even the matters of the main branch. Thinking that Shen Siwen was on duty in the palace, perhaps it was he who had told her.

But hearing that Song Zhang wouldn’t be there today, Shen Weici inexplicably felt relieved. Maybe she could really see Zhang Yuanheng.

She also had some things she wanted to say to him.
