They walked to the front gate, where three carriages were already waiting—one for the men, one for the women, and one for the maids.

Shen Siwen and Shen Kuai were waiting by the carriages. When they saw Shen Weici following Shen Mingqiu out, they couldn’t help but look at Shen Weici. Though she was dressed plainly, her beauty was like a hibiscus. Even in simple clothes, she looked stunning.

Moreover, Shen Weici had an excellent posture and a graceful, gentle demeanor. Even without makeup, her distant mountain-like eyebrows and the light in her eyes were as pure as a magnolia or a snow lotus, exuding a subtle fragrance that made people want to get closer.

Furthermore, the embroidered pouches this cousin had sent them before had very good meanings. They couldn’t help but feel a fondness for Shen Weici and wanted to take care of her. Shen Siwen even took the initiative to lift the carriage curtain for her.

Shen Weici lifted her skirt and got into the carriage. Seeing Shen Siwen holding the curtain for her, she softly said, “Thank you.”

Her voice was gentle, and for the first time, Shen Siwen felt the charm of this cousin.

Inside the carriage, Shen Zhaozhao was already seated, hugging her arms and giving Shen Weici a cold glance before snorting disdainfully.

Shen Weici then sat diagonally across from Shen Zhaozhao, trying to avoid looking at her.

As the carriage gradually moved forward, Shen Weici, hearing the lively noises outside, couldn’t help but lift the curtain slightly to look out. Last time she had wanted to look, but this time no one stopped her.

At this moment, the sky wasn’t completely dark yet, but the streets were already adorned with colorful lanterns. The five-colored lanterns illuminated the entire street. Everywhere was bustling with people, and there were various stalls and shops along the roadside. It was far more prosperous than Yu Yang.

Looking at the tall buildings, so high that she couldn’t see the end, the women’s clothing was all beautiful, and everyone looked wealthy. There were carriages and fine horses passing by continuously.

As she looked at the prosperous and lively scene before her and listened to the boiling crowd, for a moment, she felt as if all of this was unreal. She was truly here.

She was no longer in Yu Yang.

Shen Mingqiu, sitting behind Shen Weici, saw her lost in thought. The light seemed to flow across her face, and her sleeves hung gracefully. She was quiet, and no surprise or other emotions could be seen on her face. She was simply very calm.

She was so absorbed in her gaze that Shen Mingqiu couldn’t tell if she liked it or not.

She reached out and tugged at Shen Weici’s sleeve. “Are you in a daze?”

Shen Weici then smiled slightly and put down the curtain.

Shen Zhaozhao, who had been silent all this time, suddenly coldly snorted. “How unsophisticated. Is such a street worth staring at for so long?”

Shen Weici ignored her and asked Shen Mingqiu, “Where are we going now?”

Shen Mingqiu also ignored Shen Zhaozhao’s words and looked at Shen Weici with a smile. “We’ll first go to Ming Yue Tower for dinner, then go to Fa Ning Temple in the city to seek blessings and pray for a good marriage.”

“After that, we’ll go shopping at the stores, and then we’ll head back.”

Shen Weici’s heart skipped a beat when she heard Fa Ning Temple. That was exactly the place where Young Master Zhang had arranged to meet her.

As she spoke, Shen Mingqiu looked at Shen Weici. “Eldest Sister, how do you feel about this arrangement?”

Shen Weici smiled. “I think it’s excellent.”

chapters.title: She Can’t Stand It If I’m Doing Well
chapters.content:
Shen Zhaozhao spoke out of place again, her words dripping with sarcasm: “Only you would think of seeking a marriage match, such a self-deceptive thing.”

“Well, at least by seeking, one might marry into a good family. Otherwise, those noble families would never consider a concubine’s daughter first.”

Shen Mingqiu’s expression changed slightly, and she coldly scoffed: “We may not have Second Sister’s status as a legitimate daughter, but that doesn’t mean we are worse than you.”

Shen Zhaozhao’s face also changed upon hearing this, and she glared at Shen Mingqiu angrily: “You dare speak to me like this now?”

Shen Mingqiu sneered: “Being a concubine’s daughter doesn’t make me any shorter than you. You’re the one who keeps bringing up the distinction between legitimate and concubine-born. Are you afraid people won’t know you’re the precious legitimate daughter?”

Shen Mingqiu was no longer afraid of Shen Zhaozhao. In the past, there were only the two of them in the Marquis’s mansion, always seeing each other, so they maintained a facade of harmony. But now, with Shen Weici and Shen Yueqiu on her side, she had more support and courage.

Moreover, her marriage was none of the second branch’s business, and she didn’t plan to have any dealings with them in the future.

Shen Zhaozhao’s reputation was already tarnished outside, and Shen Mingqiu didn’t want to associate with her either. She wished she could spit on her.

The tension between the two escalated, and Shen Weici wanted to mediate, but before she could, Shen Zhaozhao had already lunged at Shen Mingqiu, and the two started fighting.

Shen Yueqiu, being the youngest, stood helplessly to the side, and Shen Weici shielded her while trying to pull the others apart.

Shen Weici was actually annoyed by Shen Zhaozhao’s temperament. It was likely because she had been pampered since childhood, being the only legitimate daughter in the Marquis’s mansion, doted on by the old madam, and engaged to her childhood sweetheart. She had always had smooth sailing and couldn’t tolerate the slightest discomfort.

Shen Weici’s arrival might have been the sand in her eyes.

Even though Shen Weici didn’t compete with her for anything.

Shen Weici tried to mediate but to no avail. Instead, seeing Shen Weici protecting Shen Yueqiu and trying to persuade Shen Mingqiu only infuriated Shen Zhaozhao more, making her feel excluded.

In the past, Shen Mingqiu and Shen Yueqiu had been like her little followers, always listening to her. But now, they were closer to Shen Weici.

Shen Zhaozhao was even angrier, and her hands became more forceful, messing up Shen Mingqiu’s hair accessories.

Fortunately, the carriage soon stopped in front of a restaurant. When Shen Siwen lifted the curtain, he noticed Shen Zhaozhao and Shen Mingqiu with disheveled hair, clearly having fought.

Shen Yueqiu, being only eleven, was scared and threw herself into Shen Siwen’s arms, crying: “Big Brother, Second Sister is so fierce, she even hit Third Sister and Fourth Sister.”

Shen Siwen held Shen Yueqiu as he got off the carriage, then frowned and glanced inside the carriage, his tone displeased: “If you don’t want to come out, go back. Don’t cause a commotion everywhere you go.”

With that, he let go of the curtain.

It was clear who this was directed at. Shen Weici’s hair accessories were intact, only her collar had been tugged by Shen Zhaozhao.

She adjusted her collar and said to Shen Mingqiu and Shen Zhaozhao: “Let me help Second Sister and Fourth Sister fix their hair.”

Shen Zhaozhao coldly scoffed: “Who needs your fake kindness now?”

She then lifted the carriage window curtain and called her maid in.

Shen Weici remained silent and helped Shen Mingqiu fix her hair accessories.

She knew that if she tried to mediate, Shen Zhaozhao would only get more upset at the sight of her. But she did it on purpose.

She knew that she was now a thorn in the sides of Shen Zhaozhao and Madame Wen, one that they had to remove. Now, she could only try to win over some other people in the Marquis’s mansion, making them annoyed with Shen Zhaozhao. This way, in the future, she would at least have people who could speak fairly for her, and she wouldn’t end up like last time with the double-land chess, where everyone had turned black into white and sided with Shen Zhaozhao.

Shen Weici knew all too well that the truth of many matters wasn’t as important as who believed it.

She carefully rearranged Shen Mingqiu’s hair and glanced at Shen Zhaozhao, still in a good temper: “We’ll wait for Second Sister outside.”

Shen Mingqiu directly pulled Shen Weici off the carriage: “Why talk to her? She’s a shrew.”

With that, she pulled Shen Weici off the carriage.

The word “shrew” made Shen Zhaozhao so angry she almost fainted. When had Shen Mingqiu ever dared to speak to her like this?

The anger and hatred in her eyes were almost burning.

After getting off the carriage, the maids handed them their veil hats. Through the white veil, Shen Weici looked up at the tall building before her, about five or six stories high, with colorful lanterns hanging on each floor. The glass lanterns at the bottom emitted a beautiful mist, exuding an air of wealth.

A gentle breeze lifted a corner of the white veil, revealing the fair skin underneath, as delicate as a lotus after the rain, a begonia after the shower. Her heart stirred, and she walked forward.

Shen Siwen walked up to Shen Weici and, seeing her looking up at the tall building, couldn’t help but smile: “There’s a moon-viewing platform upstairs. After dinner, we can go to the highest point and take a look.”

Before Shen Weici could respond, Shen Mingqiu beside her said: “There’s nothing special about the moon-viewing platform. I want to go to the Faning Temple early.”

Shen Weici looked at her and, rarely, joked: “You just want to seek a marriage match early, don’t you?”

Shen Mingqiu pretended to cover Shen Weici’s lips: “I’m going to pray for blessings. You mustn’t talk nonsense.”

Shen Kuo and Shen Yanli also walked over. Shen Kuo smiled at the scene: “It’s rare to hear Third Sister laugh.”

At this moment, Shen Zhaozhao got off the carriage. The first thing she saw was this scene: her once-doting cousin, and the two concubine-born sisters who used to fawn over her, now all gathered around Shen Weici, talking and laughing.

She clenched the handkerchief in her hand repeatedly, almost crushing it.

Shen Yanli saw Shen Zhaozhao come out but stand still by the carriage, so he called out to her: “Zhaozhao, come over, let’s go up together.”

Shen Zhaozhao’s face was unpleasant as she put on her veil hat and went to Shen Yanli’s side. Only then did the group enter the restaurant together.

Shen Zhaozhao pulled on Shen Yanli’s sleeve, walking at the back, and pouted: “In the future, Big Brother is not allowed to talk to Shen Weici anymore.”

Shen Yanli felt this was unreasonable. Moreover, he thought Shen Zhaozhao was being excessive. He lowered his voice to Shen Zhaozhao: “Third Sister usually gives in to you. When has she ever provoked you first?”

“She has such a good temper. Since she’s come to the Marquis’s mansion, she hasn’t competed with you for anything. Why can’t you tolerate her?”

Shen Zhaozhao gritted her teeth, her face under the veil slightly distorted: “I just can’t stand her. That day, she made me suffer such a great humiliation, and I was beaten by Father and punished by Grandmother. Don’t you feel wronged for me, Big Brother?”

Shen Yanli sighed: “Last time, why did things turn out that way? Wasn’t it because you were the one who provoked her first? Third Sister gave a purse to everyone, including you. You refused it and then spread those nonsense rumors. Of course, Father was angry.”

“I may want to side with you, but others might not. Our second branch already has a reputation for mistreating concubine-born daughters. Don’t cause more trouble. A family should live in harmony. In the future, we can still help and support each other.”

“Third Sister has both good looks and character. That Zhang Yuanheng is also promising. It will be good for our second branch in the future. Why can’t you see that?”

Shen Zhaozhao gritted her teeth and coldly scoffed: “If she’s doing well, I won’t be happy. I will definitely not let her have such a smooth life.”

Shen Yanli, through the white veil, vaguely saw Shen Zhaozhao’s distorted expression and frowned. He pulled Shen Zhaozhao to a corner of the stairs and lowered his voice: “Zhaozhao, don’t blame me for scolding you. You really went too far.”

“You should control your temper. Otherwise, you’ll cause more trouble in the future.”

“Third Sister is just a concubine-born daughter without a mother. In the future, her dowry will depend on our mother’s mood. What waves can she make? It’s really unnecessary for you to compete with her.”

Shen Zhaozhao pushed Shen Yanli’s hand away and glared at him: “I insist on competing with her. Father beat me twice because of her. Our reputations, Mother’s reputation, and Father’s official position have all become like this because of her.”

“Why shouldn’t I hate her? Don’t you hate her too, Big Brother?”

With that, Shen Zhaozhao pushed Shen Yanli’s hand away and strode upstairs.

Shen Yanli stood in place, watching Shen Zhaozhao’s back, and secretly sighed.

chapters.title: Encountering a Dandy
chapters.content:
Upon reaching the private room on the fourth floor, the fewer people there were as they ascended. On the fourth floor, as Shen Siwen mentioned, there were only eight private rooms in total, and one had to book a month in advance to secure a spot.

Shen Weici glanced around. The door panels and screens were all exquisitely crafted, and precious orchids were placed on high stands, subtly emitting a pleasant fragrance.

The private room was even more spacious, divided into several smaller rooms by screens. There were low tables, short stools, and arhat beds—everything one could need. One could even spend the night here if they wished.

Outside the four large, bright windows was a bustling street. Lanterns hung along the street stretched as far as the eye could see, like a long dragon.

The room was as warm as spring. Even with the cold wind blowing outside, one didn’t feel the slightest chill.

When the food was served, nearly twenty dishes were brought out, though there were only seven of them.

Shen Siwen had also invited pipa players to perform and servants to bring warm wine. Each person was poured a cup, filling the room with the aroma of wine.

Shen Weici looked at the small cup of warm wine in her hand, then at Shen Mingqiu beside her who had already drunk hers. She drank the wine in her cup as well.

The slight bitterness mixed with a hint of sweetness—she found it not as unpleasant as she had expected.

At this moment, the sound of fireworks suddenly came from outside. Shen Weici, kneeling by the window, heard the noise and turned her head to look. The sky was lit up with brilliant fireworks, one display after another, illuminating her eyes.

She had never seen such a prosperous scene before. This was the splendid capital that dazzled the eyes.

But as she watched the fireworks, someone from the building across the street was watching her.

The two sides of the long street were lined with tall buildings, not far apart. Shen Weici’s beauty had already caught the eyes of those looking over from the opposite side.

Shen Siwen noticed many pairs of eyes looking their way and realized just how striking Shen Weici’s face was. He ordered the servants to draw the curtains down.

At the table, they discussed recent interesting events in the capital. Shen Weici didn’t recognize the people they were talking about, so she remained silent.

Suddenly, Shen Kuo asked her: “Third Cousin, I heard you’re going to be engaged to Zhang Yuanheng from the Yiyong Earl’s mansion?”

Shen Weici paused, surprised that even the third branch knew about this.

She smiled, pressing her lips together: “It’s not settled yet. Fourth Cousin, don’t spread this outside.”

Shen Kuo laughed: “Of course not.”

“That Zhang Yuanheng—I’ve met him a few times. He’s a true gentleman. Third Cousin, if you marry him, you’ll have chosen the right person.”

Shen Weici didn’t want everyone to know about this, in case she needed to handle future changes.

She still smiled, her eyes curved: “It’s all arranged by Father and my stepmother.”

“I’ve only heard Father mention it. But it’s not official yet. Who knows if it will happen?”

Shen Zhaozhao suddenly let out a cold laugh. Everyone looked at her, unsure why she had laughed.

Shen Zhaozhao saw everyone looking at her and coldly said: “Why are you all looking at me? If it weren’t for my mother’s kindness, she wouldn’t have a chance at such a good marriage in this lifetime.”

Shen Yanli’s face darkened, and he tightly pinched Shen Zhaozhao’s wrist: “Have you caused enough trouble?”

Just as the atmosphere was tense, a servant’s voice came from outside, announcing that guests from the Yong’an Marquis’s mansion had come to pay their respects.

Shen Zhaozhao’s face lit up: “Brother Xu has come to see me.”

She then called out: “Let them in quickly.”

The door was pushed open, and two men entered with smiles. One was dressed in elegant white clothes, with a jade crown binding his hair—this was Xu Zhian.

Following him was a man in light green clothes, also handsome, but his demeanor was slightly more frivolous than Xu Zhian’s, with a hint of the reckless charm of a dandy noble. His eyes held a mischievous glint, but his face was fair, with red lips—a true pretty boy. This was Xu Qing, the second legitimate son of the Yong’an Marquis’s mansion.

Xu Zhian scanned the room and then bowed to everyone, very politely: “Originally, I had an appointment with Brother Yanli. We saw you from the opposite building just now, so we came early with my younger brother. We apologize for the intrusion.”

Shen Yanli quickly ordered the servants to bring two more cushions and greeted Xu Zhian: “Brother Zhian is too polite. Come, join us.”

Xu Zhian and Xu Qing laughed and took their seats.

However, Xu Qing’s gaze kept lingering on Shen Weici’s face. The brief glimpse earlier had stunned him, and he wished he could grow wings and fly to her side.

Now that he was closer, he could see her almond eyes, peach-like face, delicate neck, and elegant brows. He was once again mesmerized.

Shen Weici noticed the gaze and slightly lifted her eyelids to look back. She saw a bold, infatuated stare and couldn’t help but frown slightly before turning her head away.

Xu Zhian also noticed his younger brother’s gaze. Under the table, he pinched him, telling him to behave.

Although he knew Shen Weici was just a concubine-born daughter, she was still a member of the Marquis’s mansion, and appearances had to be maintained.

Xu Qing, pinched by his elder brother, came back to his senses and quickly picked up the wine pot to pour wine for everyone.

“Today is a rare coincidence. Let me treat everyone.”

Shen Siwen hurriedly declined: “There’s no need for that.”

Xu Qing inexplicably felt the need to show off in front of the beauty. No matter how much Shen Siwen refused, he insisted on treating them generously.

Shen Siwen couldn’t persuade him otherwise, so he let him have his way.

Shen Zhaozhao, seeing Xu Zhian, finally had a smile on her face. Although they weren’t sitting together, she shyly looked at Xu Zhian as he spoke, and Shen Yanli accompanied them, laughing along.

Xu Qing, however, stood up, took the wine pot, and walked to Shen Weici’s side, bending over: “Are you Sister Ci?”

“It’s our first meeting. You truly are a beauty.”

Such flirtatious words were not something ordinary people could say, but Xu Qing said them as naturally as breathing.

Shen Siwen saw Shen Weici lowering her head in silence and said to Xu Qing: “My third cousin is shy. Behave yourself and don’t scare her.”

Xu Qing was taken aback. Looking at Shen Weici’s enchanting eyes, her jade-like chin, and her graceful, charming appearance, he felt a rush of heat as he caught a whiff of her fragrance. His body leaned closer to Shen Weici as he poured her wine: “I apologize if my words earlier offended you, Sister.”

As he spoke, he poured himself a cup, his eyes fixed on her in a daze, and held the cup up to her, wanting to toast with Shen Weici.

Shen Weici hadn’t expected to encounter such a person. From the corner of her eye, she saw Xu Qing leaning toward her, his green sleeve hanging in front of her, his body emitting a powdery scent. He was a handsome young man on the surface, but inside, he was a lecherous dandy.

She looked at the cup of wine he had poured for her, picked it up with a smile, but didn’t speak. She covered her sleeve and drank.

That coy and shy demeanor drove Xu Qing wild. Even though Shen Weici hadn’t given him a single glance, he was so enchanted that he wished he could roll around by her side and get closer.

Those fair hands, those red lips—she was born to be admired and cherished by men. If he could keep such a person at home, it would be the ultimate pleasure.

His mind wandered through several fantasies. Restrained by the fact that Shen Weici was the Third Young Lady of the Marquis’s mansion, he didn’t dare to be too presumptuous. He returned to his seat, but his gaze kept drifting toward Shen Weici, his heart restless.

After dinner, Shen Zhaozhao pulled Xu Zhian to go see the river lanterns. Xu Zhian actually didn’t want to be seen in public with Shen Zhaozhao.

Recently, there had been many rumors about Shen Zhaozhao being domineering and willful. Even his close friends often teased him with these baseless rumors. Although he laughed along and defended Shen Zhaozhao, he had gradually grown annoyed with this fiancée who was affecting his reputation.

Now, with his future father-in-law demoted, and the main branch not intervening, it showed that they had given up on the second branch. Otherwise, with the connection to the Duke of Song’s mansion, they wouldn’t have been demoted.

His mother at home had also complained about this marriage. If it weren’t for the long-standing friendship between the two families and the childhood engagement, as well as the consideration for reputation, his mother would have likely called off the engagement.

These days, Xu Zhian had considered calling off the engagement several times. He knew he couldn’t be with just one woman, and he already had two concubines he liked and planned to elevate. If Shen Zhaozhao married into his family and caused a scene out of jealousy, it would be a headache.

Looking at Shen Zhaozhao’s dependent expression, he felt a hint of affection. They had grown up together, and their families frequently interacted. He did have some feelings for Shen Zhaozhao, but he just didn’t like her temperament.

He forced himself to go along with her and called Xu Qing to join Shen Yanli.

Xu Qing, however, had already grouped up with Shen Kuo and said: “I won’t go. I was having a good chat with Brother Kuo. I’ll go with them.”

Xu Zhian didn’t understand his younger brother’s intentions. He glanced at Shen Weici, who was talking with Shen Mingqiu, standing there gracefully, her every smile and frown as charming as a spring breeze.

He withdrew his gaze and looked at Xu Qing, his voice carrying a warning: “Don’t do anything foolish.”

Xu Qing nodded repeatedly and urged his elder brother to leave quickly.

Shen Weici saw that Xu Qing hadn’t left with them, and her eyebrows slightly furrowed. She stood by Shen Mingqiu’s side, her back to Xu Qing.

The group then headed to Faning Temple.

Inside the carriage, Shen Weici felt a hint of unease.

Last time, Zhang Yuanheng had written to her, but she hadn’t replied. She didn’t know if he was still waiting for her.

Upon arriving at Ning’an Temple, the place was bustling with people, and the lanterns lit up the area like daylight.

They climbed a set of stairs, obtained incense, and went inside the temple to pray. Then, they each took a bowl to receive the blessed longevity porridge distributed by the abbot.

The line was long, and as Shen Weici looked to the side, she saw a familiar figure standing under a tree on another set of stairs. Upon closer inspection, it was Zhang Yuanheng.

chapters.title: Meeting Zhang Yuanheng at Faning Temple
chapters.content:
Shen Weici’s heart stirred as she looked at the solitary figure, unwilling to break their promise.

The queue ahead was long, and it would take a while before their turn. When she came back to her senses and tried to look toward Zhang Yuanheng, she saw a green-clad figure step in front of her—it was Xu Qing, his eyes brimming with a playful smile.

Shen Weici wore a *weimao* hat, and upon seeing Xu Qing approach, she instinctively took a step back, unable to hide the annoyance in her eyes.

Yet Xu Qing asked, “What is Sister Ci looking at? Perhaps the evil-repelling sachets over there? I can buy one for you.”

“Especially since Sister Ci has just recovered from a serious illness—it would be useful.”

Those sachets were made from a mix of incense ash from devotees and cinnabar, commonly found in temples. They were often worn by children under three or placed by the beds of the sick to ward off illness.

Shen Weici shook her head. “Thank you for your concern, Second Young Master Xu, but I have no need for it. I was just looking around.”

Her voice was polite and gentle, and Xu Qing’s heart softened at the sound. He wanted to move closer.

Shen Mingqiu, however, had long noticed Xu Qing’s deliberate attempts to ingratiate himself. Ever since they had sat down earlier, Xu Qing’s eyes had barely left Shen Weici. A knowing smile tugged at the corners of her lips as she watched them.

Just then, another calm voice spoke: “Second Young Master Xu.”

Xu Qing turned in confusion, only to find Zhang Yuanheng standing there. He blinked in surprise. “And you are?”

Zhang Yuanheng knew Xu Zhian, so he naturally recognized Xu Qing. However, the two had no real connection beyond a passing acquaintance.

Seeing Xu Qing’s confusion, Zhang Yuanheng smiled. “Zhang of the Yiyong Marquis’s residence. Currently serving as a *Qiju Sheren* in the Gate of Command.”

Xu Qing suddenly realized and quickly cupped his hands in greeting. “My apologies for not recognizing you, Lord Zhang. Please forgive my oversight.”

Zhang Yuanheng chuckled. “No need to stand on ceremony.”

Shen Siwen and Shen Kuai, who were ahead in the queue, turned at the sound of voices. Upon seeing Zhang Yuanheng, they also exchanged greetings with him.

Zhang Yuanheng smiled and exchanged a few pleasantries with them before his gaze shifted past Xu Qing to Shen Weici. He smiled again. “Miss Shen San.”

Shen Weici had not expected Zhang Yuanheng to notice her, let alone approach her. She lifted the white veil before her face and looked at him, her eyes brimming with a smile. “Young Master Zhang.”

As her gaze swept over him, a fleeting yet unspoken affection passed between them in that brief exchange. Zhang Yuanheng’s breath caught in his throat.

Before he could take another look, the white veil fell back into place, obscuring her face. The tantalizing glimpse left him aching to see her fully.

Xu Qing’s eyes darted between the two. The way Shen Weici had lifted her veil for Zhang Yuanheng, revealing her face for a moment—he was no stranger to the ways of romance. How could he not understand the meaning behind that gesture?

A surge of frustration welled up within him.

The woman he fancied had eyes only for a dull, bookish scholar, while he, Xu Qing, was treated as nothing more than dust between them. Was his status as the son of the Yong’an Marquis not superior to that of a mere marquis’s son? His father was a fifth-rank capital official, his sister a concubine in the palace, and though his uncle was not currently in the capital, he was the *Sima* of Zhongzhou. Yet here he was, reduced to nothing in their eyes.

With that, he took his leave.

Zhang Yuanheng looked at the face hidden behind the thin veil, then turned to Shen Siwen and cupped his hands. “May I ask Miss Shen San for a private word?”

With Shen Yanli absent, Shen Siwen, as the eldest son of the marquis’s third branch, naturally served as Shen Weici’s elder brother in public. Zhang Yuanheng’s request was not out of line.

Shen Siwen knew the two families were currently discussing marriage. He smiled—how could he refuse? Zhang Yuanheng was always courteous, considerate of a lady’s reputation, and upright. With so many people from the marquis’s household present, there was no harm in it.

He said with a smile, “As long as my third cousin agrees, it’s fine.”

Zhang Yuanheng then turned his gaze to Shen Weici.

Shen Weici looked around, her heart fluttering with unease. She knew that if Zhang Yuanheng were to find out she had been meeting him these past days, Song Zhang would surely cause trouble for her. She shouldn’t have come.

But then she saw the way Zhang Yuanheng looked at her, and knowing that Song Zhang was likely still in the palace, she reasoned that a brief private conversation would do no harm. So she nodded in agreement.

The two walked one after the other toward the *Yinyuan* tree, its branches laden with red silk ribbons. When they reached the stone railing, Zhang Yuanheng’s first words were, “Miss Shen San, why have you not replied to my letters?”

“Or do you feel that I have not taken good enough care of you since we last met?”

His voice carried a hint of dejection, as if he had suffered from longing for a long time. Shen Weici was moved.

A gentle night breeze rustled past, lifting the white veil on Shen Weici’s *weimao* hat and stirring the hem of her skirt. The brocade fabric of her white dress, adorned with sparrow patterns, swayed slightly, accentuating her slender waist. She stood gracefully, her figure swaying like a willow in the cold wind, exuding an almost ethereal charm.

Passersby couldn’t help but glance at her. Even though her *weimao* obscured her features, her delicate, wind-swayed posture—slender and graceful—allowed one to imagine the breathtaking beauty hidden beneath the veil.

The wind was stronger here on the elevated ground. Shen Weici gathered the white veil with her hands to keep it from billowing, then listened to Zhang Yuanheng’s slightly uneasy voice. She smiled. “You overthink, Young Master Zhang. It’s just that I am not in a position to reply to your letters now. After all, our marriage is being discussed, and it would be improper for us to exchange private letters.”

Zhang Yuanheng felt a slight relief at her words.

Then he heard Shen Weici’s soft voice: “When I returned from your place last time, did your mother find anything unsatisfactory about me?”

Zhang Yuanheng’s throat tightened at her question. He hesitated, struggling to find the words.

After a long silence, he finally managed to say, hoarsely, “My mother has a very good impression of you.”

Shen Weici detected the hesitation in his voice and noticed how he avoided her gaze. She said, “Young Master Zhang, just tell me the truth. No matter what it is, I can handle it.”

Zhang Yuanheng paused, then looked at her. He stood there in silence for a long time, but the words he wanted to say still wouldn’t come out.

He shook his head. “I’m not hiding anything. My mother also hopes you will join our family soon.”

As he spoke, Zhang Yuanheng lowered his eyes. “My mother should come to propose marriage the day after tomorrow.”

He paused again, his voice rough with emotion. “Weici, trust me. I will not wrong you. You are the one I have chosen to spend my life with.”

“I will only have you by my side.”

This was the first time Zhang Yuanheng had called her by her given name.

His voice was very soft, carrying an indescribable emotion.

Shen Weici couldn’t decipher what that emotion was.

She looked at Zhang Yuanheng with slight surprise. Even with his solemn vows, she couldn’t find peace in her heart.

She looked at him and whispered, “Young Master Zhang, I am not an unreasonable woman. If you have any difficulties or secrets you find hard to speak of, just tell me. We can think of a solution together. I won’t make things difficult for you.”

Zhang Yuanheng heard her words and froze. The words in his throat almost spilled out.

He remained silent for a long time before shaking his head. “I have no secrets. I just want to marry Miss Shen San, that’s all.”

Shen Weici listened, then studied Zhang Yuanheng carefully before nodding. “Then I will wait for you.”

Zhang Yuanheng was lost in thought again at her words, “I will wait for you.”

Suddenly, he remembered something and called his attendant over. Taking an item from the attendant, he presented it to Shen Weici. “This is what Miss Shen San returned to me last time. Take it back.”

Shen Weici looked at the item, hesitated for a moment, then took it. “Last time, I thought you were in a difficult position, so I had my maid return it. Now that I understand your intentions, I will keep it safe.”

With that, she handed the item to Yue Deng, who stood behind her, then smiled at Zhang Yuanheng. “These days, Young Master Zhang, you mustn’t send me any more letters. I am fine in the marquis’s residence. Once our marriage is settled, you can write to me again, and it will be proper.”

Until the marriage was settled, exchanging private letters could be misconstrued by others and affect her reputation.

Zhang Yuanheng quickly bowed to Shen Weici. “Miss Shen San, it was thoughtless of me. I apologize.”

Shen Weici couldn’t help but laugh when she saw Zhang Yuanheng bowing in apology. She reached out and tugged at his sleeve. “Young Master Zhang, why apologize for such a small matter?”

“If in the future you truly do something that wrongs me, what then—”

chapters.title: What About Her?
chapters.content:
Zhang Yuanheng was taken aback. The gentle touch on his sleeve had vanished in an instant. He murmured, “In the future, if I ever wrong Miss Shen San, I will kneel before you and apologize, and accept whatever punishment you deem fit.”

Shen Weici smiled. “I believe you, Young Master Zhang.”

Zhang Yuanheng felt as if something were stuck in his throat and couldn’t speak for a long time.

Just then, a close maidservant of Shen Mingqiu approached. “Miss San, our young lady has sent me to fetch you. It will be our turn soon.”

Shen Weici looked at Zhang Yuanheng. “What are your plans, Young Master Zhang?”

Zhang Yuanheng looked at Shen Weici, wanting to invite her to stroll through the temple fair. But recalling her earlier words, he felt it might not be appropriate for them to be alone together right now. Even a private conversation seemed improper. He hesitated and gave up on the idea.

Yet his gaze lingered on Shen Weici. Even though he couldn’t see her face clearly, he could sense her gentle smile and the faint, almost imperceptible fragrance that clung to her. It made him reluctant to leave.

They had finally managed to meet after such a long time. Unable to bear the longing, he had written letters, but received no replies. Now, they could only share this fleeting moment together.

The crowd bustled around them, and many of the words he longed to say were restrained, difficult to utter.

Those intimate whispers had often filled his heart with warmth whenever he thought of them. The idea that she would one day be his wife, lying by his side, and he could finally say those words to her filled him with joy.

He hesitated for a moment, then looked at Shen Weici. “Miss Shen San, will you be touring the temple later? I could accompany you.”

Shen Weici smiled. “Alright.”

With that, she turned and walked toward Shen Mingqiu.

Inside the temple, people came and went. Shen Weici followed the crowd to receive alms of congee and then to draw a fortune slip.

Shen Mingqiu and Shen Yueqiu both drew the best possible fortune, *Shang Shang*, while Shen Weici ended up with the worst, *Xia Xia*.

The white-bearded abbot looked at Shen Weici, who stood holding the slip in surprise, and smiled. “When the water meets the mountain, you must cross it yourself.”

Shen Weici realized the meaning behind the abbot’s words and devoutly bowed in respect.

Whether it was the best fortune or the worst, it made no difference to Shen Weici. She had never placed her entire fate in the hands of destiny.

Shen Mingqiu comforted her, “Elder Sister San, why not draw another one?”

Shen Weici smiled and shook her head. “I don’t take it seriously.”

The group chatted and laughed as they left. Zhang Yuanheng stood not far away. From the moment Shen Weici had drawn the *Xia Xia* slip, his posture had slumped slightly, and he seemed a bit lost.

Shen Weici turned her gaze to Zhang Yuanheng, who was slightly distracted and hadn’t followed. She had thought he was concerned about the slip and wanted to comfort him. But then he suddenly walked up to her and lowered his head. “Miss Shen San, someone from my family just came with a message. There’s something I need to attend to at home.”

Shen Weici looked deeply at Zhang Yuanheng. She didn’t ask further, only hiding her disappointment as she nodded. “If there’s something at home, Young Master Zhang, you should return as soon as possible. But be careful on the way. It’s crowded today, so don’t rush.”

Zhang Yuanheng looked up at Shen Weici. Beneath her white veil, her face was as fair as jade, exuding a gentle yet resilient strength. She was unlike ordinary women in many ways. He truly wanted to marry her.

He nodded, hiding the guilt in his eyes, then turned and left.

The winter sun on the Laba Festival was already cold. It was said that in the capital, after Laba, it would snow within a few days.

Shen Weici watched Zhang Yuanheng’s retreating figure, suddenly unsure if she had misjudged him.

Shen Mingqiu also looked at Zhang Yuanheng’s back. “I’ve long heard that Second Young Master Zhang is handsome and talented, and at such a young age, he has already gained the Emperor’s favor. In a few years, he is bound to rise further. Elder Sister San, this marriage is indeed a good choice.”

Shen Weici turned her head and smiled at Shen Mingqiu. “You will have your own ideal husband waiting for you.”

As they spoke, the wind grew stronger, stirring the temple bells to chime softly. Shen Weici looked up at the sky. In the dark night, fireworks suddenly lit up, illuminating the sky for a moment.

Then, the evening breeze scattered a strand of her hair.

Meanwhile, inside the Mingde Hall of the imperial palace, a palace banquet was underway.

The Emperor sat at the highest seat, with the Grand Princess and the Empress sitting together, chatting and laughing.

Below them, the Wise and Sensitive Princess sat with Shen Dalaoye. Further down were the old madam and the second master of the Song Guogong’s residence, along with several of the Emperor’s favored officials.

Opposite them sat four princes and the Emperor’s favored princesses.

Song Zhang sat next to the Wise and Sensitive Princess, alone at a table. He glanced at the dancing girls in the hall, then listened to the flattery and toasts from the nearby officials. Feeling bored, he lowered his head.

A palace maid knelt beside him, offering a full cup of wine. He didn’t even lift a finger, simply lowering his head to drink it all.

The Wise and Sensitive Princess looked at Song Zhang. “Did the Emperor bestow a Loulan Princess upon you?”

Song Zhang gave a faint “mm” in response, then lowered his head to drink from another cup offered by the palace maid.

The Wise and Sensitive Princess frowned. “Yesterday afternoon, when I returned, that concubine came to my place to kowtow and pay her respects. She seemed aggrieved. When I asked, she said you hadn’t even touched her.”

Her expression turned serious. “Song Zhang, I told you long ago that the legitimate line of the Song Guogong’s family depends on you for descendants. Your grandfather writes in every letter about the need for an heir. How long will you continue to be so willful?”

She leaned closer to Song Zhang and whispered sternly, “Usually, I can’t even find you. Today, you must tell me the truth. There are rumors outside that you’re injured. Is it true?”

“If it is, I can arrange for someone to treat you. This matter cannot be delayed.”

As for the matter of heirs, ever since Song Zhang had returned to the capital, his ears had nearly calloused from hearing about it.

He was already tired of it.

He glanced at his mother, his cold, dark eyes devoid of warmth. “What kind of woman is worthy of bearing my child?”

The Wise and Sensitive Princess was taken aback. She looked at him. “This afternoon, while I was chatting with your great-grandmother, we talked about your marriage. What do you think of the Fifth Princess?”

At that moment, the Fifth Princess, Zhao Rou, looked over. Song Zhang didn’t even glance in her direction, coldly refusing. “I don’t think much of it.”

The Wise and Sensitive Princess was left speechless.

Her son had spent his childhood in the palace under his great-grandmother’s care. As he grew older, he had followed his uncle and grandfather, and had only lived with her for two or three years.

Last spring, when he returned to the capital, he often stayed at the Guogong’s residence or his private estate, rarely visiting the marquis’s residence.

Mother and son were, in truth, estranged. Sometimes, when they sat together, they didn’t even know what to say.

The Wise and Sensitive Princess felt that, as his mother, she should take the initiative in arranging his marriage. But every time she brought it up, the distance between them seemed to grow.

However, Song Zhang was already nearly twenty-three. If he didn’t marry soon, it would truly be inexcusable.

She restrained her temper and asked, “Then who do you like? Tell me. No matter which noble lady in the capital it is, I will arrange it for you.”

But Song Zhang simply remained silent.

The Wise and Sensitive Princess had no choice but to say directly, “Do you think you can keep delaying? After the New Year, if the Emperor bestows a marriage upon you, and you don’t like the Fifth Princess, you won’t have a choice.”

Song Zhang’s gaze was indifferent. “Mother, there’s no need for you to worry.”

This conversation was going nowhere. Shen Dalaoye, sitting next to the Wise and Sensitive Princess, saw her frustrated expression and sighed. He put an arm around her shoulders. “Song Zhang has his own ideas now. You should worry less.”

The Wise and Sensitive Princess sighed along with him but ultimately said nothing more.

At the top of the hall, the Emperor was frequently toasted by those below. The banquet was in full swing. Suddenly, Ming He approached Song Zhang from behind and whispered something.

Song Zhang glanced at Li Rongshan across from him, hesitated for a moment, then pushed away the next cup of wine offered to him and stood up, following Ming He out.

Li Zhaoyi watched Song Zhang’s retreating figure, then lowered his head again.

Outside the hall, Song Zhang stood in a corner, his dark clothes blending into the shadows. The guarding attendants instinctively stepped back five paces and turned away.

Ming He approached Song Zhang and whispered, “We’ve found the money lender behind the *fang yanggaoli* scheme. It’s a distant relative of the Censor-in-Chief’s wife. He came to the capital three years ago and specializes in this trade. If someone can’t repay, he forces young girls into prostitution to work off the debt. This operation has spread to An and Shao, even as far as Qing and Yun.”

“He has many underlings and is very careful. The temples he uses change frequently. It took this long just to uncover this much.”

Ming He looked at Song Zhang and whispered, “The Censor-in-Chief, Chen Zhong, is a man of the Second Prince. For this to have gone on so long without any trouble, someone must be protecting him from behind the scenes. Could it be—”

Song Zhang raised an eyebrow and glanced at Ming He. “*Fang yanggaoli* is a serious crime. Chen Zhong knows this better than anyone. There’s something suspicious here.”

After a moment’s thought, he said, “Send someone to that distant relative’s hometown and investigate thoroughly. This person appeared too suddenly. It’s as if he deliberately wanted me to find him.”

Ming He acknowledged with an “ei” and was about to leave when Song Zhang pulled him back. “And her—”

chapters.title: Returning to Encounter Song Zhang
chapters.content:
Ming He’s mind went blank as he suddenly realized who Song Zhang was referring to.

He hurriedly stepped forward and whispered, “Today, the third young lady Shen went out of the residence and has been with the fourth and fifth young ladies of the Hou residence. First, they went to a restaurant where they met the eldest and second young masters of the Yong’an Hou residence. Later, they went to the Fa Ning Temple, where they encountered...”

Ming He hesitated for a moment but still hardened his head and told Song Zhang, “At Fa Ning Temple, they met Zhang Yuanheng. He went over to talk to the third young lady Shen.”

As he spoke, he watched Song Zhang’s face gradually darken, hesitated again, and said, “Later, the third young lady Shen and Zhang Yuanheng talked alone for a while...”

“But they didn’t talk for long. Later, Zhang Yuanheng left first for some reason.”

“However, Xu Er of the Yong’an Hou residence kept pestering the third young lady Shen. I saw that the third young lady Shen didn’t want to pay attention to him.”

“But that Xu Qing was very attentive, constantly buying things for the third young lady Shen. But since we were far away, we didn’t know if the third young lady Shen accepted them.”

“Later, I received a message from my subordinates, so I came to the palace to find the general. The third young lady Shen’s side was being watched by Xiao Feng, so she should be shopping around now.”

Song Zhang’s face slightly darkened. After listening to Ming He, he glanced at him sideways and said, “What about the letter you were supposed to intercept?”

Ming He quickly replied, “These days, there have been no letters exchanged. A few days ago, Zhang Yuanheng came by. My men saw Laifu going to Lin Chun Yuan. They beat him up, but he stubbornly insisted it was just a verbal message, no letter. I saw that if we beat him any more, he might not have the breath to speak, so I let him go.”

Song Zhang’s phoenix-like eyes darkened. He turned and went back to the main hall.

At night, the carriage slowly stopped at the gate of the Jian’an Earl’s residence. Shen Weici followed Shen Mingqiu out of the carriage. Xu Qing eagerly ran over and took the items from Yue Deng’s hands, saying, “I’ll take them in for the third young lady Shen.”

Yue Deng felt her hands empty and looked up to see Xu Er had already taken her task.

Looking at Xu Qing bending over to approach the young lady, she felt helpless.

He was a handsome young master with red lips and white teeth, yet he acted so inappropriately, slightly dissolute.

Shen Weici also felt helpless. She reached out to take the items from Xu Qing’s hands, saying, “These things are not heavy. I can carry them myself.”

But Xu Qing dodged, saying, “It’s just a small effort. It’s worth it to carry things for the third young lady Shen.”

Shen Weici’s face showed helplessness. Just as she was about to speak, she heard Shen Li’s surprised voice, “Brother Song Er, why are you here?”

She was slightly startled and looked up to see Song Zhang standing on the steps of the gate. Dressed in black, blending with the dark night, with a large golden embroidered flower on his chest, and a jade crown holding his hair, his long eyebrows extended to his temples. His cold and noble eyes were half-hidden in the quiet night, exuding an unfathomable chill.

His phoenix-like eyes met hers, staring at her with a dark expression. Even though they were some distance apart, she could clearly see the sarcasm in his eyes.

Shen Weici’s heart skipped a beat. She saw Shen Li and Shen Siwen approaching Song Zhang to talk. Shen Mingqiu smiled at her and said, “Since Young Master Xu Er has this intention, Third Sister should let him carry it.”

Shen Weici glanced at Xu Qing, who was approaching her. She thought that if she let him carry it, it would be fine. Continuing to entangle would only cause more trouble. Once inside the residence, he wouldn’t pester her anymore.

She clasped her hands and slightly tilted her head, looking at Xu Qing, saying, “Then I’ll trouble Young Master Xu Er.”

After saying that, she withdrew her gaze and walked towards the steps of the front gate.

Xu Qing happily carried the items, following behind Shen Weici. Looking at her enchanting expression, he secretly sighed, understanding what “hibiscus in autumn water” meant.

His gaze was fixed on Shen Weici’s partially visible profile, greedily wanting to look a bit more. But as he followed her up two steps, his shoulder suddenly hurt. When he looked up, he saw Song Zhang lifting his leg and pressing his foot on his shoulder, preventing him from moving forward.

Humiliated in front of so many people by Song Zhang’s disrespectful action, Xu Qing’s face turned red. He looked up at Song Zhang and cursed, “Song Zhang, you’re going too far!”

The two had a feud, and if Xu Qing were not outmatched by Song Zhang’s skills, he would have probably pounced on him.

Shen Siwen, standing nearby, looked at this scene with slight surprise. Xu Qing hadn’t done anything, so why did it seem like he had provoked Song Zhang?

Shen Mingqiu and Shen Yueqiu, who had already entered the front gate, heard the noise and turned around. They saw Song Zhang pressing his foot on Xu Qing’s shoulder, pushing him back a step. They couldn’t help but look surprised.

Shen Weici, her face slightly pale, watched the scene. She looked at Song Zhang’s profile, seeing his cold expression, towering above, hand on his sword, showing no emotion, but inexplicably feeling that he was in a very bad mood.

Then she heard his cold and arrogant voice, “Bullying others? Is the Hou residence a place you can come to?”

“If I see you again at the Hou residence, I will have someone break one of your legs.”

Xu Qing, having made a huge fool of himself in front of Shen Weici and being humiliated like this, was furious. He cursed, “Song Zhang, aren’t you just trusted by the emperor? What are you so proud of?”

“I didn’t provoke you today. How dare you humiliate me like this? Do you believe I will report this to my sister, and have her report you to the emperor?”

“Moreover, why can’t I come to the Hou residence? You are from the Song Guo Gong residence. What does the Hou residence have to do with you?”

Shen Siwen also felt that Song Zhang was being excessive. He said in a low voice, “Xu Qing didn’t do anything on the way. He even sent her back and helped the third cousin carry things. Isn’t there some misunderstanding?”

Song Zhang ignored Shen Siwen, gave a cold laugh, took the items from Xu Qing’s arms, and then kicked him down, saying, “You just remember what I said today.”

“I’m not joking with you.”

After saying that, he turned and left without paying any more attention to Xu Qing, who was rolling on the ground in pain.

Shen Weici watched the scene in a daze. Seeing Xu Qing groaning in pain on the ground, although Xu Qing was flirtatious and pestered her, he hadn’t done anything too out of line, let alone touched her. He was just being attentive and quick. Now, he looked somewhat pitiful.

She saw his servants quickly going to help him, and Shen Siwen also walked over to talk to him. She then turned her head to look at Song Zhang, who had already disappeared into the night. She suddenly remembered that her items were still in his hands.

Her heart stiffened, and she quickly ordered Yue Deng to chase after Song Zhang and retrieve her items.

Yue Deng acknowledged and hurried into the night.

Shen Mingqiu looked at Shen Weici and asked, “What’s wrong with Brother Song Er today? Did Young Master Xu Er provoke him?”

Shen Weici shook her head and glanced at Xu Qing, who was being helped into the carriage by his servants, limping. She said to Shen Mingqiu, “It’s already night. Fourth younger sister should go back first.”

Shen Mingqiu nodded. It was indeed dark, so she pulled Shen Weici along with her.

After walking a short distance, Shen Siwen called out to her from behind, “Third cousin, wait a moment.”

Shen Weici stopped and turned to see Shen Siwen walking towards her. She waited in place.

Shen Siwen walked over to Shen Weici and looked down at her face, which was lowered in the night wind. It was gentle, fair, and as beautiful as spring water.

After shopping for a long time today, a few strands of her hair had come loose. The cold wind blew past, turning her nose and cheeks slightly red, and her eyes sparkled, enchanting like a celestial beauty.

No wonder Xu Qing was so attentive. Even he was surprised by her beauty.

He said in a low voice, “Xu Qing is usually a lecherous man. He keeps many beautiful concubines in his residence. You should stay away from him in the future to avoid being harassed.”

“But after all, he is the younger brother of Xu Shizi, and the younger brother-in-law of your second sister. I can’t say it openly, but you should be careful.”

These seemingly concerned words made Shen Weici pause. She thought that when she first entered the Hou residence, many people didn’t treat her well. Now that someone was considering her, it was a good thing.

In fact, she didn’t have a good impression of Xu Qing either. As a spoiled young master from a noble family, she didn’t consider him at all.

She nodded, her eyes filled with a smile, “Thank you, Elder Cousin, for the reminder. I will be careful and avoid him in the future.”

Shen Siwen nodded and then said in a low voice, “Last time, you made a sachet for my mother. She used it and slept very well. In a few more days, it will be my grandmother’s birthday. Could you make another one for me? My grandmother is old and has trouble falling asleep. Maybe it will help.”

Shen Weici was naturally willing to do such a favor to win people’s hearts.

She looked up at Shen Siwen and smiled, “It’s just a small effort. Since Elder Cousin needs it, I will make another one. It won’t take much time.”

Shen Siwen smiled, “Then I’ll trouble you.”

Shen Weici smiled, “Elder Cousin is too polite.”

After a few words, Shen Siwen looked at the night and saw that Shen Weici’s maid was not by her side. After asking, he learned that she had gone to chase after Song Zhang. He said, “It’s dark now. I’ll walk you back.”

Shen Weici saw that Shen Siwen had two attendants following him, each holding a lantern. Since they were cousins from the same residence, she agreed.

chapters.title: Do You Want to Seduce Every Man?
chapters.content:
The two did not speak along the way. Shen Siwen walked ahead, and Shen Weici followed behind him.

They walked all the way to the gate of Lin Chun Yuan before Shen Siwen stopped. He said to Shen Weici, “You go in. I’ll head back first.”

Shen Weici nodded and said, “Elder Cousin, take your time on the way back.”

Shen Siwen paused and turned his head to look at Shen Weici again. He smiled and said, “Alright.”

Shen Weici stood in place, watching Shen Siwen leave before walking towards the gate of the courtyard. She had only taken two steps when she stopped. She saw Song Zhang standing by the window of her inner room, looking at her. Behind him was the dim candlelight. His eyes were cold, and his posture was tall and straight.

Yue Deng came out to greet Shen Weici, her face somewhat panicked, but she didn’t dare to speak.

Shen Weici silently lowered her eyelids, then gave Yue Deng a reassuring look and walked into the room.

She had Yue Deng wait outside the curtain and ordered the other two maids to go and heat some water. She lifted the curtain and went inside.

The window had already been closed by him. As she entered, she saw him sitting on the small chair she usually sat on. His tall and broad body filled the chair completely.

She also saw his hands lazily resting on the armrests of the chair. The dark brocade robe draped down, and the white jade pendant at his waist swayed in the air.

His gaze had been on Shen Weici since she entered. With a cold and noble expression, he looked her up and down, from her temples to her slender waist. A faint, mocking smile played on his lips.

Shen Weici endured Song Zhang’s scrutiny. Her peripheral vision swept over the items on the table, which were still intact. She slightly relaxed and then looked at Song Zhang, “Thank you, Young Master Song, for bringing the items. But it’s late now, so Young Master Song should leave soon.”

Song Zhang had come at night, and the maids had seen him. She couldn’t guarantee that someone from Shen Zhao Zhao’s side hadn’t seen him either. If rumors spread, it would indeed be hard to explain.

Her gaze fell on the tightly closed window. She wanted to go over and open it. If they were to talk openly in the room, others couldn’t say much.

As she walked over to open the carved window, she passed by Song Zhang, but her wrist was tightly grabbed by him. Shen Weici struggled but couldn’t break free. She looked down at Song Zhang, her eyebrows furrowing, “What does Young Master Song want to do?”

Song Zhang’s gaze was on Shen Weici’s face. He recalled how Shen Siwen had walked her back just now, and how they had stood at the gate of the courtyard talking.

Her eyes and eyebrows were filled with smiles, her hair fluttering, her flushed face enchanting and delicate, attracting Shen Siwen to look at her more.

At this moment, under the dim candlelight, the blush on her cheeks from the cold wind was still there. Her delicate and enchanting face seemed even more gentle in the candlelight. He had been holding back his anger until now, resenting how she could always attract men wherever she went.

The fingers gripping her wrist tightened. He looked at her coldly, “How long have you been at the Hou residence? You can’t even let the people from the third branch alone?”

Shen Weici’s eyes widened as she suddenly understood Song Zhang’s implication. She looked at him, “How can Young Master Song say such things? Elder Cousin just happened to walk me back. How can you think of it in such a vulgar way?”

Song Zhang was just unhappy that Shen Weici had smiled at Shen Siwen. He knew that there couldn’t be anything between them. Not to mention their cousin relationship, Shen Siwen was supposed to get married two years ago, but it was delayed because his fiancée had fallen ill two years prior.

He knew that Shen Siwen was deeply in love with his fiancée. He was just unhappy that Shen Weici stood with any man.

His words were just anger he had been holding back, intending to mock her. Seeing her pale face now, he coldly laughed, “What about Xu Er? He kept surrounding you, eagerly buying things for you. Don’t tell me you also have the idea of marrying into the Yong’an Hou residence?”

“I really underestimated your skills. Do you want to seduce every man you meet?”

Shen Weici didn’t understand why Song Zhang always wouldn’t let her go, and why he always accused her of these baseless crimes. She was too tired to explain.

She just wanted Song Zhang to leave her alone and stop keeping his eyes on her.

She looked at Song Zhang wearily, “Since I am such a person in Young Master Song’s heart, why does Young Master Song always come to ask me?”

“I am just an insignificant illegitimate daughter in the Hou residence. I cannot deserve Young Master Song’s attention.”

“Moreover, the Hou residence is not a place I can enter just because I want to. Young Master Song can rest assured. I have no intention of marrying into the Yong’an Hou residence.”

Song Zhang stood up after hearing Shen Weici’s words. He looked down at her and pointed at the items on the table with a sneer, “Oh? Who bought the things on the table for you? Wasn’t it Xu Er?”

“You keep saying you have no intention of marrying into the Hou residence, but what have you been doing? Letting Xu Er pester you and even having him carry things for you.”

“What’s wrong? Do you think the Earl’s residence is not as good as the Hou residence?”

Shen Weici was so angry that she trembled at Song Zhang’s nonsensical words. She didn’t understand why he always misunderstood her.

Was it that because her birth was not as noble as their kind, even her character had to be looked down upon?

Her face turned pale, and her voice trembled, “I know my own status, and I have self-awareness. I will not covet things that are beyond my reach.”

“Young Master Song’s words are baseless and an insult to my character. Should I also say that Young Master Song barged into my room at night, said these insulting words, and despite his noble status, he is just a bully who doesn’t respect the boundaries between men and women?”

Song Zhang was so angry that he almost laughed. He casually picked up the wrapped item on the table and looked at Shen Weici with a cold smile, “This is from the Wei Luo Shop. Can you afford it?”

“A foot of fabric costs ten taels of silver. How much monthly allowance do you have? Don’t tell me Shen Siwen bought it for you.”

Shen Weici looked at the paper-wrapped item in Song Zhang’s hand, which bore the stamp of Wei Luo Shop. She had also heard of this shop for the first time. She said with a trembling voice, “This was a gift from my fourth younger sister. I accompanied her to the shop.”

“Fourth younger sister wanted to give me something, and I couldn’t refuse. That’s why I accepted it.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici looked at Song Zhang, “I didn’t know that the things from Wei Luo Shop were so expensive. Moreover, it was a small item. Fourth younger sister told me it wasn’t valuable, so I accepted it.”

“Small item?”

Song Zhang’s face had already darkened, “Wei Luo Shop is a ready-made clothing store. Are you trying to deceive me by calling it a small item?”

“Shen Weici, you really are a habitual liar.”

Shen Weici looked at Song Zhang’s cold face as he was about to open the package. Her heart jumped, and she rushed over to press down on Song Zhang’s hand, looking at him in panic, “That shop doesn’t only sell ready-made clothes. They also have small items.”

“But if Young Master Song insists on thinking that, then so be it. I don’t want to explain further. It’s late now, so please leave, Young Master Song.”

chapters.title: Bullying Too Far
chapters.content:
Song Zhang’s face grew darker the more he thought about it.

The unresolved anger in his heart made it hard for him to control his emotions.

The jade bracelet he had given her was far more precious than her tattered clothes.

She truly didn’t know good from bad.

Yes, she had always been ungrateful.

Song Zhang watched as she tightly clutched the item in her hand, as if afraid he would expose her lie. He scoffed and was about to reveal her.

But how could Shen Weici’s strength compare to his?

With a slight exertion of force, he easily took the item from her hand. Lowering his head, he looked at her panicked expression, raised his hand, and was about to open it under her shocked gaze.

Shen Weici felt a chill run through her body. No longer caring about anything else, she tightly grabbed Song Zhang’s lapel, stood on her toes, and reached for the item. Her face was pale as she looked at Song Zhang, her eyes barely suppressing tears, her voice trembling and hoarse with a glossy sheen: “Second Young Master Song, no matter how you misunderstand me, I will admit to it.

“Right now, I only beg Second Young Master Song to return this to me.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici blinked back the pain, her throat tight: “From now on, I won’t leave the courtyard. I won’t be in your way, Second Young Master Song. Is that acceptable?”

Song Zhang paused, lowering his head to frown at Shen Weici’s eyes. Those eyes shimmered with unshed tears, a red flush spreading from the corners. Her hair was slightly disheveled, her red lips and white teeth making her delicate beauty all the more enchanting.

Moreover, her soft fingers were still tightly gripping his lapel, a faint warm fragrance wafting from her, making his body tense.

He had a soft heart and couldn’t bear to expose her lies, but he was also annoyed at himself for always being unable to let go of this woman.

Yet, outside, she flirted with others and sought advantages for herself everywhere, while keeping him at arm’s length.

It was something he could never understand.

His fingertips twitched. The momentary softness in his heart hardened again. He opened the item in front of her, intending to thoroughly expose her.

But as soon as he opened it, Song Zhang froze at the sight of what was hanging from his hand, then looked at Shen Weici, who had loosened her grip, taken a step back, her face ashen.

Hanging from his fingers was a water-red embroidered daffodil-patterned *dudou* (a traditional undergarment).

It was an intimate item for women, yet now it was openly hanging from the hand of a man completely unrelated to her.

Shen Weici could no longer hold back the tears in her eyes. Never before had anyone seen such a thing. Now that Song Zhang had seen it, the humiliation made her nearly lose her balance. She would have no face to show anyone ever again.

Song Zhang looked at the tearful, pale-faced woman biting her lip, her face streaked with tears yet not making a sound.

His heart tightened, his throat as if scalded by boiling water, rendering him speechless.

The *dudou* still swayed between them. He didn’t even know how to position his hands. This was the first time he had ever held such a thing. His heart was in turmoil, but he maintained a calm exterior, bending down to stuff the item back into Shen Weici’s hands. His voice softened for once: “I misunderstood you. It was my mistake.”

“But did you initiate contact with Zhang Yuanheng?”

Shen Weici couldn’t believe he was still fixated on this. She truly didn’t understand—what did it matter to him if she approached someone? What business was it of his?

Even if she had approached Xu Er, what did it have to do with him?

Shen Weici didn’t want to argue with him anymore. They were two unrelated people. Even if he believed her, so what? If he didn’t, so what?

She was only waiting for Zhang Yuanheng to come and propose marriage. Once she married him after the New Year, she would have nothing to do with Song Zhang ever again.

As for the cinnabar on her handkerchief being discovered by Song Zhang, Shen Weici endured the embarrassment in her heart, biting her lip to stop herself from arguing with him.

She still turned her head away, her voice soft and hoarse: “I didn’t approach him. He came to me on his own.”

Actually, Song Zhang believed Shen Weici’s words. He was just unhappy that other men were approaching her. Hearing her say this, the displeasure in his heart lessened by half, and his temper improved by half.

He had intended to ask her about Zhang Yuanheng, but seeing her in tears now, he forcibly held back. His hand stretched halfway, wanting to wipe her tears, but then he felt that lowering himself like this would be a loss of face.

He was the Young Master of the Duke of Song’s household, the General commanding the Imperial Guards. How could he lower himself before a woman?

But he also desperately wanted to be close to her, to have her take the initiative with him, even just a smile. Even if it meant lowering himself, so what?

Yet, she kept her body turned away, not looking at him once from beginning to end. When his hand reached out just now, she had recoiled backward, as if afraid of having any connection with him.

Then he heard her hoarse voice: “It’s already late at night, and this is my boudoir. It’s inappropriate for Second Young Master Song to stay any longer. Please, for the sake of your sister, Young Lady Song, leave now.”

A clear dismissal.

She had never been this proactive with Zhang Yuanheng.

Song Zhang didn’t understand. Why could Shen Weici keep others around her, but not him?

chapters.title: Wandering Thoughts
chapters.content:
Even though Song Zhang wanted to be angry at this moment, he forcibly suppressed his impulse.

He looked down at her, his throat rolling, and said softly: “Xu Er is a libertine with many concubines in his household. I was actually worried you’d fall into a pit, so I was a bit harsh.”

“I was angry for your sake. You’re too good for someone like Xu Er.”

“If he bothers you again, I’ll break his legs for you.”

Shen Weici found these words coming from Song Zhang’s mouth utterly ridiculous.

By what right did he interfere in these matters? Was it because of his distant relation as her cousin?

He never involved himself in the affairs of the Marquis’s household, yet he singled her out, even tearing open her things.

She said nothing, truly at a loss for words. She only hoped he would leave quickly.

Seeing that Shen Weici wasn’t responding, Song Zhang didn’t press her for an answer. After a pause, he straightened up, gave her one last deep look, and walked out.

Outside the curtain, three young maids were standing in a row. Two of them held copper basins filled with hot water. Yue Deng was waiting anxiously by the door.

As soon as Song Zhang emerged, the three maids took a step back in fear.

Song Zhang’s tall and distant appearance, coupled with his usual stern demeanor, made even his handsome features intimidating.

He glanced at Yue Deng once before striding away.

Outside, Ming He was waiting. Seeing Song Zhang come out, he said: “No one is guarding here tonight.”

Song Zhang remained silent, his figure disappearing into the night, a hint of loneliness in his steps.

Meanwhile, He Xia and Yan Er entered with the hot water. Yue Deng, seeing no one in the inner room, went behind the floral bed screen and saw Shen Weici lying on the pillow, sobbing.

Yue Deng had never seen Shen Weici cry like this before. She quickly went out to tell He Xia and Yan Er to leave first, then sat on the edge of the bed, reaching out to pat Shen Weici’s back: “Miss, what’s wrong?”

Shen Weici buried her face in the pillow and shook her head.

She pulled out the *dudou* from under the pillow and placed it in Yue Deng’s hand: “Go burn it. I never want to see it again.”

Yue Deng looked at the item in her hand, confused. “This was specially bought by the Fourth Young Lady to give to you, Miss. The Fourth Young Lady said it was a token of her affection. Giving something so personal means you’ve exchanged handkerchiefs as sisters. If you burn it now, wouldn’t that be a bit unkind?”

Shen Weici pulled the blanket over her head and sobbed muffledly: “You’ve reminded me. Then lock it away at the very bottom of the trunk. Just don’t let me see it again.”

Yue Deng was baffled. She looked at the fine satin fabric—when they had gone to the shop earlier, the female shopkeeper had said it was made of silkworm silk, the most comfortable for intimate wear. The pattern was beautiful, and the embroidery was exquisite. It would be a shame not to wear it.

She tried to persuade her: “It’s such a fine thing, Miss. Why not reconsider? I think it looks very pretty.”

Before she could finish, Shen Weici’s soft, hoarse voice cut in: “Just do as I say. Don’t try to persuade me.”

Yue Deng paused at this, then had no choice but to agree. She asked: “Did Second Young Master bully you again?”

Shen Weici remained silent, her fair fingers clutching the brocade quilt. After a long while, she said: “Don’t mention him to me again.”

Yue Deng watched Shen Weici’s slender back rise and fall slightly, her dark hair scattering a little with each movement. At that moment, she suddenly felt her mistress’s sorrow.

She bent down to remove the hairpin from Shen Weici’s hair, then stood up and gently patted her back: “Miss, won’t you have trouble breathing lying like this?”

“I’ll go fetch some hot water. At least wash your face and go to sleep. I won’t ask or say anything else. We can talk about it tomorrow.”

Hearing Yue Deng’s words, Shen Weici finally emerged a little from her distress. She propped herself up, her loose hair covering the tear stains on her face. Lowering her gaze, she said softly: “I don’t know how I ended up provoking him. My situation in the Marquis’s household is getting harder and harder.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici closed her eyes: “He even found out about the cinnabar on my handkerchief...”

Yue Deng was startled by Shen Weici’s words and stared at her: “How did Second Young Master Song find out?”

Shen Weici sighed wearily: “It’s all my fault for not being careful. Him taking me away was an accident.”

“Now he has something to hold over me. It’s better not to provoke him. I just hope to leave soon.”

Yue Deng fell silent at this, quietly helping Shen Weici undo the buttons on her collar, and said softly: “Young Master Zhang said he would come to discuss the marriage in a couple of days, didn’t he? I think Young Master Zhang won’t break his promise this time.”

Shen Weici then thought of Zhang Yuanheng’s unusual behavior today, which was slightly different from what she had seen before.

She looked at Yue Deng: “Who knows? Second Madam might not let the marriage proceed smoothly.”

“I’m just afraid there might be some unexpected trouble.”

Yue Deng gently said: “As long as Young Master Zhang is determined to marry you, what can Second Madam do? Can she really stop Young Master Zhang from marrying you?”

Shen Weici closed her eyes: “She has her ways.”

Yue Deng was taken aback.

Meanwhile, after Song Zhang returned, he saw a woman standing at the courtyard gate to welcome him. She timidly stood by his side, her delicate, boneless fingers linking with his arm: “Second Young Master, I heard you drank tonight, so I specially prepared some sobering soup for you. If you drink it before sleeping, you won’t feel uncomfortable.”

Song Zhang glanced at her, shook off her hand, and strode toward the main hall.

He sat on the pearwood chair at the head of the table, looking coldly at the cautious woman who followed him in: “Do you know why I brought you here?”

Chao Huan, hearing this, quickly knelt in front of Song Zhang, looking pitiful as she lifted her head: “Because the Emperor bestowed me upon you, Second Young Master.”

Song Zhang coldly laughed: “I brought you here to deal with my mother. If I hear those words you said in front of my mother come out of your mouth again, you can go serve my subordinates directly.”

“Understand?”

At this moment, Chao Huan felt a chilling fear.

She stared blankly, trembling, as the black hem of Song Zhang’s robe fell before her. His icy voice came from above, sending a chill from her head to her toes: “I despise women who have ulterior motives in front of me. Serve me wholeheartedly, and I will keep you. But if you dare to have other ideas, remember my words—I am not joking.”

With that, the dark robe swept away. In the spacious, well-lit small hall, only she remained kneeling there, frozen in place.

She turned her head to look at the swaying curtain, not understanding why she couldn’t catch his eye.

She had once been a princess in the Kingdom of Loulan, respected and admired by all, her beauty praised by everyone. Why had he never even touched her?

Inside the room, Song Zhang called for a maid to help him undress and bathe. As soon as he closed his eyes, he saw Shen Weici’s tear-streaked face, like a pear blossom in the rain, making him exhale a breath of alcohol-laden air.

He opened his eyes, trying to forget that face, but as his gaze swept over the swaying curtain, he was reminded of the *dudou* he had held in his hand.

Even though it was just a fleeting glance, he remembered the pattern on the *dudou* was especially beautiful. If Shen Weici were to wear it...

chapters.title: Longing for Her
chapters.content:
Some thoughts, once they take root, are hard to stop.

Song Zhang’s mind was now filled with those alluring thoughts. As soon as he closed his eyes, he imagined Shen Weici wearing that water-red stomach wrap, and then his thoughts spiraled out of control.

With his eyes shut, he could feel her hand wiping his arm, her peach-blossom eyes, so enchanting, gazing at him through the misty steam: *“Er Ye, is the water too hot...?”*

Her voice grew louder, as if approaching. Song Zhang kept his eyes closed, his throat bobbing as he felt her hand moving across his body...

Suddenly, an unfamiliar sensation touched his chest. The rich fragrance was nothing like Shen Weici’s delicate scent. Startled awake from his reverie, he opened his eyes to find Chao Huan’s face before him.

She wore only a thin gauze, her fingers wandering over his body as she gazed at him with seductive, half-lidded eyes.

*Er Ye is already aroused. Soon, she would be justified in becoming his first woman...*

But the scene she expected did not unfold. Instead, she saw Song Zhang’s expression shift from arousal to a dark, suppressed fury. His voice was laced with barely contained anger: *“Get out.”*

The tone was terrifying, as if she would have her neck snapped without mercy if she lingered a moment longer.

Tears welled in her eyes as she clutched her gauze dress, stumbling out in a panic.

Song Zhang gripped the edge of the bath tub, frustrated with himself. At his age, he still suffered like this. Others had women at their beck and call, yet he was cursed to be obsessed with only her.

He gritted his teeth, but couldn’t help letting out a muffled, *“Shen Weici...”*

That night was especially torturous for him. The image of that stomach wrap haunted him. Every time he closed his eyes, all he saw was Shen Weici wearing it, and then his thoughts would spiral again.

He woke up twice during the night, practiced his spear for half the night, and stared into the dark sky in silence for a long while before finally suppressing the thoughts in his heart.

The pent-up frustration only worsened two days later, when he saw the embroidered pouch hanging from Zhang Yuanheng’s waist after morning court.

The emperor, rarely present in the Qinzheng Hall, was reviewing memorials, while Zhang Yuanheng stood respectfully to the side, holding a small notebook.

Song Zhang beckoned Zhang Yuanheng over. Hesitant, Zhang Yuanheng glanced at the emperor, who merely said, *“If he calls you, go.”*

Only then did Zhang Yuanheng step out of the hall.

Under the long corridor outside, he cupped his hands in greeting to the towering Song Zhang before him: *“General Song.”*

Song Zhang’s gaze fell only on the embroidered pouch hanging from Zhang Yuanheng’s waist.

The pouch was embroidered with a five-colored deer. Whether it was his imagination or not, the stitching seemed even more exquisite than his own.

He pointed at the pouch with a cold, mocking smile: *“Minister Zhang’s pouch is quite exquisite. Where did you get it? I might buy one too.”*

Zhang Yuanheng hadn’t expected Song Zhang to suddenly notice his pouch. He couldn’t help but clutch it in his hand, glancing at Song Zhang with a hint of shyness: *“This was embroidered for me by someone I hold dear.”*

*“I cherish her intentions, so I wear it always.”*

Song Zhang had heard those words before. That day, she had brought it to him, her manner proper and demure, her gaze lowered as she said, *“This was embroidered especially for you.”*

Her “especially” seemed to apply to everyone.

A cold smirk tugged at Song Zhang’s lips. He reached out a finger to Zhang Yuanheng: *“Would Minister Zhang be willing to let me take a look?”*

Zhang Yuanheng stared at the outstretched hand, utterly baffled. He couldn’t fathom why Song Zhang would be so interested in his pouch.

After a moment’s hesitation, he untied it and placed it in Song Zhang’s hand: *“Her embroidery is excellent. She even made a sachet for my mother, who praised her work.”*

He paused, then added: *“Actually, General Song, you should know her. She is—”*

But his words were cut short when he saw Song Zhang’s actions. The pouch he had treasured was torn in half by Song Zhang’s hands.
