Zhang Yuanheng stared blankly at the tattered fabric, then up at Song Zhang’s cold, indifferent face, as if the act had been nothing more than an accidental slip.

Song Zhang watched Zhang Yuanheng’s shocked expression, then flicked his fingers, letting the torn pouch fall to the ground. He looked at Zhang Yuanheng’s regretful sigh: *“I’ve always had a heavy hand. I didn’t expect to ruin something Minister Zhang cherishes.”*

Then, summoning Ming He, he said: *“Once you’ve arranged the border defenses, take the jade ruyi from my private residence and deliver it to Minister Zhang as an apology. Understood?”*

Ming He glanced at the pouch in pieces on the ground, then nodded quickly: *“Understood, sir.”*

Song Zhang then looked at the dazed Zhang Yuanheng, who had crouched down to pick up the scraps of his pouch. He said indifferently: *“It’s just a pouch. Is it that important to Minister Zhang?”*

*“Shall I compensate you with ten more?”*

Zhang Yuanheng tightly clutched the pouch fragments, ignoring Song Zhang’s words. After standing, he only bowed to Song Zhang with his hands clasped: *“General Song, if there’s nothing else, this official will take his leave.”*

Song Zhang watched Zhang Yuanheng’s restrained, slightly dispirited figure and felt a flicker of boredom. He had expected some outburst, but instead, Zhang Yuanheng remained so composed.

A hidden sneer played on his lips: *“Minister Zhang must accept the apology I send later. Otherwise, I’d feel guilty.”*

Zhang Yuanheng paid no mind to Song Zhang and walked straight back into the hall.

Song Zhang watched his retreating back, feeling the frustration in his chest ease slightly.

At first, he had wanted to stomp on the pouch, to ensure Zhang Yuanheng couldn’t even take back the pieces. But then he thought better of it—it was just a torn pouch. What was there to dwell on?

He withdrew his gaze, half of his pent-up anger already vented.

Ming He, standing beside him, cast a pitying glance at Zhang Yuanheng. A man of noble bearing, an upright official, and unlike the sycophants around the emperor—yet the general had kept him around.

But he was pitiful all the same, for he had caught the general’s attention.

Ming He took two steps closer to Song Zhang, studying his expression before hesitantly speaking: *“Today, the Marquis of Yi Yong’s estate sent someone to the Hou residence to propose marriage.”*

Song Zhang’s face remained impassive. After a pause, he let out a cold laugh: *“Propose, then.”*

*“Did you arrange for someone to listen in?”*

Ming He nodded: *“It’s done.”*

Song Zhang then strode away with swift, decisive steps.

As he passed Ming He, his brows furrowed, his expression turning colder. Whether it succeeded or not was another matter.

Ming He watched Song Zhang’s retreating back. Though his face was calm, he couldn’t shake the feeling that it carried a murderous aura.

chapters.title: The Zhang Family Comes to Propose
chapters.content:
In the Linchun Courtyard of the Jian’an Marquis Estate, Shen Weici was embroidering a pouch for Shen Siwen. He Xia entered, carrying a few plum blossom branches, her voice filled with excitement: *“Miss, people from the Marquis of Yi Yong’s estate have arrived!”*

*“The marchioness, along with the matchmaker and servants, first went to greet Old Madam, then went to the second courtyard with the second madam.”*

*“This servant reckons they must be here to discuss Miss’s marriage!”*

Shen Weici’s hands paused, then she asked: *“How long have they been there?”*

He Xia replied: *“This servant saw them head to the second courtyard and hurried back. It’s been about a quarter of an hour.”*

Shen Weici nodded, setting down her work. She then turned to Yue Deng: *“Later, Lady Zhang may wish to see me. Bring the newly delivered small jacket for me to change into, and help me redo my hair.”*

*“I can’t meet people looking so plain.”*

Yue Deng happily agreed, quickly fetching the clothes for Shen Weici to change into before styling her hair.

The jewelry in the vanity case was limited, so Yue Deng secured two jade hairpins diagonally in Shen Weici’s hair, then asked: *“Shall we wear the earrings Young Master Zhang gave you?”*

Shen Weici considered for a moment before nodding: *“Alright.”*

After dressing and applying a touch of rouge to her lips, her appearance became even more radiant.

He Xia stood to the side, holding a plum branch with a smile: *“If Miss wears this in her hair, she’ll look even more beautiful.”*

Shen Weici took the branch, admiring the blooming red plum blossoms, their subtle fragrance filling the air. She pushed aside the unease in her heart, a smile forming on her lips.

Soon, a maid from the second courtyard arrived: *“Third Miss, the second madam requests your presence.”*

Shen Weici had Yue Deng bring a cloak, then set down the plum branch and stood.

The past few days had been especially cold, and it was said that snow was expected soon.

Standing on the steps, Shen Weici exhaled softly, her breath visible in the cold air like wispy smoke.

She remembered her mother in Yuyang, before she had fallen ill. At night, by the lamp, her mother would gaze at her fondly, brushing her cheek with her fingers, her eyes full of affection: *“My Aci will marry a nobleman and live the life of nobility.”*

*“Aci is my greatest wish.”*

Shen Weici’s eyes reddened at the memory. In her heart, nobles were selfish. She had never wanted to become one of them.

Beside her, Yue Deng took a sharp breath, unable to help but exclaim: *“It’s only been two days—how has it gotten so much colder?”*

Then, suddenly remembering: *“I forgot to bring a hand warmer for Miss.”*

Her fingers were indeed cold, the tips red from the chill. But it was too late for a hand warmer now. Shen Weici lowered her gaze and descended the steps: *“Let’s go as we are.”*

Yue Deng realized it was indeed too late, so she followed behind.

The plum blossoms were in full bloom, and their faint scent filled the air along the bluestone path.

As they passed a stone bridge, Shen Weici noticed someone approaching from another path. Dressed in fine brocade with a trembling hair ornament, she stood at the crossroads, watching Shen Weici with a cold smirk, as if she had been waiting for her.

Shen Weici’s expression remained unchanged, her steps unhesitating as she walked up to Shen Zhaozhao.

Shen Zhaozhao studied Shen Weici’s face, her voice dripping with her usual bitterness: *“Aren’t you happy right now?”*

*“A bastard from a small place, rising to prominence in the marquis’s estate, about to marry into the Marquis of Yi Yong’s family as the young madam—you must be secretly delighted.”*

She scoffed: *“But who knows if it’ll all come to nothing?”*

Shen Weici pressed her lips together, looking at Shen Zhaozhao: *“Second Sister and I seek different things. I only want stability, not wealth or status.”*

*“Even if it all falls through, I have nothing to say.”*

Shen Zhaozhao’s expression shifted. She hadn’t expected Shen Weici to remain so composed in the face of such sarcasm.

She narrowed her eyes, examining Shen Weici’s face closely. The more she looked, the more she wanted to scratch it. Yet Shen Weici was always like soft cotton—no matter how much she mocked, it never seemed to affect her.

She was curious to see what expression Shen Weici would wear when she learned the truth.

A mocking smile curled her lips: *“As your elder sister, I naturally hope you get what you wish for. But if it all falls through later, just remember today’s words—and don’t cry.”*

With that, Shen Zhaozhao stopped looking at Shen Weici, gathered her sleeves, and walked away.

Shen Weici watched her retreating figure for a long moment. There had been an underlying meaning in Shen Zhaozhao’s words.

Yue Deng watched Shen Zhaozhao disappear into the distance, then whispered to Shen Weici: *“Miss, don’t pay attention to her words. She just can’t stand to see you happy.”*

*“Once you truly marry into the Marquis of Yi Yong’s estate, she’ll probably be furious.”*

Shen Weici lowered her lashes, pressing Yue Deng’s hand: *“This matter may not go as smoothly as we hope. Let’s go see.”*

As they approached the second courtyard, the maid at the door was more welcoming than usual. Upon seeing Shen Weici, she smiled and greeted her: *“Third Miss, at last! The second madam and Lady Zhang have been waiting for you.”*

Shen Weici glanced at the maid’s smiling face, then pressed her lips into a small smile.

The maid lifted the curtain for her, and as Shen Weici entered, she saw only Wen Shi and Lin Shi seated in the main room, chatting and laughing. When they saw her, their gazes fell upon her.

Shen Weici entered properly, first greeting Wen Shi with a respectful bow, then turning to Lin Shi with a courtesy: *“Lady Zhang, peace be with you.”*

Lin Shi observed Shen Weici’s proper demeanor and dignified appearance, just as she had been the last time they met. Though she generally disliked women with melon-seed faces, finding them too seductive, Shen Weici did indeed have such a face. Fortunately, her brows and eyes were refined, her conduct graceful, and though she had a touch of allure, she was also elegant.

Since her son liked her so much, Lin Shi had no choice but to accept it.

The only regret was that Shen Weici’s figure seemed a bit slender, lacking the plumpness she preferred.

Lin Shi reached out and took Shen Weici’s hand, surprised by how soft it was, as if boneless. Looking down, she saw slender fingers, fair and smooth as white jade, perfectly proportioned—truly a pair of delicate, beautiful hands.

She had never seen such a stunning beauty. Examining Shen Weici’s figure more closely, she noted her slender waist, full bosom, and soft cheeks. Even dressed in winter layers, she looked graceful and shapely. No wonder her son was so insistent—it was as if his soul had been hooked.

A woman of such beauty would be hard for an ordinary family to protect. She should be kept in seclusion to avoid prying eyes.

She was only fifteen now. In two or three more years, her allure would only grow, and her figure would become even more enticing. Even the most upright man might struggle to resist the gaze of others.

Lin Shi’s heart raced at the thought. She felt a pang of unease—this kind of beauty was almost too much to bear, and not exactly the daughter-in-law she had envisioned. Yet, she couldn’t deny her son’s attachment.

She took a deep breath, pushing aside her misgivings.

chapters.title: Marriage Arranged
chapters.content:
Wen Shi watched coldly as Lin Shi examined Shen Weici, slowly lifting her teacup to take a sip. Her gaze, however, remained fixed on Lin Shi’s expression, a faint smile tugging at the corner of her lips.

After a long moment of scrutiny, Lin Shi took Shen Weici’s hand and seated her beside herself. She then smiled and asked, “Earlier, I heard your mother say you usually stay in the courtyard. What do you do there all day?”

Shen Weici replied softly, “I don’t like to move around much. I mostly do embroidery, and sometimes practice calligraphy. That’s how I pass my days.”

Lin Shi nodded, then noticed how Shen Weici sat upright beside her, her back straight and posture impeccable—such discipline was rare.

She asked again, “I heard you coughed up blood some days ago. Are you fully recovered now?”

Shen Weici nodded. “I took the prescriptions the imperial physician gave me. I’m much better now.”

Lin Shi then lowered her gaze to Shen Weici’s embroidered shoes. Only the smallest tip of her foot peeked out from beneath her skirt, modest and proper. Indeed, from the moment Shen Weici entered until now, Lin Shi could find no fault with her.

Except for her excessive beauty and this frail body.

She asked further about Shen Weici’s past: “I heard you used to be in poor health as a child, which is why you lived in the countryside to recover. Are you fully restored now?”

Shen Weici knew this was the story her father and Wen Shi had spread. She lowered her voice and said, “Actually, my health improved long ago. I stayed in the village because I found it peaceful, and my mother also preferred quiet places. That’s why we remained there.”

Lin Shi nodded, then turned to Shen Weici with a smile. “As for your marriage to my son Yuanheng, I’ve settled it with your mother today. You’ll enter our household before the New Year.”

Shen Weici’s heart jolted slightly—she hadn’t expected it to happen so soon.

She lowered her head, knowing she had no say in the matter. She only gave a soft, obedient hum in response.

Wen Shi glanced at Shen Weici, then smiled at Lin Shi. “I can see the two of them are fond of each other. I’ve been wanting to find a good family for Weici. As long as your second son treats her well, I’ll be at ease.”

Lin Shi looked at Wen Shi and smiled. “I’ve taken a liking to Weici today. Not to mention my Yuanheng’s feelings for her, even I will treat her well in the future.”

“She’s truly a delightful and capable girl. The sachet she gave me last time was useful, and her embroidery is beautiful. I couldn’t be more satisfied.”

Wen Shi’s smile deepened. “Your satisfaction is all that matters.”

She then teased with a laugh, “Soon enough, I’ll be handing Weici over to your marquis’s estate.”

Lin Shi took Shen Weici’s hand and smiled. “You can rest assured.”

Shen Weici sat quietly to the side, listening to their conversation, yet it all felt strangely unreal.

She couldn’t understand why Wen Shi would so easily allow her to marry into the marquis’s estate. Was there some hidden scheme she wasn’t aware of?

She recalled how Zhang Yuanheng had hesitated when speaking to her before, and after much thought, she still felt uneasy.

As she pondered, she heard Lin Shi, still holding her hand, say, “Why are your hands so bare?”

Before Shen Weici could respond, Lin Shi removed the jade bracelet from her own wrist and placed it on Shen Weici’s. “This bracelet was given to me by my mother on my wedding day. Now I give it to you. Consider it a token of my affection, and I hope you and my Yuanheng will live in harmony, and soon bear a child for the Zhang family.”

She sighed as she looked at Shen Weici. “My two sons are already of age, yet I still haven’t held a grandchild. Once you enter our marquis’s estate, if you can bear the eldest grandson, rest assured—I will not treat you poorly.”

She then turned to Wen Shi. “Our marquis’s estate is not the kind to break promises. What we’ve agreed upon will be honored.”

“Second Madam, I appreciate your understanding of a mother’s heart.”

Wen Shi smiled at Lin Shi. “We’re both mothers. How could I not understand you?”

“Let’s not dwell on this matter anymore.”

Lin Shi nodded, then looked back at Shen Weici. “I’ve given you this bracelet as a sign of my acceptance. Don’t refuse it—just take it.”

Shen Weici lowered her gaze to the green jade bracelet on her wrist. It seemed of even finer quality than the one Wen Shi had bought for her before.

Instinctively, she tried to refuse. “Weici dare not accept such a precious gift from Madam Zhang.”

But Lin Shi tightly held Shen Weici’s hand, looking at the girl with her exquisite features, and sighed. “I give it to you, so take it. You must know my Yuanheng’s feelings for you. Since he cares for you so, I will not treat you poorly either.”

Shen Weici hesitated, then finally relaxed her fingers and nodded silently. “Madam Zhang’s kindness is noted in Weici’s heart.”

“After entering the marquis’s estate, Weici will serve you wholeheartedly and never neglect her duties.”

Lin Shi’s heart warmed at these words, and she patted Shen Weici’s hand. “It’s good that you have this intention.”

“But what’s most important is that you quickly bear a grandson to continue the family line.”

Shen Weici felt a flicker of shyness at the mention of children in front of her elders, but knowing how seriously noble families took such matters, she obediently nodded.

Lin Shi, satisfied with Shen Weici’s gentle demeanor, turned her head to speak with Wen Shi again. “Since we’ve settled matters this morning, I should take my leave.”

Wen Shi hurriedly said, “Now that our families are to be closer, why not stay and have a meal with us?”

Lin Shi released Shen Weici’s hand and stood up. “There are still some matters at the estate, so I won’t stay.”

Wen Shi, hearing this, also stood and said to Shen Weici, “Weici, come with me to see Madam Zhang off.”

Shen Weici snapped out of her thoughts, agreed, and stood up, moving to Wen Shi’s side.

As they walked, Wen Shi and Lin Shi chatted and laughed together, occasionally including Shen Weici in the conversation. Nothing seemed amiss.

The only oddity was Wen Shi’s dignified and kind smile, which showed no hint of intention to make things difficult for Shen Weici.

Also, Shen Weici remembered that Lin Shi had not been particularly warm toward her before, yet now she was unusually affectionate, constantly holding her hand as if very pleased with her.

Though Shen Weici had indeed tried to behave properly in front of Lin Shi, it shouldn’t have made Lin Shi suddenly like her so much.

She had a vague feeling that something was wrong, but she couldn’t quite pinpoint what.

As they reached the front gate to see Lin Shi off, Lin Shi, before boarding her carriage, took Shen Weici’s hand once more. “I truly like you from the bottom of my heart. After you enter the marquis’s estate, I will treat you as my own daughter.”

“Don’t overthink things. My Yuanheng has genuine feelings for you. In any case, we won’t treat you poorly. Just be at ease.”

Shen Weici felt something was off at these words and was about to ask what Lin Shi meant by “overthink,” but she saw Lin Shi had already let go of her hand and, with the help of a servant, boarded the carriage. She then bid farewell to Wen Shi from the carriage window.

Wen Shi smiled as she saw Lin Shi off, then turned to Shen Weici. The smile on her face faded slightly. “Let’s go back.”

With that, she gathered her sleeves and left first.

chapters.title: Tonics
chapters.content:
Shen Weici watched Wen Shi’s retreating figure, her brows furrowing in thought. She then looked down at the bracelet on her wrist, placed there by Lin Shi.

As she passed the threshold of the front gate, her eyes scanned the area but found no sign of Lai Fu. She ordered Yue Deng to inquire about him.

Soon, Yue Deng caught up with Shen Weici and whispered, “The gatekeeper said Lai Fu broke his leg a few days ago. He’s still recovering in his house in the alley behind the estate.”

Shen Weici recalled that Lai Fu was a native servant of the marquis’s estate. His family lived in the alley behind the estate, and their house was rented from the marquis’s estate, with the rent deducted from his monthly allowance.

Yue Deng added curiously, “Lai Fu is just a gatekeeper who runs errands. How could he have broken his leg?”

Shen Weici stopped in her tracks, looking toward the distant plum grove, a trace of sorrow in her eyes.

She had never mentioned Lai Fu to Song Zhen, precisely to protect him. Yet, in the end, she had still brought him harm.

Back in Chunshui Courtyard, He Xia pointed to the items on the table and whispered, “Miss, the second madam has sent many tonics for you.”

She then brought over a small bowl still steaming with heat. “Old Mama Chang from the second madam’s side has brought medicinal tonic. She says she must watch you drink it before returning to report to the second madam.”

The steaming bowl emitted a bitter scent. Shen Weici’s gaze fell on Old Mama Chang, who stood opposite her. Dressed in a dark yellow brocade robe, her hands tucked into her sleeves, she wore gold earrings and a forehead band with a blue agate in the center—every inch the dignified personal maid of the second madam.

Old Mama Chang slightly lifted her chin. When she noticed Shen Weici looking at her, she didn’t display her usual arrogance but instead smiled warmly. “The madam only has your best health in mind, Miss. You coughed up blood before, so it’s important to nourish your body. Once you’re married into the marquis’s estate, you’ll be able to conceive sooner, won’t you?”

So the second madam was now concerned about her bearing children for the marquis’s estate.

Shen Weici glanced at the bowl of medicine in He Xia’s hands, took it with a faint smile, and softly said, “Thank you for the trouble, Old Mama. Is this medicine to be taken just once, or daily?”

Old Mama Chang looked at Shen Weici’s calm smile and replied, “The madam said to take it daily. She told me to bring it to you every day.”

“The madam truly cares about your health, Miss. She hopes you’ll be in good health, doesn’t she?”

She then looked at the bowl in Shen Weici’s hands. “This medicine will get cold quickly in such weather. You should drink it while it’s hot, Miss.”

Shen Weici, however, carried the bowl to a small chair beside her, looking at Old Mama Chang. “I know my mother has always cared for me. But the distance from the second courtyard to Chunshui Courtyard is far. It would be too much trouble for you to come every day.”

“If you could just tell me the time, if the medicine is prepared in the kitchen, I can have my maid fetch it. If it’s prepared at my mother’s place, my maid can go and collect it.”

“But if there’s a prescription, I can have my maid prepare it here in the courtyard. That way, we won’t have to go back and forth.”

“Wouldn’t that be better, Old Mama?”

Old Mama Chang stared at Shen Weici, who held the bowl without drinking, instead speaking in a way that left her no room to argue. Her face stiffened, but she forced a smile. “Miss, you’re being too formal. What trouble is there in this?”

“My madam’s kindness is such that we servants don’t mind making a few extra trips.”

Shen Weici sighed at this. “Old Mama, you’re not young anymore, and the roads are cold and slippery. How can I let you make the trip every day?”

“My mother’s care is something I should accept and be grateful for. But having her personal maid deliver it daily makes me uneasy.”

With that, Shen Weici turned to Yue Deng. “You will go to the second courtyard every day at this time to fetch it. There’s no need to trouble my mother’s people.”

Yue Deng immediately stepped forward and said to Old Mama Chang, “Old Mama, rest assured. This servant is quick and reliable. I guarantee no mistakes, and in this cold weather, you should rest.”

Old Mama Chang felt that after living more than half her life, she was now being outmaneuvered by a girl of no more than fifteen or sixteen.

With the conversation at this point, and all the reasoning being sound, if she persisted, wouldn’t it make people suspicious?

She forced a smile. “Miss, you should drink the tonic first.”

“Otherwise, it’ll get cold.”

Shen Weici finally looked at the now lukewarm medicine in her hands. Under Old Mama Chang’s watchful gaze, she slowly drank it all.

She then looked at Old Mama Chang and smiled. “Please convey my thanks to my mother for her kindness.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici turned to Yue Deng. “See Old Mama out.”

Yue Deng quickly moved to Old Mama Chang’s side. “Old Mama, I’ll escort you.”

With that, she took Old Mama Chang’s hand and led her out.

As Old Mama Chang was being led out by Yue Deng, the latter whispered questions about the tonics in her ear. It wasn’t until they reached the courtyard gate that Old Mama Chang remembered she had forgotten to take the bowl back.

She quickly pushed Yue Deng aside and turned back, hastily lifting the curtain. She saw Shen Weici still sitting in the chair. Noticing her return, Shen Weici held out the bowl. “Did you forget this, Old Mama?”

Old Mama Chang let out a breath of relief and smiled. “This bowl is specially for serving your medicine. If it’s left behind, we’d have to find another one.”

Shen Weici smiled. “Take it back, then.”

Old Mama Chang finally took the bowl and left.

As soon as Old Mama Chang was gone, Shen Weici gripped the armrest and stood up. She leaned over the back window, her face pale as she stuck her fingers down her throat, vomiting up the medicine she had just drunk.

But after retching for a while, she only managed to bring up half of it. She supported herself on the flowered window frame, gasping for breath, her forehead beaded with fine sweat.

He Xia, standing beside her, was terrified. She rubbed Shen Weici’s back while using a handkerchief to wipe the sweat from her face. “Miss, what’s wrong?”

Shen Weici shook her head. “It’s nothing.”

Then, in a low voice, she said, “Go fetch some tea for me to rinse my mouth.”

He Xia hurried off.

When Yue Deng returned, she saw Shen Weici, pale-faced, staring blankly at a porcelain bottle in her hands. She walked over and looked at the bottle. “What’s inside?”

Shen Weici finally shifted her gaze to Yue Deng. “A little of the leftover medicine from the bowl earlier. I poured it into here.”

Yue Deng realized what she meant and looked at Shen Weici. “Do you suspect there’s something wrong with the medicine, Miss?”

Shen Weici’s eyes darkened slightly. “Yue Deng, what do you think?”

Yue Deng’s face paled as she looked at Shen Weici. “But you just drank it all, Miss. What do we do now?”

Shen Weici supported her forehead. “I vomited some of it up.”

She then looked at the porcelain bottle in her hands. “I want you to leave the estate and take this bottle to a doctor. See if they can figure out what’s in it. We’ll start with that.”

“Tomorrow, when the time is right, go and see where the medicine is being prepared. Try to get your hands on the dregs.”

“But if it’s prepared in the second courtyard, that will be difficult.”

“The second madam wouldn’t be this kind to me. I feel like there’s something off about today’s events.”

Yue Deng quickly nodded. “Don’t worry, Miss. She can’t very well prepare medicine inside her room. It must be done outside. If it’s in the kitchen, that’s even better—I know people there.”

Shen Weici listened, then smiled at Yue Deng. “You’re quite capable.”

chapters.title: Kissing Her at Night
chapters.content:
When Song Zhang returned at night, Ming He whispered beside him, “Today, the Third Young Lady’s marriage to the Earl’s mansion has been settled.”

“Before I left, I even saw Madame Zhang holding the Third Young Lady’s hand and saying many things to her.”

“But...”

As he spoke, Ming He leaned close to Song Zhang’s ear and whispered something.

Song Zhang pressed his lips together, his cold eyes revealing no emotion. His figure stood tall and straight in the night, the noble bearing of a distinguished family making him seem untouchable with just a cold glance.

He raised an eyebrow and coldly laughed, “The second branch truly cannot tolerate a concubine’s daughter. It suits me just fine.”

“And there’s no need for this lord to take action.”

But Song Zhang couldn’t help but wonder what Shen Weici would think if she knew. Or what she would do.

She was the kind of person who wanted to marry.

He only asked indifferently, “Was the item delivered?”

Ming He quickly replied, “As per your orders, it was sent in the afternoon. The people chosen are all reliable.”

Song Zhang’s expression softened slightly, “Find an opportunity to replace it. It probably won’t be needed.”

At this moment, Shen Weici had finished washing up and was about to sleep. She leaned against the pillow and talked with Yue Deng.

Yue Deng sat at the head of Shen Weici’s bed, her face full of worry. “Today, I went out and found the most famous physician. That physician examined my medicine and said it smelled like there was a cold medicine inside, with a very faint scent of safflower. Ordinary people can hardly detect it.”

“He said that drinking it for a long time would be harmful to the body. Unless one doesn’t want to have children, otherwise, this cold medicine should be consumed less.”

As she spoke, she angrily said, “I asked how could the Second Madame be so kind as to send medicine to help the young lady regulate her body? It turns out she had ill intentions, wanting the young lady to be unable to conceive after marriage. She truly has a vicious heart.”

Shen Weici held Yue Deng’s hand, “This matter needs to be considered carefully. Let’s see the situation tomorrow.”

“If she sent me such cold medicine, it’s because she thinks I won’t notice anything, or even if I do, I won’t have any evidence or way to deal with it.”

“I’ll think about it more.”

As they spoke, He Xia suddenly entered, looking somewhat embarrassed. “Young Lady, just now, Manager Qi came and said that the young lady should go to Guan Song Ju.”

Shen Weici was startled and then frowned. “You can go back and say that I have already gone to sleep. If the Young Master Song has something urgent, he can come tomorrow during the day.”

He Xia acknowledged and left, but soon returned. Standing behind the bed screen, she softly spoke to Shen Weici’s figure inside. “Manager Qi said that if the young lady doesn’t go, the Second Young Master will come himself.”

Shen Weici paused. She had already taken off her clothes and let down her hair. She couldn’t possibly get up, dress, and comb her hair just to see him at this hour.

Moreover, it was already past Hai time (around 10 PM), which was very late. It wouldn’t be appropriate for her to go to Song Zhang’s place at this hour, regardless of the reason.

Furthermore, Shen Weici more or less guessed what it was about. Song Zhang would definitely ask her about the engagement with the Earl’s mansion and accuse her of seducing Zhang Yuan Heng to get the Earl’s mansion to propose marriage. She was already overwhelmed and had no patience to deal with this.

She looked at Yue Deng and whispered, “You go out and tell Ming He that I caught a cold from the wind outside today and am seriously ill, unable to get out of bed. Ask Ming He what urgent matter it is. He can tell you directly. If he insists on telling me personally, say that I will visit him once I recover.”

Yue Deng nodded, then lowered the bed curtain and went out to deliver the message.

Ming He, holding a sword, listened to Yue Deng’s words and raised an eyebrow. He thought that this morning when he saw Madame Zhang, she was still fine. How could she be so seriously ill in just one afternoon?

He asked, “Is the Third Young Lady really too ill to get out of bed?”

Yue Deng’s expression was particularly convincing, her face full of sadness. “My young lady’s body has never been very good. She gets headaches from the slightest breeze. Tonight, she even fainted from illness. Even after taking medicine, she hasn’t recovered.”

Ming He looked at Yue Deng’s appearance and thought to himself that this girl was quite skilled at acting.

He didn’t say much more, just said, “Since your young lady is seriously ill, I won’t disturb her further.”

With that, he left.

Yue Deng watched as Ming He was finally dealt with. Looking at the sword in his hand, she felt a sense of fear. She let out a sigh of relief and told He Xia and Yan Er to go to sleep. Then she went back into the inner room to extinguish the lamp.

Inside the room, only one lamp was left lit. She went to the window, lifted the curtain, and saw Shen Weici already lying on her side, her black hair spread across the pillow. She softly said, “I think that Ming He believed me. Young Lady, you can sleep peacefully. I will sleep on the small bed in the side room. If you wake up at night, just call me.”

Shen Weici nodded, then watched as the bed curtain was closed. Inside the dark bed canopy, she curled up slightly and fell asleep.

In her drowsy state, Shen Weici suddenly felt a chill on her back. Half-asleep, she burrowed deeper into the brocade quilt, her eyelashes trembling a few times before she fell back into a deep sleep.

Song Zhang sat on the edge of the bed, looking down at Shen Weici, who was sleeping on her side with her back to him. Her moon-white inner garment was still neat, and her wrist was properly resting on the quilt. Compared to her usual gentleness, she now looked a bit more obedient and meek.

He reached out with his warm fingers, brushing aside the soft hair that fell on her side face, revealing her fair and clean small face beneath.

Half of her face was buried in the quilt, as if even in sleep she was restless. Her fingers tightly clutched the corner of the quilt, and her body was slightly curled up into a ball. Every time he saw her in this position, Song Zhang couldn’t help but wonder if she slept like this all night without turning over.

His palm propped up beside her cheek, her warm breath falling on his wrist. The bed canopy was filled with her warm fragrance, unlike the faint scent she usually carried. Now, his nose was filled with her scent.

Song Zhang couldn’t help but lower his body, his gaze carefully tracing Shen Weici’s sleeping face. He then thought of the small, exquisite embroidered shoes he had held in his hand before, and her undershirt. He wondered if she was wearing it now.

His thoughts began to wander, his breathing gradually deepening, and his gaze became more greedy.

He reached out to touch Shen Weici’s forehead, which was warm to the touch, not feverish at all. A hint of a smile appeared in his eyes.

He should have known that this woman was good at deceiving people. On the surface, she was as gentle and obedient as a kitten, but her mind was full of schemes.

She didn’t want to go to his place, so she made up lies to deceive him.

And he had actually believed her a little.

His fingers moved downward, resting on her full lips, which were small and pink, extremely tempting.

Song Zhang felt that he was not some restrained gentleman either. He had come here at night precisely for this.

He no longer wanted to endure.

As he lowered his body further, Song Zhang pinched Shen Weici’s chin, turning her head, which was facing away, towards himself. The last time he had kissed her, it had left him yearning for a long time. No matter what, he had helped her.

She couldn’t just dismiss him with a mere pouch that anyone could have. Today, he would take back everything.

His fingers applied a slight pressure, and the tightly closed red lips parted slightly, revealing a tempting gap. Song Zhang’s throat rolled, his heartbeat quickened. He wanted to kiss her but was afraid she would wake up and blame him.

In truth, he was a little afraid of Shen Weici being angry with him.

Her red-rimmed eyes and those distant words were like knives stabbing into his heart, making it hard to bear.

After a long internal struggle, Song Zhang finally leaned down and gently kissed her.

After all, he was considerate of the fact that she was asleep, and his actions were gentle, not waking her up.

Unlike the awkwardness of the last time, this time he was familiar with the process, knowing how to entangle his tongue with hers. The deeper the kiss, the heavier his scorching breath became, falling on Shen Weici’s face. In his dark phoenix eyes, he saw her dark eyebrows gradually furrow.

chapters.title: If You Agree, I Will Propose Marriage Tomorrow
chapters.content:
The only candlelight in the inner room flickered gently, casting a moving shadow of the tall figure on the wall, exuding an ambiguous charm.

Shen Weici was slightly disoriented, her bleary eyes catching a moving figure. She realized something was wrong and hastily, fearfully pushed at the person pressing down on her.

Her eyes were red-rimmed, and she kicked her legs, but couldn’t move the person.

He watched as tears filled her eyes, the candlelight reflecting off them, shimmering and pitiful.

But the next moment, Song Zhang felt a solid slap on his cheek, startling him.

His eyes narrowed dangerously as he looked down at the person on the bed, her black hair spread across the pillow, her eyes filled with tears. A cold and stern emotion surged within him.

His cold phoenix eyes narrowed as he reached out and grabbed her wrist, his fingers rubbing against the jade bracelet on her slender, fair wrist. He coldly laughed, “Is it that now that the Earl’s mansion has come to propose marriage, your courage has grown so much?”

“Have you forgotten what I told you? Not to go and see Zhang Yuan Heng again.”

Shen Weici’s face was pale as she looked at Song Zhang. The coldness in his eyes made her heart tremble. She knew she couldn’t afford to anger Song Zhang at this critical moment, just before her marriage into the Earl’s mansion.

She forced herself to endure the humiliation, propping herself up and turning her head away, avoiding Song Zhang’s expression. “I have not seen Zhang Yuan Heng again. I only found out today that the Earl’s mansion has come to propose marriage.”

“Moreover, marriage is decided by one’s parents. It’s not something I can decide.”

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici, who was still lying to him. He coldly laughed, pinching her chin to make her look at him. “You haven’t seen Zhang Yuan Heng?”

“Then who did you meet at Fa Ning Temple on the Laba Festival a few days ago?”

“Wasn’t it you who urged him to come and propose marriage?”

Shen Weici looked at Song Zhang in shock, her fingers clutching her clothes, trying to keep her emotions in check. “You had someone follow me?”

Song Zhang sneered, “On a festival like Laba, the number of patrol officers and guards is double the usual. My subordinates saw a young lady from the Hou Mansion secretly talking to a man, exchanging sweet nothings. It’s a scandal.”

“They reported it to me because they saw you were from the Hou Mansion.”

“If it wasn’t you talking to Zhang Yuan Heng, then who was it? Could it be that you did such a thing and are afraid of people finding out?”

Shen Weici found his words ridiculous. What about his own behavior just now? How was he any better?

She only wanted to marry into the Earl’s mansion peacefully before the New Year and have nothing more to do with Song Zhang.

In a month, she would be able to marry and leave the Hou Mansion. Once she was married into the Earl’s mansion, would Song Zhang still be able to trouble her?

She blinked her tearful eyes. “Young Master Song always misunderstands me. The last time I met Young Master Zhang was purely accidental, and we only exchanged a few words. There was no seduction involved.”

“Today, the Earl’s mansion came to propose marriage, which was also a surprise to me. But since my parents have arranged it, what have I done wrong?”

Song Zhang coldly looked at Shen Weici’s weak and pitiful appearance, her eyes filled with tears that seemed about to fall, as if she was truly wronged.

He then saw her suddenly cover her face and weep. “Just now, Young Master Song suddenly entered my room and did improper things to me. Does Young Master Song care about my reputation?”

“I know I am of low status and cannot aspire to the Earl’s mansion, but Young Master Song is of noble status. Aren’t you also taking advantage of my defenselessness?”

“What have I gained by coming to the Hou Mansion? What have I schemed for?”

“Young Master Song came here at night and did all this. Don’t you care about my reputation?”

Song Zhang’s face darkened slightly. The slap on his face from earlier still stung a little. Now she was playing the victim.

He coldly sneered, “This lord came here tonight to enlighten you. What do you have to be wronged about?”

Shen Weici looked at Song Zhang in confusion. “What do you mean?”

Song Zhang’s dark eyes looked at Shen Weici. “Don’t you understand what I mean? Although the Earl’s mansion is a declining family, do you think you can smoothly marry into it just because Zhang Yuan Heng likes you?”

“You are nothing but a concubine’s daughter with no background or support. Why would the Zhang family so easily agree to marry you?”

“Shen Weici, sometimes I think you are very naive.”

Song Zhang’s words were calm, but they made Shen Weici recall the scene from that morning.

She did feel that something was wrong.

Song Zhang reached out and pinched Shen Weici’s chin, his eyes tightly locked on her tearful eyes as he said in a low voice, “Also, this lord likes you.”

“As long as you agree, this lord will go and propose marriage tomorrow.”

Shen Weici’s eyes widened in shock, her heart pounding. She unconsciously moved back, her voice hoarse. “Young Master Song, what did you say about me before? That I was shameless and seducing others. Do your actions now show any shame?”

“Never mind that I have already been engaged to Young Master Zhang. Even if it were ordinary circumstances, your actions towards me are still improper and disregard human ethics.”

“I ask Young Master Song to leave immediately. Otherwise, tomorrow I will report this to the Old Madame, and let everyone in the Hou Mansion see who can do such shameless things.”

Song Zhang gritted his teeth, his eyes filled with ridicule. “You will report to the Old Madame? If I say that I want you, do you think the Old Madame will refuse to send you to my room?”

Shen Weici’s face paled, looking at Song Zhang in shock. “I am already engaged to the Earl’s mansion. Even the Old Madame cannot decide for me. Do you think your power is that great?”

Song Zhang coldly laughed. “So what if you are engaged? It’s not difficult to cancel this engagement.”

“Do you think Zhang Yuan Heng will really marry you?”

“This lord will say it again. As long as you agree, this lord will go and propose marriage tomorrow to make you my concubine. It won’t be any worse than marrying into the Earl’s mansion.”

Shen Weici felt a chill run through her body upon hearing these words.

Not to mention that she had no romantic feelings for Song Zhang at all, even if she were to become the concubine of the Prince of the Song family, even if she would be recorded in the family genealogy, it would still be as a concubine, which was never what she wanted.

Moreover, she had heard about the status of the Song family. Even as a concubine, it wouldn’t be that easy.

She tightly clenched her fingers. “I ask Young Master Song to let me go.”

“I only like Young Master Zhang and only wish to marry him. If Young Master Song forces me, then I will die tonight.”

“After all, Young Master Song doesn’t want me to live...”

chapters.title: This Lord Has Plenty of Women, One Less Won’t Matter
chapters.content:
Shen Weici held a handkerchief in her hand, turning her body slightly as she lowered her brows and shed tears. Her long black hair fell over one shoulder, and her delicate white clothes were slightly wrinkled, resembling a beautiful woman in a spring boudoir painting.

She was originally a graceful and charming person, and with her lowered brows and falling tears, she seemed like a tender beauty within ten zhang of red silk. Yet, this made Song Zhang’s heart grow cold, and his fingers trembled slightly.

He tightly grabbed Shen Weici’s wrist, his eyes slightly reddening. “Do you think I am trying to force you to death by saying I want to marry you?”

Shen Weici’s voice trembled. “Isn’t that the case?”

“I have always considered you as my relative, with no other thoughts. Your words tonight, are they not trying to force me to death?”

In Song Zhang’s mind, no matter what kind of woman, as long as he crooked his finger, they would come and cling to him. The noble ladies from prestigious families were like this, as were the women with some beauty and talent, let alone Shen Weici, who had no background.

She also knew that her best choice was to choose a man to depend on.

He knew Shen Weici was smart. She knew how to choose.

She should know who could protect her.

But in her heart, he was not as good as Zhang Yuan Heng.

Under the warm light, she looked extremely moving, and in her thin white clothes, she appeared even more fragile.

Originally a gentle and soft-tempered person, in this room filled with her warm fragrance, Song Zhang felt his breath catch.

He saw her slightly trembling shoulders, the brocade quilt piled at her soft waist, layer upon layer like the slight wrinkles in her clothes. Each of these made Song Zhang unable to control his emotions.

He wanted to hold her tightly in his arms, to cherish her, to whisper in her ear, to let her soft, boneless fingers rest on his chest, and for him to always protect her in the future.

But this woman did not appreciate his kindness.

He staggered to his feet.

chapters.title: Avoiding Song Zhang
chapters.content:
It was the first time he had ever lowered himself before a woman, only to receive a response that made him wish he were dead.

She had said she had no feelings for him at all.

As if he were a flood or a wild beast, as if he were a plague she could not avoid fast enough.

She did not like him in the slightest.

Song Zhang had never suffered such humiliation in front of a woman before. It had taken great resolve for him to say those words—he had never confessed his feelings to anyone else. But the response he received made him regret ever opening his mouth.

He lowered his gaze to Shen Weici’s still-downcast eyes. She remained as gentle and serene as ever, her warm fragrance still soft and lingering.

Her red-rimmed eyes shimmered with unshed tears.

Anyone who saw her would sigh at her boundless tenderness.

But in that moment, Song Zhang realized—she was the most heartless of them all.

His feelings were nothing but a joke to her.

He let out a cold laugh and spoke in a low voice, “Then pretend I never said those words tonight.”

“Your lordship has no shortage of women. You won’t miss me.”

“And I won’t bother helping you again.”

With that, he turned and left without a backward glance.

Shen Weici stared at his retreating figure in stunned silence, not expecting him to leave so easily.

Then, she drifted into a daze, pressing her hand to her lips, a flicker of panic appearing in her eyes.

What she had feared most was that Song Zhang would say something that would crush her hope. Fortunately, he had left, and he hadn’t done anything even more absurd. Otherwise, her life in the Marquis’s mansion would have been even harder.

She had noticed Song Zhang’s subtle approaches toward her, but she had never believed that affection could last.

Moreover, a man like Song Zhang had no shortage of women around him. She had no intention of competing for his attention.

She propped herself up and sat on the edge of the bed. Shen Weici stood, took the outer robe hanging on the bedside rack, and draped it over her shoulders. Then, she picked up the candle holder and went to the side room to check on Yue Deng.

Song Zhang had made such a commotion earlier, yet there had been no sound from Yue Deng’s side. Worried, she went to take a look.

Inside the side room, Shen Weici saw Yue Deng still asleep on the small cot. She crouched beside her, holding the candlelight close, and saw a red mark on Yue Deng’s forehead. Lowering her head further, she spotted a small pebble beneath the cot.

Without a doubt, this was Song Zhang’s doing.

She quickly reached out to check Yue Deng’s breathing. Only when she felt the steady rhythm did she exhale in relief. She adjusted the blanket over Yue Deng before standing up and leaving the side room.

Unable to sleep, Shen Weici sat in a chair by the charcoal brazier, extending her wrist to examine the bracelet Lady Zhang had given her that day. After staring at it for a long while, she gently removed it. She would wear it again on her wedding day.

Song Zhang’s words from earlier had been incomplete, leaving her even more uneasy.

The next day, Shen Weici went early to pay her respects to Lady Wen. It was a day of rest, and her father was also present. After greeting them, Shen Weici quietly sat in a chair to the side, accompanying Lady Wen in conversation. Once Lady Wen dismissed her, she could take her leave.

But today, Shen Weici showed no intention of leaving. She looked up at her father and asked softly, “Father, do you remember my birthday?”

Shen Rongsheng was sipping hot tea. Hearing this, he paused. He had indeed forgotten Shen Weici’s birthday, only vaguely recalling the year.

He glanced at Shen Weici with slight embarrassment. “It’s been so long, I’ve forgotten. Which month is your birthday?”

Shen Weici did not feel disappointed at his words. Instead, her unease deepened.

She took out a piece of paper she had prepared earlier and said to her father and Lady Wen, “I ask this not for any other reason.”

“It’s just that for the betrothal, the three rituals and six etiquettes, the exchange of birth dates and horoscopes...”

“I thought Father and Mother might not know mine, so I wrote down my horoscope.”

With that, Shen Weici walked to Lady Wen, handing her the paper. “Mother, this is my horoscope.”

As soon as Shen Weici finished speaking, Shen Zhaozhao, sitting nearby, couldn’t help but let out a laugh.

Shen Weici naturally heard it, her gaze remaining lowered.

Lady Wen’s face stiffened for a moment before she forced a smile. “Indeed, you’ve thought of everything.”

Shen Weici saw that Lady Wen had taken the paper. She pressed her lips together and silently returned to her seat.

She was confused. Why had the wedding date been set without even exchanging horoscopes? Lady Wen had never asked her about it either.

Was this matter really decided so casually?

And the wedding date seemed to have been set in haste, as if chosen on a whim.

Then there was Shen Zhaozhao’s laugh—it seemed to carry a hint of mockery, as if she knew something.

This unease made Shen Weici clench her fingers. She looked up at her father again and asked, “Yesterday, I heard Mother say the wedding is set for before the New Year in the second month. That leaves only a month. It’s probably too late to prepare the wedding dress.”

Shen Rongsheng nodded after hearing this. He looked at Lady Wen. “The marriage is rather sudden. As for the wedding dress, see if you can find more embroiderers. It would be best to have it made quickly.”

Lady Wen smiled at Shen Rongsheng. “My lord, rest assured. I’ve already ordered people to make it. Weici will have it in time.”

“The reason it’s set so soon is the Zhang family’s wish. I thought that with so many rumors outside, it would be better to marry her off sooner.”

Only then did Shen Rongsheng nod in relief.

Shen Yanli, sitting across from them, suddenly spoke up. “Third Sister is getting married so soon. I should prepare a gift for her as well.”

Lady Wen glanced at Shen Yanli. “You haven’t even settled your own matters yet.”

But halfway through her sentence, Lady Wen’s expression turned ugly, and she couldn’t continue.

A few days ago, she had taken the initiative to visit old acquaintances to discuss a marriage for Shen Yanli, only to be met with cold shoulders and veiled sarcasm. They had all avoided her as if she were a venomous snake, mocking her for being the kind of mother-in-law who would torment her daughter-in-law to death.

She had been humiliated by those women, left with no face to stay, and could only return in disgrace.

Now, arranging a marriage for Shen Yanli had become a difficult task.

The more she thought about it, the angrier she became. Her nails dug deep into her palms. Because of Shen Weici, the second branch had been ruined, yet her lord still blamed her.

On rest days, Shen Weici would stay in the second courtyard to have meals with them. After finishing, just as she was about to leave, Old Mama Chang brought over a bowl of medicine and smiled at Shen Weici. “Third Young Lady, drink this tonic before you go.”

Shen Rongsheng, seeing this, glanced at Lady Wen and asked, “What is this?”

Lady Wen smiled. “Isn’t Weici about to enter the Earl’s mansion? She coughed up blood some days ago, and the imperial physician said her body is somewhat cold. I thought it would be good for her to take some tonics these days to strengthen her body. That way, she’ll be in better health to bear children.”

Shen Rongsheng looked at Lady Wen in surprise, then laughed. “You’re the thoughtful one. If you treat her better now, those rumors outside will naturally fade away.”

He then looked at Shen Weici. “Your mother has good intentions. Drink it quickly.”

Shen Weici stared at the bowl of medicine in her hands. The dark liquid had a foul smell. She hesitated for a moment but, under her father’s gaze, slowly drank the entire bowl.

She then placed the empty bowl back into Old Mama Chang’s hands and thanked Lady Wen.

Shen Rongsheng, rarely seeing such harmony, smiled in satisfaction and left for the study with his servants.

As she exited the second courtyard, the sky was already bright.

It seemed a light snow had fallen the night before, covering the grass and trees in a layer of white frost.

Yue Deng walked beside Shen Weici and whispered, “Miss, what if that medicine is too potent? What if it harms you?”

“Clearly it’s harmful, so how can you drink it every day?”

Shen Weici felt a burning sensation in her stomach, as if her body was rejecting the medicine. The taste seemed to churn in her belly. After walking a short distance, she leaned against a plum tree and retched, but nothing came up.

Her gaze was cold as she looked at the plum blossoms scattered on the ground. In a soft voice, she said, “She’s harming me without restraint. Naturally, I cannot sit and wait for death.”

After catching her breath, her face still pale, Shen Weici stood up and tightly gripped Yue Deng’s hand, whispering something in her ear.

Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici after listening. “But what if something goes wrong?”

Shen Weici gave a faint smile. “Yue Deng, just trust me.”

Yue Deng finally agreed, then asked, “Should this servant go now?”

Shen Weici nodded. “You’re the best one for this task. You can tell my father you’re going out to buy needles and thread for me. I need to do embroidery to prepare my dowry. Father will let you go.”

Yue Deng nodded. “Then I’ll go this afternoon.”

Shen Weici shook her head. “Go to my father now and get the waist token. By midday, everyone will be at meals. Then you can leave.”

Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici. “Then will Miss be alone on the way back?”

Shen Weici adjusted her sleeve and sighed. “Don’t worry about me. I’ll wait for you in Lingchun Courtyard. Just go quickly and return quickly.”

Only then did Yue Deng agree and take another path.

The medicine had been bitter, and Shen Weici knew it was harmful. But if she hadn’t drunk it, her father would have thought her ungrateful.

She pressed her fingers against her chest, leaning against the plum tree for a while longer before continuing on her way.

Song Zhang stood on a pavilion not far away, watching Shen Weici’s movements. His dark eyes were as deep as an abyss, his emotions flickering.

It wasn’t until he saw her walking alone that his gaze shifted slightly, and his figure disappeared from the pavilion.

The flagstone path, dusted with snow, was slippery. Fortunately, the snow hadn’t been heavy, and as long as she avoided the untrodden areas, it was fine.

Her courtyard was secluded, almost at the depths near the rear garden. Few people passed by, and the cleaning was neglected. The flagstone path still bore traces of snow, but it had a certain charm.

She walked slowly. As she lifted her skirt to cross a bridge corridor, she suddenly stopped. Not far ahead, Song Zhang’s russet figure was walking toward her. Because of last night’s incident, she instinctively wanted to avoid him.

Seeing that he seemed to be getting closer, Shen Weici decided to turn onto another path leading to a scenic pavilion. Although it overlooked a lake at the end, at least she wouldn’t have to meet him on the same road.

Song Zhang’s phoenix eyes watched the figure in the distance pause and change direction. His lips pressed down, and his gaze turned cold.

So she was deliberately avoiding him.

Shen Weici sat in the pavilion, gazing at the lake, intending to wait until Song Zhang left before she moved. But as she was lost in thought, she suddenly noticed a reflection in the water. Startled, she turned her head and saw Song Zhang standing behind her, his hands clasped behind his back.

He was tall and slender, his bright russet robes making him appear more flamboyant than usual.

As always, he wore a black leather belt and wrist guards, but today he had no weapon at his waist—only a single white jade pendant with a dual-beast pattern, as if dressed for leisure.

Shen Weici felt as if something were stuck in her throat. She didn’t know how to speak, so she simply turned back to look at the lake.

Song Zhang sat down beside her, resting his long arm on the railing. His gaze was fixed on her pale profile. “Are you ill again?”

As he spoke, he leaned slightly forward and sniffed. Seeing her somewhat weary appearance, he said, “I smell medicine on you.”

Earlier, he had seen her leaning against the plum tree, looking unwell. He wondered if she had caught a chill last night.

He couldn’t help but reach out to touch her cheek.

Shen Weici’s face changed when she saw his approaching hand. She turned her head away, then glanced at him from the corner of her eye before lowering her gaze again. “I’m not sick.”

Song Zhang watched her evasive movement and raised an eyebrow. His hand froze in midair for a moment before he withdrew it, not pressing the matter. He looked at her indifferently. “Then why do you smell of medicine?”

Shen Weici felt that after last night, she could no longer speak to him properly. She didn’t understand how he could still approach her so calmly.

She truly did not want to see this man.

She pressed her fingers against the railing, closing her eyes briefly to compose herself before speaking softly as usual. “My mother prepared tonic for me.”

With that, Shen Weici stood up and looked at Song Zhang, who remained seated on the bench, watching her. She almost wanted to flee this place in panic, yet she had to steady her nerves to deal with him. “There are some matters in the courtyard. Lord Song, I’ll take my leave.”

She turned to leave, but her wrist was suddenly gripped by Song Zhang.

He looked at Shen Weici’s clean wrist—the bracelet had been removed.

His dark eyes met hers calmly. “Miss Shen, are you in such a hurry? Can’t you even spare a moment to sit with me?”

Shen Weici didn’t hesitate to refuse. “There are many things to attend to in the courtyard...”

Before she could finish, Song Zhang cut her off with a cold laugh.

She looked at him in bewilderment, only to see the coldness in his indifferent gaze. Those sharp, cold eyes bored into her, as if seeing through all her panic and pretense. His voice was low. “So eager to return to prepare your dowry?”

“The Earl’s mansion and your marriage are settled. Are you so impatient to marry into their family?”

Shen Weici instinctively looked up at Song Zhang. “You said last night...”

But before she could finish, Song Zhang suddenly released her wrist and stood up in front of her, forcing her to take a step back.

She only felt the imposing presence of his broad back as he loomed over her, his eyes full of aggression. “What did I say last night?”

“You like Zhang Yuanheng, don’t you? Why ask so many questions?”

“You’re avoiding me like this—what else do you expect me to say to you?”

Shen Weici stood there in a daze. By the time she came to her senses, he was already walking away. She belatedly watched his tall, retreating figure, her heart inexplicably heavy.

She repeatedly pondered the meaning of his words, and the more she thought, the more her heart sank.

But she couldn’t bring herself to ask him again.

When she returned to Lingchun Courtyard, Yue Deng had already come back. Seeing Shen Weici, she asked, “Miss, can we eat the bird’s nest that Second Madam sent last night?”

“Or should I take it out and sell it?”

Shen Weici looked at Yue Deng. “Bird’s nest is hard to carry. If you take it out, it’ll draw too much attention.”

“Besides, if it’s poisoned, selling it would only harm others.”

Yue Deng abandoned the idea. Seeing Shen Weici leaning back in her chair, lost in thought with a weary expression, she went over and asked, “Miss, what’s wrong?”

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.content:
On the second day, Shen Weici went to Old Madame Shen’s place early in the morning.

The servant at the door was somewhat surprised to see Shen Weici, as she rarely came here.

She led Shen Weici inside. Old Madame Shen was also slightly surprised to see her, as she had assumed Shen Weici would not want to come after the incident with Zhang Tingyi.

Old Madame Shen sat in her armchair, with a pretty young maid sitting beside her, reading scriptures. Upon seeing Shen Weici enter, the maid fell silent.

Shen Weici entered the warm chamber, greeted Old Madame Shen properly, and said, “My legitimate mother has arranged a marriage for me with the Duke of Yiyong. She says I am to marry before the New Year.”

“Since I’ve been in the Marquis’s residence for so long and have not yet had the chance to show filial piety to Old Madame, and with only a month left before my wedding, I thought I should come and attend to you for a while.”

Old Madame Shen looked at Shen Weici’s gentle and modest demeanor. Though she was not as openly affectionate as Shen Zhaozhao, who would immediately lean into her, Shen Weici’s proper conduct and refined manner were more in line with the bearing of a noble lady.

Moreover, Shen Zhaozhao had not visited her since the last time she was punished, which had disappointed Old Madame Shen slightly.

Old Madame Shen looked at Shen Weici, her expression softening into a faint smile. “It’s good that you have such a heart. I don’t need you to attend to me. Just stay in your courtyard and prepare for your marriage.”

Shen Weici, lips curved in a smile, walked behind Old Madame Shen. “I have not yet had the chance to show filial piety to Old Madame. With my wedding approaching, please allow me to fulfill some of my duties.”

As she spoke, she placed her hands on Old Madame Shen’s shoulders. “I learned some massage techniques before. Let me give you a shoulder rub, Old Madame. If you like it, I will come again next time.”

Old Madame Shen smiled. “Then let me try your skills.”

Shen Weici, smiling, began to massage Old Madame Shen’s shoulders.

Indeed, Shen Weici had studied under an old physician for a few days in the past. As a child, she had been close friends with the daughter of the Yuyang Medical Hall. After school, she would sometimes visit her friend’s home and watch her father perform tuina on others. Curious, she had picked up a few techniques, which now came in handy.

Her strength was neither too light nor too heavy, but her technique was excellent. Old Madame Shen, eyes half-closed, could not help but praise comfortably, “You are quite capable. You know a little of everything.”

Shen Weici moved to massage the back of Old Madame Shen’s neck and softly said, “As long as Old Madame likes it, I will come again tomorrow.”

Old Madame Shen smiled. “You are a filial child.”

Shen Weici pursed her lips. As her fingers pressed a certain point, Old Madame Shen suddenly cried out in pain. The servant beside her hurriedly asked, “Old Madame, what’s wrong?”

But Shen Weici said to Old Madame Shen, “Just now, your granddaughter pressed the Chengling acupoint. Have you been experiencing headaches, dizziness, and some shortness of breath recently?”

Old Madame Shen, upon hearing this, turned to look at Shen Weici. “How do you know?”

Shen Weici lightly laughed. “Old Madame’s pain at the Chengling acupoint reveals the problem.”

“But I have a prescription here. If Old Madame trusts me, drinking it once a day will alleviate the symptoms.”

Old Madame Shen, realizing Shen Weici had some skill, unconsciously trusted her and asked, “What prescription?”

Shen Weici then said to the servant beside her, “Trouble Auntie to fetch Physician Xing. I will tell him the herbs needed, have him note the quantities, and then have him prepare the medicinal meal for Old Madame.”

The servant looked at Old Madame Shen, who said, “Go quickly and fetch him.”

Shen Weici returned to massaging Old Madame Shen’s shoulders.

Soon, Physician Xing arrived. After exchanging pleasantries, Shen Weici said, “The prescription is simple: two qian of Gastrodia and Pinellia, two qian of Cassia seed and three qian of Atractylodes, one qian of Achyranthes and Uncaria. Stew them in chicken broth for two hours, and once the medicinal properties are extracted, it will be ready.”

Physician Xing listened to the prescription and looked at Shen Weici. “I never thought to add Achyranthes. That is indeed a good herb. How do you know about this?”

Shen Weici smiled and was about to speak when Yue Deng arrived with the medicine, followed closely by Constant Auntie. “Miss, your tonic is here. Drink it quickly.”

Shen Weici acknowledged and was about to take the bowl when Physician Xing, standing beside her, suddenly changed his expression and urgently said, “Third Young Lady, wait.”

Shen Weici was startled and looked at Physician Xing, puzzled. “What’s wrong?”

Physician Xing, with a grave expression, took the bowl from Shen Weici’s hands and carefully smelled it.

Constant Auntie, seeing this, had a slight change in her expression.

Physician Xing smelled it and then looked at Shen Weici. “I cannot be mistaken. There is the scent of safflower in here. Regular consumption can cause sterility.”

He looked at Shen Weici solemnly and asked, “Who brewed this medicine? This is harming someone!”

Old Madame Shen, hearing this, sat up straight. “What is this about? Is it the maids from Linchun Courtyard causing trouble?”

Shen Weici, now in shocked suspicion, looked at Old Madame Shen. “This medicine was a special tonic brewed for me by my legitimate mother.”

She then glanced at Constant Auntie beside her. “My legitimate mother had Constant Auntie deliver it to me every day...”

Old Madame Shen’s expression darkened. She forcefully slapped the armrest of her chair, her face gloomy. “What is she trying to do!”

She then ordered two of her personal servants, “You two, take a few maids and quickly go to the second courtyard to fetch the medicine pot. I must investigate this thoroughly.”

The two servants, upon hearing this, quickly left.

Constant Auntie, listening beside them, was alarmed. She tried to quietly slip away but was stopped by Yue Deng. “Constant Auntie, where are you going? Does this medicine contain safflower?”

Constant Auntie’s forehead was covered in cold sweat. Old Madame’s gaze was too piercing, and she truly did not know how to respond.

The medicine indeed contained safflower. But she had been told that safflower had a unique scent, and other herbs were specifically used to mask it, making it impossible to detect.

Originally, this medicine was to be sent to Linchun Courtyard. But Yue Deng had said that Shen Weici had gone to Old Madame’s place, and she, not trusting Yue Deng to deliver it, had followed along to ensure no mistakes were made.

On the way, the medicine had been in her hands. Somehow, a stone had appeared on the path, nearly tripping her. At that moment, Yue Deng had held the medicine for a short while, but she had been watching.

Moreover, when she had just handed the medicine to Yue Deng to give to Shen Weici, there should have been no mistake.

She truly could not understand how Physician Xing had detected it.

But she had never smelled safflower before, and the maid who brewed the medicine had not noticed anything either. What was wrong?

Old Madame Shen saw that Constant Auntie, Madame Wen’s personal servant, was trembling and unable to speak. She understood everything.

This was the second branch’s doing. Seeing that someone was about to marry, they wanted to ensure she could not have children.

How could Madame Wen do such a vicious thing!

Shen Weici stood to the side, hands clasped, looking anxious. But from the corner of her eye, she noticed Constant Auntie’s panicked expression before calmly looking away.

Madame Wen had given her medicine to harm her body, to prevent her from conceiving. No wonder she had to have a servant watch her drink it and take the bowl back.

chapters.title: The Ridiculous Face
chapters.content:
In a short while, the medicine pot was brought over, followed by Madame Wen, who looked flustered.

Old Madame Shen glared at Madame Wen, then ordered Physician Xing to examine the remaining dregs in the pot.

Physician Xing quickly fished out the dregs to inspect them. Madame Wen tried to have someone rush over to take the pot away, but she was firmly restrained by Old Madame Shen’s servants.

After a while, Physician Xing set down the dregs in his hand and hesitated before saying to Old Madame Shen, “The medicine in the pot contains safflower, coptis, anemarrhena, and white peony root. Almost all of them are cold and bitter herbs, and the dosage is quite high. If someone with a cold constitution drinks this for half a month, their body will be very difficult to nurse back to health.”

“Moreover, drinking this medicine will not cause any immediate discomfort, but a cold constitution is already hard to treat. Safflower is a forbidden herb for pregnancy and can cause great harm to the body.”

Old Madame Shen’s face darkened as she tightly pursed her lips, glaring coldly at Madame Wen. “What do you have to say for yourself?”

Madame Wen was in complete disarray. She had never expected this matter to be exposed in front of Old Madame. She had lost her composure.

Originally, she had been sending medicine to Shen Weici every day for her to drink, and she would not have noticed anything. In just half a month, Shen Weici would never be able to have children. Why had Old Madame found out?

She knew she absolutely could not admit to it.

Madame Wen suddenly stood in front of Old Madame and cried, “Old Madame, please be fair. Weici is, after all, the blood of the Master. How could I, your daughter-in-law, do such a thing?”

“I had good intentions and left this matter to the servants to handle. I never expected the medicine to be filled with harmful cold herbs.”

As she spoke, Madame Wen pointed at Constant Auntie and sternly asked, “I ordered you to find a physician to prepare a tonic. Why has the medicine turned out like this?!”

“Did you tamper with it?!”

Madame Wen then stepped forward and slapped Constant Auntie. “You wicked old thing, daring to harm the young lady of the Marquis’s residence! Today, you will be taken out and given thirty strokes of the rod, then driven out of the Marquis’s residence!”

Constant Auntie, hearing this, understood what was happening. The Second Madame was trying to push the blame onto her.

Thirty strokes would leave her old bones with no hope of survival.

She had served the Second Madame for decades, and now that trouble had come, she was to be discarded. It truly chilled her heart.

She decided to fight back, wailing as she knelt down and cried to Old Madame Shen, “Even if this old slave had ten thousand times the courage, I would not dare to harm the young lady of the Marquis’s residence.”

“I have no grudge against the Third Young Lady. Why would I do such a thing? It was all the Second Madame’s orders.”

Madame Wen, upon hearing this, flew into a rage and kicked Constant Auntie. “You old hag, how dare you spout nonsense! Do you believe I will have your daughter brought here as well, to be beaten together, and then sell your daughter to a brothel?”

“I have raised you and your daughter so highly, yet you dare to be ungrateful!”

Shen Weici listened quietly, finally understanding why Madame Wen dared to push Constant Auntie forward. Constant Auntie and her daughter’s contracts of servitude were in Madame Wen’s hands. This was the sword hanging over her head, leaving her at Madame Wen’s mercy.

She closed her eyes briefly, then glanced at Old Madame Shen’s expression with her peripheral vision. In her heart, she had already guessed the outcome.

Sure enough, upon hearing Madame Wen mention her daughter, Constant Auntie was rendered speechless for a long time, only wailing on the ground.

Madame Wen, with a look of disgust, called her servant and pointed at Constant Auntie on the ground, sternly ordering, “Hurry up and tie her up, take her outside to be beaten. If she doesn’t die, then drive her out to fend for herself!”

Old Madame Shen had not spoken again. After all, this matter, if made public, would be a disgrace. If it spread, it would be an even greater disgrace.

Everyone knew the truth: the legitimate mother was harming the illegitimate daughter, trying to ensure she could not have children. If this spread, the second branch would not be able to hold their heads high in the capital.

She closed her eyes, remaining silent for a long time before saying, “Since this was done by that old servant, she must be properly punished. Beat her and drive her out.”

Old Madame Shen then looked at Constant Auntie, her expression dark. “If anyone dares to speak of this matter outside this room, I do not care who spreads it or who says it—if I hear even a whisper, every maid in this room will be sold to a brothel, and every old servant will be given thirty strokes.”

Her cold gaze swept across the room. “Do you all understand?”

At Old Madame’s words, all the servants in the room knelt down and kowtowed in unison.

Constant Auntie was gagged and dragged out by the maids.

In the end, Old Madame Shen took Shen Weici’s hand and sighed, “Fortunately, you were with me today, or you would have been secretly harmed by that old wretch.”

She then asked with concern, “How much of it have you drunk?”

Shen Weici, composed, softly replied, “I have drunk it for two days.”

Old Madame Shen nodded with some relief. “It’s good that it was only two days.”

She quickly called Physician Xing to check Shen Weici’s pulse. “You, come and see if Weici’s body has been harmed.”

Physician Xing quickly came over to check Shen Weici’s pulse. After a while, he said to Old Madame, “Her pulse seems fine, but to be safe, she should drink a warming medicine to dispel the cold.”

Old Madame Shen nodded. “This matter is in your hands. Prepare the medicine and have someone deliver it to Linchun Courtyard.”

Physician Xing nodded, seeing that there was nothing more for him to do here. Staying any longer would be awkward, so he quickly took his leave.

As soon as Physician Xing left, the room fell silent.

Old Madame Shen patted Shen Weici’s hand. “Since this matter has been clarified, you may go back and rest. I will have a few more words with your legitimate mother.”

“Later, I will have someone send you a proper cloak. The weather is getting cold, and your body is weak. A good cloak will help keep you warm.”

Shen Weici knew this might be Old Madame’s way of compensating her. If she continued to make a fuss, it would show she did not understand the situation.

She obediently nodded, bid farewell to Old Madame Shen and Madame Wen, and then withdrew.

She lowered her gaze and lifted the curtain of the warm room. Just as she stepped out, she heard the sound of a cup shattering inside.

She did not linger, gathering her sleeves as she walked away.

After walking a distance, Yue Deng, indignant, looked at Shen Weici. “How can Old Madame be so biased? The truth is so obvious, yet she does not blame the Second Madame at all!”

Shen Weici paused in front of a banana leaf and looked at Yue Deng, softly saying, “Don’t you understand?”

“Old Madame, to maintain the face of the second branch, will never make a big deal out of this. Having an old servant take the blame is the best outcome.”

Shen Weici looked up at the white snow covering the branches in the distance and murmured, “Why can the Second Madame act so unscrupulously? Because she knows that noble families value face above all else.”

“And the life of an old servant... what does that matter?”

chapters.title: Not a Forbidden Relationship with the Second Cousin
chapters.content:
In the afternoon, an old servant from the Dowager’s courtyard delivered a fur-lined cape with cloud-and-smoke lotus embroidery and gold-threaded rolling edges. The servant placed the cape in Shen Weici’s hands and smiled, “This cape is a treasure of the Dowager’s, and it’s even inlaid with pearls.”

“The Dowager noticed that your current cape is too thin and cares for your health.”

Shen Weici quickly took it with a smile. “Weici understands the Dowager’s kindness and will remember her grace. Tomorrow, I will go pay my respects to her.”

The servant watched Shen Weici’s gentle expression, her eyes filled with smiles, and her face showed no sign of grievance or resentment. Earlier that morning, the Dowager had clearly shown favoritism, and the servant had assumed she would be upset. But now, seeing her calm and composed, speaking softly as if she had already forgotten the morning’s events, the servant thought to herself:

This is the bearing of a true noble lady—she doesn’t dwell on small matters. Her words are pleasant, unlike the Second Young Lady, who would immediately show displeasure at the slightest provocation.

No wonder the Dowager has started to praise the Third Young Lady.

The servant smiled. “The Dowager knows that the Third Young Lady is filial. Just take care of your health these days.”

With that, the servant took her leave, her face still kind.

Only then did Shen Weici lower her head to examine the cape in her hands. The lotus patterns were stitched with gold thread, shimmering faintly in the light, exuding an air of luxury.

Yue Deng stood beside Shen Weici, looking down as well. She couldn’t help but say, “This cape is truly beautiful. The Dowager is so generous—it seems she has started to value you, Miss.”

Shen Weici’s gaze fell on the pearl at the collar. She softly replied, “It’s not that the Dowager values or pities me particularly. She just doesn’t want me to speak of what happened today.”

Her fingers brushed against the pearl as she murmured, “I wouldn’t have intended to speak of it anyway. If the Dowager wants to suppress it, then speaking out would only put me against her. There’s no need to insist on justice.”

“In any case, I won’t be drinking that medicine anymore.”

Yue Deng pulled over a stool and sat beside Shen Weici. “But won’t the Second Madam resent you even more after this?”

“What if she tries to harm you again in the future?”

Shen Weici, looking somewhat weary, closed her eyes. “Just be careful for this month. Once I’m married, she’ll have to stop.”

As she said this, Shen Weici slightly opened her eyes, gazing absently at the charcoal fire. She took the cassia tea Yue Deng handed her and sipped it, but the unease in her heart refused to settle.

She couldn’t pinpoint what was wrong—perhaps it was the haste of the marriage. But she did want to marry soon. Or perhaps it was the slight look of surprise on Lady Wen’s face when she had given her birth chart that morning, as if she had never intended to ask for it.

Then there was what Song Zhang had said to her the other day—it didn’t sound like a joke or a lie.

And there was the way Zhang Yuanheng had hesitated that night, as if he had something to say but held back...

A sudden headache struck her. Fatigued, she rubbed her temples. Too many thoughts tangled in her mind like a messy knot, and she couldn’t sort them out.

Just then, He Xia entered with a bowl of medicine. “Miss, the medicine from Physician Xing is ready. Please drink it.”

Shen Weici, disliking the bitter taste, hesitated. But then she thought about the medicine Lady Wen had sent—what if it really affected her health? She took the bowl.

The medicine was extremely bitter. Even someone as tolerant as Shen Weici couldn’t suppress the churning in her stomach. She leaned back in her chair for a long time before recovering, then took a sip of the tea Yue Deng brought to rinse her mouth.
