She glanced out the window at the thin layer of snow, which glistened sharply in the light.

Supporting herself on the armrest, she stood up and lay down on the bed, turning her back to Yue Deng. With little energy, she spoke hoarsely, “Yue Deng, I’m going to take a nap. Don’t wake me.”

Yue Deng hummed in acknowledgment, then removed the hairpins from Shen Weici’s hair and tucked her in before lowering the bed curtains.

In the evening, after dinner, Shen Weici sat by the lamp, working on a pair of mandarin duck love knots to hang in the bridal chamber on her wedding night, symbolizing a good omen.

Yue Deng sat beside her, assisting, and whispered, “This afternoon, when the Second Master returned, he was immediately summoned to the Hall of Longevity by the Dowager.”

“It must be about this morning’s incident. Hopefully, the Second Master will stand up for you this time, Miss.”

Shen Weici glanced at Yue Deng, then lowered her gaze back to the embroidery. “How do you know this?”

Yue Deng smiled. “I had Yan’er wait at the intersection to see if the Dowager would call for the Second Master.”

Shen Weici paused her hands and sighed, looking at Yue Deng. “You have too much idle time. If any servant girl from the Dowager’s courtyard had seen her standing there, wouldn’t they guess her intentions? Wouldn’t the Dowager suspect me of scheming?”

Yue Deng laughed. “Don’t worry, Miss. No one saw.”

Shen Weici sighed softly. “Next time, don’t go to such lengths. I never expected my father to stand up for me anyway.”

As she spoke, her gaze settled on Yue Deng. “And why should you expect it either?”

Yue Deng froze, unable to respond for a long time.

Just as she was about to fall asleep, He Xia entered with medicine, her expression hesitant as she looked at Shen Weici. “Miss... Young Master Song is here again...”

“He’s sitting on the chair behind the screen.”

Her voice grew quieter. “This servant couldn’t stop him.”

Shen Weici stiffened at the mention of Song Zhang’s arrival. She truly didn’t want to see him these days.

Taking the medicine bowl from He Xia, she kept her expression blank and spoke softly, “I asked Prince Song to bring something. Perhaps he’s delivering it. You may go rest now.”

He Xia nodded and left.

But as she passed Song Zhang, she saw his dark, forbidding expression, his long legs sprawled as he leaned back in the chair, exuding an intimidating aura like a god of death. Frightened, she quickly hurried out.

Inside the bed curtains, Shen Weici held the medicine bowl, not intending to speak first.

As she brought the bowl to her lips to drink, she suddenly saw Song Zhang enter the bed curtains without hesitation.

His tall, slender figure stood at the head of the bed, dressed in a purple official robe with a jade belt, his hair bound by a golden crown. The hilt of his sword pointed straight at Shen Weici’s face, and his strikingly handsome features were cold.

The chill he carried seemed to fill the room, and his cold gaze made her pause as she was about to drink. She looked up at him. “Prince Song, do you enter my boudoir without any regard now?”

Song Zhang gave a cold laugh and sat directly on the edge of Shen Weici’s bed. His dark eyes glanced at the medicine bowl in her hands before settling back on her. “Tell your maid to leave. I need to speak with you alone.”

Shen Weici had been uncomfortable around him since those two incidents and no longer wished to be alone with him.

She turned her face away, avoiding his gaze, and looked down at the bowl in her hands. “It’s not as if we have anything unspeakable to discuss. And we are not in that kind of unspeakable relationship. Prince Song, just speak.”

chapters.title: Shen Weici, Do You Think I’m Easy to Fool Again?
chapters.content:
The space inside the bed curtains was small, and Yue Deng’s body was pressed to the side by Song Zhang’s towering figure. She had already sensed the tension in the air.

Shen Weici ignored the coldness radiating from Song Zhang and the chill on his face. She silently lowered her head and drank her medicine.

Song Zhang always barged in like this, completely disregarding her reputation. With Yue Deng by her side, she felt more distance between them, sparing her the awkwardness of being alone with him.

But just as she took a sip, a sudden thud came from beside her. Shen Weici turned her head in surprise to see Yue Deng lying on the floor.

Startled, she quickly placed the medicine bowl on the bedside and tried to get up to check on Yue Deng’s injuries.

But a broad chest suddenly blocked her view. A large hand pressed down on her shoulder, and a deep voice came from above her head: “She’s fine. I just sealed her acupuncture point.”

Shen Weici felt a flicker of irritation. She pushed against Song Zhang’s chest, still trying to get up. “Even if that’s the case, falling like that—how could she not be hurt? What if she hit something—”

Before she could finish, she felt her chin being pinched, and his thumb pressed against her lips. His deep, dark eyes gazed down at her. “I caught her with my leg. She’s fine.”

Shen Weici froze. She reached up to push away Song Zhang’s wrist, but he let go first.

The next moment, she saw him throw something into her hand. His dark eyes locked onto her. “Did you use this?”

Shen Weici stared blankly at the object in her hand. It was the red flower pill she had asked Yue Deng to buy. This kind of pill had a strong scent and was used by brothel women on their navels as a contraceptive.

If ingested, it could also induce a miscarriage.

Shen Weici had bought it to have Yue Deng grind it into powder and mix it into the medicine, making the scent stronger so that Physician Xing would notice it.

She looked at the dark expression in Song Zhang’s eyes, unsure what he had guessed, and asked, “Did you have someone follow my maid?”

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici with a cold gaze, his eyes flicking to the medicine bowl on the bedside. His face remained icy. “Is this what you’ve been using?”

Shen Weici realized he must have misunderstood that she was secretly using this herself.

Even though it was none of his business whether she used it or not, she didn’t know why he had come to confront her about it.

She still shook her head in explanation. “I use it as an incense ingredient.”

“Ground into powder and mixed with incense, it helps to calm the mind.”

Song Zhang gave a cold laugh. “Such a cooling medicine for calming the mind? Don’t you know this is the most taboo medicine for women?”

Shen Weici looked up at Song Zhang. “I don’t use much. It doesn’t affect me.”

Song Zhang watched Shen Weici’s cold and indifferent demeanor, and a wave of frustration rose in him.

He picked up the medicine from the bedside and asked, “What’s wrong with you now?”

As he spoke, his brows furrowed impatiently. “What kind of body do you have? Why are you falling ill every other day?”

Shen Weici silently took the medicine bowl from Song Zhang’s hands and softly replied, “It’s just a cold. Not a serious illness.”

With that, she lowered her head to drink the medicine, thinking that if she didn’t drink it now, it would get cold.

She also valued her own health and knew that Lady Wen’s medicine must contain something harmful. Even though this medicine was bitter, she had never considered not drinking it.

Moreover, Shen Weici had no intention of telling Song Zhang about this. She didn’t want anyone to intervene on her behalf, nor did she want to make a fuss out of it. In the end, the one who would suffer the consequences would always be herself.

Shen Weici’s voice was soft and gentle, like a warm breeze.

Song Zhang looked down at Shen Weici holding the medicine bowl, her delicate brows carrying a hint of uneasy melancholy, always restraining her temper.

He then noticed her fair, slender fingers resting on the celadon bowl, her neatly trimmed nails glowing faintly. The sleeves of her light-colored inner robe had slipped down slightly, revealing her delicate, fair wrists.

Every part of Shen Weici seemed to enter Song Zhang’s dreams and thoughts.

Even though other beautiful women might have the same features, why did he find Shen Weici more captivating?

Her every gentle and graceful movement, her always unhurried demeanor—it was a kind of tenderness he had never encountered before, making him unable to resist drawing closer to her.

He couldn’t help but recall the way she had composed poetry and played the game of *shuanglu* chess.

She was different from many other women—neither arrogant nor impatient, her charm seeping into one’s heart.

After finishing the medicine, Shen Weici endured the bitterness in her mouth and the discomfort in her stomach. She propped herself up to place the empty bowl on the bedside table, her gaze falling on Yue Deng, who was still unconscious on the floor.

She closed her eyes briefly, suppressing her emotions before speaking softly, “Prince Song, have you finished what you wanted to say?”

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici’s frail appearance, the usual coldness in his eyes fading slightly. Then, noticing her averted profile, he suddenly realized that she rarely looked at him directly.

In his presence, she either turned her head away or lowered her gaze, her eyes never willingly resting on him.

He recalled the heartless words she had said to him before. Why was he still chasing after her?

Song Zhang wanted to leave, but now he inexplicably felt like he, too, had become that pathetic man who was desperately pursuing her.

The slight warmth that had just softened his eyes vanished, and the coldness in his dark gaze deepened like ink.

He looked at her and asked, “Where’s the rest of the red flower pills?”

Shen Weici paused. “I threw them away.”

She had indeed thrown them away—into the lake. That was the safest place. Once dissolved, they would leave almost no trace.

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici with a detached expression. “Shen Weici, do you think I’m easy to fool again?”

Shen Weici was taken aback by his tone. She turned her head to look at him. “The incense I made didn’t smell good, so I didn’t use it. This afternoon, I had my maid throw it away.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici rubbed her temples and sighed. “Prince Song, rest assured. I wouldn’t use such things to harm others, let alone use them on myself.”

“I know it’s harmful—why would I use it?”

Song Zhang fell silent. In truth, he believed Shen Weici’s words.

Though she had some schemes, she wouldn’t harm others.

He had come to ask her because he was afraid she might use it on herself.

His mind had raced with a million thoughts—had she and Zhang Yuanheng done something in secret, leading her to buy such things?

His subordinates had told him that her maid had been acting suspiciously, and he couldn’t help but jump to conclusions.

But now, looking at her, and thinking it over, the two of them wouldn’t have had the chance to be alone together.

Moreover, someone as reserved as her wouldn’t do such a thing. He had overthought it.

In truth, he had been worried about her.

The anger and unease that had nearly overflowed in his heart had already subsided.

Her full lips still glistened, the taste of medicine mingling with her own scent, like a silent temptation.

But seeing Shen Weici’s pale face and the fine sweat on her forehead, he forcibly stopped himself from leaning forward.

His voice softened. “Did you finish the medicine I gave you last time?”

If Song Zhang hadn’t mentioned it, Shen Weici would have almost forgotten.

She shook her head. “Not yet.”

Her voice was fine and hoarse, and upon closer listening, it carried a faint obedience that made Song Zhang’s throat tighten again.

chapters.title: Reckless
chapters.content:
The warm, flickering candlelight was the most alluring.

Song Zhang seemed unable to extricate himself. His body repeatedly clamored to get closer to her, yet he couldn’t bring himself to beg for her affection.

He knew that right now, her heart was set on marrying Zhang Yuanheng, and she was probably filled with thoughts of him.

Her refusal still echoed in his ears.

Once again, Song Zhang suppressed his feelings. He got up from her bedside and strode out.

Only after Song Zhang left did Shen Weici finally let out a breath of relief. She hurriedly got up from the bed to pat Yue Deng’s face, but no matter how many times she slapped, Yue Deng wouldn’t wake up. She had no idea what acupoint Song Zhang had pressed.

It was too cold to leave someone on the floor. Shen Weici supported Yue Deng and placed her on the bed, then draped her outer robe over herself, intending to go to the side room to sleep.

The side room was unlit, and there was no charcoal fire on the floor. A cold draft hit her as soon as she entered.

Shen Weici held the candle, intending to bring over a charcoal brazier. But in the dim light, she suddenly felt a shadow loom before her. The lamp in her hand went out, and then her eyes were covered. Her lips and tongue were sealed by someone, and her body was pressed against a broad chest, falling backward onto the small couch behind her.

Besides the sound of the lamp shattering on the floor, there was hot breath at her ear, scorching enough to make her whole body tremble.

She tried to reach out to struggle, but it was as if she were surrounded by a thick, dark fog—no matter how she stretched or struggled, she could never find an end.

“Miss—”

“Miss?”

A distant, fluctuating voice reached her, as if she were still lost in a dream.

In the dream, a pair of long fingers were wantonly undoing her clothes. Those wet, hot kisses moved from the corner of her lips all the way down, until she gathered her collar with all her strength, covering the places that shouldn’t be seen.

But that hand grew bolder and bolder, and her strength was no match for his.

She pleaded over and over, “Don’t—”

“Don’t—”

But her limbs grew weak, and no matter how she struggled, it was useless.

“Don’t.”

A panicked cry escaped her throat. Shen Weici broke out in a cold sweat and suddenly awoke from the dream. She opened her eyes to the hazy candlelight. The person in front of her was blurred, as if everything around her was unfamiliar.

She stared blankly at the flickering candle, then dazedly lost her thoughts again. “A dream…”

Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici’s absentminded expression with concern and couldn’t help but squeeze her hand. “Did Miss have a nightmare?”

Yue Deng’s familiar voice brought Shen Weici back to her senses. In the dim candlelight, she made out Yue Deng’s face and suddenly remembered the dream.

Pale-faced, she quickly turned to look beside the small couch. There was no broken lamp on the floor.

The area around the small couch was clean—nothing at all.

Only two charcoal braziers burning to the side.

She remembered she had intended to bring a charcoal brazier over last night.

She looked at Yue Deng. “What time is it now?”

Yue Deng, seeing the fine sweat on Shen Weici’s forehead, said worriedly, “It’s almost the Mao hour. Miss should go to the second courtyard to pay respects.”

As she spoke, Yue Deng asked again, “How did I end up sleeping on Miss’s bed last night? And why did Miss sleep here?”

Shen Weici bent over, supporting her forehead. She felt a slight headache.

Her long hair cascaded down her back and coiled onto the blanket. She remained silent for a long time.

Then, she lowered her gaze to her undershirt. The collar was neatly fastened, just as it had been the night before—unlike in the dream, where it had nearly been undone.

Perhaps it was just a dream.

She let out a sigh of relief.

Leaning on the edge of the small couch, Shen Weici glanced at Yue Deng and briefly recounted last night’s events.

Yue Deng followed Shen Weici into the inner room and couldn’t help but say, “No wonder my neck hurts this morning. So it was him who did this.”

“That’s really unreasonable.”

Shen Weici stood in front of the bed screen, letting Yue Deng dress her. Watching Yue Deng’s indignant expression, she softly said, “He has always been unreasonable.”

After she was dressed and had washed up, He Xia’s voice came from outside: “Miss, it’s snowing outside now.”

Shen Weici had Yue Deng open the window, and a gust of wind and snow rushed in.

Yue Deng, afraid the cold air would chill the room, quickly closed the window again.

She went to fetch the cape that the Old Madam had given her. “Miss should wear this today. This white otter fur is really warm, perfect for snowy days.”

Shen Weici felt that wearing the Old Madam’s gift to see Lady Wen would be too conspicuous, so she had Yue Deng bring her old floral cape instead.

Yue Deng hesitated but obeyed, though she had Yan’er prepare a hand warmer.

Before leaving, Shen Weici went into the side room once more and counted the lamps in the room. None were missing. Only then did she feel at ease, assuming it had all been a dream.

But she had never had such a reckless dream before, and it left her uneasy. Even as she stepped out of the house, she still felt disoriented.

A cold wind carrying a hint of snow blew against her, and she gradually regained some clarity.

Yue Deng helped Shen Weici secure the hood of her cape. “The snow seems heavy today. I don’t know if the paths have been swept. Miss should be careful on the way.”

Shen Weici nodded and stepped down the stairs, with Yue Deng following with a lantern.

But the lantern was made of paper, and the wind made it sway precariously. Yue Deng ended up holding it in her hands.

Halfway there, she said softly, “If only we had a glass lantern. It could be used even in rain or snow.”

“I think the Second Young Lady uses a glass lantern.”

Shen Weici said nothing. One hand held her cape closed, the other clutched the hand warmer. She lowered her head and walked silently. Snowflakes dotted her eyebrows, bringing a slight chill.

A moment later, Yue Deng’s voice came again: “It seems like Second Young Master Song is coming from the opposite direction.”

Shen Weici dreaded hearing that title the most. She dreaded facing Song Zhang.

She froze, then lifted her gaze. Before she could even look up properly, Song Zhang had already walked up to her.

Perhaps because he was a martial artist, he was only wearing his official robes, with no padded overcoat. Tall and straight, every time Shen Weici encountered him, she had to take a step back and tilt her head up to meet his gaze.

Despite her reluctance to see him, Shen Weici still greeted him politely: “Prince Song.”

Song Zhang looked down at Shen Weici’s small face, framed by the hood of her cape. Her nose and cheeks were reddened by the wind and snow, and her cape was so thin it was almost laughable—more suited for spring or autumn.

He frowned, then glanced at the paper lantern in Yue Deng’s hands, his expression darkening further.

Then he noticed Shen Weici’s fingers tightly clutching her cape. She didn’t seem like someone who could endure the cold, yet she was dressed so lightly, without even a proper windproof hood.

He thought of her dilapidated Chun Spring Courtyard—the only place in it that held any refinement was where she stayed.

He reached behind him, took a glass lantern from his servant’s hands, then pulled Shen Weici’s fingers out from her cape. Her hand was ice-cold to the touch. He stared deeply at her downcast eyes, then pressed the lantern into her hand.

chapters.title: I Will Not Wrong You
chapters.content:
In the rustling snow, Shen Weici looked at Song Zhang with some bewilderment.

Her hand was tightly enclosed in his warm, large hand. Even in this cold, snowy weather, his hand was still somewhat scorching. It reminded her of the hand that had roamed her body in last night’s dream.

She didn’t know why she suddenly thought of this. Just as she was about to push the lantern back, she saw Song Zhang had already turned and walked away without a word.

Shen Weici blinked. She turned to see that Song Zhang’s servant still held another lantern. Then she looked down at the lotus-petal beaded glass lantern in her hand. It was inlaid with jewels on all sides, extremely precious, and quite heavy.

Yue Deng was delighted. “This glass lantern is really beautiful. It must be very expensive.”

She looked up at Shen Weici, confused. “What does Second Young Master Song mean by this? Is he giving the lantern to Miss?”

Shen Weici looked down at the lantern again, then placed it in Yue Deng’s hands. “Regardless of whether he meant to give it or not, something this precious—I cannot accept it.”

With that, Shen Weici tightened her cape and continued walking.

When they reached the entrance of the second courtyard, they happened to meet Shen Zhaozhao and Shen Yanli.

Shen Zhaozhao’s expression changed abruptly upon seeing Shen Weici. The coldness in her eyes was unhidden as she walked straight past Shen Weici.

Shen Weici watched Shen Zhaozhao’s retreating back, then followed behind her.

Inside the main hall, there was no sign of Lady Wen. Only Shen Rongsheng was seated in the upper position.

Shen Zhaozhao didn’t see her mother, so she hurriedly asked, “Where is Mother?”

Shen Rongsheng glanced at Shen Weici, then said to Shen Zhaozhao, “Your mother has been ill these past few days. You don’t need to come pay your respects.”

Shen Zhaozhao was taken aback. “How come I didn’t know Mother was ill?”

She was about to go inside to see Lady Wen, but before she could take a step, Shen Rongsheng stopped her. “Don’t disturb your mother while she’s recovering. You may leave for now.”

Shen Yanli asked Shen Rongsheng, “What illness does Mother have?”

Shen Rongsheng frowned, his face stern. “Why so many questions? Have you finished reading the essays I brought back for you? If you don’t pass the autumn imperial examination next year, you’ll be sent to a remote post!”

Shen Yanli, inexplicably scolded by his father, didn’t dare ask further. He simply left the room first.

Shen Rongsheng watched Shen Yanli’s retreating figure, then turned to Shen Zhaozhao. “You may leave as well.”

Then, to Shen Weici, he said, “Weici, stay.”

Shen Zhaozhao glanced at Shen Weici, her expression twisted and ugly. Her fingers dug into her palm, but she still turned and left with her maid.

Shen Weici more or less guessed what her father wanted to say. After Shen Zhaozhao left, she looked up at her father and asked, “What does Father wish to say?”

Shen Rongsheng looked at his daughter, standing quietly before him. He recalled what his mother had said to him the previous afternoon.

His mother had said that Shen Weici had a clever and considerate heart, knew how to act with propriety, and with proper upbringing, she would not be any worse than Shen Zhaozhao. He should assert his authority in the household and not let the women suppress him. Otherwise, the inner household would become even more chaotic.

He sighed and said to Shen Weici, “I already know about yesterday’s matter. Tell me honestly, do you blame your mother?”

Shen Weici looked up at her father and shook her head. “Daughter has never blamed her. If Mother and Father had not agreed to let Daughter come here, Daughter would have been forced by Grandmother to marry the old squire as a concubine.”

“Now that Daughter has secured a marriage with the Earl’s family, it is all thanks to Father and Mother’s arrangements. Daughter is only grateful and cherishes the days in the Marquis’s residence.”

“Even after marrying into the Earl’s family, Daughter will often return to pay respects and always remember Father and Mother.”

Shen Rongsheng’s eyes reddened as he listened. He had assumed Shen Weici would have some complaints, but her words instead filled him with a pang of guilt.

He knew that since Shen Weici had entered the Marquis’s residence, Lady Wen and Zhaoshuo had not treated her well, and she had endured many hardships. Yet she had never spoken a word of complaint in front of him. Even now, with just the two of them, she did not speak ill of anyone.

Not to mention the cold words and looks Shen Zhaozhao often gave her—he found it uncomfortable just to hear, yet she had always endured in silence.

In truth, even if Shen Weici had complained to him, he would have understood.

This time, Lady Wen had gone too far. She had given Shen Weici that potent medicine, intending to make her unable to bear children in the future.

The consequences of a woman being unable to bear children were severe. Even if she were divorced later, there would be no fault to blame, and she would never be able to remarry. It was a cruel and vicious act.

This daughter was so understanding that it pained his heart.

He said to Shen Weici, “Let the matter with your mother pass. Don’t bring it up again. I know you’re sensible. The Old Madam has also praised you. I will prepare a more generous dowry for you.”

Shen Weici’s eyes reddened, her voice hoarse. “Daughter has always known that Father has been good to Daughter. Daughter has never held a grudge. The matter with Mother was the doing of a maid. How could Daughter bring it up again?”

“I only hope to marry soon so that Father and Mother can live in harmony again, and no longer worry about Daughter’s affairs.”

“In the future, Daughter will often go to the temple to pray for Father and Mother. It will be my way of showing filial piety.”

Shen Weici was the epitome of gentleness and grace. With her eyes reddened and tears welling, even though Shen Rongsheng had not felt much affection for this daughter before, he now found her words warming and felt even more pity for her.

His chest swelled with emotion. He said in a low voice, “You are a good child. From the moment you entered the Marquis’s residence, I could see that you were an obedient child.”

“I will not wrong you.”

Shen Weici bowed her head in gratitude.

As she left the second courtyard, Shen Weici’s expression gradually turned cold. She looked up at the snow still falling heavily from the sky and exhaled a white breath.

The tears in her eyes were gradually dried by the cold wind, as if they had never been there.

Shen Zhaozhao stood behind Shen Weici with a dark expression, watching her leave. Then she turned back to the second courtyard to see her mother.

By this time, Shen Rongsheng had already left for court. The personal maid serving Lady Wen saw Shen Zhaozhao enter and quickly blocked her way. “Second Young Lady, the Lady is not inside.”

Shen Zhaozhao was startled and quickly asked, “Where is my mother?”

The maid pulled Shen Zhaozhao aside and whispered, “The Lady has been locked in the side room at the back of the courtyard by the Master. For the past three days, no one has been allowed to enter except to deliver meals.”

“The Master said to let the Lady reflect properly over these three days. You shouldn’t go either, lest the Master returns and gets angry.”

Shen Zhaozhao’s expression changed. She quickly asked, “Why did Father suddenly do this?”

The maid hesitated but eventually told Shen Zhaozhao, “The Lady was careless this time. Who would have thought that the quiet one from Chun Spring Courtyard would be so formidable? She even won the Old Madam’s favor.”

“You must endure for now. Wait until the Lady is let out, then we can talk.”

Shen Zhaozhao almost crushed the handkerchief in her hand. Gritting her teeth, she coldly hissed, “That cheap woman, Shen Weici—”

chapters.title: The Gifts from Song Zhen
chapters.content:
After returning, by morning, Shen Weici had Yue Deng bring the cloak given by the Old Madam and put it on, then went to the Old Madam’s Cishou Hall to give her a shoulder massage.

Shen Weici did this indeed to leave a good impression on Old Madam Shen.

If she wanted her marriage to go smoothly, even if the Madam Wen made things difficult for her, as long as the Old Madam could give the final say, it would be fine.

Even if her engagement to Zhang Yuanheng fell through, and she was to be betrothed to another family in the future, the Old Madam could still speak up for her, preventing Madam Wen from arbitrarily finding a family to marry her off to.

She knew that no matter how much she humbled herself, Madam Wen would never accept her. But with the Old Madam, there was still a chance.

Shen Weici was quiet and composed in the Old Madam’s presence. She did not deliberately fawn or seek favor, but earnestly gave the Old Madam a shoulder massage, then sat beside her and read scriptures for a while before leaving.

As she was about to leave, the Old Madam held her hand, “The weather is getting colder. Since you’re getting married before the New Year, go to the hot spring villa with the other young ladies in the mansion in a few days to ward off the cold.”

“Your body seems frail, and you’ve been taking cooling medicines. Soaking in the hot springs will do you good.”

Shen Weici knew that her visit to the Old Madam had been the right move. She wasn’t particularly eager to go to the hot spring villa, but she knew that she had at least left a trace of pity in the Old Madam’s heart.

That trace of pity was enough for her.

Shen Weici knelt on the ground and kowtowed to the Old Madam, tears falling as she said, “Since I came to the Marquis’s mansion, I have known that the Old Madam has been kind to me. It was the Old Madam who took me in back then.”

“The Old Madam has shown me such kindness, and I will always remember it. In the future, I will surely speak well of the Old Madam to others.”

The Old Madam listened to these words and felt an inexplicable emotion. Back then, she had taken her in to marry Zhang Tingyi, but now the girl was kneeling before her in gratitude, and she suddenly didn’t know how to respond, feeling a slight pang of guilt.

Now she was known as the old poisonous woman outside, and hearing Shen Weici say she would speak well of her, her heart stirred again.

She quickly had the servant beside her help Shen Weici up, holding her hand as she sighed, “In the past two days you’ve been here, I can see that you are a filial girl. Having such a heart is enough.”

“Your conduct and appearance are both excellent. This engagement is finally satisfactory, and it hasn’t wronged you. I can rest at ease now.”

Shen Weici expressed her gratitude again before taking her leave just before noon.

The Old Madam watched Shen Weici’s retreating figure, then suddenly turned to her personal servant and asked, “Do you think that girl Weici has said or done anything improper in my presence?”

Servant Ren also watched Shen Weici’s gradually disappearing figure, bending down to whisper to the Old Madam, “The Third Young Lady’s behavior is impeccably proper. She speaks softly and gently, does things without unnecessary words, and is earnest in her actions. Moreover, her demeanor is elegant and refined. Compared to the Second Young Lady who seeks amusement before the Old Madam, the Third Young Lady is more considerate in doing things for the Old Madam.”

“I truly cannot find any fault with her.”

Shen Weici’s figure had long since disappeared from the doorway. The Old Madam took the tea served by the maid and sighed as she drank, “She does everything perfectly. Just now, when she knelt before me, I was truly moved.”

“But I also feel that it’s too perfect—so much so that not a single fault can be found.”

Servant Ren laughed, “This is a good thing. The Third Young Lady is so outstanding that she attracts attention outside. The Marquis’s mansion’s illegitimate daughters are all so well-raised—isn’t that also the mansion’s reputation?”

“Moreover, the Third Young Lady seems quite capable. Last time, she sent that sachet, and you’ve been sleeping much more soundly these days, haven’t you?”

The Old Madam smiled, “That is true.”

“She gave me a shoulder massage twice, and my body does feel more comfortable.”

Servant Ren smiled, “It seems the Third Young Lady is thoughtful. She’s not just blindly trying to please you.”

The Old Madam nodded, then sighed again, “It’s just a pity her birth is too low.”

Upon leaving, Shen Weici returned to Linchun Courtyard. As soon as she entered, He Xia rushed over, “Miss, come in quickly and take a look. The maids from the Second Master’s courtyard have sent over many things!”

Shen Weici was taken aback and entered the small hall, where she saw several boxes placed on the table, pushing the original incense burner and vase of flowers to the side.

Shen Weici ran her fingers over the finely carved box in front of her and asked He Xia, “Did they say what they were sending?”

He Xia shook her head, “Miss Xun Mei delivered them and left immediately. She said they were all gifts the Second Master had specially prepared for you.”

Shen Weici’s fingers paused as she looked at He Xia, “Gifts?”

He Xia smiled, “Didn’t you send sachets and pouches to each courtyard some days ago? Second Master Song is returning the favor.”

As she spoke, He Xia couldn’t help but look at the boxes in front of her, “I knew Second Master Song was generous, but I didn’t expect that even a return gift would be so much.”

“No wonder all the sisters wanted to serve in Guansong Residence.”

Shen Weici’s gaze dropped as she casually opened the topmost box. Seeing its contents, she paused—it was a white fox fur hood.

She closed the box and had Yue Deng pick it up, then opened the next one. Inside was a peach-red brocade cloak lined with white sable fur.

The brocade was embroidered with pearls at each flower’s center, shimmering beautifully under the sunlight.

Yue Deng, catching a glimpse, couldn’t help but exclaim in admiration before the box was closed again.

Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici standing motionless at the desk and whispered, “That cloak looks even more precious than the one the Old Madam gave you. It’s lined with white sable fur—how warm it must be. Miss, you won’t have to fear the cold anymore.”

Shen Weici turned to look at the wind and snow outside, then lowered her head to gaze at the gifts Song Zhen had sent. She didn’t understand why he had suddenly sent so many things.

It was just one sachet, given as thanks to him. She couldn’t accept such a lavish return gift.

She noticed another small box beside the others, picked it up, and opened it. She paused again—it was a whole ginseng root.

She quickly closed the lid and said to Yue Deng, “You and Yan Er take everything back. Tell him I appreciate his kindness, but the gifts are too valuable. I dare not accept them. I’ll apologize later.”

He Xia hesitated, looking at Shen Weici, “Miss, these are such fine things. Are you sure you don’t want them?”

Shen Weici shook her head and said softly, “One should not accept rewards without merit. If I take his gifts, I’ll owe him a favor. I already owe him one—I cannot accept more. Take them back.”

He Xia, hearing this, hurried with Yan Er to carry the things back to Guansong Residence.

Yue Deng watched the gifts leave with regret, still sighing over the cloak—it was truly beautiful. It would look so good on Miss.

She turned and saw Shen Weici lifting the curtain to go inside, so she quickly followed.

Meanwhile, Xun Mei looked at the returned gifts from Linchun Courtyard and panicked inside, not knowing how to explain this to her master.

chapters.title: She Did Not Want to Accept His Kindness
chapters.content:
By nightfall, Song Zhen, worried about her, left the palace early. At the palace gate, he found the carriage of the Duke of Song’s mansion blocking the way.

Song He’an jumped down from the carriage, looking at Song Zhen with exasperation, “Your grandmother hasn’t seen you in over half a month. This time, you must come back with me.”

“Otherwise, if the Old Madam personally goes to the Marquis’s mansion to find you, I won’t be able to stop her.”

Song He’an was the eldest son of Song Zhen’s third uncle and worked in the Ministry of Justice. He was two years younger than Song Zhen.

Song Zhen knew he hadn’t visited the Duke of Song’s mansion to see his grandmother in a long time. After some thought, he got into the carriage with Song He’an.

Inside the carriage, Song He’an smiled softly at Song Zhen, “You haven’t been back in a long time. Your cousin sister, Rong Jin, has been missing you terribly. She personally made many of your favorite dishes, waiting for your return.”

Then he teased, “The Old Madam is determined to make your marriage happen. Cousin Rong Jin is beautiful, and over the years, I’ve seen her at the Duke’s mansion—she’s considerate, gentle, virtuous, and favored by the Old Madam.”

“Don’t refuse. I don’t have your kind of luck.”

Song Zhen raised an eyebrow, then leaned back against the chair without speaking, knowing this would be another tedious visit.

The Old Madam was the hardest to deal with.

When Song Zhen left the Duke of Song’s mansion, it was already late at night. He stood at the grand gate of the mansion under the winter snow, his tall and straight figure exuding an imposing presence that made it hard for people to look away.

Zheng Rongjin chased after Song Zhen’s retreating figure to the front gate. Watching him leave even in such heavy snow, she couldn’t help but look up at Song Zhen, already mounted on his horse. The large snowflakes fell on his shoulders and hair, making him look exceptionally handsome and noble in the snow.

Yet, his pair of cold phoenix eyes remained distant, like a wild beast poised to strike, exuding a terrifying power in his calmness that made people slightly fearful.

Summoning her courage, she took a step forward and said softly, “The Old Madam’s health hasn’t been good lately. Brother Song, you should come visit her more often.”

“Besides, it’s already so late at night. Brother Song, do you have such urgent business?”

Song Zhen frowned and glanced at her sideways, too lazy to respond. With a flick of the reins, he disappeared into the night.

Zheng Rongjin stood there, watching Song Zhen’s fading figure, her heart filled with loss.

At the banquet, her cousin hadn’t even glanced at her once. Was she that unlikable?

When Song Zhen returned to the Marquis of Jian’an’s mansion, his body was covered in snow. Ming He was waiting at Guansong Residence and handed a letter to Song Zhen as soon as he arrived, “It’s from Xinyang.”

“It’s related to the Second Prince.”

Song Zhen took it, standing under the corridor to read the letter.

After finishing, he raised an eyebrow, tossed the letter into the lantern’s flame, and said indifferently, “Have him stay in Xinyang for now. Wait for my news.”

With that, he turned and entered the room, only to see several boxes placed on the table. His gaze shifted, and he noticed the glass lamp he had sent over that morning.

His face darkened instantly.

Xun Mei approached Song Zhen and said softly, “When the maid from Linchun Courtyard returned the things, she said that the Third Young Lady appreciated the Second Master’s kindness but found the gifts too valuable. She would come to apologize another day.”

Song Zhen had originally planned to return early today to see if Shen Weici liked the gifts. Unfortunately, he had been delayed and couldn’t visit her, thinking he would see her tomorrow morning and ask if the cloak was warm enough.

Yet, she had refused his kindness so outright.

What more was there to say? She clearly wanted to reject any connection with him, wholeheartedly waiting to marry into the Earl’s mansion.

Song Zhen’s face remained stern as he turned to look into the night.

Shen Weici woke from her dream in a cold sweat, her back damp.

She sat up, her gaze blankly fixed on the closed bed curtains. Outside, the faint flicker of candlelight was still visible.

Everything around her was quiet.

Shen Weici pressed her forehead, breathing lightly. Her long hair fell down her back as the rapid beating of her heart continued in her chest.

Exhausted, she closed her eyes. The man’s scorching hands from her dream seemed to linger on her body once more.

She was pinned tightly beneath him, his chest pressed against hers. She parted her lips, allowing his tongue to explore her mouth as unfamiliar sounds escaped her throat.

The ambiguous sounds of water and his hot breath seemed to echo in her ears again. Cold sweat broke out on her forehead as she stared at the brocade quilt in front of her, lost in thought.

Then, belatedly, she looked down at her collar, which was still perfectly neat—unlike in her dream, where a playful hand had undone it.

She exhaled, pressing her fingers against her still restless chest to calm its pounding.

In the morning, when Yue Deng entered to wake Shen Weici, she found her already awake, sitting inside in a daze.

Yue Deng was startled, “Miss, when did you wake up? You don’t need to go to the Second Courtyard to pay respects today. I thought you were still asleep and could sleep a little longer.”

Shen Weici sat up on the edge of the bed, looking at the tightly closed flower-lattice window, “Is it snowing heavily outside?”

Yue Deng nodded, “Today’s snow is even heavier than yesterday’s. When it gets light, Miss can go out and enjoy the snow—it will surely be beautiful.”

Shen Weici stood up, letting Yue Deng help her dress, her voice soft, “We’ll see after I go to the Old Madam’s.”

Yue Deng hummed in agreement and followed her to the washroom.

The warm, damp towel on her face helped Shen Weici’s slightly dazed expression improve.

Since she didn’t need to pay respects that morning, everything was slow and leisurely, almost lazily so.

Perhaps because she hadn’t slept well the night before, she felt a weariness in her body and a lack of energy. Sitting in front of the bronze mirror, she let Yue Deng style her hair, often spacing out.

Just as Yue Deng was about to insert a silver hairpin into her hair, He Xia hurriedly lifted the curtain and entered, “Miss, Second Master Song is here.”

Shen Weici glanced at the window outside—it was still dark—and thought about pretending she was still asleep to avoid him.

At this moment, she didn’t want to see anyone, and she more or less guessed why Song Zhen had come.

But before she could speak, the curtain was lifted from the outside, letting in a gust of cold air. Who else could it be but Song Zhen?

She saw his shoulders dusted with snow, his purple robe with gold trim, and his tall, slender figure making the already small room feel slightly cramped.

His dark eyes were cold, one hand holding the box Shen Weici had returned the day before, the other resting on the hilt of his sword. His bold and cold phoenix eyes glanced at Shen Weici before he directly walked over to place the box on the table. Then, with a commanding presence, he sat down on the chair, his heavy gaze fixed on Shen Weici, who was still sitting in front of the mirror.

Yet, he remained silent.

Shen Weici felt a chill run down her back. In the bronze mirror, she could see Song Zhen’s gaze as their eyes met in another way.

Shen Weici looked at those aggressive eyes and inexplicably thought of the predatory eyes from her dream.

Those eyes had never left her body, even when he had forced himself on her, they had stared deeply into hers.

After a long moment, Shen Weici realized her own absentmindedness. She turned her body slightly, then turned her head to look at Song Zhen sitting on her chair, pondering how to speak.

chapters.title: Too Afraid to Accept Gifts from Young Master Song
chapters.content:
The room was very quiet.

Song Zhang sat there like a cold-faced Buddha, his expression extremely cold. Anyone who glanced at him would feel that this young master was suppressing his anger.

Yue Deng and He Xia, who were standing in the room, also felt inexplicably uneasy.

Shen Weici lowered her gaze, gathered her thoughts, and spoke softly, “Is Young Master Song upset that I returned the gifts?”

Song Zhang’s face was stern, his dark eyes fixed on Shen Weici’s profile. He watched the delicate earrings swaying on her beautiful jaw, her brows slightly furrowed, warm light flickering. Her slender figure was still graceful, her hands holding an embroidered handkerchief, gently placed on her lap.

This white fabric with sparrow patterns suited her extremely well. She was a graceful and delicate beauty, her voice soft and slow, almost dissipating the displeasure in his heart.

He raised an eyebrow, a cold smile on his lips, waiting for her explanation.

Shen Weici, seeing that Song Zhang wasn’t speaking, sighed, “What reason do I have to accept Young Master Song’s gifts?”

“That pouch was just a cheap trinket. Young Master Song sent such valuable things; I feel unworthy accepting them. Using them would make me uneasy, and I wouldn’t be able to reciprocate Young Master Song’s kindness.”

“I wouldn’t dare accept Young Master Song’s gifts.”

Song Zhang coldly smiled, “Do I need you to return them?”

“If this young master is happy to give you gifts, are you too afraid to accept them, or do you simply not want to have any connection with me?”

Shen Weici intended to reason with Song Zhang properly. She looked at him, “I see that among the gifts Young Master Song sent, there was a ginseng root, which must be very valuable.”

“I am grateful for Young Master Song’s kindness, but such precious things...”

Before she could finish her sentence, she saw Song Zhang suddenly stand up. His tall shadow loomed over her, and his deep voice rang out above her head, “This young master gives what he wants to give.”

“If you send them back again, I will send them over again tonight.”

“If Miss Shen wants to see me so much, I don’t mind making more trips.”

Shen Weici was taken aback and looked up at Song Zhang, asking, “Why does Young Master Song insist on giving me these things? I have nothing to give in return.”

Song Zhang listened to Shen Weici repeatedly talking about returning his gifts. His dark, swirling eyes were filled with suppressed emotions. If it weren’t for the fact that she looked exhausted, he might have said something even harsher.

She had accepted the tonic gifts from Zhang Yuanheng, but his gifts were too valuable for her to accept.

She really knew how to draw a clear line.

Keeping him at a distance.

He couldn’t tell if her feelings were truly so fond of Zhang Yuanheng.

He couldn’t tell why he was so eager to pursue her.

Clearly, she had rejected him. Normally, he wouldn’t have paid her any more mind.

Song Zhang suppressed his anger and didn’t want to hear Shen Weici speak again. He directly walked past her.

Once outside, the cold and stern snow wind blew. Song Zhang frowned and said to Ming He, who was approaching, “Deliver the letter to her.”

“Don’t intercept them anymore in the future.”

Let her know what kind of person Zhang Yuanheng really was. He wanted to see if she would still like him.

After saying that, he strode away with long steps.

Inside the room, Shen Weici watched Song Zhang leave after coming so early in the morning. She looked at the things on the table and knew that, given Song Zhang’s temperament, she definitely couldn’t return them again.

So she had Yue Deng collect the items.

Yan Er twisted a glass lamp as she entered, “Miss, this is also a lamp left by Second Young Master Song. It looks really beautiful. Should Miss keep it?”

Shen Weici stood up from the dressing table, “Put it there. It can be used in the snow.”

Yan Er’s face lit up with joy, and she repeatedly agreed.

Shen Weici walked to a chair and sat down. She took the hot tea that Yue Deng brought, lowered her head to look at the charcoal fire, her expression still listless, lost in thought.

In the morning, she went to the old madam’s place again. Seeing that the old madam was drinking the medicinal meal she had mentioned last time, she asked about it. The old madam praised her with great delight.

Shen Weici only smiled slightly.

But just as she was halfway through massaging the old madam’s shoulders, Shen Zhaozhao suddenly entered. Seeing Shen Weici standing behind the old madam, massaging her shoulders, the two of them occasionally laughing and talking, the scene was very harmonious.

Her expression changed. In the past, in the Marquis’s residence, the only one who could be so close to the old madam was her.

Shen Weici noticed Shen Zhaozhao entering. She furrowed her brows slightly, smiled faintly, and then lowered her eyelids.

Shen Zhaozhao quickly took off the cloak from her body and threw it to a maid, then rushed a few steps to nestle in the old madam’s arms, acting coy, “Grandmother, your granddaughter hasn’t come to see you for a couple of days. I’ve missed you.”

The old madam smiled, holding Shen Zhaozhao’s hand, “Then what have you been doing these two days?”

Shen Zhaozhao replied, “Mother has been in a bad mood these days, so your granddaughter has been keeping her company.”

The old madam’s smile faded slightly upon hearing this, but she still held Shen Zhaozhao’s hand, “It’s good that you keep your mother company.”

Shen Zhaozhao glanced at Shen Weici again, acting coy, “Granddaughter hasn’t talked to you for a long time. Can Third Sister go back first?”

Shen Weici could hear the implication in her words. There wasn’t much reason to stay here anymore. She had already done enough to show her respect to the old madam. Since Shen Zhaozhao had arrived, she should leave, which would show that she didn’t hold a grudge.

Shen Weici took the initiative to approach the old madam and bid farewell, then also said goodbye to Shen Zhaozhao.

Shen Zhaozhao coldly watched Shen Weici’s demeanor, then noticed the cape with embedded pearls in Yue Deng’s hands. The pearls were too eye-catching to ignore.

She knew this was something from the old madam’s room. In the past, she had wanted it too, but she didn’t expect it to be awarded to Shen Weici.

Her expression changed abruptly, and the ferocity in her eyes was almost impossible to hide. She let out a cold humph.

The old madam also heard this humph. Seeing that Shen Weici’s expression didn’t change at all, her calm and considerate nature made the old madam like her even more.

She told Shen Weici to go back first, then looked at Shen Zhaozhao and sighed, “Speak, did you come because of your mother?”

Shen Zhaozhao pouted and wrapped her arms around the old madam’s neck, “It’s all that woman framing Mother. But Father...”

Shen Weici, standing at the doorway, only faintly heard this sentence. She didn’t stay, nor did she have the mind to listen further. She had already guessed it.

Outside, the branches were covered with a layer of white.

Yue Deng couldn’t help but say, “The snow here is heavier than in Yu Yang, and it comes earlier.”

Shen Weici walked to a pavilion, looking at the desolate snowy scene, and silently calculated the days in her mind.

It seemed that she wouldn’t be getting married for much longer. Now, thinking about it carefully, it felt like a dream.

It was indeed cold outside. Shen Weici, in the cold winter, felt a faint ache in her knees. She couldn’t stay long. Just as she was about to turn back, she met Shen Mingqiu. The two sat and talked for a while.

When Shen Mingqiu heard that she was going to stay at the hot spring villa for a day, she happily said she would go back and pack her things to bring over.

After the two parted, Shen Weici returned to Linchun Courtyard. He Xia handed her a letter, “Miss, the front gate said it’s a letter from Young Master Zhang.”

Shen Weici paused, looking at the letter in He Xia’s hand, then asked, “Did Lai Fu deliver it?”

He Xia shook her head, “No.”

Shen Weici nodded and took the letter inside.

chapters.title: Sarcasm
chapters.content:
She went back and leaned against the couch. She hadn’t slept well last night, and even now, her spirits were still not great.

Her body was soft and weak as she leaned sideways against the pillow behind her. She then began to open the envelope in her hand.

Beside her, Yue Deng held a cup of hot tea. The newly inserted plum blossoms on the desk emitted a faint fragrance. The incense burner wafted with light smoke, and the room was so quiet that she could almost hear the sound of the snow falling outside.

The letter was two pages long, written in Zhang Yuanheng’s handwriting.

The letter asked how her health had been recently. It also mentioned that although the snow had been heavy these past few days, he had been tied up with trivial matters and feared he wouldn’t be able to go and enjoy the snow. He would have to wait until after the New Year to take her.

The last few lines were less restrained than his usual reserved and subtle style. He wrote a few slightly bolder words of affection, hoping she would write back to him. He also said that once his rest day came, he would visit to check on her health.

Shen Weici thought that the day after tomorrow would be his rest day.

However, if Zhang Yuanheng came to see her, she inexplicably feared that he might run into Song Zhang, and this engagement, which she had finally settled, might encounter unexpected troubles.

But Zhang Yuanheng coming to see her also eased some of the unease she had felt these days.

The old madam and her father were both concerned about her settled engagement, so there shouldn’t be any more problems.

Shen Weici stood up and went to the desk to write a letter. She said that her health had greatly improved recently and that he didn’t need to worry about her.

She also told Zhang Yuanheng that if he was too busy, he didn’t need to come. She was busy preparing her dowry and just wanted to marry him peacefully.

At the end, fearing that Zhang Yuanheng might overthink, she still wrote a couple of affectionate words to comfort him before signing off.

After the ink dried, she had Yue Deng take the letter to be delivered. She also told her to see if Lai Fu was there. If he was, have Lai Fu deliver it; if not, have the same young servant who delivered the letter earlier take it.

She also gave two tips.

Yue Deng took the letter and quickly went to the front gate.

At the front gate, Lai Fu was not seen, so she handed the letter to A Shun. Watching A Shun deftly take the letter and run out, she stood at the front gate and watched for a long time before returning.

However, this letter ultimately did not reach Zhang Yuanheng’s hands.

Song Zhang held the letter written by Shen Weici and glanced at it indifferently. He had someone deliver it to the Earl’s residence.

Then, he brushed off the snow from his clothes and walked towards Chengde Hall.

This day, Shen Weici was sitting with Shen Mingqiu, making mandarin duck sachets.

Shen Mingqiu had come early these past two days to learn embroidery from her. The two chatted on and off, and the afternoon passed.

At this moment, Yue Deng suddenly entered and whispered into Shen Weici’s ear, “Miss, Young Master Zhang is here.”

Shen Weici was taken aback and looked up at Yue Deng, softly asking, “Where?”

Yue Deng whispered, “In the Mei Shan Pavilion in the back garden. That place is very close to the master’s study. It was someone from Second Master’s side who came to say so.”

Shen Weici was stunned. Her fingers loosened, and she suddenly felt a pain at her fingertip. Looking down, she saw that, in her distraction, the needle had pricked her finger, and a small bead of blood had already formed.

Shen Weici quickly put her finger in her mouth. Her eyes gazed at the embroidery fabric, lost in thought.

Beside her, Shen Mingqiu noticed and asked, “Third Sister, how did you prick your hand? Is it serious?”

Shen Weici shook her head and said to Shen Mingqiu, “Young Master Zhang has come to visit Father. Father asked me to go and see Young Master Zhang. I can’t stay with you anymore, little sister.”

Shen Mingqiu smiled, “Then naturally, Sister’s matters are important. Hurry and go see Young Master Zhang.”

“Now that Sister is about to marry into the Earl’s residence, Young Master Zhang probably can’t wait to see his little sister.”

With that, she stood up, “Then I’ll go back first. I’ll come again another day.”

Shen Weici nodded. After watching Shen Mingqiu leave, she pondered for a moment, then had Yue Deng fetch her cape and went out.

When she arrived at Mei Shan Pavilion, Zhang Yuanheng was already waiting in the pavilion. Seeing her approach from afar, a smile appeared on his face.

Shen Weici held a hand warmer, her eyes also filled with a smile. She entered Mei Shan Pavilion, greeted Zhang Yuanheng, then walked to a spot about four or five steps away from him and asked, “Has Young Master Zhang been busy lately?”

Zhang Yuanheng paused, then smiled, “Not too bad. I’ve had people rearrange the courtyard again and wanted to ask Miss Shen if she has any preferences?”

Shen Weici smiled and shook her head upon hearing this, “I’m fine with anything.”

Zhang Yuanheng smiled, “Then I can rest assured.”

As he spoke, he watched Shen Weici sit down on a long bench. He personally picked up the teapot from the stone table and poured her a cup of hot tea, then brought it over.

Shen Weici smiled slightly as she accepted it. Then she saw Zhang Yuanheng call his attendant over, who brought a paper package. He opened the package and presented it to Shen Weici with a smile, “Last time I saw you liked eating these, so this time I brought some for you when I came to visit.”

Shen Weici looked at the plum blossom pastry in front of her that Zhang Yuanheng had brought. Seeing him standing beside her, slightly bent over, looking at her with warmth, she couldn’t help but feel a warmth in her heart.

Her eyes filled with a smile as she took one from Zhang Yuanheng’s hand and bit into it. The taste was no different from last time—soft and smooth in the mouth, not too sweet. She took another bite.

Zhang Yuanheng only watched the small, cherry-like lips open and close, plump and red, and unconsciously, he was mesmerized.

He also noticed her wearing a smoke-green embroidered half-high collar dress, with the earrings he had given her in her ears. On her wide sleeves, she wore the bracelet his mother had given her. Her skin was fair and luminous, her hair like clouds, swaying with a spring-like grace. His eyes grew warm as he looked at her.

Sometimes, he thought all of this was like a dream.

Such a gentle and soft woman, when she smiled, it was like a spring breeze. When she lowered her brows, it was like a misty rain. She was like a cinnabar mole on his heart—once seen, impossible to forget.

How lucky he was to have met such a woman.

Then he saw Shen Weici’s peach-blossom-like eyes look at him, and she softly asked, “Won’t Young Master Zhang have one too?”

Her voice made Zhang Yuanheng’s heart tighten.

He saw a strand of hair fall in front of Shen Weici’s eyes. In a daze, he reached out to tuck the strand behind her ear, “I’m happy just watching Miss Shen eat.”

Shen Weici noticed Zhang Yuanheng’s movement. She instinctively wanted to retreat but endured it, lowering her gaze and quietly waiting.

She would soon be his wife. She should get used to such touches.

Her eyes were full of graceful charm, extremely calm, and she waited shyly and timidly for his touch.

Zhang Yuanheng’s heart grew even warmer. He tucked the fallen strand of hair behind her ear.

He was very careful, restraining himself from touching her cheek. But as his fingers left, he couldn’t help but brush against her earlobe.

The warm touch was like the faint, warm fragrance on her.

He could barely control himself. He wanted to see her sitting on the bridal bed, waiting for him, in the next moment.

Song Zhang stood far away, hands behind his back, watching this scene. When he saw Shen Weici lower her brows and wait shyly for Zhang Yuanheng to touch her, a dangerous glint narrowed in his cold eyes.

A sarcastic smile curled on his lips.

chapters.title: To Be a Concubine
chapters.content:
The woman before him was so graceful and gentle that, in the white snow, she seemed as pure and clean as the snow itself.

Suddenly, Zhang Yuanheng felt a pang of guilt and shame.

Seeing that Shen Weici had finished eating, he softly said, “If Miss Shen enjoys it, I will send some every few days. Only the freshly made ones are the most delicious.”

Shen Weici looked up at Zhang Yuanheng, “How can I trouble Young Master Zhang to go back and forth?”

As she spoke, she lowered her gaze again, “I heard that our marriage date has been set, before the New Year. When I marry into the Earl’s mansion, I can eat them then.”

Zhang Yuanheng was stunned, the words stuck in his throat like a fishbone.

Then, a cold voice spoke, “Lord Zhang, do you have time to visit our mansion today?”

Zhang Yuanheng paused at the sound of Song Zhang’s voice and quickly turned to see Song Zhang, dressed in dark clothes, entering the pavilion with his hands behind his back, followed by Minghe, who carried a sword.

Zhang Yuanheng recalled the incident with his purse last time. Although he didn’t want Song Zhang’s compensation, it had been sent to his mansion. Refusing it would be ungrateful, so he had no choice but to accept it reluctantly.

Now, seeing Song Zhang again, Zhang Yuanheng still politely stood up and cupped his hands, “General Song.”

“Today, I have time, so I came to see Miss Shen.”

He and Shen Weici had already discussed their marriage; it was no longer a secret.

Song Zhang gave a faint smile and sat directly beside Shen Weici. He turned to glance at Shen Weici, then looked at Zhang Yuanheng, who was still standing, and said with a smile, “Lord Zhang, why are you still standing? Please, sit down and chat.”

Zhang Yuanheng looked at where Song Zhang had sat, right between them. He couldn’t very well walk around to the other side to sit next to Shen Weici.

He suddenly remembered his purse again and wondered if it had been intentional.

Although he wanted to be alone with Shen Weici, Zhang Yuanheng couldn’t very well ask Song Zhang to leave. So, he sat down on the stone bench.

Song Zhang’s arm, which had been resting on the railing, now lay on the railing behind Shen Weici’s back. From a distance, it looked as if he were embracing her.

Shen Weici also realized the impropriety of this and felt uneasy with Song Zhang’s sudden appearance. She used the excuse of placing her teacup back on the stone table to shift her seat far away from Song Zhang.

Song Zhang noticed all these small movements, a cold smile tugging at his lips, but his gaze remained on Zhang Yuanheng, “Lord Zhang, when is the wedding date for you and Miss Shen? On that day, I will personally escort Miss Shen there.”

“And I will bring my colleagues to congratulate you as well.”

Shen Weici was taken aback and turned to look at Song Zhang.

Song Zhang did not look at Shen Weici; his gaze was fixed on Zhang Yuanheng’s face, “What does Lord Zhang say?”

Zhang Yuanheng was also stunned and quickly stood up to bow, “I am unworthy of such importance from General Song.”

“My mother has already discussed it with the Second Madam of the Marquis’s mansion. Because Miss Shen’s health is poor, we do not plan to hold a grand ceremony to avoid exhausting her.”

Shen Weici looked at Zhang Yuanheng, stunned again.

The man before her was elegant and refined, tall and slender, with gentle features and graceful movements. Yet, at this moment, she felt a slight sense of unfamiliarity.

Without the ceremony, how could it be considered marriage?

She didn’t quite understand his words.

Song Zhang glanced at Shen Weici’s distracted expression, raising an eyebrow in confusion, “Oh? No grand ceremony and no rites?”

After saying this, he scoffed, “An outsider might think Lord Zhang is taking a concubine, not a wife.”

Zhang Yuanheng’s face stiffened at these words, his mouth opening in shock.

Shen Weici noticed Zhang Yuanheng’s expression and turned to Song Zhang, “Young Master Song, could you please leave? I would like to speak with Young Master Zhang alone.”

After saying this, Song Zhang looked down at Shen Weici, his voice low and his eyes seemingly filled with deep meaning as he stood up, “Then I won’t disturb Miss Shen and Young Master Zhang’s conversation. I’ll take my leave first.”

Song Zhang left decisively. Shen Weici watched his retreating figure disappear and then turned back to Zhang Yuanheng, her emotions in turmoil.

Clutching her embroidered handkerchief tightly, she softly asked, “What did you mean by those words just now, Young Master Zhang?”

“My health isn’t so poor that I can’t go through the rites. And these days, I’ve already recovered well.”

“Why must it be this way?”

Zhang Yuanheng looked at Shen Weici’s gaze and suddenly felt a pang in his heart.

He closed his eyes briefly, knowing he could never bear to hide the truth from her.

He sat down beside Shen Weici and had the maids waiting outside the pavilion leave. Only then did he look at Shen Weici and say softly, “Last time, your birth mother came to the Earl’s mansion and mentioned the two times you vomited blood.”

“Your birth mother said you were born with a weak constitution, which is why you’ve been raised in the countryside estate, unable to see many people or get emotionally distressed, otherwise you would vomit blood and faint. The imperial physician said it’s a chronic illness with no cure, only management.”

“My mother refused to agree to this marriage after hearing that, believing your health was too poor to be my wife, let alone bear children for the Earl’s mansion.”

“For those few days, I knelt outside my mother’s room for three days, but she still refused, even threatening to sever our mother-son relationship if I insisted. Even my father wouldn’t agree to me marrying you.”

As Zhang Yuanheng spoke, his eyes filled with pain, “I had already set my heart on you and knew you were waiting for me. I could never let you down. But my mother was too stubborn; no matter how much I begged, she wouldn’t relent. Even when I threatened to resign from my official position, she still refused.”

“In her eyes, having descendants is more important than anything else.”

“She believes your frail body cannot bear children, and nothing I say can change her mind.”

“In the end, my elder brother suggested a compromise: let me first take you as a concubine. Once you bear me a legitimate heir, I will then marry you as my wife.”

Zhang Yuanheng looked at Shen Weici with a pained expression, “I never wanted to hide this from you. I know it’s unfair to you, but I was afraid you wouldn’t agree, so I didn’t tell you.”

“Your birth mother also agreed to help keep it a secret, saying it was all for your own good.”

“With your condition, it would be difficult for you to marry anyone else in the future.”

“But you trust me completely. Even if you are my concubine, I will never take another wife.”

“I will never betray you.”

In truth, these days had been torture for Zhang Yuanheng. He couldn’t bear to deceive Shen Weici, yet he was afraid she would leave him.

He had originally planned to hide it from her until the day she entered his home. After that, nothing could be changed. He would use his actions to give her stability. Even if she could never bear a legitimate heir, he had no intention of marrying anyone else.

He knew that the only person he thought about day and night was her. He wanted to marry her.

For her, he had defied his mother and was even willing to give up his official position. Yet, there were always so many obstacles.

Shen Weici listened to all this in a daze, finally understanding the source of her unease.

Why had the marriage been arranged so quickly? Why hadn’t the Second Madam asked for her birth date? Because for taking a concubine, there was no need for such formalities.

It turned out that the Second Madam had given her those cooling medicines to ensure she could never conceive, dooming her to remain a concubine in the Earl’s mansion forever.

And the Earl’s mansion would never allow Zhang Yuanheng to go without a wife and heirs. They would certainly arrange for him to marry someone else, and she would have no choice but to accept it passively.

This was the trap the Second Madam had set for her. She had hidden it from everyone, even her father and the Old Madam. It seemed she couldn’t tolerate her at all.

Shen Weici felt a sense of disorientation. She didn’t know what to say to Zhang Yuanheng at this moment.

Should she blame him?

She knew she couldn’t.

He had rejected the marriage proposal from the Duke of Song’s mansion for her sake. He had knelt outside his mother’s door for three days for her. Everything he did was for her.

chapters.title: You Will Still Compromise in the End
chapters.content:
At this moment, it seemed to start snowing lightly again. A cold wind blew, and she felt a growing chill.

Shen Weici was silent for a while before looking at Zhang Yuanheng, “Actually, my health is not as poor as my birth mother made it out to be. The vomiting of blood only happens in extreme emotional distress and doesn’t have a significant impact on my health.”

“If I go to the Earl’s mansion tomorrow to explain this to Madam Zhang, would she reconsider our marriage?”

“Inviting a physician to re-examine me in front of Madam Zhang should clear up her misunderstandings.”

Zhang Yuanheng’s straight posture slumped slightly as he said softly, “My mother has already made up her mind about your frail health. Only the prospect of descendants can change her mind.”

“These days, my mother and I have been at odds. She has even fallen ill from my stubbornness and refuses to listen to me anymore. She will only think that all of this is an excuse I’ve made to marry you. She only believes your birth mother’s words.”

“And you did vomit blood twice; that is true.”

Zhang Yuanheng looked at Shen Weici, “Miss Shen, my family is already in turmoil because of me. Please, just comply with my mother this once.”

“Even if you cannot bear me a legitimate heir, I will never take another wife.”

Shen Weici sighed and lowered her gaze, “Young Master Zhang, do you think your mother will allow you to have no legitimate heir?”

“In the end, you will still compromise with your mother.”

Shen Weici didn’t know how to describe her current feelings; she only knew her heart was in chaos.

She stood up and looked at Zhang Yuanheng. In truth, she understood that he had done a lot for her and didn’t want to hurt him.

For a moment, she even felt unsteady on her feet.

She softly spoke, “Young Master Zhang, let me go back and think about it.”

With that, Shen Weici gathered her sleeves and walked out of the pavilion.

Yue Deng and the other maids were waiting outside the pavilion, having not heard what their young lady and Young Master Zhang had discussed.

Noticing Shen Weici’s downcast expression and the furrows of worry between her brows, Yue Deng couldn’t help but ask softly, “What did Young Master Zhang say to you just now, Miss?”

Shen Weici silently shook her head, “Let’s talk about it when we get back.”

Zhang Yuanheng stood up in a daze, watching Shen Weici’s retreating figure, his eyes inexplicably turning red.

He felt as if her figure was gradually moving away from him, and he didn’t have the strength to hold her back.

Everything made him feel trapped in a deep abyss of helplessness, making every step forward increasingly difficult.

On the way back to Linchun Courtyard, Shen Weici saw Song Zhang standing at the crossroads from afar. As she approached, he spoke casually, “Finished talking with Zhang Yuanheng so quickly?”

Shen Weici glanced at Song Zhang, paused, and hummed in response.

She wasn’t in the mood to engage with him. The cold snow fell on her face as she lowered her gaze, clutching her sleeves, intending to walk past him.

Song Zhang watched Shen Weici’s lowered brows, his usually expressionless eyes subtly raising an eyebrow.

He stepped aside without another word, letting Shen Weici pass. Then, he watched her retreating figure with a deepening gaze.

He glanced at Minghe beside him, who immediately understood and ordered another servant to attend to a task.

Back in Linchun Courtyard, Shen Weici looked at the half-finished embroidery of peacocks and mandarin ducks on the table and suddenly felt as if it were an illusion.

She leaned back in her chair, tilting her body to warm herself by the charcoal brazier. She knew she couldn’t just sit and wait for her fate.

The only solution now was to seek the Old Madam’s help.

She couldn’t let the Second Madam control her completely.

Shen Weici turned her head to look at the darkening sky, resting her forehead on her hand as she pondered how to approach the Old Madam the next day.

Yue Deng saw that Shen Weici hadn’t spoken since returning and couldn’t help but ask softly, “What’s wrong, Miss?”

Shen Weici closed her eyes and sighed softly, briefly explaining the situation.

Yue Deng, upon hearing this, was so angry she almost jumped up, “That poisonous woman, the Second Madam, actually did this to you! She hid it from so many people. If Young Master Zhang hadn’t told you today, wouldn’t you have unknowingly married into that situation?”

“This must be told to the Second Master and the Old Madam. Let everyone see how black the Second Madam’s heart is.”

“She’s harmed you once, twice, and now she’s still harming you. It’s truly despicable.”

Shen Weici took Yue Deng’s hand, “Lower your voice. Now is not the time for this. It’s true that I vomited blood twice, but she exaggerated it.”

“This matter must indeed be addressed, but we also need to dispel Madam Zhang’s concerns.”

Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici helplessly, “Should we tell Madam Zhang that your vomiting blood was fake?”

Shen Weici looked up at Yue Deng and then softly, helplessly said, “How can we say that? The vomiting blood must be acknowledged. We can only have the imperial physician re-examine me in front of Madam Zhang to prove that my health won’t affect my ability to bear children in the future.”

“And I am truly in good health and not worried about the results.”

“So, this matter can only be resolved with the Old Madam’s help.”

Yue Deng asked worriedly, “Will the Old Madam help?”

Shen Weici closed her eyes, “Not to mention the rumors outside about the Second Branch, but also, if a young lady from the Marquis’s mansion marries into the Earl’s mansion as a concubine, wouldn’t that be lowering her status? In the future, when the Fourth and Fifth Young Ladies marry, it might be difficult to find good matches for them.”

“This matter, the Old Madam will help me with.”

Yue Deng was relieved, “As long as the Old Madam is willing to help, maybe there’s still a chance to turn things around.”

Shen Weici tapped her jade bracelet with her fingers and said softly, “Having a chance doesn’t mean there really is one. Many outcomes are unpredictable, and it’s impossible for every step to go smoothly without any changes.”

Yue Deng nodded, “But tomorrow we’re supposed to go to the hot spring estate for a few days. Are we still going?”

Shen Weici shook her head, “I can’t go tomorrow. This matter can’t be delayed.”

With that, she got up and went to the bed, lying down wearily and closing her eyes, “I haven’t been sleeping well these past few nights, always having nightmares.”

“Let me rest for a while. Wake me up later for dinner.”

Yue Deng agreed and moved the charcoal brazier closer to the bed before quietly leaving.

Not long after she went outside to sit with He Xia under the corridor and speak softly, Song Zhang arrived.

By now, Song Zhang’s visits to Linchun Courtyard were no longer surprising. The two maids stood up and greeted him, “Second Young Master.”

Song Zhang glanced at Yue Deng sitting outside and asked, “Where is your young lady?”

Yue Deng quickly replied, “Miss has gone to sleep. Second Young Master, if you have any business, please tell me.”

Song Zhang raised an eyebrow. Was she really asleep as soon as she returned?

He had thought she would be hiding in the room, heartbroken.

He looked at Yue Deng and asked, “Are you going to the hot spring estate tomorrow? Is your young lady going?”

Yue Deng hesitated for a moment before shaking her head, “Miss said she’s not going.”

Song Zhang raised an eyebrow again, his gaze deepening, then turned and left.

The next morning, Shen Mingqiu hurried to Linchun Courtyard. As soon as she lifted the curtain, she grabbed Shen Weici’s hand and asked, “Why aren’t you going to the estate?”

“Even the First and Second Branches aren’t going. Only the Third Branch is going. What’s the point?”

“Wouldn’t it be nice to have someone to talk to if you came with me?”

Shen Weici smiled and slowly pulled Shen Mingqiu to sit on the arhat couch, “I originally wanted to go with you, but something has come up, and I need to see the Old Madam. I can’t accompany you for now. I’ll make it up to you next time.”

Shen Mingqiu, hearing this, asked, “What happened?”

Shen Weici pursed her lips and spoke softly, “It’s not convenient to talk about it here. You go ahead and have a good time. When you come back, I’ll find you to talk.”

Shen Mingqiu knew that Shen Weici was reserved and always spoke gently, as if she were always in a good mood.

Although she didn’t ask further, her face showed disappointment, “Without you, it’s no fun going with only Moonqiu and Elder Brother. I don’t have much to talk about with Moonqiu. In the Marquis’s mansion, only you are someone I can talk to. Without you, it’s not fun.”

With that, she stood up, “Forget it. I can’t make things difficult for you if you have business. Let’s talk when I come back.”

Shen Weici softly apologized and saw Shen Mingqiu to the door.

As Shen Mingqiu’s figure gradually disappeared, the smile on Shen Weici’s face slowly faded.

She returned to her room and sat for a while, thinking that the Old Madam should be in the warm pavilion by now. She called Yue Deng to prepare, intending to go to the Old Madam’s place. Yue Deng was about to fetch a cloak, but Shen Weici stopped her, “The cloak isn’t necessary. It’s not snowing today, and dressing lightly might make it seem like I’m in a hurry.”

Yue Deng hesitated, “But even if it’s not snowing, it’s still terribly cold. Miss, why not take a hand warmer?”

Shen Weici sighed and looked at Yue Deng, “Today, I’m going to ask the Old Madam for help. Taking all those things would be cumbersome. Let’s just go.”

Yue Deng had no choice but to comply and followed Shen Weici out.

It wasn’t snowing today, and there was less snow on the ground, but it felt even colder.

The West Courtyard was not as far from the Small West Courtyard as the East Second Courtyard. Shen Weici walked quickly, and as she crossed a plum grove and reached the stone bridge, she heard a voice from behind, “Third Younger Sister.”

Shen Weici paused at the sound and turned to see Shen Zhaozhao approaching from behind.

She responded, “Second Elder Sister.”

Shen Zhaozhao, with her sleeves gathered, stood in front of Shen Weici. Seeing that she wasn’t wearing a cloak or carrying a hand warmer, and was hurrying to the Old Madam’s place, she sneered, “You’ve really gone all out to win Grandmother’s favor.”

“One might think the Second Courtyard didn’t even give you a cloak. Could it be that you’re going like this to appear pitiful in front of Grandmother, hoping she’ll bestow more gifts upon you?”

Shen Weici lowered her eyes, enduring the cold wind that seeped into her collar, “It’s just that my cloak got dirty, and I had the maid take it to be washed. Second Elder Sister, you jest.”

Shen Zhaozhao gave another cold snort and took a step forward, closing the distance between them. She leaned in slightly, the tassels in her hair swaying gently as she spoke coldly, “Do you think I don’t know what you’re thinking?”

“Now that Father is on your side, you still want Grandmother to favor you too. You’re always running to Grandmother to win her over.”

“Are you still coveting the dowry Grandmother might leave for you?”
