Shen Zhaozhao coldly laughed, “Grandmother has always doted on me the most. What are you? Do you really think you can take what’s mine from Grandmother?”

“From now on, I forbid you from going to Grandmother’s place. I’ll be the one visiting her in the future.”

chapters.title: Falling into the Water
chapters.content:
Shen Weici frowned slightly as she looked at Shen Zhaozhao. “Since the old madam dotes on Second Sister so much, why would Second Sister be afraid of someone taking her place?”

As she spoke, Shen Weici lowered her voice. “I never had any intention of taking anything from anyone, but why have Second Sister and my stepmother tried to harm me repeatedly?”

Hearing this, Shen Zhaozhao flew into a rage, gnashing her teeth in denial. “Who has harmed you? Don’t you dare slander us!”

Shen Weici coldly watched Shen Zhaozhao’s ferocious expression. “Did Second Sister not know that you secretly had me married into the Earl’s mansion as a concubine?”

“And what about sending that cold medicine to my courtyard and forcing the servant women to watch me drink it—was that also my fabrication?”

Shen Zhaozhao was taken aback, then raised her hand to strike Shen Weici’s face. “You’re lying! Just look at your status—you’re nothing but a lowly, illegitimate wretch. Do you really think you’re worth my mother and I scheming against?”

“Being allowed to enter the Earl’s mansion as a concubine is already an honor for you, yet you’re still dissatisfied!”

Shen Zhaozhao had always been quick to resort to violence when humiliated. Seeing her raised hand, Shen Weici suddenly regretted engaging with her. At this moment, there was no point in reasoning with her.

In their minds, she was of lowly status, unworthy of respect. Everything had to be bestowed upon her by their grace—how could they ever think they were in the wrong?

They even believed that if she was wronged, she should endure it meekly. To resist would be unjust.

And yet she had hoped they would realize their mistakes.

She took a step back to avoid the strike, no longer willing to argue with Shen Zhaozhao. She turned to leave.

But seeing Shen Weici dare to evade her, Shen Zhaozhao’s pent-up frustration from the past few days finally boiled over.

She had been slapped by her father, confined by her grandmother, and now her mother had been punished by her father because of her. What infuriated her even more was that her former close friends now mocked the Second Branch in secret, refusing to associate with them.

Old and new grievances surged together, and Shen Zhaozhao’s eyes turned red with rage.

Her gaze flicked to the icy lake water beneath the stone bridge. With a dark expression, she fiercely grabbed Shen Weici’s hand and tried to shove her into the lake.

Shen Weici had been sidestepping Shen Zhaozhao, but when she realized her intent, her heart jolted. She quickly reached out and tightly grabbed Shen Zhaozhao’s sleeve.

But suddenly, another hand pressed down hard on her shoulder, ruthlessly pushing her downward.

The railing on the stone bridge only reached waist height. Shen Weici felt her body lurching forward. In that final moment, she gritted her teeth and yanked Shen Zhaozhao’s hand with all her strength, dragging her into the water with a look of terror in her eyes.

Shen Weici didn’t know how deep the lake was, but one thought filled her mind: even if she died, she would make sure Shen Zhaozhao went with her.

Moreover, she knew that if only she fell into the water, Shen Zhaozhao would surely obstruct anyone from rescuing her. With so few people around, she might actually succeed. But if both of them fell in, that would be a different story.

That tug had taken every ounce of her strength. Even the servant woman beside her, who had been pressing down on Shen Weici’s shoulder to push her into the water, hadn’t noticed Shen Weici’s movement. By the time she heard a scream and tried to grab them, it was already too late.

She looked down at the water in horror, her legs nearly giving out.

Yue Deng, who had been restrained by Shen Zhaozhao’s maid, only broke free when she heard the splash and felt the grip on her loosen. She rushed to the edge of the bridge, her face filled with terror as she looked at the lake, then let out a piercing scream.

Two young ladies from the Marquis’s mansion had fallen into the water at the same time. The few maids and servant women on the stone bridge were all in a panic, shouting urgently for guards to come and rescue them.

The icy lake water chilled her to the bone, and all she could see was an abyss of darkness.

A faint sobbing sound reached her ears. Shen Weici felt an unbearable heaviness in her head, as if she just wanted to sleep a little longer.

Since entering the Marquis’s mansion, she had never felt this relaxed before. Her mind was empty of thoughts; all she needed was to sleep soundly.

Yue Deng knelt by the bed, crying as she changed Shen Weici’s clothes. Then she heard He Xia’s anxious voice from behind: “I just saw the physician being called away by the Second Madam. Both physicians have been taken, and when I went to call for one, the people from the Second Courtyard blocked me and wouldn’t let me in. I waited at the door for a long time, but no one came out. What should we do?”

“Who knows how long it will take before the physician finishes with Second Young Lady.”

Upon hearing this, Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici’s pale face and tightly closed eyes, wiped her tears, and stood up. “This is too much. I’m going to beg the Old Madam to intervene.”

“I can’t just stand by and watch our young lady suffer.”

With that, Yue Deng instructed He Xia and Yan’er to stay and look after Shen Weici before rushing out.

Tears streamed down her face as she ran, but just a few steps outside Lingchun Courtyard, two servant women blocked her path, refusing to let her pass.

Yue Deng was so angry she nearly fainted. Pointing at the two servant women, she cursed, “You’re taking this too far!”

The two servant women gave her a cold glance. “The Second Madam has ordered that after the physician attends to Second Young Lady, he will naturally go to see Third Young Lady. Where do you think you’re going?”

“If you dare cause trouble for the Second Madam by going to the Old Madam, don’t blame us for tying you up and bringing you before the Second Madam to be dealt with according to family law.”

Yue Deng’s face paled. Almost choking back sobs, she gritted her teeth and said, “Our young lady and Second Young Lady fell into the water together. Why should Second Young Lady be seen first by the physician?”

“And why, when there are two physicians, won’t one be allowed to come see our young lady?”

“You won’t let me see the Old Madam, so I’ll go out and call a physician myself!”

One of the servant women crossed her arms and sneered. “The Second Madam is Third Young Lady’s birth mother. How could she allow Third Young Lady to go out and call a physician herself? Wouldn’t that just give people outside more reason to say the Second Madam mistreats her?”

“It’s not like we’re refusing to let a physician come to Lingchun Courtyard. You just stay put here and wait. If you try any tricks, don’t blame us old servant women for showing no mercy.”

Yue Deng finally saw the true, heartless face of the great household. The Second Madam was clearly trying to delay until her young lady was beyond saving.

She gritted her teeth, no longer bothering to argue. She made a dash for the gate, but when she broke past the two servant women, she was met with despair as four or five more servant women surrounded her.

She took a step back, her despair deepening.

Those servant women closed in, grabbed her, and forced her back toward Lingchun Courtyard, not forgetting to threaten her as they did so: “You stay put in Lingchun Courtyard. If you dare cause any more trouble for our Second Madam, she has plenty of ways to deal with you.”

Yue Deng was no match for them alone. She was pushed back into Lingchun Courtyard, where five or six more servant women stood guard at the entrance, making it impossible to leave.

Lingchun Courtyard was remote and quiet. The people from the Third Branch had gone to the hot spring villa, and the Princess Consort had gone to accompany her mother, so she wasn’t around. The Eldest and Second Young Masters were at the palace. The only one who could help was the Old Madam.

But she couldn’t even get out. No matter how much she shouted, it was useless. She was nearly in tears.

She looked at the fierce servant women guarding the entrance, then turned and went back inside, instructing He Xia to bring two more charcoal braziers.

He Xia looked at Shen Weici’s pale face, her hair still damp, and wiped her tears as she said to Yue Deng, “We should give the young lady some ginger soup now. I’ll go to the kitchen and have them prepare some.”

With that, she got up.

But before long, He Xia returned, her face filled with panic. “The servant women at the door won’t let me out. They say to wait until the physician comes to see her, and they won’t let me go to the kitchen either.”

Yue Deng’s entire body trembled. “This is outrageous.”

He Xia looked at Yue Deng in a panic. “What do we do now?”

“There are only three charcoal braziers in the room, and we can’t go out to get hot water. The young lady is so cold, and she’s still unconscious. If we keep delaying like this, something bad will definitely happen.”

“It’s been so long already, and it’s so cold outside.”

“Are we really just supposed to wait like this?”

Yue Deng tightly clutched the blanket on Shen Weici, tears streaming down her face. Choking back sobs, she looked at Shen Weici again and said to He Xia, “Bring the charcoal braziers closer. I’ll warm her hands, and you warm her feet.”

“When the kitchen servants come to deliver lunch, I’ll find a way to slip out.”

He Xia wiped her tears and said nothing. The three maids in Lingchun Courtyard were no match for the seven or eight servant women at the door. The Second Madam had sent so many to guard them precisely to delay.

Yan’er was beside them, continuously wiping Shen Weici’s face with a warm towel. She glanced out the window and saw the servant women keeping a close watch on the courtyard. Then, with another look, she cried out, “There are guards at the door now. We really can’t get out!”

Yue Deng and He Xia quickly turned to look. Yue Deng turned back, tears falling as she whispered, “The Second Madam isn’t going to send a physician.”

She recalled the moment the guards had come to the rescue. The Second Madam had ordered them to save Second Young Lady first. If it hadn’t been for the young lady tightly gripping the Third Young Lady’s skirt, and her shouting with all her might, the Second Madam, fearing the matter would escalate, might have deliberately left the young lady behind.

The situation had been perilously close. Everyone around her was the Second Madam’s person—there was no one to help. Perhaps even now, the Old Madam didn’t know that the young lady had fallen into the water.

She understood the Second Madam’s intentions all too well.

She also knew she couldn’t just sit and wait for disaster, but she couldn’t even leave the courtyard. She could only wait for an opportunity, for the servant women and guards at the door to let their guard down.

It wasn’t until the afternoon that Yue Deng noticed the meal delivery was also late. When she went to ask, she was met with hostility and sent away. Just as she was about to find a way to climb out from the back of the courtyard, she suddenly heard a few pained screams from the entrance. She ran a few steps to the door and saw Song Zhang, his face dark with anger, striding in. With one kick, he sent a servant woman flying, her mouth bleeding as she screamed in pain.

Seeing Song Zhang, Yue Deng felt as if she had seen a savior. Her red and swollen eyes welled with tears as she ran over, crying, “Second Young Master, please save our young lady! She fell into the lake, and those servant women blocked the door, refusing to let us out. Until now, no physician has come to see her!”

Song Zhang glanced at Yue Deng’s eyes, swollen like walnuts, his expression grim. Without a word, he strode inside.

The servant women who had been strutting about at the entrance were immediately tied up by Song Zhang’s guards, given a few slaps, and then dragged to a nearby spot outside to kneel, awaiting the General’s decision on their punishment.

Inside the room, the scene was bleak. Two maids knelt by the bed, wiping their tears. The person on the bed had her eyes tightly shut, her face pale and lifeless. Song Zhang felt a tightness in his chest as he strode toward the bed.

chapters.title: Angry for Her
chapters.content:
He Xia and Yan’er, kneeling by the bed, instinctively moved aside when Song Zhang approached.

Song Zhang sat at the head of the bed and turned to Yue Deng, who had just entered. “The imperial physician will arrive later. Go to the kitchen and bring some ginger soup first.”

Seeing Song Zhang, Yue Deng felt an inexplicable sense of relief. She hurried out toward the kitchen.

Song Zhang reached out to touch Shen Wei’s fingers—they were ice-cold.

He had spent the entire day accompanying the emperor to the winter hunt at the hunting grounds, which was why he had only learned of the news so late.

Her fingers were still soft, resting weakly in his palm. The fair, slender tips were as elegant and refined as ever, yet lifeless.

Song Zhang tightened his grip, enclosing her fingers in his palm.

Then, he lifted Shen Wei into his arms, pulled the brocade quilt over her, and warmed her with his own body heat.

He Xia and Yan’er stood to the side, stunned by the scene but not daring to look for long. They bowed their heads deeply.

Soon, Yue Deng returned with the ginger soup. Just as she was about to feed Shen Wei, Song Zhang took the bowl from her hands. Naturally, he held Shen Wei in his arms and lowered his head to feed her the soup.

Yue Deng hesitated, then tentatively stepped forward and whispered, “Let this servant feed the young lady.”

But she was met with Song Zhang’s cold, indifferent gaze, which carried a hint of impatience. Startled, Yue Deng froze and dared not speak again.

After all, only Song Zhang could help their young lady now.

Song Zhang fed Shen Wei the medicine without any intention of hiding it from others. He brought the spoon to her lips, feeding her bit by bit, his movements much gentler than before.

After feeding her nearly half a bowl, Ming He hurried in with Physician Lin.

Physician Lin, who had been pushed into the inner room, saw the woman being held by Song Zhang as he fed her ginger soup. Recognizing her as the Third Young Lady Shen from his previous visit, he didn’t dare to look further. He quickly bowed with his head lowered. “General Song.”

Song Zhang set aside the unfinished ginger soup, his voice heavy. “Hurry and diagnose her pulse.”

Those few words were enough to make Physician Lin’s heart race. He quickly stepped forward to take her pulse.

Yue Deng stood to the side, watching intently, her heart also tightening. With such a delay, she was terrified something might go wrong.

After diagnosing the pulse, Physician Lin examined Shen Wei’s complexion. Her skin was as fair as frost, her features as delicate as autumn water. Even with her eyes closed, her brows and eyes were so beautifully painted that they dazzled him for a moment.

Even the noble consorts in the palace did not possess such beauty.

Sensing a cold gaze from above, he quickly regained his composure and bowed cautiously to Song Zhang. “May this official examine Miss Shen’s tongue coating?”

Song Zhang pressed his lips tightly, suppressing his displeasure at the thought of others examining Shen Wei. Still, he cooperated by gently lifting Shen Wei’s chin, parting her lips slightly.

He couldn’t bear to use force. Seeing Physician Lin’s hesitant expression, he frowned and asked, “What do you need to see the tongue coating for?”

Physician Lin suddenly felt too intimidated to look. He quickly bowed again. “It’s not necessary.”

Then, he turned his gaze to Song Zhang. “Just now, this official diagnosed her pulse. Miss Shen’s pulse indicates an invasion of dampness and external pathogens. Her pulse is slippery, rough, and weak. The immediate priority is to warm and tonify her yang energy, dispel dampness, and drive out the cold.”

He furrowed his brows and lowered his voice. “Miss Shen has long suffered from a cold ailment, with internal cold energy already present. After falling into the water, her condition has likely worsened. It may take a long time to recover. Otherwise, she will only deplete her own blood and qi. Insufficient qi and blood can easily lead to a deficiency of vital energy.”

“An imbalance of yin and yang will make her body increasingly frail. In the future, it may be difficult for her to conceive.”

Yue Deng, upon hearing that it might be difficult to conceive, felt as if she had been struck by a thunderbolt.

Why did such a thing have to happen at this critical moment?

Song Zhang listened without any change in expression, then asked, “When will she wake up?”

Physician Lin pondered. “This official cannot predict, but judging from Miss Shen’s pulse, it seems stable. She should wake up.”

Song Zhang’s expression darkened, his dark eyes pressing down with coldness. “Should?”

Physician Lin felt a chill run down his spine. He quickly replied, “Miss Shen will definitely wake up, it’s just a matter of when.”

Song Zhang lowered his gaze to Shen Wei’s face in his arms and said softly, “Go and prepare the prescription.”

Physician Lin felt a weight lift from his shoulders and repeatedly acknowledged before leaving.

Ming He, who had been waiting by the curtain, followed him out.

Song Zhang reached out to cup Shen Wei’s cheek. Fortunately, there was some warmth in her face. His fingertips rested on the small mole at the corner of her eye. She was so petite in his arms that he could barely feel her weight.

He then looked at Yue Deng standing to the side. “Later, when my people bring the medicine, have someone decoct it and take good care of her.”

Yue Deng hesitated before nodding. “Second Young Master, rest assured. We will take good care of the young lady.”

Song Zhang held her, reluctant to let go. Her soft, fragrant body lay in his arms, yet she had fainted after falling into the water.

The delicate white collar of her moon-white robe was slightly loose, and the thin inner garment made her appear even more fragile.

Song Zhang’s heart tightened, his eyes filled with distress.

He looked at Yue Deng and asked, “How did she fall into the water?”

Yue Deng quickly recounted the entire incident, then tearfully said, “Fortunately, the young lady kept tightly holding onto the Second Young Lady’s clothes. Otherwise, the Second Madam wouldn’t have bothered to save her.”

“Even though we called for two physicians, the old servants blocked us at the door of Chunshui Courtyard and wouldn’t let us out. It was clearly an attempt to harm the young lady.”

Yue Deng spoke without stopping, then suddenly froze. What if the Second Young Master thought she was speaking ill of the Second Branch?

She had heard that the Eldest Branch never interfered with the affairs of the mansion...

Song Zhang listened, his expression darkening. He placed Shen Wei back on the bed, had Yue Deng attend to her, then stood up and walked out.

He exited the courtyard gate and saw the old servants who had blocked the door. He gave a cold smirk and said to the guard beside him, “Take them to Cishou Hall.”

Then, he turned to Ming He. “Call the Second Old Master, my father, as well as the Eldest Young Master and the Fourth Young Master.”

He wanted to see who would lose face.

The old servants were tied up, their hair disheveled, their bodies bruised all over. They couldn’t even cry out.

At that moment, Old Madam Shen was about to have dinner. A servant hurried in to deliver a message. “Old Madam, Second Young Master Song has arrived.”

The servant’s face showed surprise. “And he’s brought several old servants with him.”

Old Madam Shen was taken aback. Song Zhang had rarely visited her courtyard, and she didn’t mind, as he wasn’t her direct grandson anyway.

But his arrival now must mean something important.

She quickly supported herself on a maid’s arm and went to the main hall, where she saw seven or eight old servants kneeling on the ground, wailing.

She also saw Song Zhang standing to the side, tall and upright, his face cold and stern. He wore a purple official robe, and behind him stood four or five tall, knife-wielding guards. The sheer presence of it all made Old Madam Shen’s heart skip a beat.

Song Zhang properly greeted Old Madam Shen. “Old Madam, are you aware that Third Young Lady Shen fell into the water?”

Technically, Song Zhang was not part of the Marquis’s household; he was registered under the Song Duke’s family lineage. Addressing Old Madam Shen as “Old Madam” was not inappropriate.

Old Madam Shen was startled and turned to her mammy beside her. “Did Ci’er fall into the water?”

The mammy also looked confused and shook her head. “This old servant said this morning that the Third Young Lady didn’t go to the hot spring villa, perhaps because she was worried about you, Old Madam, and wanted to come keep you company. How did she fall into the water?”

Old Madam Shen looked at the tied-up old servants on the ground, then back at Song Zhang. “What happened?”

Song Zhang glanced at Old Madam Shen, lifted his robe, and sat down on a chair. “It’s nothing if Old Madam doesn’t know.”

“This kind of disgraceful matter should be known to all. I’ve never been one to care about reputation, and I can’t stand such dirty tricks.”

“Wait until everyone is here. It’s up to Old Madam how to handle it.”

“If Old Madam doesn’t handle it, or tries to cover it up, then I’ll call the officials from Jingzhao Yin.”

“At that time, don’t blame me for not considering familial ties. Let’s see who loses face.”

Old Madam Shen’s expression turned serious upon hearing this. She knew something big must have happened. She quickly ordered the maids in the room to go out and stand guard.

Shen Wei woke up in the middle of the night.

The candlelight flickered, and her mind was blank, as if she were still immersed in a long, thick dream.

Everything before her seemed unreal. She blinked her eyes in confusion, feeling as if everything around her was unfamiliar.

After staring for a long time, she felt a severe headache and a feverish heat all over her body. She couldn’t remember anything.

Her fingertips twitched, but they were quickly enveloped by a large hand. She belatedly turned her head and saw a pair of deep, dark eyes looking down at her.

Shen Wei exhaled a hot breath, squinting as she looked up at the green canopy above.

This place was unfamiliar.

She felt at a loss, unable to think clearly. The dizziness made it hard for her to even see the person sitting beside her.

When she tried to speak, a fit of coughing overtook her. She buried her face in the brocade quilt, enduring several painful coughs.

Song Zhang watched Shen Wei cough and placed his hand on her back, then called for the maid behind the screen to bring medicine.

Seeing that Shen Wei had almost buried her small face in the quilt, her dark hair scattered behind her, he feared she might suffocate. He pulled back a corner of the quilt for her.

His fingers touched her lips, feeling the scorching heat of her breath.

Song Zhang was taken aback. He looked down at Shen Wei’s dazed, watery eyes.

He saw her flushed cheeks, the fine sweat beading on her jade-like forehead, and picked up a handkerchief to wipe it away.

He knew Shen Wei was feverish. The physician had said that as long as she endured the fever, she would be fine.

Suddenly, his wrist was gripped by a soft, delicate hand. A pair of rosy lips parted to utter a single word: “Hot...”

Song Zhang was startled. He saw the restless woman in the quilt beginning to kick it off. He leaned forward, pulling Shen Wei into his arms, rubbing her shoulders as he soothed her. “Cover yourself with more blankets. Once you sweat, you’ll feel better tomorrow.”

Shen Wei didn’t recognize the man before her. She squinted, exhaling another hot breath. It seemed to take her a long time to process his words, but she obediently closed her eyes. “Okay...”

Song Zhang hadn’t expected Shen Wei to be so gentle even in illness.

She always seemed to soothe his urgency and anger.

The fragrance from her body seemed to intensify with her fever. Her slightly parted red lips glistened with moisture, an alluring temptation to anyone who saw her.

Not to mention her reddened yet enchanting peach-blossom eyes, and her fair, slender fingers unconsciously hooking onto his sleeve. Every detail softened Song Zhang’s heart.

He looked at the red lips before him, his throat bobbing as he swallowed. In the quiet, he couldn’t resist—after tasting them once, he couldn’t forget.

He lowered his head, kissing her more gently than the previous times.

“Wei Ci...”

He gazed at her watery eyes, watching a tear slide from the corner of her eye. He wiped it away with his finger, then buried his hand in her soft hair, tracing her lips, and interlacing his fingers with hers.

A maid’s voice came from behind the screen. Song Zhang reluctantly kissed her once more, then looked at her blank, dazed eyes. He stood up, holding her in his arms, covering her with the quilt before calling the maid in.

Song Zhang still took the medicine and fed it to her himself. Having done this twice before, he was experienced.

But this time, Shen Wei was not as cooperative as before. He softly coaxed her to drink, but she turned her head away like a child throwing a tantrum, her hoarse voice refusing, “Bitter...”

chapters.title: Can’t Even Say You’re Afraid of Bitterness?
chapters.content:
Song Zhang found it unbearably adorable. Though he was not a patient man, at this moment, he couldn’t help but want to coax her more.

So she was afraid of bitterness too.

He fed a piece of candied fruit into Shen Weici’s mouth, followed by a spoonful of medicine.

Watching her delicate eyebrows furrow slightly, tears welling at the corners of her eyes, her face flushed and eyes half-lidded—clearly not fully awake—she pushed his hand away, turning her face into his embrace as if unwilling to take the medicine.

Song Zhang looked down at Shen Weici, who was buried in his arms. Her eyes were closed, her breath scorching, one hand clinging tightly to his lapel, her long lashes trembling uneasily.

His heart burned at the sight. So this was how it felt when she took the initiative to lean on him.

He soothed her with gentle words, lifting her chin to feed her bit by bit. When she turned her head away, he fed her slowly until she finished the medicine.

His fingers brushed over her half-closed, dazed eyes, then used a handkerchief to wipe the fine sweat from her forehead.

Song Zhang, who had never cared for anyone before, didn’t even realize how meticulous his actions had become.

Shen Weici seemed to have fallen asleep again, burying her flushed face deep into his embrace, her fingers still tightly gripping his lapel.

Song Zhang stared at her fair, slender fingers and her luminous, pale wrists—so strikingly beautiful it was almost improper. He tried to pull them away, but his own lapel loosened, yet her fingers remained firmly in place.

Suddenly, he recalled what her maid had said—how she had clung tightly to Shen Zhaozhao’s clothes in the water, as if it were her only lifeline in a moment of utter helplessness.

He looked down at her fair fingers again, enclosing them in his own palm.

A pang of pity stirred in his heart.

He knew her days in the second courtyard had not been easy.

The candlelight flickered as Song Zhang held her, occasionally lowering his head to kiss her forehead, unable to bear letting her go.

But when he touched Shen Weici’s back again, he found it damp with sweat. Only then did he set her down and call for a maid to change her clothes.

The maid entered, and Song Zhang stepped out into the corridor. Ming He approached, handing him a letter and whispering, “We’ve found out.”

“But it seems we’ve spooked them. The middleman we discovered is dead.”

He leaned in closer to Song Zhang’s ear, adding something in a low voice before asking, “Should we arrest those people first?”

Song Zhang’s fingers paused as he opened the letter, his expression turning complex.

He muttered, “Be careful. Don’t make a scene.”

Ming He nodded quickly, then, seeing Song Zhang’s expression, asked, “What if someone from the Marquis’s mansion comes to see Miss Shen tomorrow?”

Song Zhang finally tore his gaze from the letter, glancing at Ming He. “No one is to be received.”

Ming He understood.

Seeing Song Zhang turn back toward the inner room, he couldn’t help but advise, “It’s the third watch of the night, General. You should rest for a while.”

Song Zhang found Ming He particularly talkative. He stopped in his tracks, his phoenix eyes coldly sweeping over him. Ming He immediately understood and quickly shut his mouth, turning away.

Song Zhang entered the room, standing behind the screen with his hands clasped behind his back, watching the maids bustle about. Only when they had all left did he step inside.

The person on the bed was now sleeping peacefully. Song Zhang walked over and sat at the head of the bed, touching Shen Weici’s forehead—still feverish. He lowered his gaze.

An old wet nurse remained by the bedside to care for her. Seeing Song Zhang’s cold yet subtly worried expression, she softly said, “Just now, when this old servant was wiping Miss Shen down, her body wasn’t as hot as before. Perhaps the fever will break by morning.”

Song Zhang remained silent, staring at Shen Weici for a long time before looking at the old nurse. “You stay here and take good care of her. I’ll be in the next courtyard. If anything happens, come and find me.”

Old Nurse Tan, who had long served at this estate, rarely saw Song Zhang even once a year. She quickly nodded. “General, rest assured. This old servant will take good care of Miss Shen.”

Song Zhang took one last deep look at Shen Weici’s sleeping form before rising to leave.

Bright light from the flowered window filtered through the paper, casting a glow on the bed curtains and spreading to the eyes buried deep beneath the brocade quilt.

A voice, distant at first, then growing nearer, layer upon layer, finally reached her. She slowly opened her eyes.

Through the haze, she saw a pair of eyes. The dizziness had not lessened; she moved her fingertips slightly, then placed them on the hand beside the bed. “Yue Deng.”

Yue Deng was holding a bowl of medicine, warming it. Seeing Shen Weici awake, her face lit up with joy. “Miss!”

Then she burst into tears, burying her face in the edge of Shen Weici’s bed. “Miss, you’ve finally woken up.”

Shen Weici’s head throbbed so badly that even Yue Deng’s voice seemed to come from far away.

She closed her eyes, took a few breaths, and asked, “Where am I?”

Yue Deng looked up and saw that Shen Weici’s cheeks were still flushed. Noticing the sweat on her forehead, she quickly wiped it with a handkerchief and felt her forehead—it didn’t seem as hot as last night.

Wiping her tears, she choked out softly, “After Miss and Second Miss fell into the water, the maid by Second Miss’s side called for guards and Second Madam. Second Madam hid the incident from everyone, ordered the maids to guard the Lingchun Courtyard, and wouldn’t let us out or call for a physician. She wanted to drag it out and let Miss’s condition worsen.”

“It was only in the afternoon when Young Master Song returned and called for an imperial physician for Miss.”

“Young Master Song said that recovering at the Marquis’s mansion might invite harm, so he wanted Miss to recuperate at this estate. He even asked for Old Madam’s permission.”

“Old Madam agreed and said Miss should stay here at this estate to recover in peace, and only return after she’s well.”

Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici. “This estate is Young Master Song’s private residence. There are many guards outside, so Second Madam won’t dare harm Miss anymore.”

Shen Weici kept her eyes closed, her eyes stinging.

She lowered her head into the quilt, as if something were stuck in her throat, unsure of what to say.

Yue Deng saw Shen Weici buried in the quilt and softly added, “This time, we truly owe Young Master Song. Even Old Madam didn’t know. If it had dragged on any longer, even if Miss woke up, her body would have been left with a chronic illness.”

After a long while, a muffled, hoarse cough came from beneath the quilt.

Song Zhang had been standing outside the screen, listening to the conversation inside. Hearing no further sound from Shen Weici, his expression dimmed slightly as he walked in.

Inside, Yue Deng was patting Shen Weici’s back. Shen Weici was buried under the quilt, only her dark hair and a few soft fingers pressing on the blanket visible.

The white cuffs of her sleeves covered her wrists completely, leaving only half of her fingertips exposed.

This estate was a place he rarely visited, and he usually had no time for it. Though it was regularly cleaned, the long disuse had left a lingering, aged wooden fragrance.

Yet after just one night, the room was filled with her warm, sweet scent.

Every time Song Zhang caught this scent, he thought of her—soft and yielding.

Yue Deng noticed Song Zhang entering from behind the screen and quickly called out, “Young Master.”

Song Zhang took the medicine bowl from a nearby maid’s hands and sat beside Shen Weici.

He looked at the figure buried under the quilt, recalling how she always seemed to curl up slightly in her sleep, her face buried beneath the covers.

Such an uneasy posture.

He gently pulled back the brocade quilt, and a wave of heat rushed out. He frowned, finally seeing Shen Weici’s flushed cheeks.

He raised an eyebrow, looking at her closed eyes. “Aren’t you uncomfortable like this?”

“The room has several bronze stoves burning—four or five of them. It’s warmer than spring. If you’re cold, I’ll have two more lit for you.”

Shen Weici blinked slowly, only opening her eyes after a long pause to look at Song Zhang.

Perhaps due to the fever, she was still in a daze, her eyes constantly welling with tears—not that she wanted to cry.

She exhaled a hot breath, then averted her gaze, her voice hoarse and weak. “Thank you, Young Master Song.”

Song Zhang looked at her misty-eyed appearance, like a peach in the early morning dew—soft, tender, and sweet, utterly tempting.

He truly wanted to hold her in his arms and take a bite.

He didn’t respond, only leaning in slightly, his gaze fixed on her blush-stained profile. “Drink your medicine.”

Yue Deng, realizing belatedly, hurried over to help Shen Weici sit up against the pillows. “Miss, please drink your medicine.”

As she spoke, she glanced at the bowl in Song Zhang’s hands, wanting to take it but unsure how to ask.

Song Zhang had already naturally brought a spoonful to Shen Weici’s lips, his dark phoenix eyes watching her. “Afraid of the bitterness? This medicine is very bitter.”

Shen Weici paused, then shook her head.

She took the bowl from Song Zhang’s hand and, lowering her gaze, softly said, “I’ll drink it myself.”

Song Zhang said nothing, watching the mix of sickness and flush on Shen Weici’s face as her fingers brushed against his. He hesitated imperceptibly, subtly pressing his lips together before loosening his grip.

The medicine was indeed very bitter. The moment Shen Weici smelled it, her stomach churned, nearly making her gag.

She forced herself to bring the bowl to her lips and, in one go, drank it all—only to fail to suppress the dry heaving that followed.

Song Zhang took a preserved plum from his hand and, parting Shen Weici’s hand, placed it in her mouth. His deep eyes locked onto hers. “Can’t even say you’re afraid of bitterness?”

Shen Weici’s mouth was stuffed with the plum, her cheeks slightly puffed as she looked at Song Zhang, her expression flickering with momentary bewilderment.

The sweet and sour flavor spread in her mouth. She stared at Song Zhang for a long moment before coming back to her senses, biting down on the plum to dilute the bitterness in her mouth and suppress the rising nausea.

She wasn’t really that afraid of bitterness—it was just that extremely bitter medicine was hard to swallow.

She looked at Song Zhang’s direct and cold gaze, then lowered her eyes, unsure how to respond. After a while, she obediently hummed a soft “mm.”

She truly didn’t want to speak. Her throat and eyes ached, her head spun, and she couldn’t think clearly.

She lay there listlessly, her eyes half-closed.

The more Song Zhang looked at her like this, the more he couldn’t look away. Her exquisite beauty and weary expression blended together in a strangely harmonious way.

A ray of snow light shone through the window, falling directly on the sick woman, making her delicate skin appear even more like snow.

Her long, dark hair, as soft as her temperament, cascaded down, with a few strands, warmed by her breath, lingering at the corner of her lips.

He knew he had brought her here out of selfishness—just so he could see her undisturbed.

He didn’t want her to have another chance to see Zhang Yuanheng.

When Yue Deng came back in with the empty bowl, she saw Song Zhang still sitting at the bedside. As she approached, she noticed him lifting his hand to caress the miss’s cheek.

His fingers hooked a strand of hair away from her lips, his body leaning slightly forward.

Yue Deng froze. Her miss, with her head turned, might not have noticed, but from her angle, she saw it all clearly.

His tall, imposing figure almost completely enveloped her miss. The depth in his eyes made her heart skip a beat, and she unconsciously stopped in her tracks.

chapters.title: Now You’re Not Afraid?
chapters.content:
Shen Weici had been tilting her head slightly when she suddenly felt a shadow fall over her. The fingers brushing against her cheek were slightly cool. She belatedly realized and froze, her own fingers hidden in her sleeve tightening slightly.

She covered her mouth and coughed again, propping herself up with her back to Song Zhang. Her hair cascaded down, covering her flushed cheeks and the eyes that were slightly uneasy and moist.

Song Zhang frowned as he watched Shen Weici turn away from him. Her thin white clothes were tangled with strands of her hair, and her delicate, rounded shoulders trembled slightly. Her coughs were soft, as if she were afraid of disturbing others.

Suppressed and quiet.

Song Zhang’s hand hovered in midair before naturally patting Shen Weici’s back. “The imperial physician said you have external cold and internal heat. Coughing is normal; you’ll be better in a few days.”

The large, warm hand gently patted her back, steady and calm. Shen Weici’s body stiffened slightly, and she hoarsely hummed in response.

She still had her back to him, her fingers trembling in the brocade quilt as she breathed weakly.

With her eyes closed and her back to Song Zhang, she buried herself in the covers again and rasped, “I know the Young Master Song is busy with official duties, yet you’ve come to care for me. I feel uneasy.”

“Young Master Song need not concern himself with me. Monthlight can take care of me.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici coughed softly again and whispered, “I will remember Young Master Song’s kindness in my heart. If I can repay it in the future, I certainly will.”

Song Zhang calmly watched Shen Weici’s turned back. It was rare for her, in such a sickly state, to say something so infuriating.

That “Young Master Song” was so polite and distant.

And what was this talk of repayment? He truly couldn’t think of what someone as mistreated as she could possibly repay him with.

Moreover, did he help her just to seek repayment?

Song Zhang raised an eyebrow. But seeing the distress between her brows and the watery weakness in her eyes, he didn’t have the heart to be angry with her right now.

He recalled yesterday when he had taken those servant women to the hall and heard what the Old Madam Shen had said.

Then he asked her, “Did you buy the red flower ointment to make the Old Madam help you deal with the Wen family?”

Shen Weici hadn’t expected Song Zhang to bring this up now. She couldn’t fathom his intentions.

After thinking carefully for a moment, she chose her words carefully. “It wasn’t exactly to deal with them...”

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici’s profile and asked again, “Why didn’t you tell me the truth that night?”

Shen Weici hesitated. She couldn’t exactly say outright that she didn’t trust him.

In truth, he *had* helped her. She knew that in her heart.

So she always had an inexplicable emotion toward Song Zhang—she wanted to stay far away from him, yet she also knew she should be grateful to him.

If Zhang Tingyi hadn’t been dismissed, her father probably wouldn’t have given up so easily.

And this time, when she fell into the water, he had saved her again.

She closed her eyes and hoarsely admitted, “I just didn’t want Young Master Song to have something to hold over me again.”

Song Zhang raised an eyebrow. “Now you’re not afraid?”

Shen Weici fell silent. After a long while, she softly said, “Young Master Song has helped me twice. Even if you don’t have anything to hold over me, I would still repay you.”

Song Zhang looked down at Shen Weici. Her voice was so soft it calmed the heart.

Her words always carried a warmth, even if some of them didn’t sound pleasant. But they never carried sharp, biting barbs.

Perhaps it was her always calm and quiet tone. Every time he saw her speak to others, it was with this gentle and soft voice.

She seemed so mild it was as if she couldn’t get angry.

Song Zhang couldn’t help but wonder why he, of all people, would care so much about such a fragile person.

He had always thought he liked bright, passionate, and striking women.

But in reality, Song Zhang had long been immersed in this tenderness, so deeply that he couldn’t extricate himself.

From behind the screen came Tan Mom’s voice: “Young Master, the meal is ready.”

Song Zhang saw Shen Weici’s condition and knew she couldn’t get up, so he had the servants bring everything in.

One after another, eight or nine maids entered, each carrying a dish of rare delicacies never seen before. Even Monthlight, standing to the side, was stunned—she couldn’t name half of the dishes.

When she noticed Song Zhang looking at her, she hurriedly came to her senses and went to help Shen Weici sit up. “Miss, please eat something.”

Shen Weici had been unconscious since falling into the water yesterday and hadn’t eaten anything. Though her stomach was empty, she had no appetite.

But when she heard Song Zhang ordering the maids to bring in the food, she reluctantly propped herself up.

She glanced at the maids by the bed as they placed the trays low so she could see the dishes clearly.

A kind-looking old servant woman holding a jade bowl smiled at Shen Weici. “Third Young Miss, if there’s anything you’d like to eat, this old servant will serve it to you.”

Shen Weici thought it was just one meal; there was no need for such fuss. She felt uncomfortable being watched by so many people.

After a look, she softly said, “I’ll just have some congee.”

Remembering the physician’s advice to eat light foods, Song Zhang had Tan Mom bring over the congee bowl to feed her. Then he brought over almond tofu and fed her a bite.

“These are all light dishes, none are greasy. Try a bit of each. If there’s anything you like, I’ll have them make it for you again.”

Shen Weici, overpowered by Song Zhang’s insistence, could only open her mouth to accept the food.

Just as she was about to ask Monthlight to take over, Song Zhang fed her another bite of yam and pigeon meat.

Tan Mom, holding the congee bowl, watched from the side. When had Young Master ever been so attentive to someone?

After feeding her several bites, Song Zhang saw that she wasn’t eating much and stopped, having Tan Mom take over with the congee.

He handed the empty bowl in his hand to a maid and looked at Shen Weici. “Eat well. I’ll come see you again tonight.”

With that, he stood up and left.

As soon as Song Zhang left, the room seemed to brighten, and the oppressive, cautious atmosphere lifted. Even Shen Weici let out a slight, silent breath.

The few bites Song Zhang had fed her had stimulated her appetite. With Monthlight by her side, Shen Weici relaxed and ate a few more mouthfuls.

After rinsing her mouth and the dishes were taken away, the room emptied. Shen Weici, drowsy, leaned back and looked at Monthlight. “Did the Old Madam have me come here to recover because she found out about yesterday’s incident?”

Monthlight nodded. “It was Second Young Master Song who caught those servant women and called First Master and Second Master to witness and seek justice for you.”

Shen Weici paused upon hearing this, then lowered her eyes and asked, “What was Father’s reaction when he found out?”

Monthlight shook her head. “I don’t know about that. As for how they were dealt with in the end, you’d have to ask Second Young Master Song.”

“The Old Madam kept this matter tightly under wraps. Apart from our Chun Spring Courtyard’s maids, the others don’t know.”

“Yesterday, the Old Madam’s personal maid even came to tell us not to spread this. If we do, all the maids in Chun Spring Courtyard will be sold off.”

Shen Weici frowned and nodded upon hearing this. “The Old Madam acting this way isn’t surprising.”

A coldness flickered in her eyes. “The Second Madam probably wishes I were dead.”

Monthlight looked at Shen Weici. “That’s why Second Young Master Song brought you here. Otherwise, that wicked woman, Second Madam, who knows what other vicious methods she’d use.”

Without Song Zhang blocking the light, Shen Weici slightly turned her head to look out the window.

After a long pause, she softly said, “I can’t stay here for too long.”

“I need to return soon and clarify the marriage with Young Master Zhang.”

Monthlight was taken aback by these words. Remembering what the physician had said yesterday, she couldn’t help but whisper, “Yesterday, the physician said that after falling into the icy lake in the heavy snow and being in the water for so long, the cold in your body won’t be easy to remove. It might make it difficult for you to... to conceive.”

Shen Weici’s face showed no expression. She still looked listless, her body devoid of strength.

She propped her hand under the covers and wearily closed her eyes. “Monthlight, are you tired?”

Monthlight was suddenly asked this and quickly shook her head. “As long as I can stay by your side, Miss, I’m not tired.”

Shen Weici nodded and, with her eyes closed, murmured, “Maybe my marriage to Young Master Zhang truly won’t work out. It’s all a twist of fate.”

“It’s always such a coincidence.”

Monthlight’s eyes reddened. She blinked back tears and softly said, “If it doesn’t work out, then so be it. There will be better matches waiting for you, Miss.”

Shen Weici hoarsely hummed in response and, exhausted, fell back asleep.

The room was very quiet. The burning pine and agarwood incense on the desk made one’s heart even calmer.

Even Monthlight felt drowsy in such a quiet room.

As the New Year approached, the palace was also busier than usual.

There had been many sacrificial prayers lately. Every year at this time, the Emperor would go to the hunting grounds, and Song Zhang often had to accompany him, so he was somewhat busy.

In the vast white snow, Song Zhang rode a horse beside the Emperor, with high-ranking officials following them into the depths of the forest.

Song Zhang’s gaze fell upon a white wolf, its fur pure and gleaming. He suddenly thought it would be good to make a hat or a cushion for Shen Weici with its pelt. He often saw her sitting in her room without a cushion—wouldn’t she be cold?

The thought was fleeting. He ordered the imperial guards to surround the area tightly, then took an arrow from behind him, nocked it, and aimed at the white wolf.

The sharp arrow flew out, only grazing its neck. The white wolf let out a whimper and disappeared.

Song Zhang kicked the black hound at his feet and released the hunting falcon from his hand, urging his horse to chase after it.

In the end, he carried the white wolf by its leg onto his horse. After some thought, he tossed it to a subordinate and ordered him to skin it first.

That night, there was a banquet and roasting at the hunting grounds. By the time he returned, it was late at night.

Drinking was inevitable, as the Emperor often bestowed wine upon them.

Song Zhang had drunk quite a bit today, and his steps were unsteady for once.

Ming He looked at Song Zhang with concern. “General, are you still going to the manor at this hour?”

Song Zhang held a pure white rabbit by one ear with one hand and the reins with the other. Without a word, he spurred his horse forward.

Ming He had no choice but to order the guards behind to follow closely.

By the time he returned, it was already deep into the night. Song Zhang stood in front of the main house, looking at the dim candlelight reflected on the bed for a long time before entering.

The room was very quiet. The maid guarding behind the screen saw Song Zhang enter and discreetly retreated.

Shen Weici had slept all day. Half-asleep, she suddenly felt a chill on her back. Her dizziness had improved somewhat, so she turned over and, in the dimness, saw Song Zhang sitting at the head of her bed, looking down at her.

chapters.title: Bringing Her a Snow Rabbit in the Middle of the Night
chapters.content:
His eyes were cold and distant, yet seemed to carry a trace of suppressed emotion.

She didn’t know when he had arrived or how long he had been sitting there.

She caught a faint scent of alcohol on him. He was still dressed in his dark, form-fitting attire, with faint, mottled damp marks visible on his shoulders—traces left by melting snow.

Shen Weici, seeing Song Zhang staring at her in silence, felt a slight unease at his late-night visit.

She propped herself up, coughed twice, and then asked, “Does Young Master Song have something to say to me?”

Song Zhang inhaled the fragrance from Shen Weici, a warmth that seemed to melt the coldness in his heart.

He held up the snow rabbit in his hand and presented it to Shen Weici, gazing deeply into her eyes as he asked in a low voice, “Do you like it?”

Snow rabbits were rare. Among thousands, only one might be pure white, and they were extremely adorable.

Song Zhang had seen women in the capital keeping white rabbits before. He used to think there was little point in keeping such docile creatures—only women confined to their boudoirs would enjoy them. But the moment he saw this snow rabbit, he had wanted to catch it and bring it to her.

Perhaps she would like it too.

Shen Weici stared in surprise at the snow-white rabbit dangling in the air by its ears, its legs kicking helplessly. It looked uncomfortable, so she reached out and took the palm-sized rabbit into her arms, then nodded. “I do.”

Song Zhang smiled slightly. “Tomorrow, I’ll have someone make a cage for you to keep it in.”

Shen Weici didn’t understand why Song Zhang had come in the middle of the night just to give her a rabbit.

She ran her fingers over the rabbit’s ears, lowering her gaze to the obedient little creature in her hands before nodding again.

Song Zhang kept his eyes fixed on Shen Weici’s gentle expression. The flush on her face had faded somewhat, but a faint pink still lingered. Her eyes still glistened with moisture, and her lowered lashes were dotted with tiny beads of light, like morning dew.

Her delicate features, with their misty, downcast beauty, her slender neck and fragrant shoulders—she was like a pearl cloud rising after the rain.

Her face, soft as spring blossoms, was more enchanting than green mountains.

His gaze softened imperceptibly. “I hunted a white wolf and a white marten. I’ll have them made into a hat and a cushion for you.”

“Or perhaps a collar or a stove cover.”

He paused, looking at her. “What would you like?”

Shen Weici was momentarily stunned by his words. She looked up at him, her throat tightening as she struggled to speak.

To refuse would be to reject his kindness, but to accept felt unjustified.

Her conflicting thoughts left her in a dilemma.

Song Zhang seemed to notice her hesitation. He raised an eyebrow indifferently. “It was just a wolf I happened to kill. It’s not worth much.”

“Wolf fur is a bit coarser than fox fur, so I’ll have the cushion made from it. The marten fur will be used for a hat to keep the wind out.”

As he spoke, Shen Weici realized that refusing his kindness now would seem ungrateful.

Even though she knew she shouldn’t accept his gifts.

She lowered her head again, looking at the rabbit in her hands, and whispered, “Thank you, Young Master Song.”

As she spoke, her throat tickled again, and she couldn’t help but cover her mouth and cough.

This time, it wasn’t feigned illness—her cough was real, and so was her discomfort.

Her head had been heavy and foggy all day. She had changed her undergarments several times, yet cold sweat still beaded on her skin.

She knew this illness would take a long time to recover from.

After catching her breath, her voice was even hoarser.

Shen Weici turned her head and pressed a handkerchief to her lips, weakly lowering her eyes as she said in a hoarse voice, “I appreciate Young Master Song’s concern for me at night, but I fear I might infect you. You should go rest as well.”

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici’s wrinkled undergarments, her thin, fragile shoulders, and heard her soft voice. He reached out and touched her face, lifting a strand of her fragrant hair.

Then, he gradually leaned in closer.

Song Zhang’s fingers were warm. Though they lifted her hair, they kept brushing against her cheek.

Shen Weici suppressed the flutter in her heart, feeling the shadow before her grow heavier. The scent of alcohol on him grew stronger.

She instinctively turned her head away, but the next moment, her chin was gripped by his other hand. His hot breath fanned her ear as he asked, “Why are you avoiding me?”

Shen Weici felt her heart race even more. She could almost feel the heat from his chest against her shoulder.

His ambiguous words left her at a loss. She could only cover her mouth and cough again.

She turned her back to him completely, her soft coughs lasting longer than ever. Song Zhang frowned deeply as he watched her back. The thin barrier between them, no matter how hard he tried, seemed impossible to tear apart.

But seeing Shen Weici so frail, he suppressed the discomfort in his heart and gently patted her back. “Go to sleep.”

“I’ll have the imperial physician come examine your pulse again tomorrow.”

Shen Weici’s coughing left her slightly breathless. Hearing Song Zhang’s words, she hummed in agreement.

She still had her back to him, softly saying, “Young Master Song should rest early as well.”

Song Zhang looked at her back in silence.

He still hadn’t had enough of looking at her.

But then he remembered her involvement with Zhang Yuanheng, and his mood soured.

Her affair with Zhang Yuanheng wasn’t resolved yet.

He really wanted to know—now that she knew Zhang Yuanheng could only take her as a concubine, what was she thinking?

Was she still determined to enter the Earl’s mansion, or would she sever ties with Zhang Yuanheng?

Did she still love him?

Song Zhang wanted to ask, but then he noticed the faint cold sweat on Shen Weici’s forehead.

He stayed silent for a long time. He wanted to wipe it for her but feared she would avoid him. Finally, he said in a low voice, “Alright.”

Before leaving, he picked up the snow rabbit from Shen Weici’s arms. Seeing her gaze, he said indifferently, “This thing will jump around at night and disturb your sleep.”

Shen Weici paused for a moment before nodding.

She watched Song Zhang’s tall figure leave, then exhaled a warm breath and closed her eyes.

Perhaps because she had slept too much during the day, Shen Weici didn’t sleep well that night.

In her groggy state, she had many dreams. Each time she dreamed of falling into the icy lake, she would jolt awake, only to wearily close her eyes again.

Song Zhang left very early in the morning. Before leaving, he came to check on Shen Weici. Seeing that the flush on her face had faded, he couldn’t help but stand by the bed, bending down to feel her forehead.

It was no longer burning hot.

He withdrew his hand and looked at Shen Weici’s still deeply sleeping face.

There was still fatigue in her eyes—clearly, she hadn’t slept well.

He pressed his lips together, then carefully examined her eyes before standing up and leaving.

Shen Weici didn’t wake up until mid-morning. Yue Deng, who had been keeping watch by the bed, saw her wake and asked, “Miss, are you hungry?”

Shen Weici had little appetite during her illness, but Song Zhang still sent over many dishes every day. With the maid’s urging, she had eaten some.

Though she wasn’t hungry, she didn’t want to worry those around her, so she nodded.

As usual, there were many dishes. Shen Weici ate a little hastily, then, seeing no one urging her, she finally set down her chopsticks to rinse her mouth.

While drinking her medicine, Yue Deng said, “This morning, the imperial physician came to check your pulse and said the internal heat in your body has lessened. However, the cold still needs time to recover from. As long as you take good care of yourself, your health will improve.”

Shen Weici hummed in response. After finishing her medicine and sucking on a plum, she stared blankly at the floor, lost in thought.

Yue Deng glanced at the carpeted floor but saw nothing unusual. She couldn’t help but ask, “Miss, what are you thinking about?”

Shen Weici shook her head. “Nothing.”

After staying at the estate for two more days, Song Zhang seemed busy and didn’t return for two days in a row.

Shen Weici quietly recuperated and felt a little stronger. She thought about returning the next day.

Having spent two or three days lying in bed, she felt that if she stayed any longer, her body might fall apart.

Yue Deng helped Shen Weici sit up in a chair, then brought in a cage. “Miss, look how cute it is.”

“It’s as cute as the Persian cat at Young Master Zhang’s residence.”

Shen Weici bent down to let the snow rabbit out of the cage to play at her feet. A smile crept into her eyes as she stroked the rabbit’s ears. Startled, it shrank into a tiny ball, its cuteness overwhelming.

Shen Weici looked at the little ball at her feet. She couldn’t imagine how someone as cold and aloof as Song Zhang, with his usual disdain and mockery, would think to catch this little snowball and bring it back.

She picked it up and held it in her arms. In truth, she felt that such a little creature belonged in the mountains and forests. If kept, it wouldn’t live long.

She once kept an injured gray rabbit while gathering herbs in the mountains. She had taken meticulous care of it, even picking its favorite leaves, but it still only lived a little over three months.

She thought to herself that when she left tomorrow, she would release this little one.

The doors and windows of the room were tightly shut, and a bronze stove was placed in the corner. Even though Shen Weici’s clothes weren’t particularly heavy, she still felt warm inside the room.

Song Zhang returned in the late afternoon, just as it was getting dark.

He had spent the past two days accompanying the Empress Dowager and the Empress to Taiyun Mountain to pray for blessings. His heart had been inexplicably drawn to her, and as soon as he returned, he came to see her.

As soon as he entered the inner room, he saw Shen Weici holding the snow rabbit and talking to Yue Deng beside her. Her voice was soft, likely reminiscing about her past in Yuyang. He listened for a moment, then walked over.

Without any hesitation, he sat down beside her, glanced at the snow rabbit in her arms, and then at her slightly pale cheeks. “Are you feeling better?”

Shen Weici nodded. “A little better.”

Song Zhang smelled the medicine in the room and asked, “Do you still cough?”

Shen Weici, still lowering her eyes, lightly traced the rabbit’s ears with her slender fingers. “Occasionally, a few coughs.”

Song Zhang nodded. A silent stillness settled between them, so heavy that even Yue Deng, sitting to the side, felt restless.

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici, then reached out to touch the rabbit in her arms. “Is it obedient?”

His long fingers brushed against her fingertips. Naturally, he pinched the rabbit’s ears, so she had to pretend to be calm and pull her hand back. “It is.”

Then she slightly turned her head to look at Song Zhang. “I was thinking of returning tomorrow.”

Shen Weici’s voice was very soft, gentle. “These days, I’ve been disturbing Young Master Song. It makes me uneasy.”

“And my health is much better. If I stay away too long, the Old Madam and my father might worry.”

Song Zhang listened indifferently, withdrawing his hand, and let out a cold, mocking laugh.

Shen Weici heard his scoff and fell silent. She herself felt her words were a bit ridiculous.

The Old Madam and her father wouldn’t worry about her.

She knew no one in the Marquis’s mansion would care about her.

She just wanted to return before the New Year and settle the matter between her and Zhang Yuanheng.

chapters.title: Do You Really Like Him?
chapters.content:
Shen Weici fell silent, her slender fingertips buried in the snow rabbit’s long, soft fur.

With another finger, she teased the rabbit’s neck.

She quietly lowered her eyes, as if she hadn’t heard Song Zhang’s mocking laugh just now.

Song Zhang crossed his legs and leaned back in the chair. With one hand, he pulled the snow rabbit from Shen Weici’s arms into his own lap. His tone was casual. “Stay here one more day. I’ll send you back the day after tomorrow.”

A day earlier or later didn’t matter much.

Shen Weici was grateful to Song Zhang.

After all, he had saved her.

She nodded and said softly, “Then I’ll trouble Young Master Song.”

But with the snow rabbit now in Song Zhang’s arms, the warm little ball gone, she suddenly felt a chill in her lap.

She turned her head to see Song Zhang pinching the back of the snow rabbit’s neck, holding it up in front of him and poking its round face with his finger. The rabbit scratched at the air with its paws, trying to bite his finger.

Shen Weici watched Song Zhang’s expression—his eyes slightly narrowed, amused by the playful antics.

His face was naturally noble and handsome, but with those cold, phoenix-like eyes, there was a hint of roguish arrogance. He always looked at people with a cold, aloof air, often with a sword at his side and a dagger at his back, making him seem even more untouchable.

Moreover, in the Marquis’s mansion, he wasn’t close to anyone. She had seen him exchange few words even with the Old Master, and whenever they met, it was with cold sarcasm, making him seem difficult to approach.

She never expected him to have the interest to play with a rabbit.

Shen Weici’s gaze was too noticeable. Song Zhang’s phoenix eyes flicked, meeting her gaze directly.

Shen Weici froze. She had only been looking at the rabbit in Song Zhang’s hand and had glanced at him by chance, but he caught her looking. A wave of embarrassment washed over her, and she turned her head away in a fluster.

Song Zhang placed the rabbit in front of her and raised an eyebrow. “Try it. See if it bites you.”

Shen Weici felt it was a bit childish, but seeing Song Zhang’s expectant look, she stretched out her finger and gently touched the rabbit’s nose.

But it kept kicking its legs, clearly very uncomfortable.

Shen Weici cupped it with both hands and said softly, “Maybe I should hold it.”

Song Zhang watched the white fingers reaching toward him. He loosened his grip, letting the rabbit fall into Shen Weici’s hands.

But the rabbit, perhaps startled earlier, the moment it gained freedom in Shen Weici’s hands, suddenly leapt up and bit Song Zhang’s finger in what seemed like revenge.

Song Zhang was caught off guard. The rabbit’s teeth sank in, and even after shaking his hand twice, it wouldn’t let go. He had to use force to fling it to the ground.

The rabbit hit the floor and then bolted away in a flash, but Song Zhang’s finger was bleeding.

Shen Weici saw the blood welling up and quickly ordered Tan Mama, who was standing nearby, to fetch medicine. Without thinking, she used the embroidered handkerchief in her hand to press against Song Zhang’s wound.

Song Zhang only felt a pair of impossibly soft fingers on his hand. He was startled and looked up at Shen Weici.

He saw her lowering her head, her fingers pressing on his fingertip through the handkerchief. When she looked up, she froze again, and the warm fragrance from her hand was gone.

He displeasedly extended his finger in front of her. “Aren’t you going to hold the wound for me?”

Song Zhang’s expression was calm as he looked at her, as if it were only natural for her to do so.

Shen Weici moved her fingers slightly, hesitated, then lowered her head to press on his wound again.

The cut was deep—it must have hurt a lot.

Tan Mama quickly brought the medicine. Shen Weici gently removed the handkerchief, revealing a nail-length gash. She hadn’t expected such a small rabbit to leave such a large bite.

She had Tan Mama bring a warm towel, then patiently wiped away the blood, applied the ointment, and finally wrapped it with silk cloth.

Shen Weici’s movements were methodical and composed, showing no panic at the sight of blood. She efficiently finished the task, earning Tan Mama’s silent admiration.

It only took a short while to clean and dress the wound.

By now, the sky had darkened, and the candles were lit. Song Zhang kept watching Shen Weici, taking in her lowered lashes, her painted brows, and her long, delicate eyelashes.

Perhaps because she was ill, her long hair wasn’t properly styled—just loosely pinned with a silver hairpin. Many strands had come loose, falling around her.

The silver hairpin was the one he

The first time he saw her, he noticed the silver hairpin in her hair. Later, he had also seen her wear a jade hairpin, but the one she wore the longest was this old silver hairpin.

The design on the silver hairpin was simple—two intertwined flower branches, slightly worn smooth, the pattern almost indistinct. He couldn’t understand why she liked this hairpin so much.

After his finger was bandaged, he looked at it, then turned to Shen Weici: “Have dinner with me.”

There were only the two of them, and no one else to mind.

Shen Weici lifted her gaze to Song Zhang, then nodded.

During the meal, neither spoke. Song Zhang, however, couldn’t help but glance at Shen Weici repeatedly.

She ate with delicate grace, slowly and methodically, occasionally turning her head to cough. Even in the candlelight, her sickly complexion remained gaunt.

Flickering candlelight fell on her fingertips, the tip of her nose, and her perpetually downcast eyes. Suddenly, Song Zhang asked her, “The Earl’s Mansion doesn’t intend to hold a grand wedding for you.”

“You understand what this means. Don’t you have anything to say?”

Shen Weici’s fingers, holding the jade chopsticks, tightened, then she shook her head. “No.”

Song Zhang set down his chopsticks and leaned back in his chair, studying her. “Do you really want to?”

“To be a concubine?”

Shen Weici paused, then looked up at Song Zhang. “I won’t be a concubine.”

Song Zhang stared deeply at Shen Weici. “Then do you still love him?”

Shen Weici didn’t know how to answer.

She knew she couldn’t say she truly loved Zhang Yuanheng, but she could feel his sincerity toward her.

He was such a gentle man, always careful and respectful in his gaze and approach. A man of noble birth, refined, capable, and upright—a true gentleman.

But he had nearly deceived her, trying to make her a concubine.

She also understood that her fate with Zhang Yuanheng was likely at an end.

She hesitated, then softly said, “I do.”

Shen Weici said this for Song Zhang’s sake. She knew he had feelings for her, but she would not be a concubine. It was better to end this ambiguity now.

She was painfully aware that nothing would ever come of her and Song Zhang.

Hearing her words, Song Zhang felt an inexplicable surge of anger.

He coldly studied Shen Weici’s face, searching for some other emotion, but she remained as gentle as ever. This only made him silently mock himself for his own frustration.

What did it matter to him if she loved Zhang Yuanheng?

He had no shortage of women by his side.

Yet, his body suddenly stood up, and he strode out in large steps.

The corridor was blanketed in cold snow. He stepped into it, and when a servant came with an umbrella, he kicked it away with his foot. With a dark expression, he walked out of the courtyard.

He brought his injured finger to his eyes, examining the finely wrapped silk. It still carried the faint warmth of her scent. He let out a cold laugh, tore off the silk, and threw it into the snow.

He thought about stomping on it with his boot, but hesitated mid-air and simply stepped over it.

Shen Weici stared blankly at the empty space in front of her, then at Song Zhang’s retreating figure in the heavy snow.

That night, before bed, Shen Weici took a hot bath, drank her medicine, and then, leaning against the pillow, coughed weakly several times.

Beads of cold sweat formed on her forehead.

Yue Deng sat beside her, wiping her sweat, and softly said with concern, “Miss, this illness... might take a long time to recover.”

As she spoke, she grew angry, her voice trembling, “Falling into that freezing lake, and then waiting so long... If this really leaves a lasting condition, I won’t let Shen Zhaozhao off easily either.”

Shen Weici’s body ached terribly. Even though she had just bathed and changed into fresh undergarments, she now felt sweat seeping through her back.

She asked, “Was the snow rabbit found?”

Yue Deng, red-eyed and choking back tears, replied, “Miss, you’re still thinking about that rabbit at a time like this. The maid just caught it and put it in a cage.”

Shen Weici reached out to wipe Yue Deng’s tears. “It’s nothing. There will be a chance to get it back.”

“Let’s sleep now.”

Only then did Yue Deng wipe her tears, hum in agreement, and tuck another handkerchief behind Shen Weici’s back. “Miss, don’t kick off the blankets if you feel hot at night. The imperial physician said you need to stay warm for a few more days.”

“How long until this cough gets better?”

Shen Weici lay on her side, letting Yue Deng fuss over her, half-closing her eyes in drowsiness.

Yue Deng’s voice came from behind her again, “Earlier, when the Second Young Master came back, he seemed quite cheerful, even smiled a couple of times. Why did he suddenly leave during dinner?”

Shen Weici buried her head in the blanket, her voice hoarse. “He saved me... and took responsibility for me.”

“Don’t overthink it.”

Yue Deng hummed in agreement, then pulled Shen Weici’s undergarments back down and pulled up the blanket. “How many lamps does Miss want to keep lit tonight?”

Previously, Shen Weici had only kept one lamp lit, but after having nightmares, she had started keeping two.

Shen Weici didn’t turn her head, her voice tired and soft. “Just one.”

Yue Deng hummed again, got up, and lowered the bed curtains before going to the side room to sleep.

The entire room was warm. The charcoal burner, which burned smokeless snowflake charcoal all day and night, kept the room heated. Even with the windows tightly shut, the air was thick with the heavy scent of medicine. Having been indoors for two or three days, Shen Weici felt an oppressive tightness in her chest.

Listening to Yue Deng settle down for the night, she coughed again and sat up, wanting to open the window for some air.

Barefoot on the carpet, she slightly opened the window. A gust of cold wind rushed in, but she felt her chest ease. Only then did she return to the bed.

Suddenly, her mind flashed back to the night Song Zhang had come and kissed her lips, and his figure as he stormed off today. Her heart pounded uneasily. She knew she shouldn’t have any more entanglements with Song Zhang, yet they kept running into each other.

She lay there, restless, unable to sleep despite her exhaustion. She couldn’t stop coughing, and the cold sweat returned.

Her body ached, tossing and turning.

She hadn’t been this ill in a long time.

She thought again about how she had originally wanted to ask the Old Madam to invite the Earl’s Mansion’s imperial physician to diagnose her pulse. But now, returning might not work.

Her body was weak; the imperial physician’s diagnosis probably wouldn’t be good either.

Yue Deng had mentioned that the imperial physician said this illness might affect her ability to conceive.

She couldn’t think of any other solution.

With her eyes half-closed, Shen Weici exhaled a warm breath, trying to clear her mind. But her unease only made her thoughts spiral further.

In the quiet room, footsteps suddenly approached. Then, a sliver of candlelight pierced through the dim bed curtains. Shen Weici started, turning alertly, and saw Song Zhang standing by the bed.

chapters.title: Let Me Hold You for a While, and You Won’t Owe Me Anymore
chapters.content:
His shoulders and black hair were dusted with snow, as if he had just come in. He wore a loose, dark green open-sleeved robe, revealing the pristine middle garment underneath.

His thick brows and star-like eyes were sharp, his phoenix-shaped eyes frosted over, lips tightly pressed. His towering figure stood before her, almost blocking out the candlelight behind him.

Shen Weici had never seen him dressed like this before. Moreover, in such cold weather, didn’t he feel the chill?

And why had he come so late at night...

Shen Weici noticed his expression seemed poor. Remembering what had happened at dinner, she felt an inexplicable unease and asked, “Has Young Master Song come to discuss something?”

Song Zhang only looked down at her silently.

Shen Weici couldn’t gauge his thoughts and feared being alone with him like this, so she looked at him again. “Shall I call a maid to pour Young Master Song a hot cup of tea to warm up?”

She then called out toward the outside, “Yue Deng.”

But after calling twice, no one responded. Her unease grew. Forcing herself to stay calm, she propped herself up. “Yue Deng must be asleep. Let me pour Young Master Song a warm cup of tea.”

But just as she sat up, a hand suddenly pressed down on her shoulder. She saw Song Zhang lean down, his fingers lifting her chin. His gaze met hers, and before she could react, he kissed her directly on the lips.

Shen Weici had never experienced such boldness before. Forced to accept it, her face flushed crimson, and she struggled uncomfortably.

But Song Zhang only deepened the kiss.

Panic filled Shen Weici’s eyes. She bit down on Song Zhang’s tongue, and the metallic taste of blood spread between their mouths. Song Zhang paused, narrowing his eyes at her. Through her disheveled hair, he saw her delicate, tear-streaked face, and suppressed his irritation.

The slightly ajar window was suddenly blown open by the wind and snow outside, and flurries of white snow drifted in, extinguishing the only candle on the bedside table.

Knowing Shen Weici was ill, Song Zhang feared she would catch a chill. He stood up and fumbled in the dark to close the window.

The room, now without candlelight, was pitch black, yet Song Zhang unerringly found her.

He pulled her into his embrace, tightly holding her. His cold expression finally revealed a trace of warmth he had never shown before.

He lowered his head, brushing away the moisture at the corner of Shen Weici’s eyes, then kissed her forehead. His voice was low, “You said you wanted to repay me. Let me hold you for a while, and you won’t owe me anymore.”

He held her soft body tightly, his emotions easing. His fingers gripped her slender waist, but he didn’t make any further advances.

The breathing in his embrace was shallow, punctuated by a couple of coughs, her voice weak.

He heard her slightly choked voice, “What does Young Master Song take me for?”

Song Zhang didn’t answer. Instead, he buried his head in Shen Weici’s fragrant neck and licked it lightly. The conflict in his heart tormented him just as much.

He resented how much Shen Weici liked Zhang Yuanheng, yet was annoyed at himself for caring so deeply about her.

He wanted to be close to her so badly.

Every time he saw her, he couldn’t help but go to her, yet she had never truly considered him, rejecting him time and time again.

When had he ever had to seek a woman’s favor? Why was she so difficult to please?

Song Zhang’s gaze darkened. The woman in his arms had never stopped struggling. He felt the moisture on his chest—her warm cheek pressed against him, bringing dampness.

That moisture was clearly warm, yet it gradually chilled Song Zhang’s heart.

He looked down at her silently, his fingers slowly loosening.

Song Zhang stood up and left without a word.

The restraining force on her body suddenly vanished. Before Shen Weici could react, she heard footsteps outside the curtain, accompanied by a faint candlelight, followed by the sound of retreating footsteps.

Then, there was silence.

That must have been the maid coming in to light the candle.

Shen Weici stared blankly at the slightly disheveled bed, dazed for a long time before finally closing her eyes and burying her face in the pillow.

Song Zhang’s days were no easier. He had never been one to restrain himself, especially not for women. Yet now, it seemed he was guarding his purity for Shen Weici. His mind was filled with her; no other woman caught his eye.

Among his peers from noble families, he was the only one who hadn’t yet experienced intimacy. Now, back in the capital, surrounded by beautiful women, he had to encounter someone as indifferent as her.

At his age, he hadn’t truly been with a woman—he was almost ashamed to admit it.

Yet, he restrained himself from touching her further.

As the thought stirred his emotions, his hand clenched, and he let out a suppressed breath.

He rarely did such things. Before twenty, he had been in the military camp with no time for such thoughts. Now, he felt utterly wretched.

Then, he thought of Zhang Yuanheng—what did he have that made Shen Weici love him? The mere thought of Zhang Yuanheng possibly holding Shen Weici in his arms in the future extinguished any interest he had.

The next day was a rest day. Song Zhang had even specially requested leave from the emperor the day before, just to spend it with Shen Weici.

Last night’s unpleasantness left him in a foul mood. When he coldly heard the servant report that Shen Weici’s cough had worsened and she had barely eaten breakfast, he abruptly stood up.

Halfway there, he stopped, his expression turning cold.

She was determined to marry Zhang Yuanheng. Why was he chasing after her like this?

Right now, he was no different from Zhang Yuanheng back then—both of them were distracted by her.

Song Zhang decided not to see her again. Given last night’s events, she probably wouldn’t give him a pleasant face anyway. Why should he go to her so eagerly?
