But just as he had sat down for a while, the servant came again to say Shen Weici was leaving. Song Zhang gritted his teeth, lifted the curtain, and walked out.

When he reached the courtyard, he saw Shen Weici covering her mouth with a handkerchief as she coughed, her face pale, with a faint redness in her eyes.

He couldn’t help but look at her neck. She was dressed neatly, her smoky green cross-collar jacket with a high collar covering her neck completely.

Beside her, Yue Deng was standing, tying the hood of her cloak, clearly preparing to leave.

Then, he saw her standing under the eaves, reaching out to catch the snow. He coldly walked over and stood in the courtyard, looking at her. “Leaving when you’re still sick?”

“Didn’t I say I’d send you off tomorrow morning?”

Shen Weici had already seen Song Zhang approaching. She had been waiting for him.

She coughed a couple of times, feeling dizzy and listless, her eyes lacking energy. Her voice, hoarse from coughing, remained gentle and soft. “These past few days have troubled Young Master Song. Weici doesn’t dare impose any longer and disturb Young Master Song’s peace.”

The coldness in Song Zhang’s phoenix eyes was almost as chilling as the snow.

The emotions deep in his gaze were almost uncontrollable.

Their eyes met—one cold to the bone, the other still gentle and weak.

Song Zhang stood outside the corridor, and snow had already accumulated on him. He wore only a plain black round-collar robe, without even a fur coat. Snow covered his hair and shoulders.

He stared at her coldly, silent, his eyes brewing with anger.

Shen Weici silently opened the umbrella she was holding and held it over Song Zhang’s head. She spoke softly, “Young Master Song, don’t overthink it. I still remember your kindness.”

“And I don’t mean to quarrel with you.”

“With the wedding date approaching, my matters with Young Master Zhang must be resolved soon.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici lowered her gaze, her dark eyebrows tinged with sickness, her eyes weary. “Let’s forget about last night. We won’t mention it again.”

She was self-aware. Song Zhang was a heaven’s favorite, the only legitimate grandson of the Duke of Song’s mansion, the only legitimate son of Princess Huimin, a close minister to the emperor. Even the emperor intended to marry the Fifth Princess to him.

His wife would certainly be of noble status.

She had seen the Fifth Princess by his side before—she seemed very dependent on him. And with so many women around him, there was no place for her.

She had no intention of clinging to power or favor, nor did she wish to be a concubine vying for affection.

A fleeting moment of liking was not something that could last. For her, it was not meant to be long-term.

It was better to cancel it all now. It would be best if they had no further intersections.

Song Zhang listened to Shen Weici’s words with a cold smile. If they were never to mention it again, then they would never intersect again.

He, Song Zhang, had not yet sunk to the point of begging a woman for affection.

He didn’t need her to hold an umbrella for him now.

What was the point of these fake, irrelevant gestures?

After coldly listening, Song Zhang turned to his servant and said, “Miss Shen wants to leave. Prepare the carriage and have the front gate guards escort her all the way back.”

The servant, upon hearing this, quickly nodded and said to Shen Weici, “Miss Shen, please wait a moment. I’ll prepare the carriage right away.”

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici one last time, his lips tightly pressed, then strode away.

The wind and snow blew against Shen Weici’s face. She watched Song Zhang’s retreating figure, then turned and went back inside to wait.

chapters.title: I Will Not Be a Concubine
chapters.content:
The wind and snow in the capital were much heavier than in Yuyang and arrived earlier.

Shen Weici tightly clutched her cloak, her eyes nearly forced shut by the gusts.

The embroidered carriage canopy was lifted by the wind, and Shen Weici handed the snow rabbit in her hands to the attendant beside her, softly saying, “When you have the chance, release it.”

The attendant took the rabbit and acknowledged with a sound.

This estate was located in the outskirts of the city, built on the peak of Yuqing Mountain. According to Nurse Tan, this place used to be where Song Zhang’s father frequently visited. Every summer, he would stay here and invite scholars and refined guests to compose poetry and drink wine together.

Because Song Zhang’s father had poor health and had been ill since childhood, he had not pursued a military career.

After Song Zhang’s father passed away, almost no one came here anymore. However, Song Zhang had visited twice, and the old servants who stayed behind cleaned the place daily.

The layout remained the same as before. The study was filled with books, and the tea sets and utensils were all elegant, untouched.

Shen Weici had not left the house, nor had she gone to see the cliffside snow pines that Nurse Tan mentioned. Now, she turned back to glance at the grand estate before her, faintly visible through the wind and snow.

As if sensing something, she looked up and caught sight of a figure in black on the upper floor.

Shen Weici did not linger on it, lowering her head as she entered the carriage.

The carriage seemed to be the one Song Zhang usually used. It was spacious inside, and a charcoal brazier was burning on the floor, so it was not cold.

She coughed a couple of times, placing her icy fingers above the charcoal fire. The warmth gradually spread through her body, but then a headache struck. Supporting her forehead, she fell into deep thought.

Yue Deng watched her with distress. Shen Weici still looked seriously ill, and it was impossible for her to recover in just a few days.

She softly asked, “Actually, the estate is much warmer than Lingchun Courtyard. Why did you insist on leaving, Miss? You could have stayed a few more days.”

Shen Weici felt a severe headache. She had not slept well the previous night and was now even more exhausted.

She coughed a couple of times and said in a low, hoarse voice, “My matter with Lord Zhang cannot be delayed any longer.”

Yue Deng let Shen Weici lean on her shoulder and gently patted her back.

By the time they arrived at the Marquis of Jian’an’s residence, it was already past noon.

Shen Weici first went to see the old madam.

The old madam was just about to take her midday nap when she heard the message and had someone lead Shen Weici to the warm pavilion.

The old madam sat in the upper seat. Soon, the curtain was lifted, and a slender figure entered, looking visibly haggard and pale.

As soon as Shen Weici entered, she knelt before the old madam, her face flushed with tears. “Weici has not attended to the old madam for many days. I have come to apologize.”

The old madam was usually not easily moved, but seeing Shen Weici in such a state, having returned to pay her respects despite her illness, and instead of speaking of her grievances, she apologized for not attending to her, the old madam was slightly moved.

Perhaps it was also because she knew that Shen Weici had ended up like this due to the hardships and grievances she had suffered.

The old madam quickly ordered the servants to help Shen Weici up and had her sit beside her. She saw that Shen Weici’s eyes were red, filled with tears but not falling.

With her natural beauty that could make fish sink and geese fall, like a spring sea tang flower, elegant as a lotus yet with a touch of enchanting charm.

Seeing her in such a delicate and pitiful state, even the old madam felt a pang of pity.

She reached out to wipe Shen Weici’s tears and sighed, “I do not lack your service for a day.”

“I also know that you have been wronged.”

“Your mother has indeed gone too far. Your father already knows about this matter. He has sent her to the estate to rest, so she will not be able to come out for these days. Your marriage will be handled by me.”

“I know that you have been wronged.”

Only then did Shen Weici’s tears fall. She tilted her head and dabbed her tears with a handkerchief, coughed a few times before softly saying, “Weici knows that the old madam has always had my best interests at heart. Even while resting at the estate these past few days, I have been thinking of the old madam.”

“Weici has never felt wronged, nor have I blamed my mother.”

“Second Sister is naturally more important than me. My mother had the physician attend to Second Sister first, and I do not blame her for that.”

The old madam patted Shen Weici’s hand. The whole story had been clarified when Song Zhang came the other day. She could not bear to see what Madame Wen had done. This was not about prioritizing Shen Zhaozhao; it was clearly about not wanting Shen Weici to live.

Such malice was something she had not expected.

She looked at Shen Weici and said softly, “You need not make excuses for your mother anymore, fearing that you might offend her.”

“We all know your grievances, and your father knows as well. For these days, just focus on recovering. You do not need to come and attend to me. We can talk about it after you are better.”

“I see that you are still coughing. Has Song Zhang arranged for someone to see you?”

Shen Weici nodded, “The Young Master Song has taken good care of me. Although he is busy, he has called the imperial physician for me.”

“It’s just that these past few days, Young Master Song has been busy, and I have not seen him. When he returns, I will go and thank him.”

The old madam nodded, “You should indeed thank him. If it were not for him passing by coincidentally, neither your father nor I would have known. Otherwise, it would have turned into a major incident.”

The commotion that day had been quite significant.

As she spoke, the old madam’s gaze fell on Shen Weici’s face. Even though she was still ill, there was a delicate charm to her features, a rare beauty.

Such beauty was the kind that men adored the most. In all her years, she had seen countless people, but this was the first time she had encountered someone so enchantingly beautiful yet not vulgar.

Last time, Wang Shi from the third branch had repeatedly praised her, saying that with such looks, she could even marry into a prince’s residence.

Song Zhang had always stayed out of the marquis’s family affairs. She remembered that Song Zhang used to stay at the marquis’s residence for only a day or two, paying his respects to his mother a couple of times.

But for the past two months, he had been returning every day, which coincided with Shen Weici’s arrival.

However, from what Shen Weici had just said, Song Zhang did not seem to care much about her.

She casually asked, “Are you and Song Zhang familiar with each other in private? That day, he said he wanted to take you to the estate to recover, saying that the marquis’s residence was not safe. He seemed quite concerned about you.”

Shen Weici softly replied, “We are not particularly familiar. Last time, I embroidered sachets for each room in the marquis’s residence. Young Master Song said I embroidered well and asked if I could do other patterns. We exchanged a few words.”

“Young Master Song said he would not accept my things for free and told me that if I needed anything in the future, I could send a maid to find him.”

“This time, it was my maid who was worried about me and sought Young Master Song’s help.”

Shen Weici’s words were half-truths. The old madam listened and nodded, “He does not casually accept gifts. If he accepted yours, he must have liked them. Helping you once is reasonable.”

The old madam did not probe further into the matter. Seeing that Shen Weici kept covering her mouth with a handkerchief and occasionally coughed, she said, “Now that you are back, go and rest properly.”

Shen Weici looked at the old madam, tears welling up again, “Weici came today because there is another matter I need to discuss with the old madam.”

The old madam looked at Shen Weici and asked, “What matter?”

Shen Weici tearfully said, “Weici only found out when Lord Zhang came to visit me last time. It turns out that my mother did not betroth me to the Earl’s mansion as a wife but only set a date to take me in as a concubine.”

After Shen Weici finished speaking, the old madam was shocked, “What did you say?”

“This is not something you can fabricate.”

Shen Weici stood up and knelt before the old madam, “Old madam, please see clearly. How would Weici dare to fabricate such a matter?”

“My mother told Madame Zhang of the Earl’s mansion that I was frail and would not be good for childbearing. Madame Zhang then backed out and was only willing to take me as a concubine.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici, with tears in her eyes, kowtowed, “I beg the old madam to seek justice for Weici.”

She then looked up at the old madam, “Weici is still the third young lady of the marquis’s residence. If I marry into the Earl’s mansion as a concubine, it will affect the marriages of the fourth and fifth young ladies.”

“It is not that Weici has ever thought of marrying into a highly noble family, but for a young lady of the marquis’s residence to marry into the Earl’s mansion as a concubine, it is inevitable that people will talk.”

The old madam had never expected that Madame Wen would secretly do such a thing. She was so angry that she slammed the table, furious. Madame Wen had truly gone too far.

The status of the Earl’s mansion was lower than that of the marquis’s residence. Moreover, the only notable person in the Earl’s mansion was Zhang Erlang.

Even if a legitimate daughter of the marquis’s residence married him as a wife, it would not be considered a high marriage, and it could still be considered a suitable match.

But to be taken as a concubine by the Earl’s mansion was a lowering of status, implying that the marquis’s daughter could not find a proper marriage. This would certainly affect the future marriage prospects of the fourth and fifth young ladies.

Furthermore, there were already rumors outside about the second branch’s harsh treatment of illegitimate daughters. Shen Rongsheng had already been demoted due to this matter. If this news spread, there would be no face left.

She looked at Shen Weici kneeling on the ground, frowning as she softly said, “Rest assured about this matter. Tomorrow, I will send an invitation to the Earl’s mansion and ask Madame Zhang to come over for a talk. You just wait.”

“We must seek justice. If they truly do not want to marry, the young ladies of the marquis’s residence are not unmarriageable.”

Shen Weici kowtowed, “Weici thanks the old madam for her intervention.”

The old madam bent down to help Shen Weici up, looking at her face as she said, “Your mother has indeed treated you too harshly. I understand all of this and will not let you be wronged. Rest assured.”

Shen Weici obediently nodded.

After returning from the old madam’s place to Lingchun Courtyard, He Xia and Yan Er gathered around to ask about Shen Weici’s health.

Shen Weici saw their red-rimmed eyes and knew they were genuine. She smiled and told them not to worry.

The room was indeed not as warm as the estate. Even with three charcoal braziers burning, there was still a hint of cold in the air.

Shen Weici had only forced herself to endure this trip, and now her head was throbbing. She went to the bed and lay down.

Yue Deng gently pushed Shen Weici, “Miss, you have not eaten yet.”

Shen Weici shook her head, “I cannot eat.”

She buried herself under the brocade quilt, closing her eyes as she said, “Later, when father returns, wake me up.”

Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici’s back, “Miss, you are in such a state. What is the need to get up?”

Shen Weici coughed lightly again, her voice hoarse, “Now that I have returned, I should go and pay my respects to father. I cannot return without a word. Father might overthink.”

Yue Deng did not ask further. She turned and had He Xia move the charcoal brazier to the side of the bed, then had her stay and watch over Shen Weici. She herself went out to prepare some medicine.

chapters.title: Miss Shen, I’m Sorry
chapters.content:
The next day, Shen Weici’s cough did not improve, perhaps because she had caught a cold from the wind the day before.

Early in the morning, her father came to see her, sending servants with many tonics to nourish her body and replenish her qi and blood. He sat on a stool by Shen Weici’s bedside, looking at her pale face as she lay on the bed, and said softly with a hint of helplessness, “I know that since you entered the mansion, your birth mother has always treated you harshly, yet you have never complained about her to me.”

“Last night, the old madam also called me over. She knew that you had asked her to intervene on your behalf. I feel guilty towards you as well.”

“If I had asked a few more questions, it wouldn’t have come to this.”

As he spoke, Shen Rongsheng looked at Shen Weici. “Rest assured, I will not let you marry into the Earl’s mansion as a concubine. I have also explained this to the old madam. A young lady from a marquis’s family should not suffer such humiliation. When the Earl’s family comes, I will try my best to finalize this marriage.”

“If it doesn’t work out, so be it. We can consider this engagement null and void.”

“Soon after the New Year, the imperial examinations will be held. Once the results are announced, I will choose a promising scholar for you. I won’t let you suffer like this again.”

Shen Weici’s eyes reddened, and tears fell. “Actually, it’s all my fault. I haven’t done enough to make my birth mother like me, and instead, I’ve made things difficult for you, Father.”

“I didn’t want this either.”

“Please, Father, don’t let this matter create a rift between you and my birth mother.”

Shen Rongsheng felt that this daughter was indeed very considerate, much more so than Shen Zhaozhao.

These days, Shen Zhaozhao had been crying and shouting since she woke up after falling into the water, claiming that Shen Weici had pushed her and demanding that he take action.

This was impossible to believe.

Not to mention how Shen Zhaozhao usually treated Shen Weici, but Shen Weici’s health was not as good as Shen Zhaozhao’s.

Moreover, Shen Weici usually only had one maidservant by her side, while Shen Zhaozhao had both maidservants and wet nurses attending to her. Given Shen Zhaozhao’s temperament, how could she possibly be at a disadvantage?

Furthermore, there were the things that Madame Wen had done afterwards, which made it even more impossible.

But he still asked Shen Weici, “What happened that day that caused you and Zhaozhao to fall into the water together?”

Shen Weici did not hide anything and told him everything in detail.

After listening, Shen Rongsheng closed his eyes and nodded, then sighed as he looked at Shen Weici. “Zhang Erlang came to see you the day before yesterday and found out that you had fallen into the water. Today, I will have him come and see you. You two can talk, and you can also gauge his attitude.”

“See if there is any room for reconciliation. Afterwards, I will have a long talk with him.”

“Moreover, he is genuinely worried about you falling into the water. He has been coming over these past two days to ask about you. I know he has feelings for you. It won’t hurt for you to see him.”

Shen Weici softly said, “Our engagement is uncertain now. It would not be appropriate for us to meet again.”

Shen Rongsheng looked at Shen Weici. “I know what you mean, but he has been coming every day these past few days. I am also at my wit’s end with his persistence.”

“Regardless, he is sincere towards you and genuinely worried about your health. Whether it works out or not, we can talk about it later.”

Shen Weici’s refusal was still on her lips when Shen Rongsheng added, “He is at the courtyard gate now. Our engagement is still on, so it won’t hurt for you to see him.”

After saying this, he left.

After Shen Rongsheng left, Yue Deng came in with a bowl of bird’s nest soup. “Miss, the kitchen made it early this morning.”

Shen Weici remained silent, gazing at the small porcelain bowl of bird’s nest soup, and took a bite.

Her father had never truly cared about her marriage; otherwise, he would have known that she had not actually been engaged. The three rites and six etiquettes of the engagement, he had not inquired about any of them. If he had, he would not have failed to notice.

She knew her father’s intention. He still wanted to push through with this engagement; otherwise, he would not have asked her to see Zhang Yuanheng.

Soon after, He Xia entered and said, “Miss, Young Master Zhang is outside the courtyard and wants to see you.”

“He says that the master asked him to come.”

Shen Weici rubbed her forehead and said, “Let him in.”

He Xia nodded and, after a moment, led Zhang Yuanheng in.

Zhang Yuanheng stood behind the screen, speaking to Shen Weici from behind it, his voice slightly hoarse. “Miss Shen, how have you been lately?”

Shen Weici looked at the tall and graceful figure behind the screen. He was still so courteous, never overstepping his bounds.

Now, as she looked at his figure, she couldn’t help but feel that fate was playing a cruel trick on her.

She wanted peace, but it seemed she could never have it.

Leaning on the pillow, she softly spoke to the figure outside the screen. “Master Zhang, do not worry. Everything is fine.”

Zhang Yuanheng heard her weak and feeble voice, and his eyes grew hot, his heart tightening. He walked out from behind the screen.

As soon as he entered, he had smelled a strong medicinal scent. Looking at the room’s furnishings, although everything was present, there was none of the delicacy of a lady’s boudoir, and it faintly exuded an air of antiquity.

His heart ached even more.

He had originally intended to marry her and treat her well afterwards.

He suddenly felt ashamed before her.

The promises he had made before were still fresh in his mind, but in the blink of an eye, so many things had happened.

His eyes welled up slightly, and he suddenly wanted to see what she looked like now.

He forgot about the rules and took a step forward from behind the screen. In one glance, he saw Shen Weici leaning against the bed.

She looked like he had never seen her before.

Her jet-black, soft hair was spread out, and she was wearing a light white undergarment, with a brocade quilt pulled up to her chest.

Originally a person of soft and graceful beauty, she now had a pale face, light cherry lips, and only her eyes were full of a misty, distant gaze, like a light drizzle over a distant mountain, her dark eyebrows like a wisp of smoke and rain.

He saw the sickness on her face and the fatigue in her eyes, and quickly retreated back behind the screen to apologize.

He sat down on the stool that Yue Deng had brought over.

Shen Weici had no extra energy to care about his earlier actions. She softly said first, “I heard from my father that you have been coming these past two days. It’s just that I wasn’t here before, so I couldn’t see you.”

“Don’t worry about me. I just caught a cold. I’ll be fine after resting for a few days.”

Zhang Yuanheng’s eyes reddened. He couldn’t bear to see Shen Weici like this. He lowered his head and said hoarsely, “Miss Shen, I’m sorry...”

Hearing his apology, Shen Weici felt her heart gradually grow cold. She still comforted him, “You have nothing to be sorry for.”

“I know you did your best.”

Zhang Yuanheng’s eyes were filled with redness. “I wasn’t able to come see you in time when you fell into the water, and I couldn’t take care of you by your side.”

“I was also useless. I couldn’t persuade my mother.”

“Miss Shen...”

“I couldn’t do anything.”

Shen Weici understood. After all, people always chased after their own interests.

She closed her eyes. “I don’t blame you.”

Zhang Yuanheng looked at the vague figure behind the screen. “Can you please comply with my mother just this once? After I marry you and bring you into the family, regardless of whether you can bear a legitimate son or not, I will definitely marry you as my wife.”

“Regardless of how much my mother tries to stop me, I won’t listen to her anymore. Can you do that?”

“I really want to marry you, to take care of you. I don’t want you to suffer any more grievances in this place.”

“Trust me this once. I won’t let you down. I can make a written oath in front of your father. If I let you down, I will accept any punishment from the Marquis’s family. Can I?”

Shen Weici rubbed her forehead and sighed softly.

If Zhang Yuanheng couldn’t even stand up to his mother now, how could he possibly do so in the future?

Not to mention whether Zhang Yuanheng’s feelings would change, even if he remained constant towards her, the family would be in turmoil over this matter, and a rift would form. How could she live well then?

She had originally wanted to be a good daughter-in-law and serve her parents-in-law, not to face cold treatment.

Zhang Yuanheng was currently the only pillar of his family, so it was definitely impossible for him to separate from the family. That meant they would have to live together forever. Even the deepest feelings would create rifts in endless conflicts.

Zhang Yuanheng would not be able to stand by her side forever.

Shen Weici rubbed her eyebrows, her headache still severe.

She softly said, “My grandmother will send an invitation to the Earl’s mansion today. She will invite Madame Zhang to come and discuss our engagement in detail.”

“We can talk about it then.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici also lowered her eyes and softly said, “My birth mother actually does not like me, so the things my birth mother said cannot be taken seriously.”

Zhang Yuanheng knew what Shen Weici meant. He just hadn’t told her that his mother didn’t completely believe those things either.

It was just that his mother couldn’t accept Shen Weici in her heart. She always thought that he could find a better marriage, saying it was a compromise, but in reality, she hadn’t truly compromised. She was just going along with Madame Shen’s words.

This was Zhang Yuanheng’s pain.

He couldn’t explain, and he couldn’t let go.

He wanted to ask her to endure for now and then slowly find a way later.

But as soon as he said this, he was afraid she would be unwilling.

At one point, he actually regretted telling Shen Weici beforehand.

He should have kept it from her first, even if it was a bit selfish.

But as long as she entered the family first, she would rely on him and trust him. He would be good to her and give her promises.

He just needed time.

Zhang Yuanheng’s shoulders slumped in defeat, and he nodded. “Alright, I will talk to my mother again properly after I go back.”

Shen Weici saw Zhang Yuanheng’s dejected spirit and the words she wanted to say stuck in her throat.

He seemed to want to say that she wouldn’t be his concubine, but also felt that now was not the time to say such things.

She softly said, “Master Zhang, don’t think too much. No matter what the outcome, everything will be fine.”

Zhang Yuanheng closed his eyes, his voice restrained. “I will listen to you.”

Just before Zhang Yuanheng left, he untied his pouch from his waist under the corridor and stuffed it into Yue Deng’s hand, softly saying, “I know that your miss has a hard life. Keep this silver. Don’t tell her. Take it to the kitchen and have them make more good dishes.”

“Or buy a few winter clothes to keep warm.”

“She is in such a state. You should take good care of her. I will come again later.”

Yue Deng, holding the heavy pouch, quickly refused and pushed it back. “Miss has already told me not to accept anything from Master Zhang. I cannot take it.”

“Miss is fine. Master Zhang, please take it back.”

Zhang Yuanheng had already felt distressed when he saw the room earlier. He pushed it hard. “How can her days be fine? There isn’t much silver here. Just take it.”

Yue Deng dared not accept it and continued to push it back. The two of them pulled and pushed for a long time.

Just then, Song Zan seemed to pass by the courtyard gate. Seeing Zhang Yuanheng standing in the corridor, he called out, “Master Zhang.”

Zhang Yuanheng was taken aback. He had to stop what he was doing and went to greet Song Zan with a bow. “General Song.”

Song Zan stood at the courtyard gate, glanced at the tightly closed flower window, and then looked at Zhang Yuanheng with a cold expression. “What are you doing in Miss Shen’s courtyard?”

“Did you enter her room to see Miss Shen?”

Zhang Yuanheng’s face was filled with sorrow as he nodded. “Miss Shen fell into the water. I came to see her after asking Lord Shen.”

“Just now, I went in and Miss Shen was coughing severely. I was just worried about her. I didn’t do anything else.”

Song Zan heard that Zhang Yuanheng had entered Shen Weici’s room and immediately sneered. “She hasn’t even married into your Earl’s mansion yet, and you’ve already entered her boudoir?”

Zhang Yuanheng was startled and quickly said, “General Song, you are being too harsh. I was originally behind the screen. It was Miss Shen who asked me to come in, so I took a look.”

“Moreover, there were maidservants in the room. I was just visiting the sick. There is nothing to criticize...”

chapters.title: Lingering in the Mind
chapters.content:
Shen Weici had been resting for the past two days, and the sound of her coughing had filled the Linchun Courtyard, leaving the maids there with worried expressions.

If it hadn’t been for the Second Madam delaying treatment that day, she wouldn’t have fallen so ill. Falling into icy water in the dead of winter—even the healthiest body would be forced into sickness.

Yue Deng was boiling medicine on the veranda when she saw the kitchen servant enter again, carrying a food box. She quickly stood up to take it. The servant smiled at Yue Deng: “This medicinal meal was specially prepared for the Third Young Lady. We know she can’t have greasy food, so all the oil has been skimmed off.”

Yue Deng assumed it was by the Old Madam’s order and hurried to express her gratitude before seeing the servant out.

Since the young lady had returned, the meals sent from the kitchen had all been nourishing, and Yue Deng couldn’t help but feel touched by the Old Madam’s concern.

As the servant reached the courtyard gate, she heard the faint sound of coughing from inside and turned back to Yue Deng: “The Third Young Lady’s health is still weak. With such a fragile foundation, she must take even better care of herself. I saw that the Second Young Lady also fell into the water, but when we delivered meals to her these past two days, she didn’t cough at all. She seems much better than the Third Young Lady.”

Yue Deng’s eyes reddened.

If only the young lady had seen a physician in time and had ginger water then, she wouldn’t be this sick now.

She didn’t say much, just nodded and saw the servant out.

When she returned, she saw He Xia had already opened the food box. She turned to Yue Deng: “I noticed the milk pigeon soup has ginseng slices in it. It smells strongly of medicine.”

“Does the Old Madam care so much?”

Yue Deng looked at the dishes inside—light yet delicacies they rarely had, like fish and sea cucumber. It was almost better than what the Old Madam herself ate. When had Linchun Courtyard ever received such treatment?

The meals sent these past two days had been better each time. Seeing the ginseng floating in the soup, Yue Deng didn’t think much of it: “Perhaps the Old Madam pitied the young lady and specially sent the medicinal ingredients.”

He Xia didn’t ask further, but Shen Weici, upon seeing the meal, fell silent and didn’t say a word.

In the afternoon, Xun Mei from Guansong Residence arrived. Hearing the coughing inside, she came over and whispered to Yue Deng: “The Third Young Lady’s illness is severe. Our Second Young Master said he managed to save her once, so he must help her to the end.”

She took out a small box: “This is a Qingqi Pill, prescribed by the imperial physician. Even the empress and princes in the palace use it. Whether it works or not, give it to the Third Young Lady. Maybe she’ll recover in a few days. It must be uncomfortable to keep coughing like this.”

Yue Deng hesitated when she heard it was from Guansong Residence. The young lady had said they should no longer have any dealings with Guansong Residence or accept anything from them.

Xun Mei noticed Yue Deng’s hesitation and smiled: “It’s all for the Third Young Lady’s good, isn’t it?”

“No one will know if you don’t say anything.”

“Our Second Young Master has good intentions. Don’t let them go to waste.”

Yue Deng listened, then heard another cough from inside. Her fingers twitched as she wavered between accepting and refusing, afraid the young lady would scold her.

Xun Mei sighed at Yue Deng’s expression: “If you’re afraid your young lady will blame you, just crush the pill into powder and mix it into her medicine. She won’t notice.”

Yue Deng’s heart stirred at this suggestion, and she finally accepted it.

She looked at Xun Mei: “Thank you, Sister Xun Mei. And thank the Second Young Master.”

Xun Mei smiled, patted Yue Deng’s hand, and said: “Then I’ll take my leave.”

Yue Deng watched Xun Mei leave, then looked down at the box of medicine. After some thought, she decided to go to the residence physician to check if it was safe to take.

Song Zhang stood not far from the entrance of Linchun Courtyard, watching Yue Deng run out with the box. He ordered his attendant to follow and see where she was going, then looked at the empty courtyard and the steaming medicine pot.

He hadn’t seen her for two or three days. He wanted to step inside but hesitated, then turned and walked away.

After a while, the attendant returned and cautiously reported to Song Zhang: “Yue Deng took the medicine to the residence physician to check...”

“To see if it can be taken...”

He had thought Song Er Ye would be angry upon hearing this, but instead, he heard a faint chuckle: “She’s quite clever.”

Yue Deng happily returned with the medicine box.

The residence physician had confirmed that the Qingqi Pill was indeed for exclusive imperial use, something ordinary people couldn’t obtain. It was made from rare and precious medicinal ingredients. If the young lady took it, her cough would improve much faster.

He also said the pill was safe to consume, so Yue Deng finally relaxed. She thought that Second Young Master Song wouldn’t harm her young lady.

She just found it strange that someone as busy and aloof as Second Young Master Song, who was usually hard to approach, would help her young lady without any reason.

Then she suddenly remembered the scene she had witnessed at the manor, and her heart skipped a beat.

When she returned to Linchun Courtyard, Shen Weici was leaning against the edge of the bed, a handkerchief pressed to her lips, her black hair disheveled over her white clothes.

He Xia quickly handed her a cup of hot tea: “Young Lady, clear your throat.”

Shen Weici took the cup and sipped, then buried her face in the pillow in discomfort.

Even kneeling in the snow before hadn’t made her this ill.

Her cough had actually improved. She thought it would take a month to fully recover.

Yue Deng entered and gently patted Shen Weici’s back, not knowing what to say.

Shen Weici didn’t cough much at night and felt a bit better. She got up to bathe.

She had been lying in bed for the past two days, and the sweat had made her feel sticky. Thinking that the Earl’s family might come to see her tomorrow, she should tidy up her appearance.

After her bath, she sat in a chair, holding a book that Shen Mingqiu had brought her when he visited. He had feared she would be bored and gave her a copy of *Caoshi Bitan*.

Actually, such books were not suitable for young ladies in the boudoir. It contained various anecdotes, strange tales, and even some romantic stories.

She had heard that the Third Master enjoyed reading such books, and Shen Mingqiu secretly liked them too, so he brought one for Shen Weici.

Shen Weici flipped through a few pages and found it interesting. She and Shen Mingqiu kept it a secret, never taking it outside.

Yue Deng stood behind Shen Weici, drying her hair. She craned her neck to glance at the book but couldn’t recognize many characters, so she asked: “What book is the young lady reading?”

Shen Weici’s gaze fell lightly on the page. She leaned to the side, one hand resting on the armrest of the chair, her fingertips hanging down and warmed by the charcoal brazier beside her. “The *Sanchao Poetry Selection*.”

Yue Deng smiled: “The young lady still hasn’t had enough of poetry.”

As she spoke, the curtain at the entrance was suddenly lifted from the outside. Shen Weici looked up and saw Song Zhang. He was the only one who never hesitated to enter her room.

Fortunately, her courtyard was secluded, and few people came by. If this were the East Courtyard, where the maids frequently passed through, the servants would surely have spread rumors about her and Song Zhang.

Even Old Madam Shen had started inquiring about their relationship.

Moreover, he often came at night.

Shen Weici lifted her gaze to Song Zhang, still politely addressing him: “Young Master Song.”

Song Zhang glanced at the book in Shen Weici’s hands, then at her weak and listless posture as she leaned against the chair. Her clothes, perhaps hastily put on after her bath, still had water stains at the collar, and her damp hair occasionally dripped onto her shoulders.

Her face was still pale, her expression tired, and her peach-blossom eyes, though lowered, held a slight dazed look.

Yet even in such a sickly state, her delicate and refined chin, her misty green mountain-like eyebrows, and her gentle demeanor could still stir one’s heartstrings, leaving a lasting impression.

Song Zhang noticed Shen Weici avoiding his gaze, her head slightly tilted, a strand of soft hair falling.

He withdrew his gaze, his face cold. His black clothes seemed out of place in this small boudoir.

Song Zhang sat on a stool beside Shen Weici and looked at her: “Tomorrow, I will ask the imperial physician to come again.”

Shen Weici still tilted her head, lowering her eyes to the charcoal fire on the ground. The fire was burning brightly, casting an orange glow on her cheeks.

She softly replied: “I dare not trouble Young Master Song any further. My illness has already improved a lot these days. The Old Madam and my father are also concerned.”

“Young Master Song is busy with official duties every day. It’s not good to trouble him with such trivial matters.”

Song Zhang’s gaze darkened as he looked at Shen Weici’s face.

Did he not understand what she meant by this?

She said that the Old Madam and her father were taking care of her, implying it had nothing to do with him.

Song Zhang suppressed the emotions in his eyes, his voice deep: “The Old Madam and your father are concerned about you?”

“Did they send you anything good after you returned?”

“Plenty of good things were given to Shen Zhaozhao. What good things has Linchun Courtyard received?”

“The West Courtyard is so remote. Why hasn’t anyone arranged for you to move to a better courtyard?”

“Could it be that the Marquis’s residence has no spare courtyards?”

chapters.title: Breaking the Engagement
chapters.content:
Song Zhang’s words pierced Shen Weici’s heart, and she couldn’t refute them.

She was fully aware of her own position. She had always been seeking a small gap to survive, never expecting much.

From the first day she entered the Marquis’s residence, she understood her status and had never thought to rely on the Marquis’s family for much.

She had gone to great lengths to please the Old Madam, but not for material gain.

So she was never truly heartbroken—just pained.

Shen Weici still furrowed her brows, looking at her fingertips, reddened by the charcoal fire: “Did Young Master Song come here just to tell me these things?”

“These are things I already know without Young Master Song telling me.”

Song Zhang watched Shen Weici, who still refused to meet his eyes. His fingers twitched on his knee, and the suppressed emotions in his eyes threatened to overflow.

Her soft voice came again: “Now I am in marriage talks with the Earl’s family. Although Young Master Song and I have a distant cousin relationship and are not considered outsiders, your nighttime visits are still inappropriate.”

“In the future, if Young Master Song wishes to visit, please come during the day. That way, I won’t neglect you.”

She finally lifted her eyes to glance at Song Zhang before lowering them again, her voice still soft: “I hope Young Master Song can understand.”

Song Zhang now realized that Shen Weici, though appearing weak, could speak words sharper than a blade.

His fingers tightened slightly, the veins on the back of his hand becoming visible.

Song Zhang’s face turned cold. She was drawing a line between them.

Just because he had kissed her once and held her once.

Song Zhang’s expression darkened, his lips pressed tightly together. He stood up from the stool, looking down at Shen Weici, who had kept her eyes lowered since he entered. Then he turned and walked out.

As soon as Song Zhang left, Yue Deng and He Xia, who had been standing nearby, were the first to breathe a sigh of relief.

Song Zhang’s dark expression had been terrifying, as if he might stand up and kill someone at any moment. The two young maids had shrunk back, fearing he might do something reckless.

Shen Weici, however, did not lift her eyelids even after Song Zhang left. She only caught a glimpse of the swaying curtain from the corner of her eye before quietly closing her own.

She knew the medicinal meals from the kitchen were sent by him, and today’s words were also meant for him to hear.

If he was angry, so be it. She was just a fleeting presence in his life; there was no need for him to waste his thoughts on her.

They each had their own paths to walk.

The next morning, Madame Zhang from the Earl’s family came to visit Old Madam Shen.

A mammy from Cian Hall came to Shen Weici’s courtyard to deliver a message, telling her to prepare herself as she might be meeting someone.

Shen Weici had already prepared herself. She sat in front of a bronze mirror, looking at her somewhat haggard reflection, and called Yue Deng to apply some makeup.

With a touch of rouge, her complexion improved. Her naturally beautiful eyes, now brightened, showed little trace of illness.

Yue Deng tidied Shen Weici inside and out, then took out the cloak Song Zhang had given her: “It’s cold outside, Young Lady. Since you’ve accepted the gift, you should use it. It can’t just sit there forever.”

Shen Weici still shook her head and asked Yue Deng to bring the cloak given by the Old Madam.

If she wanted to draw a clear line with Song Zhang, she couldn’t use his things.

Perhaps when she married, she would return everything to him.

Shen Weici was grateful for Song Zhang’s kindness but also understood his intentions. She simply couldn’t reciprocate.

Yue Deng had no choice but to exchange it again.

On the way to Cian Hall, there was no snow today, but the air was still cold.

It had been many days since she had left her courtyard. As soon as she stepped out, the bright white light dazzled her, and she felt a little disoriented.

Halfway there, she suddenly encountered Song Zhang coming from the opposite direction. She paused, thinking she should greet him, but Song Zhang walked straight past her without even glancing in her direction.

Shen Weici was slightly stunned, then gathered her cloak and continued walking.

On the other side, Song Zhang passed by Shen Weici, and Ming He, following behind, quietly asked: “The Earl’s family has arrived today. Should we send someone to eavesdrop?”

Song Zhang glanced at Ming He with his narrow phoenix eyes, and Ming He quickly replied: “Then this subordinate will arrange it.”

When Shen Weici arrived at Cian Hall, she was led by a servant at the door all the way to the warm pavilion inside.

Inside the warm pavilion, Old Madam Shen and Madame Zhang were chatting and laughing. When they saw Shen Weici enter, they both turned their attention to her.

Shen Weici had Yue Deng remove her cloak. With a smile in her eyes, she first greeted Old Madam Shen, then Madame Zhang.

Lin Shi looked at Shen Weici’s figure, appearance, and demeanor. A warm, fragrant breeze seemed to follow her. No wonder her son was so infatuated. Even upon seeing her again, her beauty was captivating.

She smiled: “I heard you fell into the water. Is your health better now?”

Shen Weici went to the lower seat on the other side of Old Madam Shen and sat down. She accepted the hot tea brought by a maid and replied with a graceful smile: “I have almost fully recovered.”

Lin Shi nodded, then looked at Old Madam Shen: “This girl is good in every way.”

“If only her health were better.”

Old Madam Shen detected the unyielding tone in Lin Shi’s words and replied with a forced smile: “A girl raised in the Marquis’s residence is naturally good in every way.”

“As for her health, the imperial physician has said there is no issue with Weici. We are not physicians ourselves; we cannot judge based on appearances alone.”

Lin Shi’s face stiffened at Old Madam Shen’s words, but as the younger generation, she had to maintain face. She turned to Shen Weici: “I suppose Yuan Heng has told you my intentions.”

“I don’t mean to look down on you. It’s just that my brother Yuan Heng is in poor health, and he is my only reliance.”

“For the Earl’s family, descendants are extremely important. If Shen Third Young Lady can give birth to my eldest grandson after entering the family, the Earl’s family will immediately arrange your marriage with great fanfare. That would already be very good.”

Shen Weici glanced at Lin Shi, then lowered her head and softly said: “I will listen to the Old Madam’s decision.”

She couldn’t refuse; that wasn’t her place.

She knew the Old Madam wouldn’t allow her to be a concubine.

She had long since given up on the idea of marrying into the Earl’s family.

Lin Shi turned to Old Madam Shen: “Old Madam, rest assured. If Shen Third Young Lady enters our family, she will not be treated unfairly. We will treat her as our own daughter.”

Old Madam Shen coldly humphed: “A girl from the Marquis’s family becoming a concubine in the Earl’s family? How can the Earl’s family say such a thing?”

“What do you mean by giving birth to the eldest grandson and arranging a grand wedding? It sounds as if the Marquis’s family is begging to marry into the Earl’s family.”

“I still say the same thing: if the Earl’s family truly has sincere intentions, then follow the proper procedures with the three letters and six etiquettes.”

“If the Earl’s family does not have that intention, then this matter is settled.”

Lin Shi’s face stiffened. She didn’t understand how the agreement she had made with Madame Wen could suddenly change now.

She thought that the Marquis’s family didn’t value this illegitimate daughter, and her maternal family had no backing. Moreover, Yuan Heng had said the dowry wouldn’t be much. How could an illegitimate daughter from the Marquis’s family be too good for the Earl’s family?

Currently, the second branch of the Marquis’s family wasn’t that powerful. The Second Master Shen didn’t even hold as high an official position as her son Yuan Heng.

If it weren’t for her son kneeling in her room every night begging, she wouldn’t have come to discuss this marriage.

chapters.title: The Cruelty of Fate
chapters.content:
Lin had only been testing the waters. If the old madam agreed, it would fulfill Yuanheng’s wishes and ease her own mind. If Shen Weici could truly bear a grandson, then elevating her to wife would also be acceptable.

She was indeed worried about Shen Weici’s health.

A few days ago, she had heard that Shen Weici had fallen into the water and had even invited an imperial physician to examine her. Through connections, she had managed to ask the physician about it, and to her surprise, she had learned something.

The imperial physician had said that Shen Weici’s body was too cold, making it difficult for her to conceive. If not properly regulated, it was possible she might never be able to have children at all.

This only strengthened her resolve.

If the old madam absolutely refused, and Yuanheng did not blame her, then since the Marquis’s residence disapproved, she would find another suitable marriage for Yuanheng.

Upon hearing the old madam’s words, Lin’s expression turned troubled. “As a mother, I naturally must consider my child’s descendants. I hope the old madam can understand my position.”

“Moreover, if Miss Shen’s health is fine, who’s to say she won’t bear a grandson within a year of entering the family? What is there to worry about?”

Old Madam Shen glanced at Lin. “A concubine elevated to wife is the same as directly marrying a wife?”

“I absolutely will not agree to her being a concubine.”

Lin sighed. “My Yuanheng truly has genuine feelings for Miss Shen. I also genuinely like Weici’s temperament and came with sincerity. If the old madam does not agree, then there’s nothing more to be done.”

Old Madam Shen coldly laughed upon hearing this. “Genuine feelings?”

“Sincerity?”

“If the Yiyong Earl’s residence truly had genuine feelings and sincerity, they wouldn’t have insulted our Marquis’s daughter by proposing she be a concubine.”

“This matter cannot be considered a loss for our Marquis’s residence. It is your Earl’s residence that lacks sincerity.”

“Forget it, then. Does the Marquis’s residence fear that their daughter won’t be able to marry?”

As she spoke, she looked at the servant beside her. “Since there’s nothing more to discuss today, see Madame Zhang out.”

Lin’s face paled. She glanced at the servant beside her before relaying what she had heard from the imperial physician to Old Madam Shen. “Old Madam, this matter isn’t entirely the Earl’s residence’s fault.”

“The imperial physician himself said that Miss Shen’s body is too cold, making it difficult for her to conceive. How can I not believe it?”

“It’s not as if that imperial physician would deliberately deceive me, is it?”

Old Madam Shen’s expression changed, and her voice turned cold. “Which imperial physician said this? Tell me his name, and I’ll have him brought here to question him.”

Lin calmly adjusted her sleeves. “Physician Lin of the Imperial Medical Bureau.”

“If the old madam does not believe me, you can call her here and ask her yourself.”

As she spoke, Lin stood up and softened her tone. “It is a pity that Miss Shen’s body makes it difficult for her to conceive. But my son has genuine feelings and is even willing to wait several years without marrying a wife. Isn’t this enough to prove his sincerity?”

“Old Madam, sincerity for sincerity. If you were in my position, would you happily accept her as a concubine?”

With that, Lin sighed and took her leave.

As soon as Lin left, Old Madam Shen frowned and turned to Shen Weici. “After you fell into the water, you said Song Zhang had invited an imperial physician for you. Which physician was it?”

Shen Weici’s heart sank slightly. She softly replied, “It was Physician Lin.”

Old Madam Shen’s expression changed again. She looked at Shen Weici and asked, “Did Physician Lin truly say that your body is too cold, making it difficult for you to conceive?”

Shen Weici had heard Physician Lin say this, but he had also said that as long as she regulated her body afterward, there would be no problem.

After a moment of thought, she spoke. “Physician Lin did say that my body is cold, making it slightly difficult to conceive, but as long as the cold is expelled, it will be fine.”

Old Madam Shen’s expression darkened slightly. She said to Shen Weici, “Do not speak of this matter to anyone else. The engagement with the Earl’s residence is off. After you have regulated your body for some time, I will call another physician to examine you.”

Shen Weici nodded.

Old Madam Shen added, “For now, go back and rest.”

Shen Weici lowered her head and left.

As soon as Shen Weici left, the old servant beside Old Madam Shen sighed. “Miss Shen is such a good person. What if she really ends up with this illness?”

She looked at Old Madam Shen. “This old servant sees that Zhang Erlang is a reliable man. I’ve heard he treats Miss Shen well. If she enters the Earl’s residence as a concubine, it wouldn’t be bad. In the future, if she bears a child, she could be elevated to wife. If she truly cannot conceive, with a man like Zhang Erlang taking care of her, things should still go smoothly.”

Old Madam Shen glanced at her and coldly humphed. “Even if she were to be a concubine, it would never be in the Earl’s residence.”

“With Weici’s appearance, if she truly cannot bear children, sending her to a prince or a noble family as a concubine would also bring some benefits to the Marquis’s residence.”

“If she is to be a concubine, she must be sent to a high-ranking family. How could she be sent to a declining Earl’s residence?”

Old Madam Shen sighed again. “In truth, I do like the girl Weici. Let’s see her fortune in the coming days. If she can regulate her body, it will be her blessing. If she cannot, then she can only be a concubine.”

The old servant felt an inexplicable pity. She softly said, “Miss Shen’s life has been pitiful. If she hadn’t fallen into the water…”

“If the physician had been called earlier…”

Old Madam Shen’s expression turned cold, and she cut her off. “Let’s not mention these things anymore.”

“It’s all fate.”

Shen Weici left the Cisou Hall, and the calm in her eyes finally cracked slightly.

She knew that if she truly could not bear children, her value in the old madam’s eyes would gradually diminish.

She stood under the plum tree, looking up at the flourishing branches heavy with red blossoms. Petals drifted down, and she blinked her eyes before sighing.

It was truly the cruelty of fate; no one could predict the outcome.

From afar, Song Zhang watched Shen Weici’s stationary figure, listening to the reports from his servants.

Though he could not see her face clearly, he seemed to sense her sadness.

Was she saddened by the fact that she could not marry Zhang Yuanheng?

Song Zhang’s gaze darkened.

Shen Weici was sorting through her emotions when she heard Shen Mingqiu’s voice behind her. She turned her head and saw Shen Mingqiu approaching with a smile. “Why does my sister look better today?”

Shen Weici forced a smile. “I put on some makeup.”

Shen Mingqiu linked arms with Shen Weici and walked forward. “I came out to see the plum blossoms today. I didn’t expect to run into you, sister.”

“I heard that someone from the Earl’s residence came again today. Did you come from the old madam’s place, sister? Were they talking about your marriage?”

A bittersweet feeling surged in Shen Weici’s eyes, but she maintained a smile. “No.”

Shen Mingqiu was taken aback and looked at Shen Weici. “What do you mean by that, sister?”

Shen Weici stopped walking, her eyes fixed on Shen Mingqiu. “My engagement with the Earl’s residence has been called off. Little sister, please do not mention my connection with the Earl’s residence to others in the future.”

Shen Mingqiu froze, her eyes wide with surprise as she looked at Shen Weici. “What happened?”

Shen Weici’s face held a faint smile. “It’s not a big deal. It’s just that Master Zhang and I are not compatible in temperament. The old madam has also given it much thought.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici’s slightly cold fingers tightened around Shen Mingqiu’s hand, her voice very low. “Fourth sister, I treat you with sincerity, and what I say to you is the truth.”

“From now on, I have no connection with the Earl’s residence. If you bring it up again, it will only cause embarrassment. Let’s not mention it again.”

Shen Mingqiu took a long time to recover, lowering her head to look at Shen Weici’s fingers holding her hand before nodding. “With Third Sister’s appearance, even without the engagement to the Earl’s residence, you will be able to find a better family in the future.”

Shen Weici smiled but did not speak further.

Originally, Shen Weici had planned to accompany Shen Mingqiu for a walk in the plum grove, but Shen Mingqiu was worried about Shen Weici’s health and followed her back to the Linchun Courtyard to sit and talk.

With nothing else to do, Shen Mingqiu asked Shen Weici if she knew how to play Go. Shen Weici smiled and said she knew a little. Shen Mingqiu then had a maid fetch the board, and the two sat across from each other, playing Go to pass the time.

While playing, Shen Mingqiu had assumed Shen Weici would only know a little, but she was surprised to find that every move was calculated. She could not help but admire her.

After placing a piece, she asked, “Do you know how Shen Zhaozhao is doing now, sister?”

Shen Weici’s gaze fell on the board as she softly replied, “She should have recovered by now.”

Shen Mingqiu said, “It’s been many days since I’ve seen her. It’s been quite peaceful.”

Shen Weici only smiled.

chapters.title: Zhang Yuanheng Comes
chapters.content:
It was almost noon when Shen Mingqiu left. The game of Go was not finished, and Shen Mingqiu said they could continue it next time. Shen Weici had Yue Deng place the unfinished game on the table.

As soon as Shen Mingqiu left, the room fell silent. Shen Weici leaned on the chair, resting her head on her hand, silent.

The smile she had worn while playing Go with Shen Mingqiu faded, leaving only exhaustion.

Yue Deng crouched beside Shen Weici, reaching out to speak, but Shen Weici spoke first in a soft voice. “Yue Deng, leave me alone for a while.”

Yue Deng knew Shen Weici must be feeling unwell. After a moment of silence, she quietly retreated.

She went to the outer room to prepare medicine and chatted with He Xia and Yan Er.

In the middle of the afternoon, Xun Mei from Guan Song Ju arrived. Yue Deng went up to greet her. “Sister.”

Xun Mei glanced at the tightly closed window and smiled, pulling Yue Deng aside. “Did you give the medicine I gave you to Miss Shen?”

Yue Deng nodded. “Yesterday, I mixed some into her medicine. It seems her cough has improved today.”

“Thank you, Sister Xun Mei.”

Xun Mei smiled. “No need to thank me. It’s all the second young master’s intention.”

“It’s all for Miss Shen to recover soon.”

As she spoke, Xun Mei took out what she was holding and placed it in Yue Deng’s hands. “This is what the second young master told me to bring.”

“It’s a sitting cushion made of white wolf fur and a matching hat made of white sable. Miss Shen could use these.”

“Take them to Miss Shen and say they are from the steward.”

“Such good fur, thick and warm. He even had a famous master work through the night to make them. They’re so soft to the touch, and they’re great at blocking the wind. With this hat, she won’t feel cold.”

Yue Deng looked down at the gleaming white items in her hands, unable to resist touching them. They were soft and thick; sitting on them must be very comfortable.

These days, the young miss had been sitting as soon as she got up, and these things would be very useful.

Then she looked at the hat, which was inlaid with jade and pearls. Although it looked plain at first glance, upon closer inspection, the jewels were each quite valuable.

Yue Deng was startled and looked at Xun Mei. “Our young miss is not easy to fool. With such good pearls and jewels, the young miss won’t believe it.”

Xun Mei looked at the hat in Yue Deng’s hands and softly said, “You’re right. I’ll take the hat back for now. You can take the cushion first, but don’t let it slip.”

“If anyone asks what kind of fur it is, just say it’s ordinary fox fur.”

Yue Deng acknowledged and touched the cushion again and again, suddenly thinking that such good fur would be a waste to use as a sitting cushion.

After Xun Mei left, Yue Deng took the cushion inside. “Miss, the steward just sent this. Try sitting on it.”

Shen Weici looked at what Yue Deng was holding. “Why did the steward send this?”

Yue Deng smiled. “The steward said it’s cold in winter and sent a white fox fur cushion to each courtyard’s young miss.”

As she spoke, she walked to Shen Weici’s side. “Miss, stand up. Let me put it down so you can try it and see if it’s soft.”

Shen Weici looked at what Yue Deng was holding and, not in the mood to think much about it, especially since it was getting dark and hard to see clearly, stood up.

After Yue Deng laid it down, she sat and tried it. It was indeed very soft.

Yue Deng saw that Shen Weici was comfortable sitting and secretly thought that Second Young Master Song really knew how to give gifts. Each one was a good item. It was a pity that such a good cloak had gone unused by the young miss.

She then went to pour hot tea. “Miss, have some tea.”

Shen Weici reached out to take it and had just taken a sip when the curtain was lifted again. Yan Er said, “Miss, the second old master has asked you to go to the Hanming Hall in the front courtyard. Young Master Zhang has arrived and is waiting for you.”

Upon hearing that Zhang Yuanheng had come, Shen Weici’s expression remained indifferent.

Things had come to this point; there was really no need to meet.

She paused in thought and told Yue Deng to pack up Zhang Yuanheng’s things and take them to the front. She would not go.

He would understand her meaning.

Yue Deng saw Shen Weici’s expression and thought it was better not to meet. She quickly went to pack up the things and had Yan Er and herself take them to the front courtyard.

As soon as Yue Deng and Yan Er left, Shen Weici had He Xia bring the book she was reading. She leaned back in the chair, appearing very calm.

He Xia saw that Shen Weici wanted to read and, after bringing the book, lit a candle beside her before quietly leaving.

After a while, He Xia saw Yue Deng and Yan Er rushing back. Noticing their somewhat panicked expressions, she quickly stood up to ask, “What’s wrong?”

Yue Deng had no time to talk to He Xia. She quickly lifted the curtain and went to Shen Weici, speaking in a low voice. “Miss, you should still go to the front to see for yourself.”

“Young Master Zhang seems to have had some wine and insists on seeing you before he leaves. The second old master couldn’t persuade him to stay.”

“The second old master wants you to go to the front and clarify things with Young Master Zhang to avoid further entanglement.”

Shen Weici’s fingers, which had been turning the pages, paused, and she gently closed the book.

It would be better to clarify things face to face to avoid any resentment between them.

Shen Weici stood up, glanced out the window, put on her cloak, and, accompanied by Yue Deng, went out.

On the way, she coughed a couple of times. Yue Deng, worried about Shen Weici’s health, adjusted the hood of the cloak to make sure it wasn’t blown off by the wind.

She thought that if the young miss were wearing that pearl-embellished hat, she wouldn’t have to worry about the wind.

When they arrived at the Hanming Hall in the front courtyard, Shen Rongsheng saw Shen Weici arrive. He pulled her aside and sighed softly. “Go in and persuade him properly. I’ve also heard about your situation from the old madam. It’s better to part on good terms and not drag things out.”

Shen Weici lowered her brows and hummed in agreement before pushing the door open and walking in.

Inside the elegant room, Zhang Yuanheng was sitting with his back to her, dressed in a refined blue robe with a jade crown securing his hair, impeccable in every detail.

Hearing the movement behind him, he turned quickly, his eyes red-rimmed. “Miss Shen.”

Shen Weici saw Zhang Yuanheng in this state and remained silent.

She walked over and sat across from him, lowering her gaze to pour him tea. The swirling white mist of the tea lingered between them. Shen Weici spoke softly, “Master Zhang, I cannot be a concubine.”

Shen Weici’s voice was very soft and faint.

Yet it clearly reached Zhang Yuanheng’s ears, twisting his heart like a knife.

Zhang Yuanheng’s eyes were moist as he stared intently at Shen Weici’s lowered brows, his voice low. “Even if you are a concubine, I will not marry another wife.”

“My mother will one day see my determination. Can you…”

“Can you not comply with my mother just this once?”

“Even if you can never have children, I don’t mind.”

“I have never been someone who cares about descendants. I only care about you.”

chapters.title: So Heartbroken?
chapters.content:
Shen Weici listened to these words with no ripple in her eyes.

She had never trusted anyone. The passionate vows of love now might not hold true in a few years.

If she truly bore no children, it would be like a sword hanging over her head every day, living in constant fear.

Fear that one day she would be discarded like a worn-out shoe.

This was never the kind of stability she wanted.

Shen Weici looked at Zhang Yuanheng, her dark eyebrows gentle, but her eyes cold. “I am currently the third young lady of the Marquis’s mansion. If I were to enter the Earl’s mansion as a concubine, it would make it difficult for my fourth and fifth sisters to marry in the future.”

“My marriage is not something I can decide.”

With that, Shen Weici took a deep breath and sighed softly. “Master Zhang, your wife does not like me. She is convinced that my body is weak, and no explanation will change her mind.”

“Now that I have fallen into the water, my health is even worse. I am no longer the kind of daughter-in-law your wife envisions.”

“I have not wronged you. I only seek a stable marriage. I cannot wait for your promise of making me your official wife.”

“Now, it is impossible for us. Master Zhang, you will certainly find a better match in the future. Let us end things here.”

Zhang Yuanheng’s expression was filled with grief as he looked at Shen Weici. “What better match? I only have eyes for you.”

“For you, I am willing to offend the Duke of Song’s mansion. For you, I kneel before my mother every day, begging her. Why can’t you take a step for me?”

“Your father is right outside. If you request to enter the Earl’s mansion yourself, how can the old lady and your father stop you?”

As Zhang Yuanheng spoke, he reached out and tightly held Shen Weici’s hand, his voice choked with emotion. “Weici, I beg you. I will treat you well.”

“You will only be a concubine in name. In every other way, I will treat you as my official wife.”

“The imperial physician said it would be difficult for you to conceive. Even if you miss this chance with me, whoever you marry in the future will also mind.”

“Weici, I am the only one who truly cares for you. Can’t you do this for me just once?”

“Please...”

Shen Weici’s hand was tightly gripped by Zhang Yuanheng. His grip was strong, and it hurt her fingers. She saw the redness and pain in his eyes, the hint of tears, his desperate and almost mad expression, and the faint scent of alcohol on him. She was taken aback.

In her heart, she understood. They had both given their all, and there was nothing more to say about this ending.

She looked at Zhang Yuanheng, shook her head, and said softly, “I cannot gamble my entire life away. The last time you visited me, I made myself clear.”

“What if I truly cannot bear children? Can you, Master Zhang, really resist the pressure then?”

“I am just a woman with no one to rely on. Without my father and mother to plan for me, if I am ever abandoned, I will have nothing left.”

“It is not that I do not trust you, Master Zhang. It is that in the future, when you have to choose between me and your wife, it will be a difficult choice for you.”

“Master Zhang, just consider me selfish.”

Zhang Yuanheng listened, his soul seemingly lost, his fingers still tightly gripping Shen Weici’s hand. He whispered dejectedly, “You still do not trust me...”

As he closed his eyes, he said, “Or perhaps you never liked me at all. That is why you do not care whether we can be together or not.”

“To you, I am just someone you can marry. In your heart, I am not important at all.”

Shen Weici was silent. She had never thought about whether she liked him or not.

She had only considered whether it was suitable or not.

She remained silent and sighed softly, “Master Zhang, there is nothing more to be done.”

“It is better this way.”

“I am just a woman seeking stability. I will never be a concubine.”

“Never.”

Zhang Yuanheng heard these words and blankly loosened his grip. He stood up unsteadily and looked at Shen Weici, who was still calmly kneeling by the low table. He did not understand why she could still be so calm.

He did not understand.

The woman who had shown affection for him, who had smiled shyly before him, who had written in her letters about missing him—why had she suddenly become so cold?

So cold that it made him feel a chill.

Zhang Yuanheng stood up shakily and went in front of Shen Weici. He looked up at her face, those eyes that had haunted his thoughts day and night were clear, with a faint glimmer, as if proving how heartless she truly was.

He bent down, exposing all his emotions vulnerably before her. “If I resign from my official position...”

“Weici, would you...”

“Would you...”

After saying this, he painfully closed his eyes, unable to finish his sentence. He straightened up and stumbled towards the door, pushing it open and walking out.

Outside, Shen Rongsheng saw Zhang Yuanheng come out, looking so lost. He patted Zhang Yuanheng’s shoulder, intending to say something comforting, but Zhang Yuanheng only bowed dejectedly without a word and left.

Yue Deng went to help Shen Weici up, and only then did Shen Weici stand up, supporting herself on the small table.

Shen Rongsheng came in and asked, “Did you make things clear?”

Shen Weici adjusted her sleeves, covering the emotions in her eyes, and nodded.

Shen Rongsheng finally sighed in relief and nodded. “It is good that things are clear.”

Then, seeing that Shen Weici’s face was a bit pale, he asked with concern, “You should go back now. It is not dark yet.”

Shen Weici hummed in agreement and quietly left.

Just now, Zhang Yuanheng had looked at her with eyes full of struggle. He had asked her if she was willing.

His next words were almost on the tip of his tongue, yet he never spoke them.

At that moment, she had felt a mix of pity and a sense of his humility.

Halfway back, Shen Weici’s eyes were filled with sorrow. She looked at Yue Deng beside her and asked, “Did I seem too heartless?”

Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici’s face under the brim of her hat and said softly, “Miss did nothing wrong. Who would want to be a concubine?”

“Miss, you always say that true love is the hardest thing, don’t you?”

Shen Weici looked at the plum blossoms and murmured, “I suddenly feel a sense of loss. It is not because of him, but because I am alone, and this loss feels especially cold.”

“Yue Deng, do you understand me?”

After saying this, she stared blankly, tightening her collar. Strands of hair fell from under her hat and were blown by the wind.

When she came back to her senses, a tall figure was standing in front of her.

Shen Weici was startled and spoke softly, “Young Master Song.”

Yue Deng was shielding Shen Weici from the wind when she heard Shen Weici’s words. She turned around and saw Song Zhong standing behind her. She quickly turned back.

Song Zhong’s eyebrows were furrowed, and his usually cold eyes showed no emotion.

He looked at Shen Weici’s lost eyes and raised his eyebrows slightly. “So heartbroken?”

Shen Weici had no mind to speak at this moment. She only tightened her sleeves, shook her head gently, and tried to step aside to pass by Song Zhong.

Song Zhong frowned deeply, grabbed Shen Weici’s arm under her cloak, and looked at her displeased. “Have you lost your ability to speak?”

chapters.title: How Dare I Aspire to the Height of Young Master Song
chapters.content:
Shen Weici was pulled tightly by Song Zhong and could not take a step forward. The suppressed emotions in her heart surged out. She looked up at Song Zhong. “What if I am heartbroken? Doesn’t that satisfy Young Master Song’s wishes?”

Song Zhong’s face darkened as he coldly laughed. “Satisfy what wishes of mine?”

Shen Weici blinked and looked at Song Zhong. “The marriage between Master Zhang and the Duke of Song’s mansion—does it have nothing to do with Young Master Song?”

“Those letters that were sent out but never delivered—do they also have nothing to do with Young Master Song?”

“Why was it so coincidental?”

“Why did Madame Zhang happen to find out about Physician Lin at that exact time?”

As she spoke, Shen Weici murmured to him, “Why...”

Actually, Shen Weici had buried these matters deep in her heart and did not want to bring them up again. Song Zhong had helped her, but she did not want him to interfere in her affairs like this in the future.

What Song Zhong could not stand the most right now was the loss and sadness in Shen Weici’s eyes.

He darkened his expression and looked at her with sarcasm. “Why?”

“You went to great lengths to lead Zhang Yuanheng on step by step. Naturally, I cannot stand it.”

“Moreover, if you put in so much effort, why are you heartbroken now?”

“Could it be that you truly like Zhang Yuanheng so much that you still want to be his concubine?”

As he spoke, Song Zhong let out another cold laugh. “The status of the Earl of Yiyong’s mansion is something you look up to. If you want to marry into a high branch, you might as well become my concubine. I will elevate you, and it will be a hundred, a thousand times better than the Earl’s mansion.”

Shen Weici was stunned, and the fingers gripping her sleeve trembled slightly.

There were probably more than one or two women in his room, and yet she was being insulted like this by him.

She did not speak anymore. She only wished that from now on, they would have no more intersections and never meet again.

Shen Weici met Song Zhong’s icy eyes and pushed her fingers against his hand. “How dare I aspire to the height of Young Master Song?”

“The Duke of Song’s mansion is not something someone like me can attach myself to.”

“I know I am not worthy. I only seek a stable and ordinary marriage. Please, Young Master Song, let me go from now on and stop interfering in my marriage affairs.”

The fingers pressing against the back of Song Zhong’s hand were ice-cold. He narrowed his eyes as he looked at her. The usually gentle and weak woman now had a hint of tenacity and stubbornness in her eyes.

Song Zhong still had no intention of letting go. He pulled Shen Weici towards the nearby pavilion.

Shen Weici was pulled along by him, stumbling as she followed his steps. She did not have the strength to resist him, nor did she dare to call out and attract attention. She could only passively let Song Zhong pull her along.

Yue Deng was also terrified. She followed behind and saw Miss Shen being pulled into the pavilion by Young Master Song, and the door was closed. She was so scared that she was about to rush forward when she felt a sharp pain at the back of her neck, and everything went black.

She did not even have time to cry out.

Shen Weici was pulled forcefully into the pavilion by Song Zhong. The door behind her was closed, and the already dim room became even darker.

Her heart was in a panic. The grip on her arm loosened, and she immediately turned around to leave.

But the next moment, her back was pressed tightly against the carved wooden door. The intricate patterns dug into her back, causing a dull ache. In front of her was Song Zhong’s hot breath.

Shen Weici placed her palms against Song Zhong’s chest, her voice panicked. “What exactly do you want to do?”

Song Zhong looked down at the person trapped in his arms. It had been several days since he last saw her. Today, her chin seemed a bit sharper, as if she had lost some weight.

He pinched her chin with his fingers, his tone displeased. “Is this how you speak to me now?”

Shen Weici was taken aback and turned her face away, remaining silent.

The tip of Song Zhong’s nose was filled with Shen Weici’s scent. He lowered his body even more, almost touching her cheek. He deeply inhaled her scent, removed the hat from her hair, and then met her gaze in the darkness. “Tell me the truth. Do you really like Zhang Yuanheng?”

“Or do you only value his family background and think he is a suitable match?”

Song Zhong’s nose was almost touching hers. The man’s scent and the heat from his body pressed down on her like his usual dominance. Shen Weici could not bear this close distance. She wanted to turn her face away, but Song Zhong’s fingers held her chin, preventing her from moving.

She spoke hoarsely, “What if I do like Master Zhang? What else does Young Master Song need to confirm?”

Song Zhong felt a strong sense of irony in his heart upon hearing Shen Weici’s admission.

Why was he asking again?

Had Song Zhong fallen so low as to beg a woman?

He was just unwilling to accept it and repeatedly sought confirmation from her, as if this would make him give up.

The ambiguous atmosphere condensed, along with Song Zhong’s hot breath.

He moved away from her, releasing her from his embrace, took a step back, then pushed open the door and walked out with large strides.

Ming He had just carried Yue Deng to a place without wind when he saw Song Zhong come out, his face extremely gloomy, as if the conversation had not gone well.

He quickly glanced inside the door, then untied Yue Deng’s acupoint before hurrying to catch up.

He walked up to Song Zhong and said in a low voice, “Just now, a maid saw the general taking Miss Shen into the pavilion. She is still dizzy. How should we handle this?”

Song Zhong sneered. “Handle what? Let her go.”

Ming He was taken aback. Was the general no longer going to do things secretly?

After Song Zhong left, Shen Weici stayed in the darkness for a while longer before walking out. She bumped into Yue Deng, who was rushing in anxiously.

Yue Deng saw that Shen Weici’s clothes were still the same as before, except that the hat on her cloak had fallen off. She could not help but sigh in relief. “Miss, what did Young Master Song pull you in there for?”

Shen Weici shook her head. “Nothing.”

She looked around at the quiet surroundings. No one was around, so she stepped out of the doorway and said in a very low voice, “Let’s go back.”

Back at Linchun Courtyard, Shen Weici sat by the charcoal fire to warm her hands.

After being out for a while, she felt cold all over and could not help but cough a few times.

Yue Deng quickly brought over some hot tea. “Miss, after you have eaten, go to bed early. You were out in the wind for so long.”

Just as she was speaking, He Xia came in and said that the eldest young master had arrived. Shen Weici paused, her fingers not yet fully warmed, and she put down the tea cup and stood up to go to the small hall outside.

She saw Shen Siwen standing in the middle of the small hall, dressed in white, not seated, with his hands behind his back as if he was examining the room’s decorations.

Soon, the curtain was lifted, and a slender, graceful figure walked out from behind it, with delicate features and eyes like a painting.

A slight smile appeared on his face as he took a step forward. “Third cousin.”

Shen Weici quickly greeted Shen Siwen. “Eldest cousin.”

As she spoke, she looked up at Shen Siwen. “Has eldest cousin come here for something?”

Shen Siwen smiled. “It is not anything important.”
