“The last time you made me a sachet, my maternal grandmother liked it very much. This time, after hearing that you fell into the water, she specially sent me to give you something as a token of my regards.”

As he spoke, Shen Siwen had his servant bring the item over, opened the box, and presented it to Shen Weici. “This windproof hat is something I specially prepared for my third cousin. I think you will find it useful.”

Shen Weici looked down at the item in Shen Siwen’s hands and quickly declined. “Making a sachet for eldest cousin was just a small effort. How can I accept such a precious gift from you?”

Shen Siwen smiled and looked at Shen Weici. “This is not precious to me. This kind of windproof hat is just a fashionable style among the women in the capital. I had my servant buy it. Third cousin, do not be polite. It is just a token of my regards.”

Shen Weici heard Shen Siwen’s words but still hesitated. “But a sachet cannot compare to eldest cousin’s gift.”

Shen Siwen sighed and placed the item into Shen Weici’s hands. “Can regards have a value? The sachet you gave was a token of your regards, and the windproof hat I give is also a token of my regards. If you refuse, wouldn’t that also betray my regards?”

Shen Weici heard Shen Siwen’s words and could not refuse any longer. She spoke softly, “Then I thank eldest cousin.”

Shen Siwen smiled. “Then I will take my leave.”

Shen Weici saw this and was about to see Shen Siwen out, but Shen Siwen stopped her. “You are still recovering from falling into the water. There is no need to see me out.”

With that, he left with his servant.

Shen Weici looked down at the item in her hands, feeling its soft texture.

Yue Deng watched from the side, knowing what was going on, and said, “It is eldest young master’s regards. Although it may not be precious to him, it is something you can use, and it came just in time.”

Shen Weici nodded and did not look at it any further. She asked Yue Deng to put it away.

On his way out, Shen Siwen saw Song Zhong standing not far from Linchun Courtyard. He walked over with a smile and asked, “If you care so much, why didn’t you deliver it yourself?”

He smiled again. “It is rare to see you meddle in others’ affairs.”

Song Zhong’s expression was cold and indifferent. He only said, “I did not want to deliver it.”

Then he turned and left.

Shen Siwen stood there, watching Song Zhong’s retreating figure, then looked back at Linchun Courtyard, as if deep in thought.

chapters.title: Shen Zhaozhao Falls into the Water Again
chapters.content:
The next morning, Shen Mingqiu rushed over and pulled Shen Weici: “Sister, why don’t we go to Wenxiang Courtyard together to see Second Sister?”

As she spoke, she leaned down and whispered in Shen Weici’s ear: “I heard her body had almost recovered. This morning, when she went to the Old Madam’s place, she passed by the corridor bridge, and for some reason, she suddenly fell into the pond.”

“Those old servants and maids panicked and called for help everywhere, but coincidentally, there wasn’t a single person around. As a result, she sank into the water, and it was only after a long time that the guards arrived.”

As she spoke, Shen Mingqiu sat beside Shen Weici and watched her cover her lips with a smile: “Third Sister, look, isn’t this karma?”

“Her body had just recovered, and she was running around recklessly. Now she’s fallen into the water again. I reckon she’ll have to rest for a while more.”

“I heard her mother was sent to the estate by the Old Madam for some reason. We might as well go and see her make a fool of herself.”

Shen Weici pressed Shen Mingqiu’s hand: “What’s the point of us going? Won’t she see that we’re there to laugh at her?”

“Then she’ll hold a grudge against us, and the resentment will just keep growing. It’s tiring to the heart.”

Shen Mingqiu listened to Shen Weici’s words and gave up the idea. She called Yue Deng to bring the unfinished game of Go from last time and then looked at Shen Weici: “You’re right. She’s the best at holding grudges. Relying on her status as a legitimate daughter and the Old Madam’s favor, how could she tolerate others mocking her?”

After finishing her words, she coldly humphed: “I saw that during all the days she was ill, Young Master Xu of the Yong’an Marquis’s mansion only came to see her once. Who knows what kind of days she’ll have after marrying there. What’s there to be proud of?”

Shen Weici remained silent, quietly placing her piece: “It really has nothing to do with us.”

Shen Mingqiu smiled: “Indeed, why bother worrying about her?”

She then curiously asked Shen Weici: “In the past, Second Uncle always listened to Second Aunt. How come this time, Second Aunt was sent to the estate? Even after returning, I haven’t heard of any major incidents. I always feel it’s a bit strange.”

“My birth mother was curious too, but she couldn’t find out anything from the Old Madam.”

Shen Weici smiled slightly: “After all, what’s the reason? Even if we knew, it wouldn’t be of much use.”

Then she said: “If you don’t focus on the game, I might win.”

Shen Mingqiu finally looked at the board and saw that Shen Weici had captured several of her pieces. She hurriedly said: “This is bad, this is bad, I’m afraid I’m going to lose.”

Shen Weici smiled: “Then play properly.”

After a few more days, Shen Weici’s body had recovered a lot.

During these days, she had not gone out much, at most just sitting in the pavilion at the back of the courtyard, or when Shen Mingqiu came to talk to her.

The next morning, when she got up, Yue Deng came in and said that a heavy snow had fallen outside last night, and now everything outside was white.

Shen Weici dressed herself, her eyes showing a hint of fatigue. She watched Yue Deng open the flower lattice window and saw the thick layer of snow outside. Only then did she realize how fast time had passed.

In a few more days, it would be the New Year.

She had been resting for a long time.

Today was also the day to visit Cishou Hall. After the meal, Shen Weici tidied up a bit before going to the Old Madam’s place. Yue Deng hurriedly brought the windproof hat and put it on Shen Weici: “Miss, didn’t you say you had a headache? This will be just right.”

Shen Weici had been getting headaches whenever she came back from outside and caught a cold wind. Wearing this would be just right.

With a hand warmer in her hand, she also had Yue Deng adjust her cloak. Only then did the mistress and servant head to the Old Madam’s place.

Shen Weici arrived early, and there were not many people in the warm pavilion yet.

When Old Madam Shen saw Shen Weici come so early, she took her hand and asked: “Have you been feeling better these days?”

Shen Weici nodded: “Thank you for your concern, Old Madam. I am much better now.”

Old Madam Shen nodded and then patted Shen Weici’s hand: “Wait a few more days until you are fully recovered, and I will call the imperial physician to check on you again to see if there are any lingering issues.”

Shen Weici gratefully nodded: “It’s all thanks to Old Madam’s care.”

“I have been unable to attend to you these days, and I feel guilty in my heart.”

Old Madam Shen smiled: “I know you have filial piety, and that’s what matters.”

Then she asked: “Have you settled the matter with Second Young Master Zhang? You should make it clear. If you are to break it off, do it cleanly. Don’t leave any lingering ties that might cause rumors. It wouldn’t be good for your future marriage.”

Shen Weici nodded: “Old Madam, rest assured. Weici understands. I will not bring any trouble to the Marquis’s mansion.”

Old Madam Shen saw that Shen Weici seemed to understand everything, so she didn’t say much more. She casually asked about the recent medicines she was taking and what was lacking in her room.

Shen Weici answered each question one by one.

As they were talking, everyone from the third branch, except for the Third Master, arrived together.

As soon as Third Madam Wang entered, she saw Shen Weici and asked about her illness. Shen Weici quickly replied: “I am almost fully recovered.”

Her voice was soft and gentle, and her eyes were full of charm.

Third Madam Wang was dazzled and smiled: “Third Young Lady, after this illness, you seem to look even more beautiful.”

Shen Weici smiled gently: “I cannot accept such praise from Third Aunt.”

After talking for a while, someone suddenly entered from outside the curtain. The person was wearing a windproof hat, and her body was wrapped in a fur-lined cloak, tightly bundled up. Her pale face was full of sickness.

The usually bright and beautiful face now had a slight yellowish tint, and her spirit was not as good as before.

Following behind her was Shen Yanli.

As soon as Shen Zhaozhao entered, her gaze first swept over Shen Weici, who was sitting next to Old Madam Shen. She paused for a moment, then took off her cloak and threw herself into Old Madam Shen’s arms: “Grandmother.”

Shen Weici looked at Shen Zhaozhao’s actions and quietly got up to sit in a lower position.

Up front, Shen Zhaozhao buried her head in Old Madam Shen’s arms, looking wronged, crying and coughing, which made Old Madam Shen’s heart ache.

Shen Mingqiu went over to sit next to Shen Weici and whispered in her ear, so only the two of them could hear: “I heard that after Second Sister fell into the water, Old Madam went to see her several times and sent her many things.”

Then she looked at Shen Weici and asked: “I see that Old Madam seems to like you recently. Has she come to see you?”

Shen Weici shook her head.

Shen Mingqiu sighed: “Old Madam still prefers her legitimate granddaughters. Marrying into the Yong’an Marquis’s mansion is a glorious matter. How can we gain Old Madam’s favor?”

“In Old Madam’s eyes, we probably cannot marry into such a family.”

Shen Weici looked at Shen Mingqiu and softly said: “It doesn’t matter if Old Madam doesn’t like us. Marriage is not about the family status; it’s about the person being good.”

At this moment, Shen Siwen looked at Shen Weici a few times. She sat there gently, her white jade fingers holding an embroidered handkerchief. A pair of silver earrings hung from her ears, and a jade hairpin was in her hair. She was graceful and charming, and her slightly lowered head made her even more eye-catching.

Beside her, Shen Yanli also looked at Shen Weici, his expression slightly complicated. His usually easygoing nature was not as talkative today. Instead, Shen Hua came over to talk to him for a while.

Shen Hua asked Shen Siwen: “Previously, Second Brother Song came over twice. Why isn’t he here today?”

Shen Siwen smiled: “It’s normal for him not to come.”

Everyone was chatting, and suddenly, Shen Yanli walked up to Shen Weici and whispered: “Third Sister, come out with me for a moment.”

chapters.title: Meeting Princess Huimin
chapters.content:
Shen Weici looked up at Shen Yanli. She had not seen him for many days. During her illness, he had not come to visit her even once.

Now he suddenly came to her, and she already guessed what he wanted to say.

She still lightly responded with a soft “mm” and stood up to follow Shen Yanli out.

Yue Deng followed behind, and as they stepped out of the room, she draped the cloak over Shen Weici’s shoulders.

Shen Yanli glanced at the maid beside Shen Weici and then whispered: “Do you know about the matter of Mother being sent to the estate by Old Madam?”

Shen Weici gently lowered her eyebrows and bit her lip: “I heard Old Madam mention it.”

Shen Yanli looked down at Shen Weici. He didn’t have much affection for this suddenly appeared sister, but he liked her gentle and quiet nature. Moreover, she was beautiful, which he also liked.

But now, so many things had happened in the second branch, all because of her. Unconsciously, he felt a little sorry for her.

He said in a low voice: “Regarding the matter of you and Zhaozhao falling into the water, that day, we indeed did not call the physician to see you in time. It was my mother’s fault. But now that your body has recovered and your complexion is as good as before, it is also a relief.”

“You are part of our second branch. You should also care about Mother’s situation.”

“The matter started because of you. You should also go to Grandmother and Father to plead for mercy.”

“Now, the second branch is cold and desolate, and the other branches are laughing at us. Father is also worried. Can you bear to see this?”

After the incident, no one from the second branch had come to see her or take care of her. Only when it affected themselves did they think of her.

Shen Weici listened to Shen Yanli’s words. Although she felt ironic, she looked up at him, her pale eyes filled with grievance.

She coughed twice: “No matter what Third Brother says, it doesn’t matter. I naturally do not wish for things to be like this.”

“Last time when I fell into the water, I did not blame anyone. I was just fortunate that Young Master Song saved me, which allowed me to wake up with a breath of life.”

“Because of that fall, my body was ruined, and I lost the engagement with the Earl’s mansion. I cannot blame anyone else; it’s all my fate.”

“When I returned from Young Master Song’s countryside estate, I immediately went to Old Madam’s place to pay my respects. After learning about my birth mother’s situation, I went to plead for her.”

“But I am of low status and my words carry little weight. How could Old Madam listen to me?”

“At that time, Old Madam said that a young lady from the Marquis’s mansion could not marry into the Earl’s mansion as a concubine. It was all nonsense.”

“She told me not to interfere anymore, and I did not dare to ask further.”

Shen Yanli was taken aback by these words. He had only learned about this later, and it was from Zhaozhao’s mouth. He also knew that his mother had gone too far.

He looked down at Shen Weici: “It’s hard to persuade Grandmother. You should go and persuade Father.”

“With the New Year approaching, can Mother still be alone in that desolate estate?”

“We are all part of the second branch. If the second branch is well, aren’t you also well?”

Song Zhang entered from outside the courtyard. At a glance, he saw Shen Weici and Shen Yanli standing in the corridor. The cold wind blew on Shen Weici’s white cloak, making her black hair appear even softer and more beautiful.

He walked over, and as he passed by, he only heard her soft and gentle voice: “I will remember what Third Brother said. I originally did not want things to turn out like this. Later, I will plead with Father for my birth mother.”

Song Zhang heard this sentence and could not help but pause. He only paused for a moment before frowning and walking in.

Behind Song Zhang, Princess Huimin followed his gaze and also looked at Shen Weici’s back for a moment before being led inside by the Eldest Master.

Shen Weici’s cheeks were slightly red from the cold wind. She looked at Shen Yanli again: “But I also don’t know if I can change Father’s decision. If I can’t, Third Brother, please don’t blame me.”

Shen Yanli looked at Shen Weici’s fragile and weak appearance and felt that he had made things difficult for her.

When Old Madam made the decision, she was still outside. What could she decide?

Even Zhaozhao had not been able to plead with Old Madam.

He nodded and then asked with rare concern: “How is your body recovering?”

Shen Weici replied: “My body has almost recovered. I just have a slight cough, but it’s nothing serious.”

Shen Yanli then nodded and let Shen Weici follow him back inside.

When they entered the warm pavilion, the room was already filled with people. Shen Weici’s gaze swept over Princess Huimin and the Eldest Master, who were in the most prominent seats, before going to sit next to Shen Mingqiu. As she looked up, she found herself facing Song Zhang.

She slightly turned her head away.

At the front, Shen Zhaozhao was still buried in Old Madam Shen’s arms, looking extremely wronged.

Below, the women were chatting in groups. Shen Weici slightly turned her body to chat with Shen Mingqiu. Suddenly, Wang Shi said to Shen Weici: “Since your engagement with the second young master of the Earl’s mansion is off, I can introduce a marriage for you. It’s my nephew. He’s quite handsome. What do you think?”

Shen Weici listened and slightly lowered her head, softly saying: “Weici cannot decide on her own.”

Wang Shi smiled: “I just like your considerate and understanding nature. You’re skilled, capable, and don’t fight or grab. Moreover, you’re so beautiful. I like you very much.”

“Next time, I’ll have my nephew come over. You can take a look at him from behind the curtain. If you think he’s good, I’ll go to Old Madam and speak for you.”

“He’s been doing business with my younger brother since he was young. His family is quite wealthy. He’s been honest and knows how to care for others since he was a child. He just turned twenty, which is a perfect match for your age. Maybe you’ll be a good fit.”

As she spoke, Wang Shi looked at Shen Weici’s expression and lowered her voice: “It’s just that his mother has been bedridden for years and needs someone to take care of her. There are many maids in the mansion, so you won’t have to do much.”

“But since your mother-in-law is not well and he is the only son in the family, you might have to help manage the household after marrying him, right?”

“I see that you are thoughtful and quiet. I like you and trust you, which is why I have this idea.”

Shen Weici’s heart stirred. She felt that the more prestigious the family, the more they cared about one’s background. If she married an ordinary merchant’s son, perhaps there would not be so much trouble.

Shen Weici pursed her lips and still softly said: “Third Aunt, thank you for your concern. But this matter must be decided by my birth mother and father. Weici cannot decide on her own.”

Wang Shi smiled: “This is not difficult. After the New Year, I’ll talk to your father about it.”

“First, let’s ask him about his thoughts.”

Shen Weici’s eyes held a smile: “Thank you for your trouble, Third Aunt.”

Wang Shi looked at Shen Weici’s smiling eyes and liked her more and more. She could not help but reach out to touch Shen Weici’s face, clicking her tongue: “Look at this face, how did it come to be so beautiful?”

“I’m actually having second thoughts now.”

At this moment, Wang Shi was indeed having second thoughts. With Shen Weici’s appearance, how could a merchant’s family protect her?

Her nephew was a honest and sincere person. She thought that Shen Weici, being capable, would complement him, and their life would get better and better. But her appearance was indeed too outstanding.

Shen Weici heard Wang Shi’s words and seemed to lower her eyes shyly, but she did not ask further.

On the other side, Song Zhang leaned against the chair, his gaze always on Shen Weici. He watched as her eyes brightened slightly because of Wang Shi’s words, her shy and charming demeanor, and his eyes darkened.

The silver earrings swaying by her ears were as graceful as the bright moon, lightly veiled by the morning mist.

The cup in his hand tightened, and when he loosened it, there was already a crack.

Princess Huimin had long noticed Song Zhang’s gaze. She looked at Shen Weici for a moment and then slightly furrowed her brows.

Shen Weici noticed a gaze on her and slightly lifted her head. Seeing it was Princess Huimin, she was slightly startled and then lowered her eyelids.

Shen Weici still remembered the first day she came to the Marquis’s mansion and the time when Princess Huimin spoke to her while playing the double-six board game. Although the two of them had not exchanged a single word, Shen Weici had a very good impression of Princess Huimin in the Marquis’s mansion.

Perhaps it was because of her noble status; she had never needed to pay attention to others’ opinions and could say whatever she wanted.

But just now, Princess Huimin had looked at her with such a gaze... which made her feel a slight unease in her heart.

She only felt her heart skip a beat and silently composed herself.

As the gathering was about to end, Shen Weici and Shen Mingqiu walked together. After parting ways at the crossroads, a richly dressed matron in a dark green cross-collar jacket suddenly blocked their path: “Third Young Lady, our Princess Consort invites you to come and talk.”

Shen Weici paused, almost thinking she had misheard. Why would Princess Huimin suddenly invite her to talk?

She looked at the seemingly wealthy matron and asked: “What does Princess Consort want with me?”

The matron was quite polite and smiled: “It’s just that Princess Consort finds you pleasant to the eye and wants to chat with you.”

chapters.title: A World of Difference
chapters.content:
Shen Weici never expected Princess Huimin to take notice of her. She nodded and followed the old servant.

This was the first time Shen Weici had visited Princess Huimin’s Rongfang Courtyard. As soon as she stepped inside, she was slightly taken aback.

This courtyard was more than twice the size of Song Zhang’s.

She had heard that when Princess Huimin remarried into the Hou residence, the Hou family had purchased the adjacent mansion and renovated it into this grand courtyard.

Inside, there were pavilions, towers, lakes, and waterside pavilions—everything one could imagine. No wonder Princess Huimin rarely left; this courtyard alone was larger than most people’s entire homes.

Following the old servant for a long time, they finally arrived at the main house, nestled among plum trees with a babbling stream nearby, an extremely elegant setting.

The old servant opened a door and stepped aside, gesturing for Shen Weici to enter.

Shen Weici lowered her gaze and walked in. At first glance, she saw Princess Huimin seated beside a small table, with tea being brewed on it and precious celadon tea sets placed beside her.

As she approached, she noticed another gentle and refined woman kneeling beside Princess Huimin, skillfully preparing tea.

Shen Weici took a few steps forward and respectfully greeted Princess Huimin.

Princess Huimin looked at Shen Weici. Her dark hair was neatly arranged, and her features were graceful and composed. She stood there naturally, with poised and dignified bearing.

She smiled slightly and asked Shen Weici to sit across from her.

Shen Weici watched as a maid placed a cushion in front of her. Only then did she lift her skirt and kneel in front of Princess Huimin.

Once seated, she noticed a vast expanse of green banana trees and the lake to the side, offering a uniquely beautiful view.

The woman beside Princess Huimin looked at Shen Weici, smiled warmly, and personally poured her tea. “This is brewed with plum blossom snow water. Try it, little sister.”

Shen Weici looked up at the smiling eyes before her, took the cup with both hands, and after a sip, smiled. “Elder sister has such skill.”

The woman modestly smiled. “I merely picked up a few things haphazardly from Her Highness. I’m far from proficient.”

Princess Huimin kept her gaze on Shen Weici the entire time. Seeing her speak clearly and move with grace, she slowly spoke amidst the fragrance of tea: “Rongjin’s father was once the beloved subordinate of my late former father-in-law. After he died in battle, my late former father-in-law brought her back and raised her in the Song National Duke’s residence.”

“She and Song Zhang grew up together and was raised by Old Madame Song. Old Madame Song intends for her to be taken as Song Zhang’s concubine in the future.”

“After all, having watched her grow up, they know her roots and her character. She is capable and filial.”

As she spoke, Princess Huimin glanced at Shen Weici. “The women by Zhang’er’s side cannot be just anyone. They must be approved by Old Madame Song and me. Even as a concubine, she must be a well-bred young lady from a noble family.”

Shen Weici was taken aback. Hearing Princess Huimin’s words, she faintly perceived something.

She lowered her gaze and nodded. “Weici admires Young Master Song. With Her Highness and Old Madame Song overseeing the women around him, he is sure to choose a good partner in the future.”

Princess Huimin heard this and lifted her eyelids to glance at Shen Weici before calmly saying, “Your mother is just an embroideress. How did she manage to send you to a girls’ school?”

Shen Weici spoke softly, “Though my mother is an embroideress, she has a mother’s heart and hopes I can marry an ordinary man as his lawful wife, someone who can hold her own in society.”

She paused, then softly added, “My wish is also to marry an ordinary man as his lawful wife. I do not seek a high-ranking family, nor do I covet wealth. I only wish not to disappoint my mother’s hopes for me.”

Princess Huimin listened, her gaze resting on Shen Weici’s face as she carefully appraised her.

Those eyes were calm, and her posture was proper. She spoke neither servilely nor arrogantly, which even surprised Princess Huimin slightly.

She had called Shen Weici here to warn her not to harbor improper thoughts about her son. Yet, Shen Weici seemed quite clever. In fact, Princess Huimin found herself liking her a little.

Princess Huimin smiled and looked at Shen Weici. “I know your engagement to the Yiyong Earl’s residence was canceled. It was a twist of fate; blame it on encountering a cruel stepmother.”

“In the future, if you face any obstacles in your marriage prospects, come to me. If I can help you, I will.”

Shen Weici, upon hearing this, quickly knelt and kowtowed to Princess Huimin. “Weici thanks Her Highness.”

Princess Huimin looked down at Shen Weici kneeling before her. If she had any lingering doubts before, seeing her kneel like this dispelled them. She believed Shen Weici would not dare to have designs on her son. Perhaps it was her son who had taken a liking to her.

A woman with such looks, even if she were interested, would be nothing out of the ordinary.

It was a pity that she knew her status—a country girl, after all, was lacking.

Just as Song Zhang hurriedly entered from outside, he saw Shen Weici kneeling on the ground, kowtowing to Princess Huimin.

His brows furrowed, his expression darkening. In a few strides, he grabbed Shen Weici’s arm and pulled her up. “Are your bones so weak?”

Shen Weici was startled. She was pulled up by Song Zhang and saw his dark expression as he looked at Princess Huimin. “Mother, what are you doing?”

Princess Huimin looked up at Song Zhang, then lowered her head and slowly sipped her tea. “I invited the Third Young Lady to chat. What are you doing here?”

Song Zhang’s face was impassive as he pursed his lips. He then loosened his grip on Shen Weici’s arm, ordered a maid to bring another cushion, and sat down. “Then I’ll keep Mother company.”

He turned to Shen Weici. “Why are you standing? Don’t you know how to sit?”

Shen Weici looked at Princess Huimin, thinking that it might not be appropriate for her to stay while the family sat together.

Just as she was about to excuse herself, Princess Huimin looked at Shen Weici. “You may leave first.”

Shen Weici felt a weight lift and quickly took her leave.

As she turned, she noticed the gentle woman beside Princess Huimin bowing to pour tea for Song Zhang, her eyes filled with unhidden affection.

Stepping outside, she inhaled the faint floral scent in the courtyard and walked away with lowered gaze.

Song Zhang had never lacked for women around him. High-born ladies and noble daughters were all carefully selected for him by Princess Huimin.

She had never harbored any thoughts about Song Zhang, and she knew her status made it impossible for her to marry him.

Moreover, if she had to compete with so many women for his favor, she could never bring herself to do it.

But if Princess Huimin could help her in the future, her marriage prospects might go more smoothly.

As she reached a waterside pavilion, Shen Weici lowered her gaze to the lake, pondering whether to visit Shen Zhaozhao.

After all, they were sisters of the same branch. Since their father was here today, it would be good to at least put on a show of sisterly affection for his sake.

She looked around and realized that Shen Zhaozhao’s courtyard was probably not far from here, so she decided to go.

But just as she turned, she felt her forehead bump into a hard chest. She looked down at the dark chest before her, then up into Song Zhang’s deep, dark eyes.

She had no idea when he had silently approached her. Instinctively, she tried to step back, but he pulled her into his arms, his hand on her waist.

chapters.title: Please, Young Master Song, Restrain Yourself
chapters.content:
This was still outside, and there were many servants coming and going.

The meaning behind Princess Huimin’s summons just now was clear: she wanted Shen Weici to stay away from Song Zhang. She was counting on Princess Huimin to help her with her marriage prospects in the future.

She always felt that Princess Huimin’s word might carry more weight than Old Madame Shen’s.

If it weren’t for fear of Princess Huimin suspecting her of having designs on Song Zhang, she would have liked to frequently appear before Princess Huimin to gain some presence.

But if Princess Huimin’s people were to see her entangled with Song Zhang outside, it would give the impression of hypocrisy, which would be bad.

Shen Weici pushed Song Zhang’s hand away and sidestepped to a distance of four or five steps from him. She furrowed her brows, bowed to Song Zhang, and said in a low voice, “Please, Young Master Song, restrain yourself.”

Song Zhang stared blankly at Shen Weici, who seemed eager to put as much distance between them as possible. Every time he took a step forward, she took a step back.

He stopped, and so did she.

Song Zhang clenched his fists at his sides, watching her pale, delicate face under the white hood of her cloak. Her eyes remained downcast, never once meeting his gaze.

With a darkened expression, he continued to approach her. She retreated until her back was against the railing, with nowhere left to go, before finally lifting her eyes.

He heard her slightly trembling voice: “Young Master Song, how far do you intend to push me?”

“The engagement with the Earl’s residence was canceled as you wished. What more do you want from me before you’ll let me go?”

Song Zhang paused, his gaze fixed intently on Shen Weici’s eyes. “I’m pushing you?”

Shen Weici turned her face away and said softly, “Young Master Song and I were never meant to have any connection. You may be able to endure rumors, but for an unmarried woman like me, even the slightest rumor could ruin my life.”

“Please, show me some understanding.”

Song Zhang felt a sharp pain in his liver. He had come chasing after her, worried she might have been wronged by his mother, and he wanted to stand up for her.

Yet now, she was avoiding him as if he were a venomous snake or a scorpion.

He took a step back, clenching his hands tightly behind his back. His cold eyes were filled with emotion as he turned and left.

Shen Weici watched his retreating figure, then averted her gaze.

She looked around. Although no one was in sight, her heart still felt uneasy.

If someone had seen the way Song Zhang had his hand on her waist just now, even a baseless rumor could spread. Old Madame and her father might not believe her; they might even think she was immoral and send her to be Song Zhang’s concubine.

Yue Deng approached Shen Weici. She had seen the entire scene where Young Master Song had held the young lady. She couldn’t help but look at Shen Weici and ask softly, “Young Master Song towards you…”

Shen Weici looked at Yue Deng, patted her hand without speaking, then after a pause, said, “Let’s go visit Second Sister in the afternoon.”

Yue Deng nodded and followed Shen Weici back.

Shen Weici’s illness had not fully recovered. Though she no longer coughed, the slightest breeze gave her a headache.

After returning to Linchun Courtyard, she felt drained and dozed off for a while.

It was mid-afternoon when Shen Weici finally went to Shen Zhaozhao’s courtyard.

When Shen Weici arrived, the maid at the gate was surprised to see her. This was the first time Shen Weici had visited, so the maid’s surprise was understandable. She quickly went inside to announce the visit.

Shen Weici adjusted her cloak, looking at the luxurious and spacious courtyard, where every corner was meticulously arranged.

Yue Deng looked at the two embroidered towers connected by a corridor and whispered in Shen Weici’s ear, “Second Young Lady lives in such a fine courtyard. I wonder where she gets the nerve.”

Shen Weici smiled slightly but remained silent.

Soon, the maid returned and invited Shen Weici inside, quite politely.

Following the maid into the main house, as soon as she reached the veranda, she heard faint sounds from inside. As she approached the beaded curtain, she heard Shen Zhaozhao’s unabashed loud voice: “Who wants that wretched girl to visit me? She’s only here to laugh at me.”

“I don’t want her in here.”

This was followed by a voice trying to console her in vain.

Shen Weici listened to the voices inside, suppressing the sarcastic smile at the corner of her lips. She lifted the curtain and walked in.

Her father and eldest brother had never once visited her.

Shen Zhaozhao’s boudoir was exquisitely decorated. The treasure pavilion was filled with books and paintings, the walls adorned with calligraphy and art by famous masters. The floor was covered with intricately patterned carpets that radiated warmth underfoot.

She inhaled the mix of medicinal and fragrant scents in the room, walked past the partition screen, and saw her father sitting by the bed, softly coaxing Shen Zhaozhao. Shen Yanli was bent over, feeding medicine to Shen Zhaozhao, while a maid held a small jar of preserved fruit nearby.

Shen Zhaozhao’s face was deathly pale, her hair disheveled, and there were faint traces of tears at the corners of her eyes.

Shen Weici entered, removed her cloak, and handed it to Yue Deng. She greeted her father and Shen Yanli with a neither too loud nor too soft voice, then approached Shen Zhaozhao and asked, “Is Second Sister feeling better?”

As soon as Shen Zhaozhao heard Shen Weici’s voice, she flew into a rage, coughed a couple of times, snatched the medicine bowl from Shen Yanli’s hand, and hurled it at Shen Weici. “Wretched girl, who asked you to come?”

“I don’t need your concern. Was it you who caused me to fall into the water the second time?”

The last time, as she passed the stone bridge, she had distinctly felt something strike her ankle, followed by a sharp pain. Her body had uncontrollably tumbled into the water.

None of the maids or wet nurses around her could swim. Coincidentally, that day, all the guards had gone to the East Courtyard to search for something Princess Huimin had lost. It took a long time before they found a young servant who could swim.

She had clearly felt that if it had taken any longer, she would have drowned.

But when she woke up, no matter how she explained, her father, eldest brother, and even her grandmother refused to believe her. Since only her own people had been around her at the time, they simply didn’t trust her.

Shen Weici’s clothes were drenched in the warm, brown medicine. She looked down at it, then heard her father sigh. “Zhaozhao, stop making a scene.”

Then he spoke to her, “Weici, Zhaozhao has a difficult temperament, and she’s seriously ill. You should yield to her.”

Shen Weici’s face showed a trace of concern. She looked up at her father. “This daughter would never quarrel with Second Sister.”

“I came specifically to visit Second Sister.”

As she spoke, she took a sachet from her sleeve. “This is a special evil-repelling sachet I made for Second Sister. Though it’s nothing precious, it represents my sincerity.”

Shen Rongsheng took the sachet from Shen Weici’s hand. It was embroidered with the Five Poisons pattern, a design meant to ward off evil and illness. He looked at Shen Weici’s considerate demeanor with satisfaction. “You’ve always been so thoughtful.”

He handed the sachet to Shen Zhaozhao. “This is your Third Sister’s goodwill. You two sisters should get along and interact more. After all, you’re from the same branch. If your Third Sister does well, it’s good for you too, isn’t it?”

Shen Zhaozhao, however, snatched the sachet from Shen Rongsheng’s hand and threw it into the charcoal brazier beside the bed. Coughing, she glared at Shen Weici with malice. “Who is her sister?”

“This bastard doesn’t deserve to be my sister.”

chapters.title: Why the Second Cousin Helps You
chapters.content:
Shen Weici knew deep in her heart that she and Shen Zhaozhao would never be able to be sisters.

No matter how low-key she acted, Shen Zhaozhao would always see her as a thorn in her eye and a bone in her throat.

Even though Shen Yanli, her father, Lady Wen, and the old madam all doted on her, Shen Zhaozhao still couldn’t stand her.

Anyway, Shen Weici didn’t really come to see her. She just thought that if she didn’t come to visit Shen Zhaozhao after her fall into the water, she might be caught in a bad situation. Plus, her father was here today, so she wanted to prove to her father that she had come.

It was fine that Shen Zhaozhao didn’t like her; she wouldn’t come again.

She pretended to look aggrieved, shedding a few tears, then coughed and said to her father, “Daughter was not fully recovered from her illness before. I was afraid of passing it to Second Sister, so I didn’t come.”

“Now that I’m a little better, seeing Second Sister with my own eyes puts my mind at ease.”

“As for Second Sister’s accusation that I harmed her, Daughter knows nothing about it. I beg Father to judge fairly.”

Shen Rongsheng looked at Shen Weici, seeing her so aggrieved, and felt a pang of guilt in his heart.

In truth, during the days Shen Weici was ill, he hadn’t visited her either. All the tonic medicine had been sent to Zhaozhao. Now, he felt a little ashamed.

He said softly, “Zhaozhao was just talking nonsense in a fit of anger. I naturally believe you. Since you’re not fully recovered, go back soon.”

Shen Weici lowered her gaze and nodded, then quietly turned to leave.

But just as she turned, Shen Zhaozhao, from nowhere, found the strength to leap off the bed with a scream from Shen Yanli. Like a madwoman, she grabbed Shen Weici’s clothes and demanded, “How dare you say my fall into the water has nothing to do with you?”

“Song Erge helps you in every way. Who knows if you secretly seduced Song Erge and made him help you take revenge on me?”

She gritted her teeth, her expression ferocious. “You wretched girl, if my body doesn’t recover, I’ll make sure you wish you were dead.”

As she spoke, her sharp nails viciously scratched toward Shen Weici’s face. Shen Weici quickly turned her head away and tried to push Shen Zhaozhao off.

But Shen Zhaozhao, like a madwoman, held on tightly, her eyes filled with hatred and rage, making Shen Weici’s heart tremble slightly.

She felt a sharp pain on her neck and realized Shen Zhaozhao had scratched her.

Shen Yanli hurriedly pulled Shen Zhaozhao away and couldn’t help but shout, “Zhaozhao, can’t you stop making trouble?”

Shen Zhaozhao cried as she looked at Shen Yanli, “Big Brother, my fall into the water was not an accident. It was really this wretched girl taking revenge on me.”

“I clearly felt someone hit my ankle. How could that be fake?!”

Shen Yanli looked at Shen Weici in surprise. He didn’t think she had the ability to make Song Zhang help her.

Just as he was about to speak, Shen Rongsheng beat him to it, anger in his voice: “If you keep making trouble like this, I won’t come see you again in the future.”

“Do you think the second branch doesn’t have enough problems already?!”

With that, he called two servant women to forcibly pull Shen Zhaozhao away, then told Shen Weici to leave first.

Shen Weici, one hand covering her neck, silently nodded and walked out.

Shen Yanli watched as Shen Zhaozhao continued to scream like a madwoman, then looked at Shen Weici’s retreating figure. He lifted his leg and followed her.

Shen Yanli caught up with Shen Weici in the corridor. Seeing the bloodstains on her collar from the wound on her neck, and her pale cheeks, he asked softly, “What is your relationship with Song Erge?”

Shen Weici hadn’t expected Shen Yanli to suddenly ask her this. She looked up in confusion. “What does Third Brother mean?”

Shen Yanli looked at Shen Weici’s surprised expression. Thinking that Shen Zhaozhao had so firmly accused her, perhaps she wasn’t lying.

Her second fall into the water was indeed too coincidental.

But if Shen Weici had done it, he wouldn’t believe it. She didn’t have that kind of ability.

But if it was Song Zhang, then it would be easy.

His younger sister was exceptionally beautiful; it wasn’t impossible.

He looked down at Shen Weici and asked, “Last time, Song Erge helped you at the teahouse. Then, after you fell into the water, he took people to the old madam to plead your case and even took you to the manor to recover.”

“Song Erge usually doesn’t interfere in the affairs of the Hou residence. Why would he help you?”

Shen Weici, her face pale, said, “The first time, Song Shizi helped me because I gave him an embroidered pouch, and he said he was returning the favor. The second time, it was a coincidence. His attendant happened to pass by, and Yue Deng called out to him loudly, so Song Shizi came to help me.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici’s eyes reddened with tears. “That time I fell into the water, my maid was so worried about me, afraid I would die, that she called for help without thinking. It was all a coincidence.”

Hearing this, Shen Yanli paused for a moment.

Then he heard her say through tears, “My life was saved by Song Shizi. If it weren’t for him that time I fell into the water, I would have died long ago. If Third Brother really wants to blame someone, don’t blame Song Shizi. I, Weici, am willing to take all the blame.”

“If Third Brother and Father want to punish someone, punish me. Now that my body is weak, the Earl’s residence has even canceled my marriage. I have no other thoughts. If Third Brother doesn’t believe me, I will accept all the blame.”

For some reason, hearing Shen Weici’s words, Shen Yanli felt a tightness in his heart.

He knew everything his mother and sister had done to her, even giving her poison. Yet, she had never made a fuss, and here he was, blaming her.

Now, thinking carefully, what had she done wrong?

Shen Yanli saw the tears in the corners of Shen Weici’s eyes, her head lowered in a pitiful manner, her delicate eyebrows drooping, and the shocking bloodstains on her fair neck. He realized he had been too harsh.

What was the difference between him and his mother and sister? They all just thought she was easy to bully.

Shen Yanli’s heart was filled with guilt. He had never cared for this sister, so how could he have the right to blame her?

He said softly, “Don’t overthink it. I was just asking casually. I don’t blame you.”

“It’s just that Zhaozhao has been spoiled since childhood, so her temper is so hasty. Don’t take it to heart with her, and don’t come here again.”

Shen Weici nodded and said softly, “Then I’ll leave.”

Seeing Shen Yanli nod, she turned and walked out.

Shen Yanli still stood in the corridor, watching Shen Weici’s retreating figure. Suddenly, he had a strange feeling.

Although Shen Weici was always modest and quiet in front of them, when she faced him, no matter how much she was wronged, she remained too calm, as if she would never get angry.

This made him feel that although Shen Weici was gentle, she was also cold and indifferent.

She could handle any words with ease.

He watched Shen Weici’s figure for a long time until it disappeared at the courtyard gate. Then he said softly to the servant beside him, “Send a few people to guard Lingchun Courtyard these days. See if Song Erye has been there or not.”

The servant, after listening, said, “Third Young Master, rest assured. This servant will handle it properly.”

chapters.title: Little New Year’s Eve
chapters.content:
As soon as Shen Weici left the courtyard, her expression turned cold.

Shen Yanli’s suspicion of her was something anyone could think of with a little consideration. If she hadn’t mentioned how Lady Wen had harmed her, perhaps Shen Yanli wouldn’t have believed her so easily.

But she couldn’t guarantee that he fully believed her.

Once suspicion began, it would linger everywhere.

A sharp pain came from her neck. Yue Deng, heartbroken, pressed a handkerchief to Shen Weici’s wound. “Did Second Young Lady grow such long nails just to scratch people? That’s really too vicious.”

“It was her own fault for falling into the water, yet she blames it on you, Young Lady.”

Shen Weici told Yue Deng not to say such things outside and, covering her neck, returned to Lingchun Courtyard.

By nightfall, Shen Weici was sitting in a chair reading a book. Outside, snow had begun to fall. She turned her head to look at the snow, lost in thought.

Yue Deng came over and placed a hand warmer in Shen Weici’s hands. “Young Lady, why aren’t you sleeping yet?”

Shen Weici shook her head. “Wait a little longer.”

Yue Deng then sat beside Shen Weici, planning to make a couple of thick socks.

He Xia and Yan Er had already gone to the back room to sleep. Under the lamp, the mistress and servant sat in silent companionship, the only sound in the room being the turning of pages.

Outside, the snow was falling heavily. Shen Weici seemed to hear the rustling sound and finally closed the book in her hands and stood up.

Yue Deng saw Shen Weici take a cloak and drape it over herself. She couldn’t help but stand up as well. “Young Lady, are you going out?”

Shen Weici lifted the curtain and walked out. “I’m going to look at the snow.”

Yue Deng was taken aback. Look at the snow in the middle of the night?

She followed behind, watching as the young lady picked up a lantern and walked out of the courtyard. Worried, she said, “Young Lady, your body hasn’t fully recovered. It’s late and windy. Let’s look at the snow tomorrow instead.”

Shen Weici said nothing. She carried the lantern and walked around the courtyard. In the white snow, she saw footprints, deep and shallow, exactly as she had suspected.

Shen Yanli still didn’t fully trust her; he had sent people to watch.

She finally set her mind at ease. It was better to know that someone was watching Lingchun Courtyard than to be in the dark.

She carried the lantern back, letting the strong wind and snow mess up her hair.

After going inside, Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici with an uncertain expression. “This place is quite remote. Why are there so many footprints at the root of the wall?”

Shen Weici sat on the edge of the bed and looked at Yue Deng. “Someone is watching Lingchun Courtyard. Tomorrow, just have He Xia go to the entrance to keep an eye out. If she sees Song Shizi’s people from afar, she should come and tell me immediately.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici lay down on her side and said to Yue Deng, “It’s not a big deal. You should go to sleep too.”

Yue Deng, who had been vaguely worried, inexplicably felt at ease after hearing Shen Weici’s words. She nodded and went to sleep.

After Yue Deng left, Shen Weici turned over.

She stared blankly for a while before finally closing her eyes.

Soon, it was New Year’s Eve. Shen Weici had already told Yue Deng to distribute the New Year’s money to He Xia and Yan Er. The two maids were overjoyed and came to Shen Weici, smiling. “We heard that the maids in Wenxiang Courtyard only received 300 coins each, but you gave us one tael of silver each.”

Shen Weici stood on the veranda, looking at the unusually heavy snow outside, and smiled faintly. “There are too many maids in Wenxiang Courtyard, so naturally, they receive less.”

The last time she had gone to Wenxiang Courtyard, she had seen seven or eight maids and servant women. Since they were all supported by the Hou residence, it wasn’t a big deal.

Yue Deng beside her said, “It seems about time. Young Lady, let’s go.”

As she spoke, she went to put a hood on Shen Weici’s head. “The wind and snow are heavy tonight. Wear this so your head won’t hurt from the cold.”

The sky was nearly dark but not completely so. Yue Deng was going to take a glass lantern to use on the way back.

Shen Weici originally didn’t want to use the things Song Zhang had given her, but with this weather, she had no choice. So she told Yue Deng to take it.

They went to the front courtyard’s flower hall. Shen Weici arrived neither early nor late. The people from the third branch always arrived first, followed by the second branch, and then the first branch.

Only Song Zhang returned to the Duke of Song’s residence every year to celebrate the New Year and did not stay in the Hou residence.

Third Madam Wang was accompanying the old madam in conversation, while Third Master and Shen Siwen stood together.

Shen Weici looked around and saw that no one from the second branch had arrived yet. She went to sit next to Shen Mingqiu.

Shen Mingqiu saw Shen Weici arrive. Seeing her take off her cloak, revealing the peach-pink ruyi-patterned dress underneath, she couldn’t help but smile. “Elder Sister looks so good in this dress. Such a bright color would look ugly on me. Only Elder Sister can pull it off.”

Shen Mingqiu was telling the truth. As soon as Shen Weici entered, the maids’ eyes were drawn to her. Her graceful and elegant demeanor, along with her gentle and picturesque features—her almond eyes, peach-like cheeks, and eyes filled with smiles, soft as ripples on a lake—unconsciously captivated everyone.

Shen Weici smiled and sat down. The cold air on her body was warming up, and her cheeks flushed slightly.

After sitting and chatting for a while, the people from the second branch finally arrived.

Shen Yanli accompanied Shen Zhaozhao, with Shen Rongsheng following beside them, looking like a family.

Only she was alone.

Shen Weici’s gaze swept over Shen Zhaozhao’s face, which was pale and weak, clearly still not recovered.

Then she averted her gaze.

Beside her, Shen Mingqiu leaned in and whispered, “Your birth mother was sent to the countryside. Doesn’t she come back even for occasions like this?”

Shen Weici shook her head. “Even if she comes back, she won’t talk to me.”

Shen Mingqiu said, “It seems she won’t be coming back.”

Shen Weici remained silent.

Finally, when everyone had arrived, the old madam ordered the servants to serve the food and for everyone to take their seats.

The masters and young masters sat at one table, while the ladies sat at another.

The table was lively, with people coming and going, chatting. Only Shen Zhaozhao remained silent.

After the banquet, everyone went to the side hall to keep the old madam company, gathering around her to say auspicious words.

Shen Weici also went over and said a few words. The old madam pulled her close. “The medicinal cuisine you mentioned last time was really effective. My head doesn’t hurt anymore. It’s all thanks to you.”

Shen Weici smiled. “As long as the old madam’s body is well, Weici is happy.”

The old madam liked Shen Weici’s words and pulled her closer. “Are you fully recovered from your illness?”

Shen Weici nodded. “Thank you, Old Madam. I am fully recovered.”

The old madam then called a servant woman to bring a box and placed it in Shen Weici’s hands. “This is a reward for you. Take it.”

Shen Weici had seen the old madam give similar boxes to the other young ladies, so she didn’t refuse. She knelt down and kowtowed to the old madam.

Shen Zhaozhao, standing to the side, saw that the box in Shen Weici’s hands was better than the one the old madam had given her.

She also thought about how the old madam had just been holding her hand and talking. When had she become so favored by Grandmother?

Shen Zhaozhao’s fingers tightened, her eyes filled with resentment.

Shen Yanli noticed Shen Zhaozhao’s gaze and felt a jolt in his heart. He tightly gripped Shen Zhaozhao’s hand and said, “My people have been guarding Lingchun Courtyard for so many days, and they haven’t seen Song Erge go there. Don’t make trouble anymore.”

Shen Zhaozhao’s face darkened. “I don’t believe it.”

Shen Yanli looked at Shen Zhaozhao’s expression and sighed.

After the banquet, Shen Weici intended to leave. Shen Rongsheng went up to her and said, “Let’s go to the second courtyard. Our family can sit together for a while.”

Shen Weici was startled for a moment, then nodded.

It was rare for the entire second branch to walk together. Shen Weici walked at the end, while Shen Yanli and Shen Zhaozhao walked side by side in front, chatting. Shen Weici paid no attention to what they were saying.

After walking for a while, Shen Yanli suddenly turned his head toward Shen Weici. “Third Younger Sister, can you see the road?”

After walking for so long, he suddenly asked her this. Shen Weici smiled slightly. “I can see. Third Brother, don’t worry about me.”

Shen Yanli looked at Shen Weici’s slightly cold smile under the dim lamplight and was stunned for a moment before turning back.

When they arrived at the second courtyard and sat down, Shen Rongsheng ordered the servants to bring the items. He sat in the host’s seat and spoke about family harmony, urging Shen Weici and Shen Zhaozhao to be close as sisters in the future and not to quarrel anymore.

Shen Weici smiled and agreed, while Shen Zhaozhao coldly snorted.

Shen Rongsheng sighed, and a few white hairs were visible in his hair.

He ordered the servants to give the items to Shen Weici, Shen Zhaozhao, and Shen Yanli, then said, “See if you like them.”

Shen Weici only glanced at it before closing the box. Shen Yanli, however, leaned over and asked, “What’s yours?”

Shen Weici opened it again for him to see.

Inside was a ruyi pendant, made of coarse jade, a style that could be found anywhere.

Shen Zhaozhao also leaned over to look. Seeing the contents of Shen Weici’s box, she sneered, her eyes filled with sarcasm.

Shen Weici’s face maintained a faint smile. Her peripheral vision swept over Shen Yanli’s box, but she showed no other emotions.

chapters.title: Wei Ci, Hold Me
chapters.content:
Shen Rongsheng looked at the smile on Shen Weici’s face, then at Shen Yanli’s awkward expression, and couldn’t help but frown.

Shen Weici closed the box, stood up, and faced her father with gratitude. “Weici thanks Father for your kind intentions.”

Shen Zhaozhao couldn’t help but sneer, looking at Shen Weici. “You sure know how to pretend.”

Shen Weici remained silent and bid her father farewell again.

Shen Rongsheng couldn’t help but say, “Let’s sit together as a family on New Year’s Eve and talk more.”

Shen Weici looked at her father. “Just now at the banquet, your daughter drank some wine. I’m feeling unwell now and fear I might cause trouble for Father later. I’ll leave early so Father can have some peace.”

Shen Rongsheng was taken aback for a moment, then saw Shen Weici bow respectfully before retreating with lowered eyes.

Only after Shen Weici’s figure had completely left did Shen Zhaozhao turn to her father with a smile. “Father gave her a trinket that can be bought anywhere on the street, and yet he still honors her.”

“In my heart, she doesn’t even deserve a trinket.”

Shen Rongsheng was stunned. “What did you say?”

Shen Yanli looked at his father. “Father, your favoritism is too obvious. Just now, Third Sister still managed to thank you with a smile. Even I found it hard to bear.”

“Third Sister hasn’t done anything wrong. How can Father treat her like this? Zhaozhao and I received precious gold-inlaid jade and a jade fan, but Third Sister only got a trinket worth a few hundred coins. Isn’t this openly belittling her?”

Shen Rongsheng, upon hearing this, was suddenly furious.

He glared at the servant beside him. “I told you to prepare properly. Is this how you do it?”

As he spoke, he kicked the servant. “The thing for the Third Young Lady is something that can be bought from any street stall—a worthless trinket. How dare you deceive me!”

The servant quickly knelt and begged for mercy. “Master only gave so much silver. Naturally, I had to prioritize Second Young Lady and Third Young Master. By the time it came to Third Young Lady, there was no silver left, so I just bought a trinket to pass off, thinking Third Young Lady might not recognize it.”

Shen Zhaozhao, seeing her father’s anger, couldn’t help but say, “Father, why are you angry? What if she really didn’t recognize it?”

“Didn’t you see her smiling and thanking you just now?”

Shen Rongsheng sighed deeply and sat down in his chair.

Shen Weici was indeed a little drunk. On a day like New Year’s Eve, it was hard to refuse, so she endured and drank several cups of fruit wine, making her body and mind uncomfortable.

When she returned to Linchun Courtyard, He Xia and Yan’er had already left. Only Yue Deng was left to attend to her.

Yue Deng looked at Shen Weici, who had turned over and dozed off with a squint, then at the box in her hand. She couldn’t help but speak to Shen Weici. “Even Old Madam gave the young lady a pair of agate earrings and a hairpin.”

“But Second Master gave this thing. This kind of thing can be found anywhere. How did the young lady endure it?”

“If it were me, I would have exposed it on the spot. Let’s see who would be embarrassed then.”

She finished speaking and didn’t know if Shen Weici had heard. For a long time, there was no response.

Just as she was about to get up and leave, she finally heard Shen Weici’s soft voice. “I’ve only been here for less than three months, Yue Deng. There’s no reason to fight over these things.”

“You still can’t see the difference between close and distant?”

“No matter what they do, no matter how they harm me, in the end, they are the close-knit family.”

“I am always an outsider.”

Yue Deng was slightly startled upon hearing this. She looked at Shen Weici’s cheeks, tinged with a peach blush, then heard a murmur. “Yue Deng, I miss my mother.”

“What to do...”

Yue Deng’s eyes instantly reddened, and she choked up, unable to speak.

In the end, she stepped outside, looking at the snow outside the window. She recalled the scenes from past New Year’s in Yuyang, where the young lady bustled around the stove making rice balls, filled with laughter.

Now, even though many people sat together in lively celebration, she felt the young lady was particularly lonely.

She lowered her head and looked at the box in her hands. This marquis’s mansion was truly not worth staying in.

The snow fell silently. Song Zhen braved the wind and snow as he entered the room. The warm fragrance filled his nose, and he saw a single candle flame left burning. With his long legs, he strode straight to the bedside.

He reached out a finger to lift the bed curtain and looked down at the sleeping figure on the bed. The corners of her eyes and cheeks were flushed, carrying a faint scent of rose and green plum—clearly from the fruit wine.

Song Zhen softened his expression. Originally, he had wanted to return to the marquis’s mansion early to spend New Year’s Eve with her, but he had been delayed. Now, in his haste to return and see her, she was already asleep.

He leaned down close to her, seeing the moisture still at the corners of her eyes. Her delicate, flower-like face was more radiant than a hibiscus, and her soft cherry lips always made one want to taste them.

He reached out to stroke her hair, pausing at her lips.

He saw her lips part slightly as she murmured a few words. He couldn’t hear clearly, so he leaned in closer.

It made him pause slightly.

Song Zhen furrowed his brows. Then he noticed a tear trace at the corner of her eye—she looked utterly wronged.

He couldn’t help but soften his expression, placing his palm beside her face as he leaned down to kiss her lips.

In her hazy dream, Shen Weici only felt a heavy pressure on her chest. She couldn’t help but reach out to push it away, but her hand touched something furry, like a dog lying on top of her.

Shen Weici was so startled that she woke up from the dream. She stared blankly at the pair of black eyes that met hers, hearing him call her Weici, her mind going blank.

Her eyes reddened as she didn’t understand why Song Zhen would treat her like this.

Was her purity and chastity so unimportant in his eyes?

Shen Weici struggled fiercely, forcing Song Zhen to hold her hands down as he kissed her deeply again, leaving her with no way to retreat.

The candlelight flickered beside them. Song Zhen, dressed in black, contrasted sharply with Shen Weici, who wore only a light moon-white undergarment. From behind, only a hint of white clothing could be seen peeking out.

Warm fragrance and soft jade—Song Zhen wished he could drown in her tearful, shimmering gaze.

chapters.title: Where Else Can You Find a Better Man Than Me?
chapters.content:
Shen Weici was held down and kissed by Song Zhen for a long time until he finally broke away, gasping for breath, then pulled her tightly into his embrace, burying his face in her neck.

With his eyes closed, he inhaled her scent. His restless fingers kept trying to slip under her clothes but hesitated, only pinching and kneading her slender waist.

It had been many days since he last saw her, and he was lost in her tender embrace. Suddenly, a slap landed on his cheek. Though it didn’t hurt much, it still made him lift his head in surprise. He saw Shen Weici, her eyes red-rimmed, looking at him with a choked voice. “Is this all you know how to do—bully me?”

Song Zhen lowered his gaze, looking at her aggrieved, tear-filled eyes. “Is being with me so bad?”

Shen Weici closed her eyes. “Yes.”

“I never thought of being with you.”

Song Zhen’s face darkened, and he coldly scoffed. “Do you think that just because you have a bewitching face and know some coy tricks, all men will flock to you?”

“Do you think you can find a better man than me anywhere else?”

“In terms of background and status, I am stronger than anyone else you could find.”

Shen Weici didn’t want to look at Song Zhen’s face. She lowered her voice, her eyes red. “I would rather marry an ordinary commoner than be with you.”

Song Zhen’s face turned gloomy. He grabbed her chin, which was trying to avoid him, and looked at her with annoyance. “Are you saying that in your heart, even an ordinary commoner is better than me?”

“Your coy tricks should have limits. I am not a patient man.”

Shen Weici widened her eyes and looked at Song Zhen, her soft voice slightly choked. “What coy tricks? I never had any such intentions toward you.”

“I am grateful for your help, but I never had any feelings for you.”

At that moment, Song Zhen felt as if his entire body had been drenched with cold water, extinguishing the burning passion in his heart.

The one woman who had stirred his heart was telling him she felt nothing.

He gritted his teeth in hatred, his fingers trembling as they rested beside her face. His eyes reddened as he stared at her, then stood up and strode out.

Back at Guan Song Ju, Song Zhen took out the hairpin he had prepared for Shen Weici from his embrace and smashed it fiercely onto the ground. The servants in the room were all trembling, afraid that their master’s rage would implicate them.

Song Zhen’s suppressed anger filled him. After all, it was just a woman. Did he lack women?

Why had he rushed back so eagerly?

Immediately, he went out, mounted his horse, and rode toward the flower boat.

The servant, Ling Feng, watched Song Zhen’s retreating figure, wondering why he had rushed back in such a hurry, only to leave in a hurry again in the middle of the night.

Inside the private room of the flower boat, Pei Zhan, the legitimate grandson of Minister Pei, saw Song Zhen enter and quickly pushed away the woman beside him to greet him. “Earlier, when you left the palace, I invited you to come, but you refused. Why are you here now?”

Several young masters from noble families were seated in the private room, all acquaintances from the capital’s aristocratic families. Having grown up together in the capital and being of similar age, they were all familiar with Song Zhen. Seeing him arrive, they all curiously gathered around.

Since Song Zhen’s return to the capital, he had spent the first few months drinking and having fun with them, but lately, he had almost stopped coming.

Today was truly a rare sight.

Song Zhen glanced at Pei Zhan, his demeanor cold, his phoenix eyes chilling. “Are there any better-looking women here?”

Pei Zhan smiled. “You’ve come at the right time. The female slaves bought from Mount Li are all quite charming. I guarantee you’ll like them.”

Song Zhen remained silent and walked over to find a table to sit at. Soon, two women with alluring figures and stunning beauty approached him.

Song Zhen, amidst the sound of silk and bamboo music, narrowed his phoenix eyes as he looked at the approaching women, his expression filled with desire.

He reached out and pinched the woman’s chin, asking, “Do you like me?”

The woman flattered, “This slave’s heart is entirely devoted to you, my lord.”

Song Zhen scoffed and asked her, “What do you like about me?”

The woman smiled with seductive eyes. “My lord is handsome and the General of the Imperial Guards. Which woman wouldn’t like you?”

Song Zhen’s face turned cold, and his heart ached unbearably.

He looked at every woman, as if trying to find a trace of Shen Weici in them.

It was as if this had become an instinctual habit.

He stood up again, kicking away the woman beside him, and walked out of the private room.

Pei Zhan watched Song Zhen’s retreating figure. The man who used to join them for drinks and laughter had changed so much.

He chased after him and, after searching for a while, found Song Zhen standing on the deck. The snow and cold wind blew against his dark robes, fluttering loudly.

His back looked unusually lonely.

Pei Zhan braved the snow and walked over, patting Song Zhen’s shoulder. “Aren’t those beautiful women to your liking?”

“You even kicked her. Still so unappreciative of beauty.”

Song Zhen remained silent, his mind in turmoil.

Pei Zhan looked at Song Zhen’s cold demeanor and couldn’t help but speak. “Rumors outside say you’re going to marry the Fifth Princess. I hear the Fifth Princess is beautiful and graceful. You’ll have a good life. What’s troubling you?”

Song Zhen shot a cold glance at Pei Zhan. “I have no interest in other women.”

“But the one I have interest in has no interest in me.”

Pei Zhan was stunned, then burst into exaggerated laughter. He then asked curiously, “Which woman?”

Song Zhen glanced at the smile on Pei Zhan’s face, his own face filled with impatience. “An unimportant woman.”

Pei Zhan laughed again. If she was unimportant, why was he standing here alone in the cold wind, looking so lost?

He leaned in and said, “What woman could possibly have no interest in you? Besides, as long as you put in the effort, what woman can’t you win over?”

Song Zhen looked at him with a cold smile. “You think I haven’t put in the effort?”

“She’s a heartless stone Bodhisattva, a cold ice pick that stabs you until you bleed, then freezes you so you forget the pain, letting her stab you again and again.”

Pei Zhan was even more curious. Which woman could make Song Zhen feel this way?

He pondered for a moment and said, “Actually, women are all two-faced. If you take more initiative, give her more beautiful gifts, maybe she’ll like you.”

“Besides, you’re General Song. Do you still care about a woman’s feelings? If she’s of high status, just propose marriage. Which family wouldn’t agree?”

“If she’s of lower status, take her as a concubine. If you really like her, promote her to a side consort. It’s not impossible. Is it worth the effort?”

Song Zhen paused, tightening his lips.

Pei Zhan whispered in his ear again, “Moreover, women all like men of high rank and power. They’re just being coy, pretending not to admit it out of shyness.”

“If you ignore her for a while or get close to other women, maybe she’ll get anxious, even jealous, and come to you on her own.”

“Then the initiative would be in your hands. You could do whatever you want, and she wouldn’t dare to make a fuss.”

“Those noble ladies in the capital are all like this. When they like someone, they won’t admit it. If you cold-shoulder them and stop showing affection, they’ll try hard to hint at you.”

“Didn’t the most beautiful woman in the capital end up begging to marry me after I approached her with hot-and-cold tactics?”

As he spoke, he sighed regretfully. “Who would have thought that after marriage, all her tenderness would disappear? Now she’s like a tigress, and I can only sneak out at night to find amusement.”

Song Zhen, hearing this, turned his head to look at Pei Zhan. “Really?”

Pei Zhan smiled. “Do you not trust me?”

chapters.title: Cousin
chapters.content:
After the incident with Song Zhang at night, Shen Weici had the maid lock the room door tightly from the inside before sleeping, and the windows were also closed tightly.

These past two days, when she visited Old Madam Shen, she heard the old lady cough a few times, so she personally went to the kitchen to brew hawthorn and honeysuckle water.

Old Madam Shen looked at Shen Weici, who was sitting beside her, taking care of her, and feeding her medicine spoon by spoon. “I only coughed a few times, yet you are the only one who cares.”

Shen Weici attended to her meticulously and softly said, “Old Madam’s health is more important than anything else.”

Old Madam Shen was genuinely moved.

She then asked Shen Weici how she knew this prescription.

Shen Weici told her past: “My mother passed away from tuberculosis. To treat her illness, I read many prescriptions for coughs.”

As she spoke, Shen Weici lowered her gaze and softly added, “Unfortunately, my family didn’t have the money to buy good medicinal herbs, so I could only find some substitutes.”

She paused again, seemingly regretful: “If my grandmother had given me more money to buy medicine back then, my mother might have been cured.”

Shen Rongsheng walked in just in time to hear Shen Weici’s words. He paused slightly, his emotions complex.

He approached Old Madam Shen: “Your two nephews have come to pay New Year’s respects. They have sent gifts and are waiting in the front hall to see you.”

Old Madam Shen nodded and told Shen Rongsheng to go with his elder brother to entertain them first; she would join them later.

Shen Rongsheng glanced at Shen Weici, who had come early to feed the old lady soup, then left.

Old Madam Shen looked at Shen Weici again: “It’s rare to see such filial piety in you. Your mother’s passing was indeed a pity.”

Shen Weici pressed her lips together and looked at Old Madam Shen: “So when I see Old Madam cough, I worry about your health and hope you recover soon.”

The maid standing beside Old Madam Shen couldn’t help but be moved, thinking that although Third Young Lady had grown up in a small place and had not properly studied the rules of conduct for women at the clan school, her demeanor and manners were the best among the young ladies of the Marquis’s household. No one could find fault with her.

Even Second Young Lady couldn’t compare.

What was even more precious was this filial piety; it was never just empty words. This alone made her far better than Second Young Lady.

Old Madam Shen was also moved. Looking at Shen Weici’s jade-like face, she softly said, “Although you haven’t been in the Marquis’s household for long, your birth mother is unreliable. From now on, I will take better care of you.”

“Your marriage, I will also carefully choose for you.”

“After the New Year, I will have the imperial physician come to check your health.”

Shen Weici looked at Old Madam Shen: “Weici is not in a hurry. Being able to attend to Old Madam is good enough.”

Old Madam Shen smiled: “You are of age. It’s better to arrange your marriage early.”

Shen Weici then lowered her head bashfully.

In the front hall, Shen Weici supported Old Madam Shen as they entered.

Old Madam Shen’s maternal relatives had arrived. When they saw Old Madam Shen enter, they all looked toward her until they saw the woman in a pink dress beside Old Madam Shen, with a graceful appearance and gentle demeanor. Their eyes were inevitably drawn to her.

Her fair skin, graceful figure, and lotus-like steps exuded an otherworldly charm.

Shen Zhaozhao sat in the middle. Seeing everyone’s gaze on Shen Weici, she couldn’t help but feel a pang of jealousy. When had it become Shen Weici’s turn to stand beside Old Madam?

Wei Xiangyi sat among them. His gaze fell on Shen Weici, and he couldn’t look away for a long time. It wasn’t until his father beside him nudged him that he hurriedly took his sister to the center to greet Old Madam Shen with the others.

Shen Weici’s gaze fell on the young man standing in the center. Seeing his courteous posture, refined appearance, and neat blue attire, she thought he must be Old Madam Shen’s nephew from her maternal family.

Hearing him address Old Madam Shen as “Aunt,” she confirmed her guess.

Her gaze then fell on the young woman beside the blue-clad young man. She was also wearing a charming pink dress, with almond-shaped eyes that sparkled, looking quite lovely.

Old Madam Shen’s two nephews and four or five grandsons stood in the center, creating a lively scene.

Old Madam Shen kept her two nephews to sit and talk, asking about her maternal family, and told Shen Weici to go to the side hall with the other young ladies to chat.

Shen Weici lightly excused herself. As soon as she stepped over the threshold, she noticed a shadow falling beside her. The blue-clad young man walked up to her, bent down, and curiously asked, “How should I address this young lady? I don’t recall seeing you before.”

Shen Weici stopped and softly said, “My father is the second master of the Marquis’s household. I grew up with my mother in the suburbs due to her illness and only returned recently. It’s no wonder you don’t recognize me, Cousin.”

Wei Xiangyi had an epiphany: “So you are the young lady from Second Uncle’s family. May I know your name?”

Shen Weici curtsied gracefully: “Among the young ladies of the Marquis’s household, I am the third. You can call me Third Cousin.”

Wei Xiangyi nodded. Looking at Shen Weici’s lowered gaze, her polite and gentle voice, he felt a stir in his heart. He thought she was a truly gentle and refined beauty.

Her black hair and red lips, the swaying strands of hair, exuded a captivating charm that made it hard to look away.

He hastily invited her: “Let’s go to the side hall together.”

The bright and beautiful young woman beside him also came over boldly to look at Shen Weici’s face: “Third Cousin is truly beautiful. Let’s go to the side hall to chat and liven things up.”

Shen Weici glanced at Shen Mingqiu, who had come with her, and linked arms with Shen Mingqiu, nodding.

Yesterday, Shen Mingqiu had mentioned that Old Madam Shen’s maternal relatives would be visiting today. After asking a few questions, Shen Weici learned that the young man beside her was likely Wei Xiangyi, Old Madam Shen’s only unmarried grandson.

Wei Xiangyi was exactly twenty years old this year. Having passed the imperial examination, he was preparing for this year’s spring examination. Although he had a concubine in his room, his character and conduct, as described by Shen Mingqiu, were both good.

Shen Weici’s heart stirred slightly.

As they walked together, they encountered Song Zhang on the way.

Song Zhang was cold and indifferent, not even glancing at Shen Weici as he directly passed by.

Shen Mingqiu called out, “Second Brother Song,” but he only responded with a simple “mm.”

Wei Yunshuang, standing beside Wei Xiangyi, directly went up to Song Zhang, grabbed his arm, and called, “Brother Zhang.”

Song Zhang looked at this young girl he didn’t recognize at all, who had suddenly pounced on him. His displeased brows furrowed, but as his gaze subtly passed over Shen Weici, he paused and then smiled, gently touching Wei Yunshuang’s hair: “Little sister.”

Wei Xiangyi was stunned. He knew that his sister, in private, was infatuated with Song Zhang to the point of obsession. In reality, she had only seen Song Zhang once before, and that was by chance at the Marquis’s household.

He was afraid that Song Zhang would be displeased by his sister’s boldness, but unexpectedly, Song Zhang made such an intimate gesture.

He had heard about Song Zhang’s temperament before. Today’s scene truly shocked him.

He quickly went over to pull his sister aside and whispered, “Second Cousin still has matters to attend to. Don’t bother him.”

Song Zhang, however, looked at Wei Xiangyi with a faint smile: “It’s the New Year, and I have nothing to do. Where are you all going?”

Wei Xiangyi was still in a daze and hadn’t had time to respond when Wei Yunshuang, already holding Song Zhang’s hand, spoke: “We’re going to the side hall to chat. Brother Zhang, would you like to come along?”

Song Zhang raised an eyebrow: “Sure.”

Shen Weici stood to the side, watching as Wei Yunshuang almost pressed her entire body against Song Zhang. Song Zhang, however, maintained a faint smile, allowing her to hold his hand, and even had a hint of a smile in his eyes. She couldn’t help but wonder if their relationship had always been this close.

Although she wanted to avoid Song Zhang, she had already agreed to go to the side hall. Backing out now would seem too deliberate, so she had to harden her resolve and go along.

chapters.title: Such a Good Temper?
chapters.content:
The side hall was filled with people from the Marquis’s household and Old Madam Shen’s maternal relatives, chatting in small groups. Maids weaved through the crowd, creating a lively atmosphere.

Shen Weici’s gaze swept over Lady Wen, who was sitting among them. Lady Wen also gave her a cold look.

Shen Weici lowered her head, thinking that perhaps because the clan relatives were visiting these days, Old Madam Shen was afraid of the hassle of explaining, so she had Lady Wen brought back.

She wondered if Lady Wen would be sent back again.

Lost in thought, she was pulled by Shen Mingqiu to sit down.

Song Zhang sat prominently among the crowd, and the other cousins, upon seeing him, went over to ingratiate themselves.

Song Zhang responded indifferently, but his sleeve was still held by Wei Yunshuang.

Everyone watched this scene, secretly wondering if Song Zhang had some feelings for Wei Yunshuang.

Wei Yunshuang was not bad-looking. On the contrary, she had fair and delicate features, a coquettish and lovely temperament, which was very charming.

Shen Weici glanced at Song Zhang, who was surrounded by people, then averted her gaze.

Wei Xiangyi came over to strike up a conversation. The few of them stood in front of a large vase and chatted for a while, finding they had things in common.

Shen Weici found Wei Xiangyi’s speech a bit shy and reserved, but it also exuded a scholarly air.

Wei Xiangyi felt the side hall was too noisy and, after glancing at Shen Weici, said, “Let’s go to the small hall next door to talk.”

Shen Weici, holding onto Shen Mingqiu and Shen Yueqiu, went with him.

Song Zhang’s gaze swept over Shen Weici following Wei Xiangyi to the small hall, and he clenched his fist, almost walking over to pull Shen Weici out.
