He hadn’t spent much time at the Marquis’s household for the New Year. Today, he had left a pile of matters to return, fearing that she might take a fancy to those cousins. He hadn’t expected that in such a short time, she would already be getting along with someone.

Going over directly would show that he cared about her. Remembering Pei Zhan’s words, he endured the torment here, but couldn’t let go of his worry. He called a servant to go and check.

Wei Xiangyi was of the right age for Shen Weici. If Wei Xiangyi truly took a fancy to Shen Weici, he wanted to nip it in the bud early.

In the small hall, a chessboard was placed on the table, with pastries beside it. Shen Weici sat to the side, watching Shen Mingqiu and Wei Xiangyi play chess, occasionally joining in their conversation.

Shen Weici was also quiet, nibbling on a piece of plum blossom cake.

Wei Xiangyi saw Shen Weici’s elegant manner of eating the plum blossom cake and couldn’t help but ask her age.

Shen Weici smiled: “I’ve passed fifteen.”

Wei Xiangyi was taken aback, his heart stirring slightly. He then smiled and asked, “What does Third Cousin usually like to do?”

Shen Weici pursed her lips: “I just do some needlework and read books.”

Shen Mingqiu, sitting across from them, looked at Wei Xiangyi: “Are you only going to talk to Third Sister?”

Wei Xiangyi then realized and, blushing to the roots of his ears, hurriedly made his move.

Shen Weici found Wei Xiangyi’s flushed face amusing.

Recalling the sight of Wei Xiangyi’s father in the front hall earlier—his gentle and courteous demeanor—he seemed like a man with a good temper.

However, Wei Xiangyi’s mother wasn’t present, so she didn’t know if she was also a gentle woman.

Shen Weici only knew that Wei Xiangyi’s father was merely a seventh-rank official in the capital. Old Madam Shen’s maternal family had once been glorious, producing several Hanlin scholars. By the time it came to Old Madam Shen’s generation, their fortunes had declined. Only Old Madam Shen’s eldest brother had once served as a Minister, but he had long since retired from his position.

Shen Weici pondered that in such a scholarly family, they valued rules and status, and could be quite rigid and old-fashioned. If they found out that her mother wasn’t even a concubine, they would likely have many reservations.

Moreover, Old Madam Shen, although she had some sympathy for her, was fundamentally selfish and heartless. Shen Weici didn’t know if she would reveal the truth.

She had already given up on this matter in her heart. Whether it succeeded or not, she wasn’t holding out much hope.

Seeing Wei Xiangyi constantly trying to engage her in conversation, she still maintained her smile. After all, leaving a good impression was never wrong.

In such a scholarly family, marrying into it would mean more rules, but they also valued face. Generally, they wouldn’t do anything that would damage their reputation.

Half the morning passed with a game of chess that wasn’t finished. Shen Mingqiu gradually fell into a losing position and pulled Shen Weici over to help her.

Shen Weici was dragged over to look at the board, carefully observing the flaws in the game before making her move.

She hadn’t played chess in a long time. Much of what she had learned from her female tutor in the past had been forgotten. She had only played a few games with Shen Mingqiu in recent days, so her hand wasn’t completely out of practice.

Wei Xiangyi looked at where Shen Weici placed her piece and was stunned. He looked up at Shen Weici: “Third Cousin is also proficient in chess.”

Shen Weici smiled: “I’ve only learned a little. Third Cousin, please go easy on me.”

Wei Xiangyi looked at Shen Weici’s smile, her peach blossom eyes shining, her eyebrows like the moon, her cloud-like hair lightly framing her face, her red lips exuding fragrance. He was mesmerized.

He had never seen such a beautiful woman before. Just hearing her voice made his heart race. He couldn’t help but keep looking at her.

His ears burned, and the heat never subsided.

Shen Weici had also never seen a man blush like this before. His clear, infatuated gaze didn’t make her feel violated; instead, she sensed a touch of innocence in him.

Such a young man was honest. Shen Weici felt he would be easy to manage.

She lowered her head and softly said, “Third Cousin, it’s your turn.”

Wei Xiangyi, as if waking from a dream, hastily and embarrassedly made his move.

Shen Mingqiu, sitting beside them, saw this scene and smiled, picking up her tea to take a sip.

Soon, it was almost time for the feast. The game of chess still wasn’t finished.

Wei Xiangyi reluctantly looked at Shen Weici as they walked out together: “Third Cousin’s chess skills are excellent. I also found it challenging.”

Shen Weici smiled: “It’s just that Cousin was letting me win.”

As they spoke, a wall suddenly blocked their path. Who else could it be but Song Zhang?

Song Zhang still didn’t glance at Shen Weici, only casting a faint gaze at Wei Xiangyi: “Shall we go together?”

Wei Xiangyi had never expected Song Zhang to address him. Thinking that his father also wanted to ingratiate himself with Song Zhang, he quickly agreed.

Song Zhang, having said his piece, took a step forward.

Wei Yunshuang still followed behind Song Zhang, like a little tail, pulling at his sleeve. She didn’t forget to look back at Wei Xiangyi: “Big Brother, hurry up and follow.”

Wei Xiangyi paused, responded with an “mm,” and then reluctantly bade farewell to Shen Weici.

After the midday feast, it wouldn’t be long before they had to return. Who knew when they would meet again?

He looked at Shen Weici once more before leaving.

Shen Mingqiu looked at Wei Yunshuang, who was always following Song Zhang, and expressed her surprise: “Second Brother Song has such a good temper?”

“He never used to let women get close to him before.”

As she spoke, she looked at Shen Weici: “Could it be that Second Brother Song really likes Cousin Wei?”

Shen Weici shook her head: “It has nothing to do with us.”

Shen Mingqiu nodded, then looked at Shen Weici again: “Today, Princess Hui Min is in the Princess Dowager’s palace. Why has Second Brother Song returned to the Marquis’s household?”

“In the past, during the New Year, Second Brother Song would only return on the second day to pay respects to Princess Dowager, and then he would disappear. This time, he’s been seen several times.”

Shen Weici shook her head and, linking arms with Shen Mingqiu, walked forward and asked about Shen Mingqiu’s marriage prospects.

Shen Mingqiu smiled: “I will have my coming-of-age ceremony next March. My birth mother said she would look for any newly appointed Jinshi scholars.”

Shen Weici looked at the smile on Shen Mingqiu’s face and tightly held her hand: “I truly envy you.”

Shen Mingqiu laughed: “I envy you too. If I were as beautiful as you, I could pick anyone I wanted.”

Shen Weici gave a bitter smile. How could she pick anyone she wanted? Lady Wen wouldn’t allow her to have it so easy.

chapters.title: Forced Kiss in the Rockery
chapters.content:
In the afternoon, as the Wei family was about to leave, two of Wei family’s young ladies suddenly approached Shen Weici and whispered, “Is what’s being said outside true?”

Shen Weici quickly understood their meaning, but she couldn’t answer that.

She had intended to brush them off vaguely, but unexpectedly, Song Zhang stood by her side and coldly stated, “Why wouldn’t it be true? What the young master says is never false.”

Shen Weici was taken aback and looked up at Song Zhang, only to see him turn his head away with a cold expression, not saying another word before leaving.

He was being so arrogantly coy.

The two Wei family young ladies, upon hearing Song Zhang’s words, knew it was true. They looked at Wen Shi and Shen Zhaozhao, who was standing beside her, with disdain. “So wicked.”

Then they turned to Shen Weici, taking her hand with sympathetic expressions. “You’ve suffered, sister.”

Shen Weici was startled but soon gave a faint smile.

Wei Xiangyi followed his father and uncles toward the main gate, but he kept turning back to look at Shen Weici.

Seeing her standing and talking with his two cousins, not even coming to see them off, he felt an inexplicable sense of loss.

He said to his father beside him, “My two cousins are still back there. I’ll go call them over.”

As he was about to run back, someone blocked his path. Looking up, he saw it was Song Zhang.

Song Zhang stood with his hands behind his back, wearing a rust-colored round-collar, narrow-sleeved robe with large floral patterns. A silver belt with silver pendants and a silver incense pouch hung at his waist, and a ruby dagger was tucked into his belt. His tall and imposing figure stood out against the snowy backdrop, appearing particularly refined without the heavy winter cloak that others wore.

Wei Xiangyi only saw the mocking, half-smile on Song Zhang’s thin lips, and the warning in his phoenix-like eyes, which made him inexplicably uneasy and panicked.

Instinctively, he turned away.

Meanwhile, Shen Weici finished her conversation with the Wei family ladies and walked toward the front gate with them. As they reached the gate, one of them took her hand and said, “When early spring comes, I’ll send an invitation for you to visit my place. We can go to the flower-viewing banquet together.”

Shen Weici smiled. “Alright.”

Beside them, Shen Zhaozhao watched as the cousins who used to be close only to her now treated Shen Weici with such warmth. She was so angry that her body trembled.

Earlier that morning in the cloister, she had taken the initiative to talk to them, but they had lazily ignored her, even speaking ill of her behind her back. When she confronted them, they had left with sarcastic remarks.

In the past, within the Marquis’s residence, she had been the legitimate daughter who was the center of attention wherever she went. Even her cousins had doted on her. Why had everything changed now? Even Wei Xiangyi was getting close to Shen Weici.

Shen Zhaozhao tightly gripped her mother’s hand. Wen Shi noticed her daughter’s distress and looked down at her expression. She quickly stepped in front of her and whispered, “Endure it.”

“Shen Weici isn’t that easy to deal with. There will be a chance to teach her a lesson.”

Shen Weici had long sensed Shen Zhaozhao’s hateful gaze. She looked over and saw Wen Shi blocking Shen Zhaozhao, saying something to her. Shen Zhaozhao’s ferocious expression then softened.

Shen Weici pressed her lips together and averted her gaze.

During the New Year holidays, Shen Weici had a rare moment of leisure.

She still went early to the kitchen to prepare soup for Old Madam Shen and gave her a shoulder massage. On her way back, she would visit Shen Mingqiu.

She paid no mind to Wen Shi’s affairs. When she went to greet her father in the morning, she learned that Wen Shi had returned for only three days before being sent back to the countryside.

It was said that Old Madam Shen had forcefully made this decision. That day, Wen Shi had knelt in the snow, begging Old Madam Shen, and even Shen Yanli had knelt to plead, but Old Madam Shen had not relented in the slightest.

Shen Weici was not surprised by Old Madam Shen’s reaction. After all, the incident of her falling into the water had been handled by Song Zhang on her behalf. Song Zhang was not bound by the Marquis’s residence, and whatever he said outside was the truth—there was no choice but to believe him.

If Song Zhang had not intervened with Old Madam Shen for her, Old Madam Shen would likely have kept the matter hidden, as it was a scandal that would tarnish the reputation of the Jian’an Marquis’s household.

Old Madam Shen considered interests and reputation above all else. Wen Shi’s pleas were insignificant.

The New Year holidays passed quickly. Shen Weici was called to her father’s study. As soon as she entered, she saw her father holding a box for her. “This is for you.”

Shen Weici looked at the box in her father’s hand, startled. She took it and opened it, only to find a gold-inlaid jade bracelet inside.

She looked at her father in bewilderment. “Father, why are you suddenly giving me this?”

Shen Rongsheng looked at Shen Weici with a guilty sigh. “Last time, the gift sent to you was a mistake made by the servants. This is to make it up to you.”

As he spoke, Shen Rongsheng looked at Shen Weici’s face and said softly, “I’ve seen how filial you’ve been to Old Madam Shen these days. You’ve endured hardships before and are a sensible child. I haven’t shown you much care either.”

“You’ve never caused trouble despite how your mother has treated you. I’ve seen it all.”

Shen Weici placed the box back into her father’s hands and seriously shook her head. “Your daughter has never cared about these things. As long as Father is well, your daughter has never felt wronged.”

“If Father is giving this to me out of guilt, your daughter does not wish to accept it. Please give it to Second Sister instead. She needs Father’s care more now.”

After saying this, Shen Weici looked at her father again. “Father, your daughter understands why the second branch has come to this. Once your daughter is married off, my mother will be at ease, and the family will be harmonious again.”

Shen Rongsheng stared blankly at the returned box in his hands, feeling a pang of heartache at how sensible his daughter was.

If Zhaozhao were half as sensible as Weici, the family wouldn’t be in such a mess now.

He also understood that Shen Weici’s words were not wrong. He looked at her and said softly, “Rest assured, from now on, your marriage will be arranged by me and Old Madam Shen. We won’t let your mother handle it anymore.”

“After the spring imperial examinations in March, I will carefully select a good family for you.”

Shen Weici expressed her gratitude to her father.

As she left Lingzhu Residence, the white snow fell on her face. Yue Deng came over with an umbrella to shield her. Shen Weici lightly extended her finger to catch the snowflakes, her gaze filled with a sense of loss.

Her heart felt empty, and she didn’t know why.

Perhaps it was the moment her father had given her the bracelet—she had suddenly felt nauseous.

The feeling of disgust had almost made her lose control of her emotions and vomit.

That sense of weariness had not subsided even now. She walked silently along the twilight-lit bluestone path, tightly wrapping her cloak around herself. With each step, she trod on the freshly fallen snow, watching it melt and disappear in an instant.

As she walked with her head down, passing by the lake, she suddenly felt a hand reach out. Before she could react, she was pulled into a cave within a rockery.

Inside the cave, it was even darker, and she couldn’t see anything. Before she could cry out in surprise, her lips were sealed by someone’s passionate and forceful kiss.

The kiss was fierce and overpowering. A scorching hand tightly gripped her waist, as if trying to press her deeply into his embrace.

Shen Weici couldn’t breathe.

chapters.title: Have You Agreed to Be Mine?
chapters.content:
Song Zhang unleashed all the coldness he had endured these days onto Shen Weici.

That bastard Pei Zhan and his terrible idea—it hadn’t made Shen Weici ache for him. Instead, it had left him sleepless and restless, driven to the brink of madness.

He ignored her, and she didn’t spare him a single glance.

He paraded women in front of her, yet she still smiled and chatted with other men.

He deliberately approached her, giving her the chance to initiate conversation, but she remained distant, politely addressing him as “Young Master Song” before walking past him.

Song Zhang felt as if Shen Weici was stabbing his heart.

Even if she was playing hard to get, he couldn’t bear it.

He realized that a woman had to be taken by force.

In those border countries, didn’t they also take beautiful women by force?

At this moment, Song Zhang was like a wild beast. His ragged breathing made Shen Weici’s heart race with fear.

She struggled, kicking her legs and pushing against his chest, but he impatiently gripped her chin, forcing her to submit and focus.

After kissing her to his satisfaction, Song Zhang reached out and gently brushed away the moisture from her eyes, tucking her loose hair behind her ear. Then, with a hoarse voice, he questioned her, “You go to Old Madam Shen every day to show your devotion. Are you hoping she will arrange a good marriage for you?”

The hot breath sprayed over her, forcing Shen Weici to turn her face away.

She didn’t want to answer him.

Her fingers still pushed against his chest as she gritted her teeth, enduring her trembling emotions. In a low voice, she said, “What does that have to do with Young Master Song?”

Hearing this, Song Zhang was furious.

For Shen Weici’s sake, he had suppressed much of his temper. If it were in the past, once he took a liking to someone, he would take them directly. Yet with her, he had approached step by step, which was already more than patient enough.

He sneered, “How many times have I kissed you already? And then you’ll marry someone else, using the lips I’ve kissed to kiss another man?”

Shen Weici hadn’t expected Song Zhang to speak so vulgar and shamelessly.

She trembled slightly. “If Young Master Song still knows shame, then you should know how ridiculous your words are.”

As she spoke, she pushed him forcefully. “I want to go back now.”

Song Zhang was annoyed by her pushing.

Though Shen Weici’s strength was not great, her resistance irritated him.

He had no patience left to coax her. She was just a commoner-born daughter—why should he have to coax her so much?

Without further hesitation, he scooped her up by the waist and carried her out.

He couldn’t endure the torment any longer. It was her fault for ignoring him.

Shen Weici was terrified by Song Zhang’s boldness in carrying her out of the rockery. Although it was dusk, if a maidservant saw them, how could she live with the shame?

She tightly clutched Song Zhang’s clothes, tears welling in her eyes, her voice trembling. “Don’t...”

Song Zhang, however, looked down at her with a dark expression. “Relax.”

“No one will see.”

Then he pressed her face into his chest, covering her with his cloak, and strode off in one direction.

Shen Weici’s entire body was rigid. She didn’t dare struggle or make a sound, but her body trembled violently.

She only heard the sound of a door being kicked open, and then she was thrown onto a bed.

Shen Weici panicked and propped herself up from the bed, only to see Song Zhang immediately lean down and pin her to the bed, kissing her without a word.

Shen Weici was terrified by Song Zhang’s actions, her face turning pale. She looked into his dark, desire-filled eyes and bit down hard with her teeth.

Song Zhang couldn’t retreat in time, and his tongue was bitten, drawing blood. He hissed in pain, then angrily gripped her chin, his face dark with anger. “What are you afraid of? Do you think I won’t take responsibility?”

“At worst, I’ll make you my concubine. I’ll still marry you with full honors, and after that, I’ll give you a grand dowry. Whatever you want, I’ll provide. Do you think I’d let you suffer?”

A concubine was only half a step below a wife and would not be at the mercy of the main wife like a mere concubine. She would have a voice in the household, and any children would be raised as legitimate.

In truth, Song Zhang thought Shen Weici should be satisfied.

Shen Weici, with her chin gripped by Song Zhang, couldn’t speak, but she sobbed and shook her head, refusing to agree.

Song Zhang lowered his head and began to untie his leather belt, his forehead beaded with sweat from restraint. He felt that if he endured any longer, he might go mad.

He had never truly been with a woman before and was actually a little nervous, afraid he wouldn’t perform well.

After binding her, he rarely showed tenderness as he leaned down and coaxed her, “I’ve never mistreated my women. Right now, I’m wholeheartedly devoted to you. Be sensible, and I’ll treat you well.”

“If you’re not sensible and insist on opposing me, I’ll take you and then go directly to Old Madam Shen to ask for you as a concubine. Do you want to be a concubine or a secondary wife?”

Shen Weici’s tear-filled, flushed eyes were brimming with tears. She choked out, “Even if you ask for me, I am still chaste. How can you treat me like this? Where is my dignity?”

Song Zhang had truly never considered this. Whether she was chaste or not, no one else would know.

Then he heard Shen Weici’s soft, hoarse voice, “Besides, my mother has been gone for less than a year. I must at least observe a year of mourning before I can marry. Can’t Young Master Song wait a little longer for me?”

Song Zhang was taken aback. He looked at the soft, impossibly beautiful woman beneath him, then at the tears in her eyes, and couldn’t help but say, “Then why did you agree to marry Zhang Yuanheng without mentioning the mourning period?”

Shen Weici blinked her tearful eyes. Her fair skin was dotted with tears, and her peach-blossom eyes, already captivating, became even more alluring with the tears, her brows like distant mountains in a light, gentle painting.

Even someone like Song Zhang, who had never known how to cherish beauty, couldn’t help but loosen his grip.

With a blink, a line of tears fell from Shen Weici’s eyes into her hair, the pure white jade-like color blending into the clouds, tempting Song Zhang’s restless heart. His body uncontrollably pressed down on hers.

Then he heard her soft voice, “I had already discussed it with Young Master Zhang. If the marriage was settled, we would only consummate it after July. He agreed.”

Song Zhang’s face darkened upon hearing this, and he frowned in displeasure. “You even discussed this with him?”

Shen Weici turned her face away, biting her lip and refusing to speak.

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici’s expression and paused again.

Shen Weici’s reasoning was actually quite sound.

For commoners, the rules for observing mourning were not so strict, and even less so for women.

But if a woman wanted to mourn her mother, it was a display of filial piety.

He had originally made up his mind to take her tonight, but Shen Weici’s words made him feel that he shouldn’t disregard her filial piety.

He knew she and her mother had relied on each other and had not had an easy life.

Song Zhang forcibly suppressed his anger and looked down at her with his dark eyes. “Then have you agreed to be mine?”

“I’ll go to your father after July and ask for your hand.”

“From now on, you’re not allowed to flirt with other men.”

“Otherwise, after all this, do you think I’ll tolerate it?”

Shen Weici saw that Song Zhang had said this and knew he had likely agreed.

She couldn’t find the words, so she simply closed her damp eyes.

Song Zhang took her silence as consent. He supported himself with a hand on Shen Weici’s cheek and leaned down to kiss her fiercely once more before untying the leather belt that bound her wrist.

chapters.title: Call Me Brother Zhen
chapters.content:
Although Song Zhang had spared Shen Weici this time, the discomfort in his body had not subsided.

He held Shen Weici tightly in his arms and looked at her. “This time I’m doing as you wish, but you must not deceive me.”

“From now on, you must not avoid me when you see me. Do you agree?”

The deep, scorching voice echoed above her head. Shen Weici was momentarily stunned, and before she could react, she saw his displeased expression and nodded blankly.

Then she saw Song Zhang’s expression darken. He lowered his head to kiss her, took her hand downward, and buried his face in her neck, hoarsely asking, “Will this do?”

Shen Weici’s mind went blank. “Do what?”

Sweat had already beaded on Song Zhang’s forehead. Gritting his teeth, he guided her hand in motion, then bit her neck. “From now on, in private, you’ll call me Second Brother, Brother Zhen. Understand?”

Shen Weici hadn’t heard a word Song Zhang said. All her attention was on her hand, which terrified her. Her face paled as she tried to pull back, but he held it tightly, not allowing the slightest movement.

Seeing that Shen Weici didn’t respond, Song Zhang bit down harder in dissatisfaction, his throat rolling. “Call me once, let me hear it.”

Shen Weici belatedly realized and called out, “Second Brother.”

Song Zhang urgently pressed her, “Say it a few more times. Good Weici, quickly...”

Shen Weici was at a loss, her hand gripped tightly by Song Zhang. She wanted to lower her head and look, but her lips were suddenly captured by Song Zhang’s kiss. In the trembling candlelight, she let out a soft, pleasing whimper.

It wasn’t until the room was completely dark that Song Zhang finally released Shen Weici’s hand. He squinted at her in his arms, watching her slight panting.

Her forehead was damp with tears, and fine strands of hair clung to her temples. The jade earrings at her fair ears were half-hidden in her dark hair, only a hint of green visible.

He reached out a long finger to trace her moist, alluring eye corners, then noticed her slightly swollen lips and red-rimmed eyes. He thought of how even when she was angry, her voice remained soft and gentle. Being treated like this must have grieved her.

He pulled her into a full embrace, his heart aching with both pity and affection. From her forehead to her nose, then to her lips, he showered her with tender, loving kisses.

Shen Weici remained still, lowering her lashes and allowing Song Zhang to do as he pleased.

She understood that things had come to this point. Given Song Zhang’s nature, she couldn’t resist him.

She could only comply with him for now.

Perhaps he was just momentarily infatuated. A gentle and obedient woman might bore him quickly.

Shen Weici had seen too many such stories.

Song Zhang was very pleased with Shen Weici’s current compliance. The closer he looked at her, the more beautiful she seemed.

But her eyes avoided him, which displeased him.

He lifted her chin, forcing her to look at him. His phoenix-like eyes held satisfaction and tenderness. “Tired?”

Shen Weici heard the word “tired” and thought of what he had just done. Her face paled, and she shook her head.

She glanced at Song Zhang’s expression a few times before softly asking, “Where is my maid?”

Song Zhang, unwilling to let go of Shen Weici’s soft fingers, replied, “My men have taken her to rest. Don’t worry.”

Shen Weici’s gaze then shifted to the unfamiliar room. She lowered her voice and asked, “Where is this?”

Song Zhang looked at her. “The Moon-Facing Pavilion in the bamboo forest behind my courtyard. This is my territory, with my people. No one will come in.”

Shen Weici felt a slight relief in her heart.

As long as it wasn’t Song Zhang’s own courtyard, it would be fine. Otherwise, if Princess Huimin wanted to investigate, she could easily find out at Guansong Residence.

She pressed her lips together, her tearful vision blurring as she looked at Song Zhang’s chin. “Can I go back now?”

Her peripheral vision caught Song Zhang’s expression, and she softly added, “I’m afraid if I return too late, it will be hard to explain.”

Song Zhang, unsatisfied, pulled her closer. “Why go back so early?”

“It’s just that I stayed out a bit long. Anyway, I’ll send you back later.”

“Absolutely no one must see.”

Shen Weici said no more.

She understood that saying more wouldn’t make much difference. She and Song Zhang were of different statuses, with different concerns. She could only be held tightly in Song Zhang’s arms.

Song Zhang was uncomfortable and his trousers were soiled; he needed to bathe.

He stood up and looked at Shen Weici. “Wait for me a moment. I’ll send you back after I bathe.”

With that, he directly walked toward the bathtub behind the screen.

Shen Weici hadn’t expected Song Zhang to have a bathtub prepared here, with hot water already ready. It seemed he had planned this all along.

Shen Weici watched Song Zhang’s figure disappear behind the screen. She stood up from the bed, intending to leave.

But as she reached the door, she hesitated. She had finally managed to placate Song Zhang; leaving now would ruin everything. So she turned back and sat on the bed, straightening her clothes.

Behind the screen, Song Zhang had heard her footsteps and held his breath, waiting for her next move. Fortunately, she didn’t leave, and his cold gaze finally relaxed.

When Song Zhang emerged from behind the screen after bathing, he wore only white trousers, with nothing on top. Shen Weici glanced at him and quickly averted her eyes.

Seeing Shen Weici’s shy profile, the jade earrings swaying against her fair skin, and the delicate point of her chin above the neat white collar, Song Zhang’s heart softened.

He chuckled softly and placed the clothes in his hand into hers. “Dress me.”

He said this as if it were the most natural thing in the world, as if she should do it.

Shen Weici looked down at the bright red, flamboyant round-collared brocade robe in her hands. After a long struggle, she stood up to dress Song Zhang.

Men’s clothing was much easier to put on than women’s, but Song Zhang was tall, with broad shoulders and a narrow waist. Combined with the embarrassment of his bronze skin approaching her, Shen Weici found it very difficult.

Song Zhang bent slightly to make it easier for her, constantly lowering his head to watch her movements.

Her actions were meticulous and gentle, her fingers brushing against his skin like a feather.

Her beautiful brows were lowered, and those lips he had just kissed, with their warm breath on his chest, could make his breath catch.

Although he had been attended to by many since childhood, only when Shen Weici dressed him did he feel an indescribable sense of satisfaction.

Shen Weici bent down to fasten his belt, then adjusted his lapels before looking up at him. “Done.”

Song Zhang looked into her eyes and couldn’t help but cup her face, bending down to kiss her forehead, a smile playing at his lips.

He then took a cloak to drape over Shen Weici. Seeing his clumsy attempts, she hesitated before saying, “Let me do it myself.”

But Song Zhang insisted on fastening it for her. After securing it, he even considerately adjusted it for her.

chapters.title: In Private, You Are Mine
chapters.content:
Shen Weici lowered her head to look at the cloak Song Zhang had fastened. It was neat and proper, with nothing amiss, so she set her mind at ease.

Song Zhang then helped Shen Weici put on the hood of the cloak. Looking at the small face framed by the fox fur, with her reddened nose, red-rimmed eyes, and those cherry lips that always caught his attention, he couldn’t resist bending down to kiss her lips once more.

The recent days of unrest and anxiety in his heart were finally soothed. Holding Shen Weici’s hand, he walked forward.

He was still worried she might be cold, so he kept her shoulder in his arms, unwilling to let go.

Seeing Song Zhang’s increasingly bold and improper actions, Shen Weici quickly pushed against his chest and whispered, “It’s not good if someone sees us.”

Song Zhang looked down at Shen Weici’s seemingly shy expression. That was true—he couldn’t marry her until after July, and she valued her reputation. So he reluctantly loosened his hold.

He walked in front of her, his tall body shielding her from the wind and snow.

The path from the small bamboo forest behind to the rear west courtyard was deserted. Song Zhang would walk a few steps, then stop, and whenever they reached a secluded spot, he would pause to hold Shen Weici’s hand, teasing her until she was almost angry before letting go.

As they neared the entrance of Linchun Courtyard, Song Zhang released Shen Weici’s hand and looked down at her. “Out there, I’ll keep my distance as promised. But in private, you are mine. Don’t forget that.”

Shen Weici was taken aback for a moment before nodding, then lowered her head to leave.

Song Zhang couldn’t bear to part with her. It was rare for Shen Weici to be so compliant, allowing him to kiss and hold her. He didn’t know when he’d have the chance again.

Tomorrow, he had to accompany the Emperor to Nanshan Temple to pray for five days. He wouldn’t be able to see her until he returned.

He held Shen Weici’s hand, his eyes gleaming in the night. “Call me Brother Zhen once more.”

Shen Weici hesitated slightly before softly saying, “Brother Zhen.”

Satisfied, Song Zhang finally let go of her hand and let her leave.

Shen Weici sighed in relief and quickly lifted her skirt to move forward. She saw Yue Deng, her maid, looking around in confusion near the courtyard gate.

Upon seeing Shen Weici, Yue Deng hurried over and asked, “How did we end up here?”

Shen Weici saw that Yue Deng’s expression suggested she had been knocked out by Song Zhang’s men again. She tightly held her hand and whispered, “Just say we stayed too long at Father’s place.”

Yue Deng understood and nodded.

Song Zhang stood in the night, watching Shen Weici’s retreating figure enter Linchun Courtyard before turning to leave.

A few more days passed, and the weather gradually warmed. The heavy snow outside had also lessened.

Shen Weici sat in her room, collecting plum blossoms to dry for a while. She planned to make some plum blossom pastries to send to each courtyard for tasting.

Ever since her maternal grandmother arrived, her mother had fallen seriously ill. The kitchen chores had fallen to her, and from time to time, she would make some pastries with the available ingredients for her mother to try.

Shen Weici crouched in the courtyard, carefully selecting plum blossoms, when a voice calling her “Third Sister” made her look up. She saw Shen Zhaozhao entering with a smile.

Shen Weici looked at Shen Zhaozhao’s smiling face and paused before smiling back and standing up. She walked over and asked, “Second Sister, have you come to drink some tea?”

Shen Zhaozhao glanced at Shen Weici’s smile, then went over and affectionately linked arms with her. “That’s fine. I haven’t had tea at Third Sister’s place before.”

Yue Deng and He Xia stood to the side, stunned, their eyes nearly popping out of their sockets.

Shen Weici glanced at Yue Deng. “Quickly, pour Second Sister a cup of silver plum tea.”

Yue Deng snapped out of it and hurried to pour the tea.

Shen Zhaozhao followed Shen Weici to the small table by the west side room and sat down. She took the teacup handed to her by Yue Deng, took a light sip, and the fragrance filled her nose. She couldn’t help but ask curiously, “This tea is truly fragrant.”

Shen Weici smiled. “This is made by boiling plum blossoms and honeysuckle with snow water, then adding some pine tips. Yu Yang doesn’t have as many fine things as the capital, so I just picked some ordinary ingredients. I was worried Second Sister wouldn’t be used to it.”

Shen Zhaozhao laughed. “How could I not be used to it? Next time, I’ll come to Third Sister’s place for tea again.”

Shen Weici smiled. “Second Sister is welcome anytime.”

Shen Zhaozhao looked around the simple room, then had her senior maid bring over the fabric she was holding and placed it in front of Shen Weici. “Sister, I was foolish before, always targeting you. You don’t blame me, do you?”

“Consider this my apology. From now on, we’ll be close sisters, supporting each other. Don’t you agree?”

Shen Weici lowered her gaze to the fabric Shen Zhaozhao pushed forward—a goose-yellow floral satin, elegant and understated yet eye-catching. It clearly wasn’t cheap.

She looked at Shen Zhaozhao and softly said, “I’ve always considered Second Sister a good sister and never felt that you were targeting me.”

“The fabric... I can’t accept it for no reason. Second Sister, please take it back.”

But Shen Zhaozhao forcefully pushed the fabric toward Shen Weici again. “If Third Sister doesn’t accept it, doesn’t that mean you’re rejecting my goodwill?”

She then looked dejected. “Father always says we are sisters of the same family and should be close. Now that I’m taking the initiative to be friendly, it seems Third Sister still won’t forgive me.”

Shen Weici looked at Shen Zhaozhao’s expression and smiled again. “Since it’s Second Sister’s kind intention, I’ll have to accept it.”

With that, Shen Weici called Yue Deng to take the fabric away and put it aside.

Yue Deng, standing nearby, was so shocked by Shen Zhaozhao’s words that she almost dropped her jaw. For a moment, she even thought the person in front of her wasn’t Shen Zhaozhao. It wasn’t until she heard Shen Weici’s voice that she snapped back to reality and quickly took the fabric outside.

As soon as she went out, He Xia and Yan Er rushed over. Seeing the floral satin in Yue Deng’s hands, they found it unbelievable and repeatedly asked, “Is this really from Second Young Lady?”

Yue Deng pinched Yan Er and He Xia’s arms. “It’s true, I swear. Believe me now.”

Back inside, Shen Zhaozhao saw that Shen Weici had accepted the gift and said to her, “Yesterday, Grandmother told me that she had invited an imperial physician to see us today. Shall we go to Grandmother’s place together now?”

Shen Weici glanced at Shen Zhaozhao and nodded with a smile. “Alright.”

The two stood up and walked outside together.

Shen Zhaozhao’s hand remained linked with Shen Weici’s wrist the entire time, leaning close to her and speaking with a smile, as if they were extremely close.

Shen Weici, of course, didn’t believe that Shen Zhaozhao had suddenly changed. She simply went along with it.

She didn’t believe that a person’s nature could change so suddenly, nor that someone who had looked at her with hatred just a few days ago could now be so affectionate toward her.

As they passed the stone bridge, Shen Weici still couldn’t help but tense up, bracing herself in case Shen Zhaozhao pulled the same stunt as before. Fortunately, she did nothing of the sort.

When they arrived at Ci’an Hall, Old Madam Shen was also slightly surprised to see Shen Zhaozhao and Shen Weici entering arm in arm, but she soon smiled. “It’s good to see you two getting along.”

Shen Zhaozhao let go of Shen Weici’s hand and went to Old Madam Shen’s side, leaning against her shoulder. “In the past, it was your granddaughter who was foolish. Grandmother won’t blame me, will you?”

Old Madam Shen pinched Shen Zhaozhao’s face, her expression full of affectionate sighs. “As long as you understand, you’ve been the one I’ve watched grow up since you were little. How could Grandmother blame you?”

Shen Weici watched the scene with a detached expression, her face unreadable.

chapters.title: Unable to Conceive
chapters.content:
Shen Weici sat quietly to the side, watching Shen Lao Tatai and Shen Zhaozhao sitting together, a flawless smile on her face.

Shen Lao Tatai turned to Shen Weici: “Zhaozhao was a bit off before, don’t take it to heart. You share a room, so you should interact more.”

Shen Weici smiled gently: “I’ve always wanted to be closer to Second Sister. Grandmother, rest assured.”

Only then did Shen Lao Tatai nod in relief.

Soon after, the imperial physician Lin Yizheng arrived. Seeing Shen Weici sitting to the side, he instinctively prepared to bow in greeting, then suddenly remembered the presence of the elder matriarch and instead greeted her first.

Shen Lao Tatai was courteous to Lin Yizheng as well, exchanging pleasantries before asking him to examine Shen Weici and Shen Zhaozhao.

Lin Yizheng agreed and first took Shen Weici’s pulse.

The hall was completely silent during the examination. Shen Lao Tatai watched Lin Yizheng intently, and as soon as he released her wrist, she hurriedly asked, “How is she?”

Lin Yizheng replied: “Her pulse still shows some cold energy, but with further regulation, there should be no major issues.”

Shen Lao Tatai pressed further: “And what about her ability to bear children?”

Lin Yizheng smiled slightly: “No major issues there.”

Shen Lao Tatai nodded in relief: “That’s good.”

Next, Lin Yizheng took Shen Zhaozhao’s pulse. After a moment, his expression turned solemn. He cupped his hands toward Shen Lao Tatai and said, “Miss Shen’s pulse is light and floating, with deep cold syndrome. I fear conceiving may be difficult for her. She must take great care to nurture her health.”

Shen Lao Tatai was taken aback—she hadn’t expected it to be Shen Zhaozhao who would struggle with fertility now.

She quickly asked what to do, and Lin Yizheng said that warming the body and replenishing qi, with long-term care, could still restore her health.

Shen Lao Tatai immediately ordered a maid beside her to follow Lin Yizheng to prepare the prescription.

Hearing Lin Yizheng’s words, Shen Zhaozhao was also startled. Her eyes reddened, and she buried her face in Shen Lao Tatai’s arms, sobbing, “Grandmother…”

Shen Lao Tatai held her tightly, comforting her, “It’s alright, Grandmother will never let anything happen to you. We will definitely restore your health.”

As she spoke, she turned to the personal maid beside her: “Go to my storage room and bring the two decades-old ginseng roots for Zhaozhao. Also send some bird’s nest and blood-tonifying pills.”

Chang Momomo glanced at Shen Weici with a hint of confusion. When the old matriarch had learned that Shen Weici’s cold constitution was unfavorable for childbearing, she hadn’t given her a single thing—only a cloak during the boating accident.

Yet, of those who had served at her side these days, no one had been as devoted as the Third Young Miss.

But seeing Shen Weici’s calm and concerned expression as she watched Shen Zhaozhao, Chang Momomo sighed silently. The most understanding children always ended up the most wronged. She could only hope the old matriarch would be kinder to the Third Young Miss.

Shen Weici listened to Shen Zhaozhao’s distressed sobs and the affectionate exchange between her and Shen Lao Tatai. She didn’t want to stay, but leaving would make her seem heartless, and staying would leave her with nothing to say. She had no choice but to endure it silently.

Fortunately, Shen Yanli arrived with Wei Xiangyi. Seeing Shen Zhaozhao crying, Shen Yanli quickly went to console her, giving Shen Weici an excuse to leave first due to the arrival of guests.

Once outside Cishou Hall, she let out a breath of relief and prepared to return.

But then a voice called out from behind. Turning, she saw that Wei Xiangyi had followed her.

She watched his approaching figure, wondering why he had left the old matriarch’s presence to chase after her.

Wei Xiangyi stopped in front of Shen Weici. The young man’s eyes were exceptionally clear, and though he was only two years younger than Song Zhang, his features were more open and refined, far more serene than Song Zhang’s.

As soon as he arrived, his bright gaze fell on Shen Weici, and he called out, “Cousin Ci.”

Shen Weici assumed he now knew her name, so she smiled slightly and asked softly, “Does Cousin have something to say to me?”

Wei Xiangyi looked at Shen Weici’s smiling eyes. Though she had peach-blossom eyes, her gaze was gentle, and her voice was soft. Her delicate eyebrows were like ink-wash landscapes, graceful as willows by a lake—both enchanting and tender.

It was the first time he had seen someone so beautiful, and he had heard the rumors about her.

He knew Shen Zhaozhao’s temper could be arrogant, and seeing how delicate Shen Weici appeared, he couldn’t help but worry about her as he returned.

Then he noticed her green dress, the embroidered flowers at the collar as tranquil as she was, and his heart began to race again.

He stammered slightly, embarrassed: “Just now, I hadn’t spoken to Cousin yet when you left. I also remembered our last chess game and was wondering if we’d have another chance to play.”

His fair skin was clear and refined, with red lips and white teeth—a clear sign of a well-bred young master from a noble family.

Seeing his ears turn completely red, Shen Weici couldn’t help but smile. She truly couldn’t tell he was someone who already had a concubine.

She could also sense that Wei Xiangyi might have feelings for her, but she didn’t hold much hope for this potential match. She gave a polite, noncommittal smile: “If the opportunity arises, we can play chess again, Cousin.”

Wei Xiangyi quickly replied, “I came today to borrow some current affairs books from Yanli. I happen to have time to play chess with you, Cousin.”

Shen Weici looked at him and said, “I’ve heard you passed the imperial examinations. This year is the spring palace exams, so you should focus on that first.”

Wei Xiangyi’s eyes were fixed on Shen Weici’s every expression. Seeing her refusal, his face flushed with embarrassment, and he stammered, “It’s… it’s fine.”

Shen Weici watched as Wei Xiangyi’s cheeks turned red. She thought that perhaps, having grown up reading Confucian classics in a scholarly family, his concubine might have been arranged by his mother.

In truth, Wei Xiangyi could be a suitable candidate for her future husband. After all, he had a good temperament, came from a scholarly family with proper etiquette, and was closely connected to the Marquis’s mansion.

But she didn’t entirely expect Wei Xiangyi to come forward with a marriage proposal. Scholarly families valued reputation and background, and as a concubine’s daughter, she might not be deemed worthy by them. Moreover, Wei Xiangyi seemed like someone who listened to his family.

She smiled again, still gently declining: “Cousin, the spring palace exams are important. I wouldn’t dare delay you. With just over a month until the exams, I’d rather see you achieve success and have your name listed on the golden roll.”

Hearing this, Wei Xiangyi was stunned. He looked at Shen Weici, his lips parting as if he wanted to say something, but his mind was stuck on her words—*I’d rather see you achieve success and have your name listed on the golden roll.*

Did she perhaps have feelings for him too?

Wei Xiangyi stood there in a daze for a long time. By the time he came to his senses, Shen Weici had already turned and left. He was frustrated with himself for forgetting to speak earlier.

He watched her retreating figure, graceful and slender, and stood there a while longer.

Yue Deng, walking beside Shen Weici, glanced back and then at her mistress, unable to suppress a smile as she covered her mouth: “Miss, he’s still watching you.”

“Could it be that he’s taken a liking to you, Miss? He’s quite handsome, and his family background is respectable too.”

Shen Weici lowered her gaze without responding. She simply stepped past a fallen plum blossom petal and disappeared from Wei Xiangyi’s line of sight.
